chapters.title: Chapter 251
paragraphs: My prediction that Zhuge Gyun would win turned out to be spectacularly wrong.
By the time we reached the area where his duel and several others were being held, the crowd was roaring the Invincible Divine Sword’s name while Zhuge Gyun sat there in a daze.
“What happened? You lost?”
Zhuge Gyun gave a bitter nod.
“I was completely toyed with. I couldn’t touch so much as a hair on his head.”
Zhuge Gyun was a direct descendant of the Zhuge Clan, one of the Five Great Families.
As his epithet, the Divine Marvel Dragon, suggested, his true weapon was his brilliant mind. But he had also learned his family’s secret arts and was an exceptional martial artist in his own right.
Intelligence alone wasn’t enough to earn a place among the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes.
And someone toyed with him?
Then his opponent was clearly a league or two above him.
My curiosity piqued, I asked Zhuge Gyun, “Where is he?”
“He probably left right after the duel... Huh? There he is.”
I followed Zhuge Gyun’s finger and narrowed my eyes.
“That guy? The one stuffing his face with dumplings?”
“Yes.”
“What’s wrong?”
“Nothing. There’s just something familiar about him.”

He wore a baggy robe and a bamboo hat pulled low over his face. I couldn’t make out his features or even his build, but there was something strangely familiar about the sight of him shoveling dumplings into his mouth.
Where have I seen him before?
At times like this, the direct approach was best. I headed toward the Invincible Divine Sword.
The closer I got, the less certain I became that I recognized him. But I did realize one thing.
He’s strong.
His posture was full of openings, and he looked so carefree that he didn’t seem remotely on guard.
Yet the energy I sensed from the Invincible Divine Sword was in no way inferior to mine.
Was there always someone like this around?
After a moment’s thought, I spoke.
“Excuse me.”
Chomp, chomp.
The Invincible Divine Sword’s mouth stopped in the middle of devouring dumplings as if possessed.
“You’re the Invincible Divine Sword, correct?”
“Sorry to bother you when we’ve never met, but I have something I’d like to ask.”
“Excuse me?”
What was wrong with this guy? Why wasn’t he answering when I was talking to him?
As I stared, the Invincible Divine Sword’s Adam’s apple bobbed beneath his bamboo hat.
Gulp.
“Ahem. Ahem.”
“Ahem. J-Just a moment.”
After clearing his throat several times, he spoke in a low baritone.
But how should I put it? The voice was painfully forced.
“Why? No—I mean, what is it?”
“I have something I’d like to ask.”
“Please go ahead. No—speak.”
What the hell was this guy doing?
I regarded the Invincible Divine Sword through narrowed eyes. Perhaps sensing my suspicion, he tugged his bamboo hat even lower.
I’m starting to get a feeling about this.
I casually tossed out some bait.
“Oh, I should’ve introduced myself first. I’m Park Taekyung of the Taiyuan Park Family.”
“Huh? When did you change your surname?”
An icy silence fell.
Realizing his mistake, the Invincible Divine Sword frantically waved his hands. Instead of the forced baritone, a clear, youthful voice spilled out in a rush.
“No, that’s not what I meant. The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi is so famous that I already knew who you were.”
“Oh. I see.”
“Yes. Yes.”
“May I ask your name?”
“The Invincible Divine Sword.”
“Your name, not your epithet.”
“K-Kang Pung.”
What kind of Pung?
What a talent for names.
I let out a quiet laugh of disbelief.
There was no need to confirm it with the Qi Sense Skill. At this point, it would have been stranger if I still hadn’t figured it out.
“It’s been a while. Let’s talk somewhere quiet.”
“W-Why? I’ve never met you before.”
“Really? Then should I send a messenger pigeon to Huashan?”
The Invincible Divine Sword slowly raised his bamboo hat.
A young man with an innocent face looked at me, resignation and delight mingling in his eyes.
“Hello, Benefactor.”
It was a welcome face I hadn’t seen in a year.
Laughing, I flicked the brim of Cheongpung’s bamboo hat.
The Murim Alliance was practically a city unto itself. It had residential areas, along with every facility needed for daily life.
So it wasn’t particularly surprising that it had an entertainment district as well.
We settled into an inn tucked away in the most secluded alley we could find.
Other than the ancient, nearly deaf proprietor, there wasn’t another customer in sight.
“I heard what happened. You ran away on the way back to Huashan?”
“Yes. Right after Benefactor left with Grandpa Jeok.”
“Why? Huashan is practically your home.”
“I didn’t want to go back. Grandpa wasn’t there anymore, and I hadn’t seen much of the world.”
“Still, I’m surprised you managed to escape.”
“My Martial Nephews tried to stop me, so I used a little force. They probably wouldn’t have woken up for three days. I ran away while they were out. Hehe.”
Just how much force had he used?
Still, only someone like Cheongpung could have pulled that off.
Baek Museong might be known as Huashan’s Lone Crane and one of the Three Plum Blossom Elites, but Cheongpung was a true genius on an entirely different level.
Even a Third Rate sword technique like the Three-Talent Sword Technique became a Peak martial art when performed by him.
From what I had seen, no one could match the depth of his understanding or the speed at which he learned martial arts.
If there were another genius like him, it would probably be Jin Mukyung.
Lost in thought, I listened to Cheongpung’s excited account of his travels through the martial world.
I had expected as much, and sure enough, he hadn’t done a damn bit of martial arts training. His stories were all about roaming around, goofing off, and eating to his heart’s content.
“I ate dumplings in Sichuan, but they were spicy!”
“Ah, yes. How astonishing.”
“Dumplings in Guangdong and Hainan have seafood in them!”
“That makes sense. They’re near the sea.”
“Dumplings in Zhejiang Province...”
Had this bastard done nothing but eat dumplings all year?
By the time he started talking about dumplings in Hunan Province, I couldn’t take it anymore and cut him off.
“So what are you going to do now?”
“About what?”
“The Invincible Divine Sword. Are you going to keep this up?”
“Yes. Martial Nephew Baek Museong knows I’m participating in the Star-Array Grand Banquet. If I disguise myself like this, no one will recognize me!”
“Hehe. I’ve fooled everyone completely.”
I would have bet my right hand and my entire fortune that they had already found him out. I was even willing to double down.
No wonder there were so many Huashan disciples near the dueling platform earlier.
The Star-Array Grand Banquet was open to martial artists from across the world, so there were no real restrictions against hiding one’s identity.
But Huashan was one of the Nine Sects and One Gang. There was no question its disciples had noticed Cheongpung long ago.
And yet they were merely watching him from a distance.
At this point, this is basically a group hidden-camera prank.
They could make a whole movie out of it and call it The Cheongpung Show.
I clicked my tongue inwardly as I watched Cheongpung enjoying himself. Then a thought occurred to me.
“Then I guess we’ll meet later?”
The smile on Cheongpung’s face widened.
“I hope so.”
“You hope so?”
“Yes. I was curious how strong Benefactor had become. I’ve wanted to spar with you at least once.”
The feeling was mutual.
Cheongpung and Jin Mukyung were two of the reasons I had decided to participate in the Star-Array Grand Banquet.
“What do you think, now that you’ve seen me again?”
“Be honest.”
I leaned back against the old chair.
Amid the creaking sounds, Cheongpung was silent for a moment. Then he suddenly tapped the scabbard hanging from his waist.
“Grandpa used to say that martial artists should speak with their weapons.”
“He was right.”
Straight from the Sword Saint himself.
I let out a quiet laugh and rose from my seat.
“Where are you going, Benefactor?”
“To prepare for the finals. We’ll finish our conversation there. With our respective martial arts, of course.”
“The finals...”
Cheongpung slowly repeated the word, then nodded with an unusually serious expression.
“Good. I’m going to win anyway.”
“Big talk from someone who spent the entire year eating dumplings.”
“I trained sometimes too.”
“Sure you did.”
Ignoring Cheongpung’s disgruntled muttering, I paid the bill and left the inn.
As soon as we emerged from the narrow, dark alley, we ran into a familiar face.
“Jongni Chu?”
Jongni Chu smiled and waved.
“Oh, we meet again. It seems we must be bound by fate.”
“What fate? It’s probably just a coincidence. What are you doing here?”
“I came to grab a bite.”
“Here?”
The secluded alley held only a few shops lined up beside one another. Even those looked so old they were on the verge of collapsing.
It didn’t look like a good place to find a meal by anyone’s standards.
But Jongni Chu nodded calmly.
“I had some thin noodles at a nearby street stall, and the vendor told me that shop’s dumplings were exceptionally good.”
By sheer coincidence, he was pointing at the sign of the very inn Cheongpung and I had just left.
“Really?”
“Of course. Apparently, it’s a hidden gem known only to a select few. Have you tried it?”
Cheongpung, who had already pulled his bamboo hat low over his face, abruptly joined in with his awkwardly altered voice.
“They’re incredibly delicious. No, I mean, delicious they are.”
Jongni Chu turned toward Cheongpung.
“I don’t believe we’ve met. Would it be rude of me to ask who you are?”
“The Invincible Divine Sword, Kang Pung.”
“Now that is an impressive epithet. I’m Jongni Chu, the Always-Victorious Sword. I hope we’ll get along, friend.”
“F-Friend?”
Cheongpung raised his bamboo hat slightly and stared at Jongni Chu before nodding furiously.
“Great! No—I mean, good! I’m delighted! You’re the first person who’s ever asked to be my friend!”
“...Enough. That’s more than enough.”
Why didn’t he just walk around with Cheongpung of Huashan written across his forehead?
Jongni Chu smiled gently as he watched Cheongpung bouncing with joy while I tried to calm him down.
“It seems you already have a good friend at your side. In any case, I’ll see you next time, friends.”
“Yeah, let’s just happen to run into each other once in a while. Not too often.”
“Farewell! Farewell, my friend!”
“I’ll keep that in mind.”
He dipped his head and disappeared into the dark alley.
Once we stepped onto the bright, sunlit street, Cheongpung grinned.
“He seems like a good person. I can just tell.”
I offered him some serious advice.
“Not everyone who likes dumplings is a good person.”
“Oh, I should have told him to dip them in only a little soy sauce.”
He really didn’t listen to a word I said.
Cheongpung’s concern proved unnecessary.
Jongni Chu never entered the inn.
His steps didn’t stop even after he passed it.
How long had he walked through the dark alleys tangled together like a maze? At last, in a place containing nothing but a few rats and filth, Jongni Chu stopped.
A quiet voice slipped from his lips.
“The Invincible Divine Sword. The more I think about it, the better that epithet sounds. What do you think?”
The moment he finished speaking, the silent alley erupted into motion.
Swish, swish, swish! Pak!
Three streaks of light shot toward Jongni Chu’s vital points.
At the same time, a small masked figure shot into the air. His steps as he ran along the wall were swift and stealthy as the wind.
His qinggong was exceptional, and his concealment technique surpassed even that. Just as the masked man gathered his strength to leap—
Thud.
“Where are you going in such a hurry?”
“Come down. Let’s talk.”
An immense force pressed down on both his shoulders. Breath brushed the back of his neck.
The masked man’s plummeting body trembled as if struck by lightning.
How can this be?!
He had completed hundreds of missions, but never once had anything like this happened.
Overwhelming. Irresistible.
Never had those words felt so real. He realized that only one path remained to him.
Pavilion Master, it seems this is as far as I go.
The face of the superior he had loyally served for decades—the Thousand-Faced Fox—flashed before his eyes.
Just as Shadow Killer—the Hidden Shadow Pavilion’s finest agent, whose name had since been forgotten—was about to bite down on the poison pellet hidden in his tooth—
“As expected of the Hidden Shadow Pavilion. Not a moment’s hesitation. But...”
Tap, tap.
Lightning-fast fingers struck Shadow Killer’s entire body. A low voice burrowed into his ears as his body stiffened.
“You should have known who you were following.”
Consumed by utter despair, Shadow Killer felt his consciousness plunge into the abyss.

chapters.title: Chapter 252
paragraphs: One day, two days, three days.
As time passed, the tournament bracket steadily shrank. More than five hundred participants had entered the main event on its first day. Now barely ten remained.
And as the crowd’s excitement rose with each passing day, one man’s spirits soared with it.
“This old man has been giving it some thought...”
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, continued in a solemn voice.
“I’m beginning to think our sect’s martial arts truly are the greatest under heaven. What does everyone think?”
The people in the seats of honor struggled to keep their faces from twisting.
This was hardly anything new, and they had all expected it. That did not make it sting any less.
What made it even more infuriating was that they could not refute him.
Their inability to risk offending the Fire King was one thing. More importantly, the performance of his disciple, the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, had been nothing short of astonishing.
He had caused a tremendous stir from the preliminaries onward, then continued advancing triumphantly while displaying overwhelming skill against one renowned master after another.
Yesterday, he had even beaten the Hebei Peng Family’s Hunyun Saber as mercilessly as a dog marked for slaughter.
Damn old man. He couldn’t even wait before bragging again.
The greatest martial arts under heaven, my ass. All he did was raise one talented brat.
Still, the kid’s the real deal. Where did he find such a monster?
Their thoughts were written plainly across their faces. Under normal circumstances, Jeok Cheongang would have threatened them for failing to control their expressions.
But right now, he was the very image of a benevolent Buddha.
He smiled contentedly as he looked around, then his gaze stopped on one man.
“Hey, Virility Saber King.”
The enormous old man, the Thunderbolt Saber King, pretended not to hear and stared toward a distant mountain. His face had turned bright red.
“When someone calls you, you should answer. I’m three years older than you, too. Isn’t that right?”
“...Shut your mouth while I’m still asking nicely.”
“Oh, come now. Why are you so angry?”
Jeok Cheongang responded slyly, widening his eyes in feigned surprise.
“Is it because that eldest grandson of yours—the one you praised until your mouth went dry, calling him the greatest prodigy in Hebei or whatever—spent fifteen minutes getting beaten by my disciple?”
“Good grief. Haven’t you heard that victory and defeat are simply part of war? Why get so worked up over it?”
Only then did the Thunderbolt Saber King, who had been snorting furiously, slowly turn his gaze toward Jeok Cheongang.
“Th-That’s right. Sometimes you win, and sometimes you lose.”
“Exactly. That’s how it goes at that age.”
“You’re finally saying something sensible. Since we’re on the subject, my grandson was exhausted from such a long journey. That’s why he couldn’t display his full strength.”
Jeok Cheongang smiled kindly and nodded.
“I understand. When someone’s skill is lacking, he needs an excuse.”
“...What did you say?”
“Come to think of it, they aren’t even the same age. Your eldest grandson is over thirty, isn’t he? Our Taekyung is only twenty-two. Heh heh. It can happen. It can.”
“Y-You damned old bastard!”
“Hm? What was that? I can’t hear you very well. You’re the Grand Family Head of the Hebei Peng Family who was eliminated in the quarterfinals, after all. Hahahaha!”
The Thunderbolt Saber King’s eyes rolled back as he started to surge to his feet.
A hand holding a string of prayer beads blocked him.
The Dharma King, Hong Dao, sighed as he looked at the two men.
“Amitabha. The two of you should act your age. Have you forgotten where you are?”
This was the dueling arena of the Star-Array Grand Banquet, with thousands upon thousands of spectators watching.
Only then did the Thunderbolt Saber King notice all the curious gazes directed toward the seats of honor. He lowered himself back into his seat.
“Urgh.”
“Benefactor Jeok, what about you?”
Jeok Cheongang stared at Hong Dao for a moment, then gave a small nod.
“...Fine. I understand.”
“Good. Everyone should get along. What will you do when I’m no longer here?”
“What do you think? I’ll break that old man’s nose.”
Despite the Thunderbolt Saber King’s taunt, Jeok Cheongang did not react.
After glancing sidelong at Hong Dao, he merely stared toward the dueling arena with a heavy expression.
Something Hong Dao had said before continued to echo in his mind.
I intend to step down after this Star-Array Grand Banquet.
His old friend was preparing for death.
Had he said he had a year left at most? Hong Dao could no longer read the heavenly patterns as clearly as before, but if the Dharma King said it was so, then it was so.
Damn bald monk. You should live another ten years at least.
No matter how high Jin Taekyung’s victories lifted his spirits, thoughts of Hong Dao soon weighed them down again.
Just as they were now.
Sensing the change in Jeok Cheongang’s mood, Hong Dao suddenly spoke.
“In any case, there have been an unusual number of upsets at this Star-Array Grand Banquet. Wouldn’t you agree?”
“The Abbot is right.”
“None of us expected these results.”
The Sect Leaders in the seats of honor nodded.
“The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi goes without saying...”
At the mention of Jin Taekyung, the muscles in Jin Wikyung’s face twitched from his seat at the lower end of the table.

He remained silent only because he still lacked the age and standing in the martial world to speak freely among those present. Given the chance, he would have leaped to his feet and danced for joy long ago.
The Sect Leaders looked at him with undisguised envy as they continued.
“But the most unexpected upsets were the Life-Sustaining Sword—or rather, the Always-Victorious Sword—and the Invincible Divine Sword.”
“Ah, yes. Those two surprised me the most as well.”
What kind of place was the Star-Array Grand Banquet?
It was a gathering attended by countless young, renowned martial artists from every corner of the world.
Yet the Always-Victorious Sword and the Invincible Divine Sword were not disciples of any famous major sect, nor had either of them ever made a name for themselves.
That they still remained in the bracket was even more surprising than Jin Taekyung’s advancement. After all, Taekyung was both the Fire King’s disciple and a member of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
“The Invincible Divine Sword is particularly impressive. He seems capable of holding his own against even an Elder of our sect.”
At the words of one of the Sect Leaders from a mid-sized sect, Jeok Cheongang, who had been quietly listening, suddenly spoke.
“Keep your mouth shut. At least then you might pass for average.”
“...Excuse me?”

“I don’t know what sect you belong to or who you are, but that child is already far beyond the level of a young prodigy. Are you truly unable to guess, or are you pretending not to know even though you do?”
Hong Dao and the Thunderbolt Saber King also chuckled in agreement.
“Benefactor Jeok’s words are harsh, but he is right.”
“I hate agreeing with that old man, but he’s right. Perhaps that’s only natural. He is the Sword... Ahem. In any case, the kid is incredible.”
The Thunderbolt Saber King abruptly trailed off and glanced sidelong at someone.
It was a middle-aged man with a gentle smile—the Sect Leader of Huashan, the Heavenly Sword True Person.
“Hahaha. As expected, there is no deceiving the eyes of my esteemed seniors.”
At the Heavenly Sword True Person’s ringing laughter, the others asked suspiciously,
“Could it be...?”
“That’s right. The Invincible Divine Sword is a disciple of our sect.”
“Ah, I knew it!”
“You have an outstanding disciple, True Person.”
A few of the stronger martial artists nodded silently, as though they had already guessed. Others exclaimed in astonishment.
But an even more shocking statement soon passed the Heavenly Sword True Person’s lips.
“Not my disciple. He is my junior brother.”
“Th-Then you mean...”
“By a twist of fate, we came to serve the same master. The last time I saw him was more than ten years ago... It pleases me to see how splendidly he has grown.”
The same master.
No one properly heard what followed. Not a single person present was unaware that the Heavenly Sword True Person’s master was the Sword Saint, Mae Jonghak.
The Invincible Divine Sword is the Sword Saint’s disciple?
As the people around him were swept up in shock, the Heavenly Sword True Person merely smiled in silence.
He looked like a Daoist who had attained enlightenment.
His thoughts, however, were another matter entirely.
I finally caught you, you little punk!
First his master, the Sword Saint, had run away. Then his youngest junior brother had done the same.
A year ago, the Heavenly Sword True Person had thought he had finally caught up with the boy, only for Cheongpung to beat down his disciples and flee again.
Every time the Invincible Divine Sword stepped onto the dueling platform, he had to suppress the urge to grab the boy by the collar and drag him back to Huashan.
“Heh heh heh. He is a treasure of our Huashan.”
The Heavenly Sword True Person hid his true feelings behind the smile of an immortal. Congratulations poured toward him.
“What a joyous occasion. The Sword Saint’s name will remain in Huashan for another generation.”
“Congratulations, True Person.”
“My congratulations!”
“A duel between the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi and the Invincible Divine Sword... This makes the finals even more exciting. Hahaha!”
Amid the warm atmosphere, Jeok Cheongang’s brow furrowed.
At the same time, a strand of Sound Transmission reached Hong Dao’s ear.
—Everyone is forgetting one person.
Hong Dao quietly rolled his prayer beads.
—You mean Jongni Chu, the Always-Victorious Sword?
—That’s right. Him.

The Star-Array Grand Banquet was a gathering of the martial world where anyone could participate regardless of background or affiliation. As a result, participants did not have to undergo a particularly detailed verification process before applying.
But that was only how things looked from the outside.
—I mobilized the Hidden Shadow Pavilion to investigate the identities of every participant who advanced to the main event.
A year ago, when Hong Dao first sensed the existence of Dark Heaven, the first person he sought out was the Thousand-Faced Fox, Song Ho.
After hearing the circumstances, Song Ho summoned his former subordinates without hesitation. Thus, the Hidden Shadow Pavilion, which had been reduced to little more than a name, was reborn.
—And the result?
—The result remained the same no matter how many times we checked. Everyone’s identity was confirmed except for one. We could find no trace of the Always-Victorious Sword, Jongni Chu, anywhere.
—Are you certain? If he had thoroughly concealed his identity for some reason...
—It was only a suspicion—until we lost contact with Shadow Killer three days ago.
—Shadow Killer? You mean someone got to him?
Shadow Killer was extraordinary enough that even Jeok Cheongang knew of him.
He was the Hidden Shadow Pavilion’s finest intelligence agent, as well as an assassin who had reached the Supreme Peak.
It was not difficult to imagine Shadow Killer as a cold corpse by now.
—What do you think? Can you identify Jongni Chu’s martial arts?
Hong Dao’s Sound Transmission caused Jeok Cheongang’s gaze to deepen.
—I don’t know either. In fact, that is the greatest mystery.
He had encountered countless martial arts throughout his life.
He had witnessed them with his own eyes, faced them himself, and defeated them.
But the martial arts Jongni Chu displayed were utterly unfamiliar to him.
—His martial arts don’t even seem particularly powerful...and yet he has somehow won every time and made it this far. They are unlike anything I have ever seen.
—Then are you saying his martial arts defy common principles?
—Defy common principles?
Jeok Cheongang’s face hardened.
Decades ago, saying that something defied common principles meant only one thing.
The Demonic Path!
At the same time, the same word crossed both men’s minds.
Hong Dao and Jeok Cheongang had lived through an age of war. They understood its meaning better than anyone.
—Then are you saying he is a descendant of the Demonic Cult?
—I don’t know. Dark Heaven, the Demonic Cult... He may belong to either one, or perhaps to something else entirely.
Just as the two men ended their Sound Transmission with grim expressions, a shout infused with internal energy shook the dueling arena.
“Fellow martial artists, allow me to introduce the rising young master known as the Invincible Divine Sword—and Wudang’s Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon!”
The Invincible Divine Sword—or rather, Cheongpung—looked especially excited as he climbed onto the dueling platform.
As thunderous cheers poured down on him, he hopped up and down in place and waved.
“Wow! Woooow! Hello! This is my first time reaching the quarterfinals of the Star-Array Grand Banquet!”
His opponent, the Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon, was warming up with a stiff expression.
He was one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes, the finest young prodigies of orthodox Murim. Along with Jin Mukyung, he was said to stand at the very top.
He’s definitely strong.
He was already over thirty and the direct disciple of Wudang’s Sect Leader.
According to Zhuge Gyun, he had accumulated considerable real-world combat experience while traveling from place to place for duels.
But still...
Well, you never know how a duel will turn out.
I leaned back comfortably in the spectator stands.
Only yesterday, I had crushed the Lesser Family Head of the Hebei Peng Family as Jeok Cheongang had wished and advanced to the semifinals.
Barring a major upset, I should make it to the finals without much trouble.
And my opponent there would probably be Cheongpung.
Let’s see what you can do.
At the same moment my eyes began to shine, the flag signaling the start of the duel rose.

chapters.title: Chapter 253
paragraphs: Swish!
There was no opening stance or anything of the sort. The instant the flag signaling the start of the duel rose, the two combatants charged at each other.
As the distance of roughly ten zhang closed in a flash, a dazzling beam of light erupted from the Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon’s waist.
Sword Energy right from the start?
Everything had its advantages and disadvantages.
Sword Energy was tremendously powerful, but it consumed an enormous amount of internal energy.
The Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon had chosen a swift victory over a drawn-out battle.
Whoosh!
Blue energy streamed from his Pine-Pattern Ancient Sword and slashed down toward Cheongpung’s shoulder.
A clean strike, stripped of all wasted motion. He had probably followed that same trajectory countless times since the day he first picked up a sword.
But...
If I can see it, Cheongpung can see it too.
Boom!
Half a step. That was all it took for Cheongpung to evade. The Pine-Pattern Ancient Sword, wreathed in blue Sword Energy, slammed into the dueling platform.
But the Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon was an experienced Peak master. As though he had anticipated the dodge, he twisted his sword and swept it toward Cheongpung’s ankle.
“Oops!”
Swish! Swish-swish-swish!
Cheongpung twisted away from the sword with a playful cry.
The Sword Energy raked and split the air in every direction like the claws of a wild beast. The loose hem of his robe caught in its path was shredded into tatters and scattered through the air.
Screams and gasps rose from the crowd.
“Eek!”
“Gasp!”
But I could see clearly. Cheongpung didn’t have so much as a scratch on him, and a smile played across his lips.
He was enjoying himself. Dancing lightly out of the sword strikes, Cheongpung broke into a broad grin and clapped.
“Wow! That was the Great Clarity Sword Technique, right?”
“Y-Yes.”
The Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon answered reflexively, his face blank with bewilderment.
And who could blame him? Anyone would have reacted the same way. What was that? How did that bastard dodge? His mind had to be overflowing with questions.
“The sword path is really interesting. Have you perhaps not learned the Taiji Wisdom Sword?”
“Why would you ask that...?”
“I’ve always wanted to see it. My grandfa—no, someone I know praised it several times. He said it was an excellent martial art.”
The Taiji Wisdom Sword was Wudang’s greatest secret art, famous enough that even I had heard of it a few times.
Cheongpung had spoken with pure intentions, but to anyone unfamiliar with his personality, his words were unbearably rude.
The Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon standing before him was no exception.
“Our sect’s martial arts exist neither to be judged by you nor to entertain you.”
His expression stiff, the Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon raised his Pine-Pattern Ancient Sword and pointed it at Cheongpung.
“But if you desire it so badly, I will show you just how fearsome it is.”
A gentle yet powerful aura arose and bore down on their surroundings. At the same time, the tip of his sword moved slowly, tracing a circle.
Taiji.
The essence of Wudang’s martial arts was about to unfold in his hands.
“The Taiji Wisdom Sword! It’s the Taiji Wisdom Sword!”
“Give this everything you have. Otherwise, you will regret it.”
Whoosh!
The moment he finished speaking, the Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon vanished like a phantom.
The next moment, blue Sword Energy rippled through the air and aimed at Cheongpung’s upper body.
That was when Cheongpung’s sword, which had remained sheathed throughout the duel, finally appeared.
Screeeech—boom!
Sword Energy collided with Sword Energy. It was only a single clash, but who held the advantage was obvious.
The Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon skidded back a full zhang, his eyes wide. Blood flowed from his torn hand.
“W-What is this?”
“Can I go this time?”
With that question, Cheongpung’s figure scattered like an illusion.
The Dark Fragrance Drift of Huashan. It was the exact movement I had grown sick of watching during my duels with him in the past.
A year had passed, and his Dark Fragrance Drift had become even more secretive and faster.
Swish!
A faint violet aura gathered around the tip of the sword sweeping toward the crown of the Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon’s head.
He avoided attacks as much as possible, and only used Sword Energy at the exact moment of striking.
It was proof that he was reducing unnecessary expenditure of internal energy while controlling his own power perfectly.
“Gah!”

The Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon, startled, hurriedly knocked his sword upward. But this time, things were different from before. The Pine-Pattern Ancient Sword slid along Cheongpung’s blade and changed direction.
Softness overcoming hardness.
That was the foundation of Wudang’s martial arts and the principle embodied by the Taiji Wisdom Sword.
But...
“Oh, I know how to do something similar too.”
Shhk.
Cheongpung’s wrist rotated fluidly as he spoke with childlike innocence.
The Pine-Pattern Ancient Sword had clung tenaciously to Cheongpung’s blade, pressing it down. But with that single motion, it was swept aside as if it had no strength at all.
The Pine-Pattern Ancient Sword wavered in midair, and Cheongpung’s blade immediately ensnared it.
“Got it. This is how you do it, right?”
“Or not? Wait, I think it’ll work better like this. Ah, that’s it.”
Cheongpung abruptly withdrew his sword and sank into thought. Then he smiled brightly.
In contrast, the Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon stared at him in utter shock.
So did every martial artist watching the duel.
“Gah!”
“T-The Taiji Wisdom Sword...!”
Strength was overcome by greater strength. Softness, by even greater softness.

Wudang had built its martial arts upon the principle of softness overcoming hardness, and the Taiji Wisdom Sword was its greatest supreme technique. Cheongpung had just defeated it through that very same principle.
The shock was immense.
Cheongpung is one move ahead of the Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon. No, at least two moves ahead.
There was no way the Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon, who was facing him directly, hadn’t realized it.
“H-How did you do that?”
“Hmm. You just have to think of embracing your opponent. Then your body reacts on its own and knows where and how to move. Easy, right?”
Easy, my ass. You crazy bastard.
More importantly, was that really something a person could do?
And this is the guy who supposedly spent a whole year eating nothing but dumplings.
As I stared at Cheongpung in disbelief, the Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon’s eyelids trembled from the shock.
Then he suddenly charged.
Tzzzz!
Blue Sword Energy blazed more brightly than ever. He had clearly gathered every last bit of his internal energy into that one strike.
The blade approached as though it would split Cheongpung’s chest open at any moment. Just as the spectators began screaming at the sight of Cheongpung standing there blankly—
Swish-swish-swish-swish!
Brilliant violet light-flames filled the dueling arena. The sword in Cheongpung’s hand traced a beautiful path through the air.
That single movement told me exactly which martial art he was using.
The Thirty-Six Plum Blossom Swords.
It was supremely fast and smooth.

For a moment, it seemed as though the scent of plum blossoms brushed the tip of my nose. The violet Sword Energy of the Zaha Divine Technique burst like flower buds and bloomed into thirty-six plum blossoms.
The next instant, the Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon’s Pine-Pattern Ancient Sword stopped dead in front of Cheongpung’s chest.
Crack.
The Sword Energy that had poured from it in torrents only moments ago had vanished. Hairline fractures spread like a spiderweb across the straight, snow-white blade.
The Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon stared at his cherished sword, and a weak voice slipped from his lips.
“Plum blossoms... I see. You are a disciple of Huashan.”
Cheongpung jumped and stammered.
“Ah, I’m not.”
“Well, I suppose it hardly matters.”
Resignation—and understanding.
The Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon’s arm slowly sank. His Pine-Pattern Ancient Sword shattered into hundreds of fragments that tumbled across the dueling platform.
“I concede.”
Only then did the silence break.
The judge came to his senses and lowered the flag. The pent-up roar of the crowd burst free like a dam, sweeping through the arena from every direction.
“How was I? I did well, right?”
The innocent voice pulled me from my thoughts. Cheongpung’s face was inches from mine, his eyes sparkling like a child’s.
“Whoa, you scared me. Let’s cut that out.”
“Benefactor, I asked how I did.”
Was the young man pestering me for an answer really the same person who had just fought?
The Invincible Divine Sword had utterly overwhelmed the Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon, one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes and the future of Wudang.
Watching the duel had reminded me once again that Cheongpung had long since surpassed the realm of young prodigies.
Was he always this strong?
The higher you climbed, the more of the landscape you could see. The same was true of the mountain called Cheongpung. A year ago, I hadn’t been high enough to see this view.
He’s incredible. It’s almost impossible to believe that all of this comes from natural talent.
His martial prowess was astonishing, but his talent was even more so.
Watching him, even I could almost believe he was a System user.
“Benefactor. Why aren’t you answering?”
“Are you a child? Do I have to praise you for that too?”
Cheongpung muttered with a slightly downcast expression.
“Grandpa always told me I did well...”
“That’s your problem.”
Just as I answered him curtly on purpose—
“Wow, that was a great duel, friend!”
At the sudden voice that seemed to leap out of nowhere, Cheongpung turned around with a brightened expression.
“Jongni Chu!”
“Oh! You remember me, friend!”
“Of course I remember you. Of course I do—uh, yeah, of course!”
What a pair of fucking idiots.
I silently watched Jongni Chu and Cheongpung embrace and laugh together. Then a thought occurred to me.
“Wait. You two.”
“Hm? What is it?”
“Why?”
“Aren’t you each other’s next opponents?”
The two of them stared blankly at each other, then both gasped.
“T-That’s right!”
“I-I see. You’re my next opponent, Kang Pung.”
I could already hear their friendship cracking.
I clicked my tongue as they awkwardly pulled apart.
Well, the result is more or less obvious anyway.
As with everything else, luck played a part in the Star-Array Grand Banquet. In that respect, Jongni Chu had been blessed by the heavens.
For some reason, he had kept drawing middling opponents and made it all the way to the semifinals.
Of course, the opponents he had defeated only seemed middling to me. They had all been comparable to Jongni Chu or even stronger.
And apparently he even got a bye yesterday.
From what I’d heard, Jongni Chu’s quarterfinal opponent had suffered a severe injury and withdrawn.
Whatever else one might say about him, the bastard’s luck was phenomenal.
Still, making it to the semifinals is no small feat.
Cheongpung wasn’t someone who could be defeated through luck. Perhaps they knew that too, because they exchanged a few words with regretful expressions.
“Sorry. I’ll go easy on you. No, wait—sorry, pal. I’ll go easy on you.”
“If you would, I’d be grateful. Please do.”
One openly promised to go easy on the other, while the other thanked him without a shred of pride. Neither of them was in his right mind.
I shook my head.
“You two childhood friends can settle that yourselves. I’m leaving. I have a prior engagement.”
“A prior engagement? But Benefactor, you don’t have any friends.”
“What? Did you have any friends besides me?”
The saddest part was that I couldn’t deny it.
Just as I found myself at a loss for words, the judge’s shout, amplified by internal energy, rang through the arena.
“Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung! Come up to the dueling platform!”
“Yes, I’m coming.”
Cheongpung and I each had one more step to climb before we could face each other in the finals.
I stepped lightly onto the dueling platform and looked at my opponent.
“You got lucky too. I never thought you’d make it this far.”
My semifinal opponent muttered gloomily.
“Our sect’s Eighteen Dragon-Subduing Palms is one of the five greatest palm techniques under heaven.”
“But you’ve only mastered five tenths of it.”
“That is correct.”
“Then concede.”
“If I did, my Master would beat me like a dog on Boknal.”
“Then?”
“There is only one path left.”
Gung Gibang, the Successor Beggar of the Beggars’ Sect, spat out a thick gob of phlegm. He pointed his well-worn bamboo staff at me and continued.
“Our sect’s Dog-Beating Staff Technique is the greatest under heaven. I’ll beat you senseless like a back-alley dog.”
“Sure. Go ahead.”
Exactly fifteen minutes later, Gung Gibang clung to my calf, both eyes swollen, and shouted,
“I’ve only mastered five tenths of the Dog-Beating Staff Technique!”
Why was this bastard stuck at five-tenths mastery with everything?
As I tossed aside the bamboo staff, now split in two, the judge lowered the flag.
“Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung advances to the finals!”

sentences.text: Swish!
There was no opening stance or anything of the sort.
The instant the flag signaling the start of the duel rose, the two combatants charged at each other.
As the distance of roughly ten zhang closed in a flash, a dazzling beam of light erupted from the Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon’s waist.

Everything had its advantages and disadvantages.
Sword Energy was tremendously powerful, but it consumed an enormous amount of internal energy.
The Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon had chosen a swift victory over a drawn-out battle.
Whoosh!
Blue energy streamed from his Pine-Pattern Ancient Sword and slashed down toward Cheongpung’s shoulder.
A clean strike, stripped of all wasted motion.
He had probably followed that same trajectory countless times since the day he first picked up a sword.

If I can see it, Cheongpung can see it too.
Boom!
Half a step.

The Pine-Pattern Ancient Sword, wreathed in blue Sword Energy, slammed into the dueling platform.
But the Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon was an experienced Peak master.
As though he had anticipated the dodge, he twisted his sword and swept it toward Cheongpung’s ankle.
“Oops!”
Swish!
Swish-swish-swish!
Cheongpung twisted away from the sword with a playful cry.
The Sword Energy raked and split the air in every direction like the claws of a wild beast.
The loose hem of his robe caught in its path was shredded into tatters and scattered through the air.
Screams and gasps rose from the crowd.
“Eek!”
“Gasp!”

He was enjoying himself.
Dancing lightly out of the sword strikes, Cheongpung broke into a broad grin and clapped.
“Wow!

“Y-Yes.”
The Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon answered reflexively, his face blank with bewilderment.
And who could blame him?
Anyone would have reacted the same way.

How did that bastard dodge?
His mind had to be overflowing with questions.

Have you perhaps not learned the Taiji Wisdom Sword?”

The Taiji Wisdom Sword was Wudang’s greatest secret art, famous enough that even I had heard of it a few times.
Cheongpung had spoken with pure intentions, but to anyone unfamiliar with his personality, his words were unbearably rude.
The Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon standing before him was no exception.

A gentle yet powerful aura arose and bore down on their surroundings.

Taiji.
The essence of Wudang’s martial arts was about to unfold in his hands.

“Give this everything you have.

Whoosh!

The next moment, blue Sword Energy rippled through the air and aimed at Cheongpung’s upper body.

Screeeech—boom!
Sword Energy collided with Sword Energy.
It was only a single clash, but who held the advantage was obvious.
The Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon skidded back a full zhang, his eyes wide.
Blood flowed from his torn hand.
“W-What is this?”
“Can I go this time?”
With that question, Cheongpung’s figure scattered like an illusion.
The Dark Fragrance Drift of Huashan.
It was the exact movement I had grown sick of watching during my duels with him in the past.
A year had passed, and his Dark Fragrance Drift had become even more secretive and faster.
Swish!
A faint violet aura gathered around the tip of the sword sweeping toward the crown of the Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon’s head.
He avoided attacks as much as possible, and only used Sword Energy at the exact moment of striking.
It was proof that he was reducing unnecessary expenditure of internal energy while controlling his own power perfectly.
“Gah!”
The Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon, startled, hurriedly knocked his sword upward.
But this time, things were different from before.
The Pine-Pattern Ancient Sword slid along Cheongpung’s blade and changed direction.
Softness overcoming hardness.
That was the foundation of Wudang’s martial arts and the principle embodied by the Taiji Wisdom Sword.
But...
“Oh, I know how to do something similar too.”
Shhk.
Cheongpung’s wrist rotated fluidly as he spoke with childlike innocence.
The Pine-Pattern Ancient Sword had clung tenaciously to Cheongpung’s blade, pressing it down.
But with that single motion, it was swept aside as if it had no strength at all.
The Pine-Pattern Ancient Sword wavered in midair, and Cheongpung’s blade immediately ensnared it.
“Got it.
This is how you do it, right?”
“Or not?
Wait, I think it’ll work better like this.
Ah, that’s it.”
Cheongpung abruptly withdrew his sword and sank into thought.
Then he smiled brightly.
In contrast, the Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon stared at him in utter shock.
So did every martial artist watching the duel.
“Gah!”

Strength was overcome by greater strength.
Softness, by even greater softness.
Wudang had built its martial arts upon the principle of softness overcoming hardness, and the Taiji Wisdom Sword was its greatest supreme technique.
Cheongpung had just defeated it through that very same principle.

Cheongpung is one move ahead of the Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon.

chapters.title: Chapter 254
paragraphs: “Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung, wins!”
At the judge’s shout, tens of thousands of spectators rose to their feet as one.
As Jin Taekyung came down from the dueling platform beneath a storm of cheers and applause, the eyes of the man watching him were sunk deep in thought.
What a strange fellow.
The Dog-Beating Staff Technique was the Beggars’ Sect’s greatest secret art, one that could only be taught to someone who had become the Successor Beggar.
Despite its comical name, its power and the subtlety of its forms ranked among the top ten martial arts in the world.
And yet Jin Taekyung had countered it far too easily without using any particularly notable martial art.
He had shattered a bamboo staff infused with internal energy using his bare fist, and even after taking the Eighteen Dragon-Subduing Palms head-on, all he did was frown.
He had even seemed to deliberately take attacks he could have avoided. No, that had undoubtedly been his intention.
Why?
At first, Jongni Chu wondered if Taekyung was some kind of oddball who enjoyed pain, but judging by the agonized faces he made each time, apparently not.
Besides, what kind of lunatic would take the Dog-Beating Staff Technique head-on just to raise his Toughness?
Whatever the reason, he’s interesting.
Jongni Chu still could not forget the surprise he had felt when he first saw Jin Taekyung.
His Muscles and Bones seemed to have been bestowed by heaven itself. If there was such a thing as the Heavenly Martial Physique, surely this was it.
A Disciple of the Fire King... I’ll have to watch him closely.
With that final thought, Jongni Chu, the Always-Victorious Sword, turned away and blended into the cheering crowd.
Several pairs of eyes followed him.
A merchant with a generous belly, a hunched old man, a Third Rate martial artist and a wandering martial artist dressed in cheap martial-arts uniforms...
All of them had ordinary faces one might see anywhere.
Yet whenever their lips moved, Sound Transmission passed between them—a technique only Peak masters could use.
—Your orders, Pavilion Master.
—Two and Three will follow him. But stay at least a hundred zhang away.
—We may lose track of him.
—I know. But this is our best option.
—...Understood.
—Four and Five, keep an eye on Jin Taekyung and Cheongpung. If he approaches again, report it immediately.
—Yes, sir.
—Then I wish you all good martial fortune.
The brief conversation ended without another reply. The ordinary-looking figures continued walking as though nothing had happened and disappeared into the crowd.
Meanwhile, a middle-aged beggar sitting by the roadside continued bowing to the people who tossed him a few coins. Only after some time had passed did he rise to his feet.
The transformation began in a deserted alley.
Crack. Sssrk.
His hunched shoulders straightened, and his twisted spine grew perfectly erect. Then his facial muscles began to quiver as though invisible hands were kneading them.
Before he had taken ten steps, the middle-aged beggar had become a genial-looking old man.
Tap. Tap.
A wooden prosthetic leg made of ebony, hard as steel, struck the stone pavement.
Jongni Chu, the Always-Victorious Sword.
The old man, Song Ho, the Thousand-Faced Fox, repeated the name in his mind.
Before he was the Pavilion Master of the Hidden Shadow Pavilion, he was also an intelligence operative and a master of disguise.
He never forgot a face he had seen even once, and the smallest habit or the structure of a person’s bones was enough for him to recognize them. Even disguise techniques could not deceive his eyes.
But there was one exception.
Jongni Chu.
I’ve definitely crossed paths with that bastard before.
But when? And where?
Song Ho was deep in thought, recalling Jongni Chu’s face, when a stab of pain from his leg brought him to a halt.
It’s starting again. It’s been getting worse lately.
It was a very old injury.
Decades ago, when he was still young, he had taken part in the final battle against the Demonic Cult and lost one of his legs.
After countless twists and turns, he had barely survived. But the memory of that day remained branded deep into his mind.
So did the voice of one man, deep and dark as a bottomless abyss.
Thousand-Faced Fox Song Ho. You’re quite large for a fox. Shall I start by tearing off a leg?
Song Ho shuddered all over, endured the pain, and started walking again.
That past was long gone. Not even its dregs remained. He had to focus instead on the far more tangible present.
Jongni Chu... who are you? And what are you plotting?
He had already finished making every possible preparation. Even so, the unease lingering in his chest kept shaking him.
Am I getting old? Or has the peace simply lasted too long?
A quiet sigh escaped the old man’s lips.
I closed my eyes.
In the darkness, I pictured one person: a boyish face that always wore a bright smile and an unremarkable build.
But the moment he drew his sword, everything changed.
Whoosh!
I could see it without seeing. I could hear it without hearing.
Violet Sword Energy shot forth, leaving no opening in any of the thirty-six directions.
It was as swift as a ray of light and as gentle as drifting flower petals. As I watched that beautiful sight, I thought,
The Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist, the Flame Divine Palm, or...
Several other martial arts flashed through my mind before disappearing again.
Cheongpung was an opponent I would have to face with everything I had. In the end, there was only one answer.
After a brief moment of thought, I reached for the cool shaft of my spear.
Creak.
“Captain. Captain.”
The voice boring into my ear shattered my thoughts. Cheongpung and the illusory Sword Energy he had conjured vanished as if washed away.
When I lifted my eyelids, I saw Hyuk Mujin poking his head through the crack in the door.
“Hehe. I’m here.”
I stared at him for a moment before speaking.
“What are you doing here?”
“I came to keep you company in case you were lonely.”
“Keep me company?”
“Yes. Isn’t that thoughtful of me?”
“Thoughtful?”
I let out a deep sigh and pulled a leg off the chair.
“Get down on your stomach, you despicable bastard.”
“W-Why are you doing this?”
“Did Cheongpung send you to interrupt my training?”
“Gasp! You were training?”
“Then do you see people sitting cross-legged and falling asleep?”
Mujin glanced around nervously before speaking hesitantly.
“I heard that when you were young, you tried to practice Horse Stance while sitting in a chair.”
“That wasn’t me... Wait. Did you just talk back to me?”
“What? Am I not even allowed to talk back?”
What the hell? Had this guy gone crazy?
I stared at Hyuk Mujin in disbelief. In the past, he would have thrown his hands over his head at once. Now he merely flinched before puffing out his chest.
“What are you doing?”
“Now that the subject has come up, I believe I’ve made no small contribution while serving you, Captain.”
“So?”
“Treat me accordingly.”
“What kind of treatment? The four mandatory insurances? Workers’ comp if you get hurt from now on?”
“I don’t know what the four mandatory insurances or workers’ comp are, but if you keep treating me like this, I’ll quit and take over the textile shop.”
I thought it over, then nodded.
“Go ahead.”
“Pardon?”
“Good work. No—thank you for your hard work, Mr. Mujin. May your textile shop prosper from here on out.”
“Wait. Wait a moment.”
“Oh, right. I don’t know about the other locations, but prepare to close the main branch in Shanxi Province.”
Grab!
Hyuk Mujin wrapped his arms around my calf and spoke with an imploring look in his eyes.
“I misspoke.”
“Did you?”
“Yes. Please hit me once on the back of the head.”
“Didn’t you ask me to treat you accordingly?”
“No. I’ve become a man who can’t live even a day without your blows.”
Had he gone insane?
I shook my head and lightly tapped him on the forehead.
“Enough nonsense. Get to the point. Why are you here?”
“The thing is, I really did come to keep you company.”
“What?”
When I glared at him, Mujin’s voice grew even smaller.
“I thought you might be feeling pressured since the final is tomorrow...”
“My opponent hasn’t even been decided yet. Don’t you know today is the last day of the semifinals?”
The sun was beginning to set, so Jongni Chu and Cheongpung’s duel would start soon.
The winner would face me in the final, and barring some enormous upset, Cheongpung was certain to win.
Mujin shrugged at my words.
“I know. I stopped by anyway.”
“What a silly guy. Use this time to train, you idiot.”
That was what I said, but something stirred warmly in a corner of my heart. Come to think of it, Mujin had been through a lot while following me around.
Maybe his occasional deranged behavior was because I had destroyed too many of his brain cells by smacking him in the back of the head.
Now that I think about it, I feel bad.
I was resolving to treat him better from now on when Mujin asked,
“Cheongpung will win, right?”
“Of course he will... Wait. How do you know that?”

“Even if no one else does, I need to know. With that ridiculous epithet, Invincible Divine Sword, his name being Kang Pung, and the fact that he used the Zaha Divine Technique in his last duel, how could I not?”
“You’re smarter than I thought.”
“Rumors have been spreading too. Cheongpung isn’t particularly famous, so most people have only figured out that he’s a disciple of Huashan.”
He had a point. The Zaha Divine Technique was distinctive enough for people to deduce that much.
“So Cheongpung is definitely going to win, right?”
“Isn’t it obvious?”
“It has to be certain. Absolutely!”
What was with that greedy look in his eyes?
The moment I nodded uneasily—
“Waaaaah!”
A roar echoed from not far away.
I picked up White Flame, the spear resting beside me, and rose to my feet.
Cheongpung will advance anyway. That won’t change.
This was clearly a fight between an egg and a rock.
But watching how the egg collided with the rock, and how the rock shattered the egg, would be a great help in the final duel.
“What are you doing? Aren’t you getting up?”
“Yes, sir.”
“Life-Sustaining Sword!”
“I bet one silver nyang on you! Pull off the upset!”
“Hahaha! You bet on the Life-Sustaining Sword instead of the Invincible Divine Sword? There’s no bigger sucker!”
Jongni Chu was climbing onto the dueling platform amid blazing torches and peals of boisterous laughter when he suddenly stopped.
It was because of the gazes looking down at him from the seats of honor.

No fewer than three of the Supreme Peak masters known as the Ten Kings were present. He could also see the leaders of the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families, as well as Song Ho, the Thousand-Faced Fox, watching quietly from the very back with gleaming eyes.
“Jongni Chu, the Always-Victorious Sword. Take your designated position.”
His pause lasted only an instant. At the judge’s words, Jongni Chu trudged onto the dueling platform and drew his sword without hesitation.
Ssshing!
The sudden action made the surrounding crowd fall silent for an instant, but quiet snickers soon broke out.
The hilt was so caked with dirt that its pattern could not be made out, while the blade was covered in reddish rust.
Martial artists ordinarily cherished their weapons as they did their own lives, but Jongni Chu’s sword looked as though it had never been cleaned once since the day it was forged.
“What the hell is that?”
“I thought something serious was happening. Gave me quite a start.”
“That’s why they call him the Life-Sustaining Sword. What did you expect?”
Ignoring the laughter behind him, Jongni Chu scrutinized the rusty blade and clicked his tongue.
“I can’t use this for now.”
Just then, Cheongpung, who had been enthusiastically waving to the crowd, held out his own sword.
“Want to borrow mine? Ah, would you care to use mine?”
“No. You should use that.”
“I’m fine, though...”
“You’re fine? Then what will you use?”
“It doesn’t matter. We’re friends.”
Cheongpung nodded vigorously, and Jongni Chu let out a genial laugh.
“I appreciate the thought. Mine will be enough.”
“But we’re friends...”
“Listen.”
Sssrk.
The rust-red blade pointed at Cheongpung.
The playfulness in Jongni Chu’s eyes had vanished. Now only torchlight flickered within them.
“I’ve never had a friend like you.”

sentences.text: “Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung, wins!”
At the judge’s shout, tens of thousands of spectators rose to their feet as one.
As Jin Taekyung came down from the dueling platform beneath a storm of cheers and applause, the eyes of the man watching him were sunk deep in thought.
What a strange fellow.
The Dog-Beating Staff Technique was the Beggars’ Sect’s greatest secret art, one that could only be taught to someone who had become the Successor Beggar.
Despite its comical name, its power and the subtlety of its forms ranked among the top ten martial arts in the world.
And yet Jin Taekyung had countered it far too easily without using any particularly notable martial art.
He had shattered a bamboo staff infused with internal energy using his bare fist, and even after taking the Eighteen Dragon-Subduing Palms head-on, all he did was frown.
He had even seemed to deliberately take attacks he could have avoided.
No, that had undoubtedly been his intention.
Why?
At first, Jongni Chu wondered if Taekyung was some kind of oddball who enjoyed pain, but judging by the agonized faces he made each time, apparently not.
Besides, what kind of lunatic would take the Dog-Beating Staff Technique head-on just to raise his Toughness?
Whatever the reason, he’s interesting.
Jongni Chu still could not forget the surprise he had felt when he first saw Jin Taekyung.
His Muscles and Bones seemed to have been bestowed by heaven itself.
If there was such a thing as the Heavenly Martial Physique, surely this was it.
A Disciple of the Fire King...
I’ll have to watch him closely.
With that final thought, Jongni Chu, the Always-Victorious Sword, turned away and blended into the cheering crowd.
Several pairs of eyes followed him.
A merchant with a generous belly, a hunched old man, a Third Rate martial artist and a wandering martial artist dressed in cheap martial-arts uniforms...
All of them had ordinary faces one might see anywhere.
Yet whenever their lips moved, Sound Transmission passed between them—a technique only Peak masters could use.
—Your orders, Pavilion Master.
—Two and Three will follow him.
But stay at least a hundred zhang away.
—We may lose track of him.
—I know.
But this is our best option.
—...Understood.
—Four and Five, keep an eye on Jin Taekyung and Cheongpung.
If he approaches again, report it immediately.
—Yes, sir.
—Then I wish you all good martial fortune.
The brief conversation ended without another reply.
The ordinary-looking figures continued walking as though nothing had happened and disappeared into the crowd.
Meanwhile, a middle-aged beggar sitting by the roadside continued bowing to the people who tossed him a few coins.
Only after some time had passed did he rise to his feet.
The transformation began in a deserted alley.
Crack.
Sssrk.
His hunched shoulders straightened, and his twisted spine grew perfectly erect.
Then his facial muscles began to quiver as though invisible hands were kneading them.
Before he had taken ten steps, the middle-aged beggar had become a genial-looking old man.
Tap.
Tap.
A wooden prosthetic leg made of ebony, hard as steel, struck the stone pavement.
Jongni Chu, the Always-Victorious Sword.
The old man, Song Ho, the Thousand-Faced Fox, repeated the name in his mind.
Before he was the Pavilion Master of the Hidden Shadow Pavilion, he was also an intelligence operative and a master of disguise.
He never forgot a face he had seen even once, and the smallest habit or the structure of a person’s bones was enough for him to recognize them.
Even disguise techniques could not deceive his eyes.
But there was one exception.
Jongni Chu.
I’ve definitely crossed paths with that bastard before.
But when?
And where?
Song Ho was deep in thought, recalling Jongni Chu’s face, when a stab of pain from his leg brought him to a halt.
It’s starting again.
It’s been getting worse lately.
It was a very old injury.
Decades ago, when he was still young, he had taken part in the final battle against the Demonic Cult and lost one of his legs.
After countless twists and turns, he had barely survived.
But the memory of that day remained branded deep into his mind.
So did the voice of one man, deep and dark as a bottomless abyss.
Thousand-Faced Fox Song Ho.
You’re quite large for a fox.
Shall I start by tearing off a leg?
Song Ho shuddered all over, endured the pain, and started walking again.
That past was long gone.
Not even its dregs remained.
He had to focus instead on the far more tangible present.
Jongni Chu... who are you?
And what are you plotting?
He had already finished making every possible preparation.
Even so, the unease lingering in his chest kept shaking him.
Am I getting old?
Or has the peace simply lasted too long?
A quiet sigh escaped the old man’s lips.
I closed my eyes.
In the darkness, I pictured one person: a boyish face that always wore a bright smile and an unremarkable build.
But the moment he drew his sword, everything changed.
Whoosh!
I could see it without seeing.
I could hear it without hearing.
Violet Sword Energy shot forth, leaving no opening in any of the thirty-six directions.
It was as swift as a ray of light and as gentle as drifting flower petals.
As I watched that beautiful sight, I thought,
The Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist, the Flame Divine Palm, or...
Several other martial arts flashed through my mind before disappearing again.
Cheongpung was an opponent I would have to face with everything I had.
In the end, there was only one answer.
After a brief moment of thought, I reached for the cool shaft of my spear.
Creak.
“Captain.
Captain.”
The voice boring into my ear shattered my thoughts.
Cheongpung and the illusory Sword Energy he had conjured vanished as if washed away.
When I lifted my eyelids, I saw Hyuk Mujin poking his head through the crack in the door.
“Hehe.
I’m here.”
I stared at him for a moment before speaking.
“What are you doing here?”
“I came to keep you company in case you were lonely.”
“Keep me company?”
“Yes.
Isn’t that thoughtful of me?”
“Thoughtful?”
I let out a deep sigh and pulled a leg off the chair.
“Get down on your stomach, you despicable bastard.”
“W-Why are you doing this?”
“Did Cheongpung send you to interrupt my training?”
“Gasp!
You were training?”
“Then do you see people sitting cross-legged and falling asleep?”
Mujin glanced around nervously before speaking hesitantly.
“I heard that when you were young, you tried to practice Horse Stance while sitting in a chair.”
“That wasn’t me...
Wait.
Did you just talk back to me?”
“What?
Am I not even allowed to talk back?”
What the hell?
Had this guy gone crazy?
I stared at Hyuk Mujin in disbelief.
In the past, he would have thrown his hands over his head at once.
Now he merely flinched before puffing out his chest.
“What are you doing?”
“Now that the subject has come up, I believe I’ve made no small contribution while serving you, Captain.”
“So?”
“Treat me accordingly.”
“What kind of treatment?
The four mandatory insurances?
Workers’ comp if you get hurt from now on?”
“I don’t know what the four mandatory insurances or workers’ comp are, but if you keep treating me like this, I’ll quit and take over the textile shop.”
I thought it over, then nodded.
“Go ahead.”
“Pardon?”
“Good work.
No—thank you for your hard work, Mr.
Mujin.
May your textile shop prosper from here on out.”
“Wait.
Wait a moment.”
“Oh, right.
I don’t know about the other locations, but prepare to close the main branch in Shanxi Province.”
Grab!
Hyuk Mujin wrapped his arms around my calf and spoke with an imploring look in his eyes.
“I misspoke.”
“Did you?”
“Yes.
Please hit me once on the back of the head.”
“Didn’t you ask me to treat you accordingly?”
“No.
I’ve become a man who can’t live even a day without your blows.”
Had he gone insane?
I shook my head and lightly tapped him on the forehead.
“Enough nonsense.
Get to the point.
Why are you here?”
“The thing is, I really did come to keep you company.”
“What?”
When I glared at him, Mujin’s voice grew even smaller.
“I thought you might be feeling pressured since the final is tomorrow...”
“My opponent hasn’t even been decided yet.
Don’t you know today is the last day of the semifinals?”
The sun was beginning to set, so Jongni Chu and Cheongpung’s duel would start soon.
The winner would face me in the final, and barring some enormous upset, Cheongpung was certain to win.
Mujin shrugged at my words.

I stopped by anyway.”
“What a silly guy.
Use this time to train, you idiot.”

Come to think of it, Mujin had been through a lot while following me around.
Maybe his occasional deranged behavior was because I had destroyed too many of his brain cells by smacking him in the back of the head.
Now that I think about it, I feel bad.

chapters.title: Chapter 255
paragraphs: Crash!
Jeok Cheongang shot to his feet, not even noticing the chair toppling behind him.
Every one of his senses was focused on a single person: Jongni Chu.
“This is...”
The moment had been so brief it could scarcely be called an instant, but he had definitely felt it.
The wave of qi emanating from Jongni Chu had been powerful enough to make his eyes fly open.
“Returning to Simplicity... He was hiding his strength.”
Dharma King Hong Dao groaned the words, his voice filled with sheer astonishment.
Returning to Simplicity. It was a realm that allowed a martial artist to appear no different from an ordinary person. Their bulging temples flattened, and they could control their aura at will.
To reach such a realm, one had to set foot beyond Peak—
into the realm of supreme mastery permitted only to the greatest martial artists.
“That young punk is a Supreme Peak master? Have you all gone mad? How could that possibly make sense?”
At the Thunderbolt Saber King’s barrage of questions, Hong Dao and Jeok Cheongang shook their heads.
“Amitabha. Then how would you explain this, Benefactor Peng?”
“He has reached the realm of Returning to Simplicity. Enough to deceive even our eyes completely.”
The people in the seats of honor, who had been listening closely to the three men’s conversation, gaped in shock.

Jongni Chu had scraped through every round from the preliminaries onward, always advancing by the narrowest of margins. Why else would people have given him the mocking nickname Life-Sustaining Sword?
But no longer.

The qi they had sensed from that supposedly lucky young martial artist, brief though it had been, was powerful enough to send chills down the spines of even the leaders of the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Family Heads of the Five Great Families.
“What in the world...”
The Thunderbolt Saber King fell silent.
He, too, was a Supreme Peak master and one of the Ten Kings. Deep down, he agreed with Jeok Cheongang and Hong Dao, but he could not bring himself to accept it so easily.
“How could someone who isn’t even thirty be a Supreme Peak master?”
As the Thunderbolt Saber King muttered in dismay, someone who had been silently observing the situation spoke up.
“It’s possible.”
“What?”
Every head turned in the same direction.
Their gazes demanded an explanation, and Thousand-Faced Fox Song Ho gave them one.
“If he has Returned to Youth.”
Leaving the shock spreading through the gathering behind him, Song Ho leaned back in his chair and stared at Jongni Chu with brooding eyes.
Who are you?
The more the question swelled within him, the worse the pain grew at the stump where his leg had been severed decades ago.
Song Ho knew now.
This was no mere coincidence.
Jongni Chu was closely connected to the day he had lost his leg.
Show me your true face.
At that moment, the judge’s flag shot into the air.
Whoosh!
A red arc swept through the air without hesitation. Cheongpung had stood there blinking, and by the time he twisted aside, it was already too late.
Jongni Chu’s strike was faster than he had expected.
Slice!
A searing pain spread across his chest. The long slash through the front of his robe welled with beads of crimson.
The sharp scent of blood stung his nose.
Cheongpung stumbled backward and stared blankly at Jongni Chu.
His friend—or rather, the man he had thought was his friend—gazed back with disconcerting calm.
“Too bad. It was too shallow.”
Just as Jongni Chu had said, the wound was shallow. The blade had only grazed the skin, leaving no deeper injury.
But Cheongpung’s wound was not merely one of flesh.
“J-Jongni Chu.”
He was the first friend Cheongpung had ever made in the Murim—no, in all his twenty-two years of life.
The man who had first held out a hand and asked to be friends was now pointing a sword at him. Without the slightest hesitation, he had swung it and cut Cheongpung across the chest.
“I don’t understand what you mean.”
Jongni Chu casually flicked the blood from his sword.
“This is the Murim, isn’t it? Don’t tell me you completely trusted someone you’d only just met after exchanging a few words.”
“Judging by your expression, you did. How have you survived this long with so little sense? I heard you were a Disciple of Huashan.”
He glanced at the Heavenly Sword True Person, the Huashan Sect Leader seated among the honored guests, and clicked his tongue.
“The Sect Leader did a terrible job teaching his Disciple. Pathetic.”
At those words, Cheongpung’s tightly pressed lips parted. Unlike before, his voice was low and formal.
“The person who taught me martial arts was my grandfather. Not that man.”
“Really? Whoever he is, he must be a senile old fool. What’s the old man’s epithet?”
“The Sword Saint.”
“The Sword Saint Mae Jonghak?”
Cheongpung nodded, and astonished cries burst from the silent stands.
Not a single person present was unfamiliar with the illustrious name of Sword Saint Mae Jonghak. He had long since become a living legend.
And now the Disciple of the Sword Saint, who had vanished for decades, had appeared.
Right here!
Countless eyes widened in shock. Only one man remained unmoved.
“The Sword Saint’s Disciple...”
Jongni Chu stroked his smooth chin out of habit, then gave a quiet laugh.
“Then the Sword Saint is nothing special either.”
“A child is still a child, no matter how strong he is. You shouldn’t carelessly leave one by a river. Look away for a moment, and the current will sweep him off.”
Cheongpung suddenly remembered something his grandfather had always told him.
Always remember this. The world is vast, and there are many strong people. Your martial arts are not yet complete, so you must always beware those who harbor malicious intent.
At the time, those words had meant little to him. Huashan had been peaceful, and his days with Mae Jonghak had been happy.
But his curiosity about the outside world had grown with each passing day, until he finally left without his grandfather’s knowledge.
And then...
Ah. So this was what he meant.
Only now did he understand.
It merely hurt that he had needed to bleed by the sword of his first-ever friend before realizing it.
Grandpa.
Cheongpung tightened his grip on his sword hilt. The scent of blood lingering beneath his nose faded, and his mind cleared.
Ssshing.
With a sound that set his hair on end, a pure white blade slid from its sheath.
At the same time, the internal energy coiled in his dantian rose like a cloud, covering his acupoints and spreading in billowing waves.
Tzzzzzz!
The distinctive purple qi of the Zaha Divine Technique blossomed across Cheongpung’s entire body. His eyes, filled with the colors of sunset, fixed on Jongni Chu.
“You’ll regret this.”
“Then...”
Jongni Chu rested his lowered sword against his shoulder.
“Let’s see what you can do.”
Whoosh!
Cheongpung jerked his head back. Jongni Chu’s sword passed within a paper’s width of the bridge of his nose. Instead of Sword Energy, the blade was thickly coated in reddish rust.
Fast!
Cheongpung had mastered a supreme eye technique under his grandfather’s guidance, but Jongni Chu’s movements surpassed even that.
A warning bell rang in his head as a wave of sword strikes followed.
Whoosh! Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!
The blade slashing toward his chest changed course in midair.
A thrust became a slash, then the slash gave way to an unexpected palm hurtling toward his shoulder.
Boom!
“Urgh!”
The palm struck Cheongpung’s shoulder and sent him flying more than ten zhang.
He spun through the air like a top. The instant his feet touched the ground—
Boom!
The bluestone paving the dueling platform exploded into powder.
Cheongpung surged toward Jongni Chu even faster than he had been thrown back.
His sword streamed purple Sword Energy as it danced with effortless grace, flowers blooming in its wake.
Ssshhh!
The Thirty-Six Plum Blossom Swords, executed with eight-tenths mastery, scattered around Jongni Chu from every direction.
Surrounded by purple Sword Energy, Jongni Chu suddenly curled his lips into a smile. It was wholly out of place amid such mortal peril.
“This is more than I expected.”
Before he had even finished speaking, the sword in his hand moved.
A blinding flash and deafening roar erupted, so intense that the spectators could not keep their eyes open.
Boom! Krrrraaaash!
Sword Energy exploded, spraying shattered fragments through the air.
The thick cloud of dust billowed upward, then split apart to reveal a lone figure.
Cheongpung’s eyes widened as he watched Jongni Chu cover his mouth and cough softly.
This man...
This time, he had seen it clearly.
He had seen Jongni Chu deflect every last strand of Sword Energy.
The dozens of Sword Energy attacks capable of piercing steel had been countered by none other than his rusted sword.
Not a trace of Sword Energy coated the blade, yet it had swept every attack aside, redirecting them as naturally and effortlessly as flowing water.
How is that possible?
Along with his astonishment, Cheongpung was seized by a strange emotion he had never felt before.
His heartbeat thundered in his ears, and the hand gripping his sword hilt would not strike.
A bead of sweat gathered on his forehead, rolled down the bridge of his nose, and fell.
“Are you afraid?”
Jongni Chu strolled toward him at a leisurely pace. His deep, cold gaze made Cheongpung’s heart sink.
Then Cheongpung realized that the word Jongni Chu had just spoken was the name of this strange emotion.
“...Afraid?”
It was an emotion he had never experienced before.
Fear was a foreign feeling he had only ever heard of from his grandfather. Now it constricted both his body and mind.
Pung. Do you know fear?
Fear? What’s that?
Something that hides deep in everyone’s heart. Not knowing fear is your greatest weakness.
Sword Saint Mae Jonghak had deeply loved the grandson who shared none of his blood. His gaze had always been warm, and he had cared for Cheongpung day and night.
Just as beautiful flowers bloomed from good soil, Cheongpung had grown into a lovable child.
This old man is at fault. I shouldn’t have done that...
Having grown up surrounded by boundless love, he had learned only how to love.

On the mountain peak where grandfather and grandson lived happily together, there was none of the arrogance, greed, jealousy, or anger that overflowed in the outside world. The child had grown without ever learning how terrifying human malice could be—or what it meant to feel fear.
If that day ever comes, do not let fear devour you. That is all I can tell you.
His grandfather had said those words the day before Cheongpung secretly left Lotus Peak.
Perhaps he had known this would happen.
But faced with a master unlike any he had ever encountered, Cheongpung found himself backing away without even realizing it.
Grandpa, what do I do?
Step.
Whenever Jongni Chu advanced a step, Cheongpung retreated.
Another step.
Then another.
The distance between them remained fixed at five zhang as Jongni Chu raised his sword.
“This could go on forever. I expected more from the Sword Saint’s Disciple. Is this all you amount to?”
“You do know what it means to lose in the Murim, don’t you?”
Ssshhh.
A ghostlike movement.
Paralyzed by fear, Cheongpung could not react. In a world slowed to a crawl, Jongni Chu alone seemed to move unhindered.
One step erased the distance between them, and his sword glided forward.
Just as the rusted blade was about to pierce Cheongpung’s throat—
Swoooosh! Boom!
A terrifying sound split the air, followed by a boom loud enough to leave his ears ringing.
Jongni Chu twisted his sword at the last instant and blocked the attack. At the sight of the translucent spearhead, he grinned.
“As expected, you’ve got a good friend.”
“He’s not a friend. He’s my Benefactor. But...”
Jin Taekyung spat out a wad of phlegm and continued,
“What the fuck are you?”
