Show me your true face.
At that moment, the judge’s flag shot into the air.
Whoosh!
A red arc swept through the air without hesitation.
Cheongpung had stood there blinking, and by the time he twisted aside, it was already too late.
Jongni Chu’s strike was faster than he had expected.
Slice!
A searing pain spread across his chest.
The long slash through the front of his robe welled with beads of crimson.
The sharp scent of blood stung his nose.
Cheongpung stumbled backward and stared blankly at Jongni Chu.
His friend—or rather, the man he had thought was his friend—gazed back with disconcerting calm.
“Too bad.
It was too shallow.”
Just as Jongni Chu had said, the wound was shallow.
The blade had only grazed the skin, leaving no deeper injury.
But Cheongpung’s wound was not merely one of flesh.
“J-Jongni Chu.”
He was the first friend Cheongpung had ever made in the Murim—no, in all his twenty-two years of life.
The man who had first held out a hand and asked to be friends was now pointing a sword at him.
Without the slightest hesitation, he had swung it and cut Cheongpung across the chest.
“I don’t understand what you mean.”
Jongni Chu casually flicked the blood from his sword.
“This is the Murim, isn’t it?
Don’t tell me you completely trusted someone you’d only just met after exchanging a few words.”
“Judging by your expression, you did.
How have you survived this long with so little sense?
I heard you were a Disciple of Huashan.”
He glanced at the Heavenly Sword True Person, the Huashan Sect Leader seated among the honored guests, and clicked his tongue.
“The Sect Leader did a terrible job teaching his Disciple.
Pathetic.”
At those words, Cheongpung’s tightly pressed lips parted.
Unlike before, his voice was low and formal.
“The person who taught me martial arts was my grandfather.
Not that man.”
“Really?
Whoever he is, he must be a senile old fool.
What’s the old man’s epithet?”
“The Sword Saint.”
“The Sword Saint Mae Jonghak?”
Cheongpung nodded, and astonished cries burst from the silent stands.
Not a single person present was unfamiliar with the illustrious name of Sword Saint Mae Jonghak.
He had long since become a living legend.
And now the Disciple of the Sword Saint, who had vanished for decades, had appeared.
Right here!
Countless eyes widened in shock.
Only one man remained unmoved.
“The Sword Saint’s Disciple...”
Jongni Chu stroked his smooth chin out of habit, then gave a quiet laugh.
“Then the Sword Saint is nothing special either.”
“A child is still a child, no matter how strong he is.
You shouldn’t carelessly leave one by a river.
Look away for a moment, and the current will sweep him off.”
Cheongpung suddenly remembered something his grandfather had always told him.
Always remember this.
The world is vast, and there are many strong people.
Your martial arts are not yet complete, so you must always beware those who harbor malicious intent.
At the time, those words had meant little to him.
Huashan had been peaceful, and his days with Mae Jonghak had been happy.
But his curiosity about the outside world had grown with each passing day, until he finally left without his grandfather’s knowledge.
And then...
Ah.
So this was what he meant.
Only now did he understand.
It merely hurt that he had needed to bleed by the sword of his first-ever friend before realizing it.
Grandpa.
Cheongpung tightened his grip on his sword hilt.
The scent of blood lingering beneath his nose faded, and his mind cleared.
Ssshing.
With a sound that set his hair on end, a pure white blade slid from its sheath.
At the same time, the internal energy coiled in his dantian rose like a cloud, covering his acupoints and spreading in billowing waves.
Tzzzzzz!
The distinctive purple qi of the Zaha Divine Technique blossomed across Cheongpung’s entire body.
His eyes, filled with the colors of sunset, fixed on Jongni Chu.
“You’ll regret this.”
“Then...”
Jongni Chu rested his lowered sword against his shoulder.
“Let’s see what you can do.”
Whoosh!
Cheongpung jerked his head back.
Jongni Chu’s sword passed within a paper’s width of the bridge of his nose.
Instead of Sword Energy, the blade was thickly coated in reddish rust.
Fast!
Cheongpung had mastered a supreme eye technique under his grandfather’s guidance, but Jongni Chu’s movements surpassed even that.
A warning bell rang in his head as a wave of sword strikes followed.
Whoosh!
Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!
The blade slashing toward his chest changed course in midair.
A thrust became a slash, then the slash gave way to an unexpected palm hurtling toward his shoulder.
Boom!
“Urgh!”
The palm struck Cheongpung’s shoulder and sent him flying more than ten zhang.
He spun through the air like a top.
The instant his feet touched the ground—
Boom!
The bluestone paving the dueling platform exploded into powder.
Cheongpung surged toward Jongni Chu even faster than he had been thrown back.
His sword streamed purple Sword Energy as it danced with effortless grace, flowers blooming in its wake.
Ssshhh!
The Thirty-Six Plum Blossom Swords, executed with eight-tenths mastery, scattered around Jongni Chu from every direction.
Surrounded by purple Sword Energy, Jongni Chu suddenly curled his lips into a smile.
It was wholly out of place amid such mortal peril.
“This is more than I expected.”
Before he had even finished speaking, the sword in his hand moved.
A blinding flash and deafening roar erupted, so intense that the spectators could not keep their eyes open.
Boom!
Krrrraaaash!
Sword Energy exploded, spraying shattered fragments through the air.
The thick cloud of dust billowed upward, then split apart to reveal a lone figure.
Cheongpung’s eyes widened as he watched Jongni Chu cover his mouth and cough softly.
This man...
This time, he had seen it clearly.
He had seen Jongni Chu deflect every last strand of Sword Energy.
The dozens of Sword Energy attacks capable of piercing steel had been countered by none other than his rusted sword.
Not a trace of Sword Energy coated the blade, yet it had swept every attack aside, redirecting them as naturally and effortlessly as flowing water.
How is that possible?
Along with his astonishment, Cheongpung was seized by a strange emotion he had never felt before.
His heartbeat thundered in his ears, and the hand gripping his sword hilt would not strike.
A bead of sweat gathered on his forehead, rolled down the bridge of his nose, and fell.
“Are you afraid?”
Jongni Chu strolled toward him at a leisurely pace.
His deep, cold gaze made Cheongpung’s heart sink.
Then Cheongpung realized that the word Jongni Chu had just spoken was the name of this strange emotion.
“...Afraid?”
It was an emotion he had never experienced before.
Fear was a foreign feeling he had only ever heard of from his grandfather.
Now it constricted both his body and mind.
Pung.
Do you know fear?
Fear?
What’s that?
Something that hides deep in everyone’s heart.
Not knowing fear is your greatest weakness.
Sword Saint Mae Jonghak had deeply loved the grandson who shared none of his blood.
His gaze had always been warm, and he had cared for Cheongpung day and night.
Just as beautiful flowers bloomed from good soil, Cheongpung had grown into a lovable child.
This old man is at fault.
I shouldn’t have done that...
Having grown up surrounded by boundless love, he had learned only how to love.
On the mountain peak where grandfather and grandson lived happily together, there was none of the arrogance, greed, jealousy, or anger that overflowed in the outside world.
The child had grown without ever learning how terrifying human malice could be—or what it meant to feel fear.
If that day ever comes, do not let fear devour you.
That is all I can tell you.
His grandfather had said those words the day before Cheongpung secretly left Lotus Peak.
Perhaps he had known this would happen.
But faced with a master unlike any he had ever encountered, Cheongpung found himself backing away without even realizing it.
Grandpa, what do I do?
Step.
Whenever Jongni Chu advanced a step, Cheongpung retreated.
Another step.
Then another.
The distance between them remained fixed at five zhang as Jongni Chu raised his sword.
“This could go on forever.
I expected more from the Sword Saint’s Disciple.
Is this all you amount to?”
“You do know what it means to lose in the Murim, don’t you?”
Ssshhh.
A ghostlike movement.
Paralyzed by fear, Cheongpung could not react.
In a world slowed to a crawl, Jongni Chu alone seemed to move unhindered.
One step erased the distance between them, and his sword glided forward.
Just as the rusted blade was about to pierce Cheongpung’s throat—
Swoooosh!
Boom!
A terrifying sound split the air, followed by a boom loud enough to leave his ears ringing.
Jongni Chu twisted his sword at the last instant and blocked the attack.
At the sight of the translucent spearhead, he grinned.
“As expected, you’ve got a good friend.”
“He’s not a friend.
He’s my Benefactor.
But...”
Jin Taekyung spat out a wad of phlegm and continued,
“What the fuck are you?”

chapters.title: Chapter 256
paragraphs: “What the fuck are you?”
Jongni Chu’s eyes curved like half-moons at the loaded question.
“Do I need to tell you again?”
“Jongni Chu from Yunnan. Yeah, I know. So...”
My next words came out calm enough to surprise even me.
“Who are you? You.”
“Shouldn’t you catch that friend behind you first?”
Jongni Chu was right. I caught Cheongpung by the arm as he crumpled.
There was a little bleeding from the shallow cut across his chest, but it was nowhere near enough to bring down a master of Cheongpung’s caliber.
“What did you do to him?”
“Nothing. His mental strength merely took a blow.”
“If anything happens to Cheongpung...”
“You worry too much. It was only a feint, so nothing like what you’re imagining will happen.”
“A feint? That strike just now?”
“If you don’t believe me, I can’t help that. Friendship is a wonderful thing.”
As I watched Jongni Chu smile gently, my stomach burned as though I had swallowed a ball of fire.
He fooled me completely.
I remembered when we had first met.
He had been a cheerful loudmouth who asked to become friends, saying even brushing sleeves was enough to forge a connection. Annoying, yes, but I hadn’t disliked him.
Now, though, I didn’t know what to think. Everything about him was shrouded in mystery.
My hand tightened around White Flame of its own accord.
“W-Wait!”
The urgent voice belonged to the judge. He was visibly flustered by the unexpected turn of events.
“Both of you, step back. And Young Hero Jin, barging into a duel violates the rules of the Star-Array Grand Banquet.”
Without taking my eyes off Jongni Chu, I answered.
“So I’m supposed to stand there and watch while someone nearly gets killed?”
“B-But he said it was only a feint!”
“That’s what he says.”
The judge bit his lip at my firm reply.
“If you don’t withdraw now, you may be disqualified under the rules.”
“Disqualified?”
“Of course. You don’t want to be disqualified with the final still ahead of you, do you?”
I laughed under my breath.
Winning the Star-Array Grand Banquet would certainly earn me a huge amount of EXP and Fame, or perhaps an even greater Reward.
Jin Wikyung would hug me for raising the family’s reputation, and Jeok Cheongang would be pleased as well.
But that’s all it would be.
The year I had spent in Fire Gate Cavern had not been for the sake of winning the Star-Array Grand Banquet.
And the same was surely true of the sinister bastard standing before me.
“Let’s fight.”
Jongni Chu deliberately widened his eyes.
“Now?”
“Yeah.”
“Good grief. If you don’t withdraw immediately, you’ll be disqualified.”
“I don’t give a damn about that.”
“Thank you. Thanks to you, I’ll be able to win easily and make my name known throughout the world.”
“Cut the crap. Drop the lousy acting and tell me what you really think.”
Jongni Chu paused, then grinned.
“I was right about you. You really are an interesting friend.”
“Friend? That’s not the word you use in a situation like this. Especially not between you and me.”
“That stings a little, but... well, it can’t be helped.”
“So what’s your answer?”
“I did want to fight you at least once.”
The judge, who had been listening to us, cut in with a grim expression.
“Did you not hear what I said? Under the rules, the Star-Array Grand Banquet final must take place tomorrow.”
At that moment, a low voice pierced everyone’s ears.
“Then change the rules as of today.”
“Who dares!”
The judge spun around with a roar, only to freeze at the sight of the tiny old man who had approached like a ghost.
“G-Great Hero Jeok?”
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang. His eyes glowed faintly red as they passed over me and Jongni Chu before settling on the judge.
“That’s right. It’s me.”
“I-I apologize. I misspoke.”
“Forget it. Get the next duel underway immediately.”
“B-But...”
“But?”
The judge swallowed hard.
“To change the schedule, we must hold a meeting and receive the presiding chair’s approval.”
“The Martial God presided over the first Star-Array Grand Banquet. After he disappeared, the position passed to the Abbot of Shaolin, who could be considered the organizer. Is that correct?”
“Y-Yes, that’s correct.”
“Then it’s settled.”
“Pardon?”
“Hong Dao had to step away on urgent business. Considering seniority and standing in the Murim, I am the presiding chair now.”
Everyone’s eyes turned toward the seats of honor a hundred zhang away. Just as Jeok Cheongang had said, the seat where Dharma King Hong Dao should have been sitting was empty.
No. There was one more person missing.
Song Ho, the Thousand-Faced Fox.
Two important people had left at the same time. What was going on?
The question flashed through my mind, then vanished. That wasn’t what mattered right now.
“Now we can forget about those damn rules or whatever they are. Am I wrong?”
The judge hesitated, then nodded.
“No. We’ll proceed.”
“Good. And you.”
Jongni Chu, who had been watching the scene with great interest, pointed at his own chest.
“Me?”
“Yes, you, the bastard with half a tongue.”
“My tongue hasn’t been cut in half, but I understand.”
Even though he clearly knew who he was dealing with, he remained completely unruffled.
Jeok Cheongang fixed Jongni Chu with a grave, steady glare.
“I’ll ask you directly. Did you come from Tianshan?”
The Tianshan Mountains. The headquarters of the Demonic Cult.
The judge flinched as though he had touched a flame, while Jongni Chu wore a faint smile, as if enjoying the situation.
“I think I’ll save that answer for later.”
“If you don’t want to die young, you’d better think carefully before answering.”
Jongni Chu rubbed his smooth chin.
“What will you do if some unfortunate accident occurs before you hear my answer?”
“An accident?”
“You never know what might happen in the Murim. For example, a certain master might lose his only Disciple.”
At that moment, a deathly silence pressed down on the surroundings.
Jeok Cheongang stared at Jongni Chu with emotionless eyes before speaking.
“If such a regrettable thing were to happen... the master who lost his Disciple would become very angry.”
“Would you kill the culprit even if you had to spread a net over heaven and earth?”
“Of course not. I’d burn him alive. You have my word.”
“Aren’t you making quite a promise? You don’t even know who we’re talking about.”
“Coincidentally, it’s someone I know very well.”
“Oh, dear.”
Jongni Chu burst into cheerful laughter.
“Then I suppose I’ll have to go easy on him.”
“Are you underestimating my Disciple?”
“I’m looking forward to it, but he probably won’t be a match for me.”
“That’s what he says. What do you think?”
At Jeok Cheongang’s question, I tightened my grip on the spear shaft.
“That bastard’s thinking is pretty screwed up.”
Jongni Chu looked at me with amusement.
“I can’t tell whether that’s confidence or arrogance.”
“Neither. I want to live a long, full life. But there’s one thing I do know.”
I enunciated each word clearly.
“You don’t know anything until you try.”
“Good thinking. But will that still hold true this time?”
“I hope so.”
“You could die.”
“That’s why I have to give it everything I’ve got. If I die after that... well, I’ll feel like shit, but someone will avenge me. Won’t they?”
Jeok Cheongang nodded.
“Go in peace. I’ll avenge you, so don’t worry about what comes after.”
“Seriously? You call that comforting?”
“Then stop talking nonsense and remember one thing. If that bastard kills you, I’ll kill you myself.”
“If I don’t want to die twice, I’d better work hard.”
Jongni Chu burst into loud laughter as he listened to us.
“Ha-ha-ha! What an interesting Master and Disciple pair.”
I stared at him and muttered inwardly.
Before we fought, I needed to peel back even a little of the veil surrounding him.
Skill, Qi Sense.
A chime rang.
System You have used Qi Sense. - Since you are currently at the eighth stage, you can detect targets at Level 100 or below within eighty zhang.
I possessed two kinds of Qi Sense: the Qi Sense that existed as a Skill, and the Qi Sense I had developed as a martial artist.
When I first came to the Murim, I had relied entirely on the former. But as time passed, I realized that Level and strength were not directly proportional, so I gradually used it less and less.
The Murim had too many variables to judge anyone by Level alone.
Show me something. Even a little. Show me what you really are.
Swoooosh!
Once Qi Sense reached the eighth stage, I could focus it entirely on a single person.
A blue line visible only to me shot forward without hesitation and reached Jongni Chu.
No—just as I thought it had reached him—
Beep!
System Qi Sense has failed! - Unable to identify the target! - An unknown force is rejecting the Skill!
What?
My eyes flew open at the unbelievable System notification. I stared at Jongni Chu in confusion.
The blue line of Qi Sense had seemed to strike something, circled around him, then disappeared.
“What the hell did you do?”
“That’s what I’d like to ask you.”
Jongni Chu had stopped laughing. His interested gaze settled on me.
“You have quite an interesting trick.”
His words suddenly brought back a memory from a year ago—the first person who had ever detected my Qi Sense.
Well, aren’t you an interesting fellow?
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
As befitted a Supreme Peak master, he had been able to control his qi freely. Through that encounter, I had first realized that the System was not omnipotent.
But even Jeok Cheongang couldn’t repel the Skill.
And now an unknown force had rejected the Skill. I had never heard of anything like it.
The more I saw Jongni Chu violate common sense, the more one word floated through my mind.
Demonic martial arts.
Martial arts that defied reason.
My suspicion hardened into certainty. At last, I understood the meaning behind the question Jeok Cheongang had asked him earlier.
“You really are from the Demonic Cult, aren’t you?”
“Beat me and I’ll tell you. What kind of trick did you use?”
“Even if you beat me, I won’t tell you.”
“That puts me at quite a disadvantage. It can’t be helped.”
Sssrk.
The rusted sword slowly rose and pointed between my eyebrows.
A humming voice followed, utterly at odds with the suffocating edge of his sword.
“Come. Let’s have some fun.”
I raised White Flame and answered.
“Yeah. Let’s have a brutal good time.”
Fwoosh!
The fire dragon curled within my dantian awoke from its slumber and stretched.
Give it everything you’ve got.
Jeok Cheongang used Seizing an Object Through Empty Space to pull Cheongpung toward him, then stepped through the air as he retreated. At the same time, the judge’s frantic voice rang out.

“Under the revised schedule, the Star-Array Grand Banquet final will begin immediately! The Life-Sustaining Sword—no, the Always-Victorious Sword, Jongni Chu, and the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung...!”
The judge’s announcement was already meaningless.
We were already charging toward each other.
Swoooosh!
One step. The distance vanished.
Krrrraaaash!
Two steps. Two streaks of light bursting from our hands collided in midair.

System Qi Sense has failed! - Unable to identify the target! - An unknown force is rejecting the Skill!
What?
My eyes flew open at the unbelievable System notification.
I stared at Jongni Chu in confusion.
The blue line of Qi Sense had seemed to strike something, circled around him, then disappeared.
“What the hell did you do?”
“That’s what I’d like to ask you.”
Jongni Chu had stopped laughing.
His interested gaze settled on me.
“You have quite an interesting trick.”
His words suddenly brought back a memory from a year ago—the first person who had ever detected my Qi Sense.
Well, aren’t you an interesting fellow?
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
As befitted a Supreme Peak master, he had been able to control his qi freely.
Through that encounter, I had first realized that the System was not omnipotent.
But even Jeok Cheongang couldn’t repel the Skill.
And now an unknown force had rejected the Skill.
I had never heard of anything like it.
The more I saw Jongni Chu violate common sense, the more one word floated through my mind.
Demonic martial arts.
Martial arts that defied reason.
My suspicion hardened into certainty.
At last, I understood the meaning behind the question Jeok Cheongang had asked him earlier.
“You really are from the Demonic Cult, aren’t you?”
“Beat me and I’ll tell you.
What kind of trick did you use?”
“Even if you beat me, I won’t tell you.”
“That puts me at quite a disadvantage.
It can’t be helped.”
Sssrk.
The rusted sword slowly rose and pointed between my eyebrows.
A humming voice followed, utterly at odds with the suffocating edge of his sword.
“Come.
Let’s have some fun.”
I raised White Flame and answered.
“Yeah.
Let’s have a brutal good time.”
Fwoosh!
The fire dragon curled within my dantian awoke from its slumber and stretched.
Give it everything you’ve got.
Jeok Cheongang used Seizing an Object Through Empty Space to pull Cheongpung toward him, then stepped through the air as he retreated.
At the same time, the judge’s frantic voice rang out.
“Under the revised schedule, the Star-Array Grand Banquet final will begin immediately!
The Life-Sustaining Sword—no, the Always-Victorious Sword, Jongni Chu, and the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung...!”
The judge’s announcement was already meaningless.
We were already charging toward each other.
Swoooosh!
One step.
The distance vanished.
Krrrraaaash!
Two steps.
Two streaks of light bursting from our hands collided in midair.

chapters.title: Chapter 257
paragraphs: Rrrrrumble.
The ground trembled faintly as a distant roar rolled in.
The commoners who knew nothing of martial arts merely tilted their heads and continued on their way.
But the Thousand-Faced Fox, Song Ho, was different.
This is...
The Hidden Shadow Pavilion agents secretly following him sent messages through Sound Transmission.
—About seven hundred zhang north.
—Something appears to have happened at the dueling platform.
—Pavilion Master, your orders.
Song Ho hesitated. His wealth of experience told him that the roar had been caused by the aftereffects of martial arts.
And not just any martial arts...
A Supreme Peak master?
Even if one turned the entire world upside down and scraped it bare, there might not be more than thirty Supreme Peak masters in existence.
The aftermath he had sensed clearly indicated a clash between Supreme Peak masters.
This was no ordinary matter. Had the Always-Victorious Sword, Jongni Chu, finally made his move?
But adequate precautions should already be in place.

They had already searched every inch around the Murim Alliance. They had thoroughly inspected everyone and everything in preparation for any possible situation, even taking into account the possibility that explosives might have been brought in and planted.
A tiger was still a tiger even after losing its teeth. The Hidden Shadow Pavilion might not have been what it once was, but its intelligence network was still capable of controlling Henan Province.
And three of the Ten Kings are there.
Then there were the leaders of the Nine Sects and One Gang, the Family Heads of the Five Great Families, and the elites of the sects and families they had brought with them.
It would be no exaggeration to call that place the Murim world in miniature.
I must be getting old. Perhaps I’ve worried too much.
It was all because of those unknown beings who had yet to reveal their true identities.
Song Ho clearly remembered the conversation he had shared with the Dharma King, Hong Dao, when the man had come to find him a year ago.
Dark clouds are covering the sky.
Could they be clouds from Tianshan?
I don’t even know where they’re coming from or when they’ll arrive. All I have are two words: Dark Heaven.
Dark Heaven...
Help me. I need your strength.
Half a century had passed since the Great Faction War.
The fox who had left the secular world and buried himself in the countryside had returned to the realm of martial artists, only to be reminded of just how much time had passed.
The Thousand-Faced Fox, Song Ho, let out a shallow sigh and moved his lips.
—Tell the Abbot I’ll leave once I finish my business.
A Hidden Shadow Pavilion agent who had joined them seven and a half minutes later replied.
—Dharma King Hong Dao left after you did, Pavilion Master.
—The Abbot left?
—Yes.
Song Ho hesitated briefly, then shook his head. He did not know what had happened, but he trusted Hong Dao’s judgment.
Hong Dao would trust his in turn.
—One of you, go to the dueling platform. Two will remain here. Report immediately if anything happens.
—Understood.
—The rest of you, follow me. As soon as we arrive, seal off the entire area. Let nothing slip through.
—Yes, sir.
Whoosh!
Black figures scattered through the alleyways.
As Song Ho raced across the endless rows of rooftops, his thoughts remained fixed on the report he had received fifteen minutes earlier.
We found Shadow Killer.
Tap!
He drove his wooden crutch down harder, accelerating with qinggong.
The pain intensified in equal measure.
Bang!
White Flame’s transparent spearhead collided with the rusted blade.
A single exchange.
A roar that seemed to split the heavens rang out, and a violent blast of wind engulfed my entire body.
Kraaaaoom!
A whirlwind rose around us, blocking everyone else’s view.
Amid the dust clouds raging in every direction, I saw Jongni Chu staring wide-eyed at me over our locked weapons.
“Impressive. I didn’t expect to be pushed back.”
Sssrk.
Just as he said, he had been forced several steps backward. Clearly, he could not withstand my strength, which had long since surpassed the limits of the human body.
But...
What the hell is this bastard?
If Jongni Chu was surprised, I was stunned.
I had spent an entire year training with an iron ball weighing more than a thousand catties attached to me. Both my martial arts and my stats were worlds apart from what they had once been.
And he withstood that?
That exchange should not merely have given me the upper hand. I should have overwhelmed him completely.
Yet all Jongni Chu had done was retreat a few steps.
Even that rust-covered sword had not broken.
Who the hell is this guy?
A bead of cold sweat slid down the back of my neck.
A playful smile tugged at Jongni Chu’s lips.
“Four Ounces Deflecting a Thousand Catties. Rather than trying to overpower your opponent, you must read the flow.”
Kaaaang!
His blade coiled around my spearhead and wrenched it aside.
I tightened my grip on the shaft, but the more force I used, the more it felt as though I were sinking into a swamp.
Jongni Chu’s sword was the horse, and my spear was the cart. The cart had no choice but to follow wherever the horse led.
The instant White Flame’s transparent Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron spearhead plunged into the ground, Jongni Chu thrust out his palm.
Boom!
Compressed air exploded in front of my chest, and my vision swam.
I barely kept myself from being hurled backward. Clinging to the spear shaft buried deep in the ground, I spun around it and closed in on Jongni Chu.
Blue flames gathered around my right foot, which carried one jiazi of internal energy.
Flame Wheel Kick.
The blazing flames slammed into the back of Jongni Chu’s neck.
Bang!
He slid backward and lowered his elbow.
His blackened sleeve crumbled into ash and scattered through the air.
“Too bad. I liked this outfit.”
Crack. Crack.
He rolled his neck from side to side like some Third Rate street thug, then grinned.
“But truly, you’re impressive. I’m liking you more and more. Now...”
Whoosh!
His figure vanished with a sharp rush of wind.
A quiet voice pierced my ear from right beside me.
“Let’s get started for real.”
Hummm.
The wind stopped.
This time, my senses were one step ahead of my body. At the last instant, I crossed my arms, and Jongni Chu’s fist slammed into them.
It was a strike carrying an enormous amount of internal energy, unlike anything he had used before.
Kra-boom!
Its power surpassed all ordinary limits. Though it was only flesh colliding with flesh, the resulting roar sounded like a bomb exploding.
Even after anchoring myself with the Thousand-Catty Drop at the last instant, I bent backward until my waist nearly touched the ground.
Crack.
Even my extraordinary Muscles and Bones, fine enough to be called the Heavenly Martial Physique, were useless this time.
I clenched my teeth and endured the sharp pain running along my spine.
How dare this bastard.
Boom!
I slammed my free left hand into the ground.
I shot upward two or three times faster than I had fallen. Jongni Chu’s brightly smiling face appeared before me.
I roared.
“I haven’t even gotten to use this back yet!”
The fire dragon stretching through my four limbs and hundred bones surged toward my open palm.
A scorching gale erupted with lava-like heat.
The martial art that had once driven me to the brink of death—the Flame Divine Palm—collided with Jongni Chu’s punch.
Bang!
My ears rang, and the ground shook.
Still gripping White Flame, I was hurled backward.
I sprang to my feet and saw Jongni Chu standing perfectly still beyond the hazy cloud of dust, the entire dueling platform charred black around him.
“That was a poor choice. As you can see, internal energy happens to be one of my strengths.”
I glared at his serene smile, then coughed up a surge of blood.
The blood was black.
Proof that I had suffered an Internal Injury.
Damn it.
My opponent was a Supreme Peak master who had reached the realm of Returning to Simplicity.
I had expected him to be strong, but he was far stronger than I had imagined.
Even allowing for the fact that he had learned demonic martial arts, it was difficult to understand how someone that young could possess such martial power.
“What the hell are you, really?”
I wiped the blood from my mouth with my sleeve.
Jongni Chu let out a hollow laugh.
“That’s what I’d like to ask you. I never thought I would encounter a monster like you in my lifetime.”
“Now you’re fucking with me, too?”
“I’m sincere.”
“Sincere, my ass. If I’m a monster, what does that make you?”
“I’m... a little special. Let’s leave it at that.”
I studied Jongni Chu’s enigmatic smile, then spat out a mouthful of bloody phlegm.
My insides burned from the Internal Injury.
“Is this another one of those legendary demonic martial arts?”
“Whenever people encounter something beyond the bounds of common reason, their thoughts turn to the word ‘demonic.’ It is difficult to accept things for what they are.”
“Yeah, it really isn’t easy. So what kind of demonic martial art did you learn?”
“Any further exchange of questions would be a waste of time.”
Jongni Chu raised his sword and pointed it at me.
Streams of qi as clear as mountain water flowed from the blade and took shape.
Sword Force.
The concentrated manifestation of energy permitted only to those who had set foot in the exalted realm of the Supreme Peak.
Tzzzzzzzz!
The mere sight of it chilled me to the bone.
The aura pouring from Jongni Chu left my palms damp and my lips parched.
This is... dangerous.
I drew a deep breath.
I had lost count of how many brushes with death I had survived.
What mattered was that I had survived every one of them.
And it would be the same from now on.
Wasn’t that why I had followed the Fire King and endured training that had seemed utterly impossible?
One shichen of sleep a day. Every moment left over goes into training!
That damn old man.
The words Jeok Cheongang had spoken before my training began in earnest suddenly came to mind, drawing a short laugh from me.
One shichen, my ass.
I had been allowed only half a shichen.
Without the System’s power to rapidly restore my body, I could never have endured those days.
My sleeping time had dwindled while the iron ball grew heavier and heavier. Even under those brutal conditions, I had punched, kicked, and swung my spear.
“That really was the perfect move.”
“Hmm?”
“My Master was right. Sleep is a luxury for a martial artist. And...”
Status Window, open.
As soon as I muttered the words inwardly, a holographic window filled my vision.
A great deal had changed over the past year—the Level displayed in my Status Window, the numbers, and even the number of Titles.
But only one thing mattered right now.
System Remaining Points: 500
“Repeat Quests are fucking awesome.”
Endlessly repeating the same training meant one thing: Repeat Quests.
Then there were the points I had gained from leveling up.
The points I had diligently deposited over the past year had become a hefty lump sum. Just looking at them filled me with satisfaction.
“This is why people need to save.”
“What does that mean?”
Jongni Chu tilted his head, unable to understand my words.
I grinned at him and raised White Flame.
“It means things are about to get a little harder for you.”
At the same time, countless System commands echoed through my mind.
Strength. Agility. Stamina.
Muscles and Bones. Sinews and Meridians.
Everything advanced another step. New power gathered, connected, and seeped into me.
In a world slowed almost to a standstill, I took a step.
Swish.
There was no sound.
One step carried me directly in front of Jongni Chu.
The Fire Dragon Divine Spear, now at the seventh stage, danced along the spearhead, burning through air and sound alike.
Papapapapat!
The spearhead became streaks of light that poured toward every part of Jongni Chu’s body.
At the same time, his sword, wrapped in transparent Sword Force, moved.
Kwaaang!
Within a moment split and split again, we exchanged dozens of blows.
I saw Jongni Chu’s eyes widen in astonishment.
The roars erupted without end, overlapping one another.
Perhaps this was what it would sound like if the heavens collapsed.
Screeech! Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!
Whenever spear and sword parted, fist met palm.
Each time I narrowly evaded an attack and retreated, another was already waiting where I landed.
Krrrzzzt!
A single punch and a single kick created massive craters, laying waste to everything around us.
The impossibly solid dueling platform became riddled with pits and cracks spreading like a spiderweb.
But more astonishing than anything else was Jongni Chu.
“Incredible! Truly incredible!”
He laughed as he unleashed one form after another, his eyes shining with joy.
Even though I was fighting with all my strength, his movements kept growing faster.
Stronger.
What the hell is this bastard...?
My mind wavered, and my hands and feet fell out of rhythm.
That shattered composure immediately led to a mistake.
Pow-pow-pow!
“Gah!”
My vision flashed white as excruciating pain surged through me.
I staggered backward.
Jongni Chu watched me with open admiration.
“Jin Taekyung, the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi. I’ll remember you well. You truly are...”
At that moment, Jongni Chu’s expression hardened.
As if drawn by something, he stared fixedly into the distance.
Then he abruptly kicked off the ground and shot upward.
Bang!
It all happened in an instant.
I stared blankly at his back as he stepped on empty air and vanished.
Then I snapped out of it and screamed after him.
“Where are you going, you son of a bitch!”

chapters.title: Chapter 258
paragraphs: I saw red.
“Where the hell are you going, you son of a bitch!”
If this had happened before, my first thought would have been, Why is he suddenly leaving? Maybe I would even have breathed an inward sigh of relief at escaping the crisis.
But not now.
This bastard beats the hell out of me and then runs?
Unlike me, who was still at the Peak realm, Jongni Chu was unquestionably a Supreme Peak master. I could admit that he was several levels above me.
But to leave before the duel had even been decided?
I gritted my teeth. Ignoring the Internal Injury needling my insides, I focused all my internal energy into my lower body.
“Stop right there.”
Crack! Boom!
I launched myself into the air with a thunderous blast. Cold wind slapped my face, and Jongni Chu’s foot appeared right in front of me.
He was close enough to touch if I simply reached out. One certainty flashed through my mind.
Got you.
Whoosh!
But the spearhead I thrust out with a triumphant smile sliced uselessly through empty air.
I blinked, unable to understand what had happened.
How?

Even with my seventh-tier grades, I knew the law of universal gravitation. Jongni Chu’s body had already reached its highest point and was falling, while I was still rising with the momentum of my leap.
He had definitely been close enough for me to grab his ankle with my bare hand.
But in my certainty, I had overlooked one crucial fact.
Martial artists—Supreme Peak masters in particular—were beings who shattered common sense.
“What the hell...”
The curse slipped through my parted lips. The sight unfolding before me was that shocking.
Papapapat!
He was stepping on the air.
There were no walls. No branches. Nothing at all.
As though invisible stairs had appeared beneath his feet, Jongni Chu climbed through empty air, soaring higher and higher.
Stepping on Empty Air...
What kind of bullshit was this? How was I supposed to catch him?
Cursing inwardly as I fell, I saw the confused crowd below.
Among them stood a tiny old man, his eyes gleaming coldly.
“You bastard! How dare you run!”
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
His roar shook the heavens as a streak of red light shot from his wrinkled hand. A sword imbued with Extreme Yang internal energy crossed dozens of zhang in an instant and struck its target.
Rumble-rumble-boom!
The air trembled, and a flash of light burst in midair, stabbing at my retinas. When I opened my eyes again, I saw Jongni Chu plummeting.
No. I had to correct myself.
That isn’t a fall.
Unfortunately, unlike my previous prediction, I was right this time.
Jeok Cheongang’s low groan was the proof, and Jongni Chu’s body shooting away like an arrow was the result.
He blocked it.
Jongni Chu had not only blocked Jeok Cheongang’s sword. He had used the tremendous internal energy behind it as propulsion, accelerating in the direction he wanted.
It was an astonishingly clever and efficient choice—one that was difficult to believe he had made in that split second.
Screeeeeech!
Now there was no one who could stop Jongni Chu as he shot through the sky like a meteor from that dizzying height.
Tap.
The instant I landed on the devastated dueling platform after experiencing the law of gravity firsthand, Jeok Cheongang’s furious voice rang out.
“What are you doing? Chase that bastard immediately!”
Everything had happened without warning. Only Jeok Cheongang’s shout jolted the leaders in the seats of honor into action.
“Capture Jongni Chu, the Always-Victorious Sword!”
“Seize the Demonic Cult spy plotting some vile scheme! Whoever captures him, dead or alive, will receive a great reward!”
The Nine Sects and One Gang. The Five Great Families. Even influential sects that wielded considerable power in their respective provinces.
Everyone gathered here was a key figure who moved the Murim.
Naturally, their attendants were renowned Peak masters in their own right.
“Yes, sir!”
Hundreds of martial artists scattered in every direction. At their head were Jeok Cheongang, the Thunderbolt Saber King, several other leaders, and me.
Screeeeeech!

We raced ahead of everyone else. I could not keep pace with Jeok Cheongang, who had mastered the Fire Gate Clan’s signature movement technique, Flamefire Path, to the ninth stage, but I was fast enough to keep his back in sight.
When you don’t have teeth, you make do with your gums.

My movement technique was still at a low stage, and my martial arts had yet to break past the uppermost reaches of the Peak realm. But my physical abilities had already surpassed their limits, making such speed possible.
“How’s your Internal Injury?”
“I can manage.”
I nodded in response to Jeok Cheongang’s voice through the fierce wind.
At that moment—
Ding.

System Under the rules, ???, who left the dueling platform first, has been declared the loser by ring-out! - Quest, Star-Array Grand Banquet, completed successfully! - Great Achievement, Star-Array Grand Banquet Victory, achieved! - Rewards will be distributed according to the participants’ caliber and the difficulty of the competition! - You have obtained a vast amount of EXP and Fame, as well as additional Points! - Level up! - Level up! - Level up! . . .
Ding. Ding. Ding.
As System notifications relentlessly rang in my ears, the changes began.

Vitality flooded my exhausted body, and the Internal Injury that had been stabbing at my insides vanished without a trace. The fire dragon in my dantian, drained by our all-out exchange, stirred and surged through my limbs and every corner of my body.
I never expected to win the Star-Array Grand Banquet like this.
But I had no time to check the System messages.
Finding Jongni Chu, who had vanished ahead of us, came first.
“Damn it. Whoever that bastard is, he’s fast as hell.”
Just as Myriad-Mile Pursuit—the Beggars’ Sect Leader and a master of qinggong—had said, Jongni Chu was unimaginably fast.
He had long since disappeared from everyone’s sight. Jeok Cheongang quickly issued orders.
“We’ll lose him at this rate. The Beggars’ Sect will take the west. The Kunlun Sect and the rest of you cover the gaps.”
“Yes, Great Hero Jeok.”
“Understood.”
Papapat!
The Sect Leaders of the Beggars’ Sect and Kunlun Sect—two sects renowned for their movement techniques—vanished with their disciples in tow. Jeok Cheongang turned to the Thunderbolt Saber King.
“You take the east.”
“Then what about this direction?”
“I’ll handle it.”
The Thunderbolt Saber King’s expression was grim.
“Be careful. That bastard calling himself the Always-Victorious Sword... He’ll be difficult to handle alone.”
Difficult to handle?
Those words had come from the Thunderbolt Saber King, a man whose pride was second to none.
In other words, Jongni Chu was comparable to the Ten Kings—or perhaps even stronger.
Jongni Chu was that powerful?
How had someone so young reached such a realm?
He was a monster among monsters. As I swallowed my surprise, Jeok Cheongang snorted.
“That only applies to weaklings like you. Don’t lump this old man in with the rest of you.”
He said it like a joke, but it was obvious he had not dismissed the Thunderbolt Saber King’s warning.
The corners of Jeok Cheongang’s mouth were raised, but his eyes had gone cold and still.
“That’s enough grumbling. Get going.”
“Damn it. Even the heavens are heartless. Why did Hong Dao, that damn monk, have to disappear at a time like this?”
After leaving behind a single lament, the Thunderbolt Saber King turned away and vanished from sight.
Now only Jeok Cheongang and I remained.
We continued at high speed, leaping over rooftops and racing past the hundreds of buildings stretching endlessly before us as we exchanged words.
“If you find him, do not act rashly. Understood?”
“I can’t promise that. I have a score to settle.”
“Jongni Chu is beyond your ability to handle. Do not engage him until I give the order.”
“Just how strong is he?”
After a brief silence, Jeok Cheongang’s lips parted.
“I don’t know.”
“What do you mean by that...?”
“Even I could not determine what martial arts he had learned or what realm he had reached.”
First the famously proud Thunderbolt Saber King, and now Jeok Cheongang—who ranked among the strongest of the Ten Kings in terms of sheer martial power—had given such an answer.
I was licking my parched lips when—
Kwoooong!
Far in the distance, a cloud of dust rose with a thunderous roar. Screams and shrill whistles rang out from every direction, announcing the enemy’s appearance.
I opened my senses wide and gathered the information.
West. About five hundred zhang away.
That was the direction of the Beggars’ Sect.
If I pushed my movement technique to its limit, I could reach it in moments.
“Old Master!”
“I know.”
Boom!
Jeok Cheongang and I shot forward like cannonballs.
The scenery whipping past us began to change. The endless rows of pavilions dwindled one by one, and tall city walls came into view.
The harder we ran against the fierce pressure of the wind, the heavier my chest felt.
What is this feeling?
Could it be the pressure of facing Jongni Chu again?
I glanced sideways. Jeok Cheongang’s expression had hardened. The emotion etched across his face was unmistakable foreboding.
A moment later, we discovered the source of that inexplicable feeling.
“Chase that bastard!”
“Master! Please come to your senses, Master!”
A massive pit about thirty zhang wide.
Through the gathered Beggars’ Sect disciples, I caught sight of a blood-soaked monk’s robe.
A wrinkled hand trembled at irregular intervals. Below where both legs had been severed, a pool of blood had formed, and prayer beads stained crimson with their owner’s blood bobbed on its surface.
“...Damn monk?”
Jeok Cheongang’s steps stopped dead when he saw his friend.
Jeok Cheongang’s vision went hazy.
Their last conversation echoed endlessly in his ears.
“Something came up. I need to step away for a while.”
“Now?”
“I’ll take care of it and be right back.”
“Is it something small or something serious?”
“Amitabha. As Shakyamuni said, if you resolve the greater matter first, the smaller matter will resolve itself.”
“That damn Amitabha. This is why people call you a damn monk.”
“What does it matter whether I’m a Buddha or a damn monk? Ha-ha-ha.”
He remembered clearly how Hong Dao had left with a laugh half a shichen ago.
But why...
Why are you lying here like this?
Splash.
Mud and bloody water splattered. The Beggars’ Sect disciples surrounding the fallen old monk hurriedly stepped aside and bowed their heads.
“G-Great Hero Jeok!”
“Our Sect Leader is pursuing Jongni Chu. B-but by the time we arrived, it was already too late...”
“Move.”
The voice that slipped from Jeok Cheongang’s lips was as dry as spent ash.
Every sound stopped. It was as though the world itself had frozen.
His senses were already focused on one person alone.
“I’m here.”
It was the same greeting as always. But instead of Hong Dao’s sly voice, a labored cough answered him.
Cough.
The Dharma King Hong Dao’s chest heaved, and black blood spilled from the corner of his mouth.
A grave Internal Injury. Fragments of his organs were mixed into the blood. There was no need to examine him to know what had happened inside his body.
“Well, now. Your friend is here, and you couldn’t even wait for me before lying down again?”
Jeok Cheongang spoke calmly as he dropped down beside Hong Dao.
He grasped the blood-soaked old monk’s wrist and sent internal energy into him. What he had suspected became reality.
Beyond saving.
The painful, crushing verdict filled Jeok Cheongang’s mind.
“Do you remember when we first met? Back when we fought those Demonic Cult bastards in Gansu almost every day?”
Was Hong Dao listening? Could he even hear him?
Everyone shared the same question, but Jeok Cheongang paid it no mind and continued speaking.
“At first, I wondered what kind of damn monk you were. But they say even dislike can become affection, and when the time came to part with you, I found myself reluctant.”
Although he had never once said it aloud, Hong Dao was the only friend Jeok Cheongang had ever opened his heart to.
To his Master, he had needed to be a reliable Disciple. To the first Disciple he later accepted, he had needed to be a dependable Master.
But with Hong Dao, it was different.
When he was with Hong Dao, he did not have to be anyone’s anything. He could simply be Jeok Cheongang, an ordinary human being.
“Did you know?”
Jeok Cheongang sent internal energy into Hong Dao’s Mingmen acupoint and spoke in a low voice.
“You’re my best friend.”
The breath that had been so weak it seemed ready to stop at any moment eased. The eyelids that looked as though they would remain closed forever finally opened a sliver.
A final rally.
Jeok Cheongang gazed into Hong Dao’s gray eyes as the final flame of life flickered within them.
“Speak. Anything at all.”
Hong Dao’s blood-soaked lips moved faintly. Jeok Cheongang put his ear to Hong Dao’s mouth and listened to his final words, his expression changing by the moment.
Anger. Shock. The realization of something.
And the final emotion to appear was sorrow.
Slowly. Then with a soft thud.
The coughing voice fell silent. The heaving chest and trembling eyelids settled peacefully.
Hong Dao closed his eyes as though he had fallen asleep, a satisfied smile still resting at the corners of his mouth.
Jeok Cheongang stared at him before opening his mouth.
“We’re going to Shaolin.”
His voice boiled like molten lava.

chapters.title: Chapter 259
paragraphs: Dharma King Hong Dao.
He was the Abbot of Shaolin, known as the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of the Murim, and one of the Ten Kings. He had breathed his last.
Here in Henan, of all places—at Shaolin’s doorstep, where the Star-Array Grand Banquet was being held.
“H-How could this happen?”
“Master Hong Dao!”
Sorrow and shock weighed upon everyone gathered there, but my gaze remained fixed on one person.
I spoke toward his back, which had gone rigid as a plaster statue.
“Old Master—no, Master.”
Jeok Cheongang, who had been looking down at Hong Dao’s corpse, turned his head.
“I’m going to Shaolin.”
His voice boiled like molten lava.
The blade-sharp aura pouring from the entire body of the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, made it difficult to breathe and prickled my skin.
Only his eyes were cold and still.
He was clinging to the last thread of his reason, suppressing the urge to hunt Jongni Chu down and tear him apart this instant.
What could possibly take precedence over avenging his dearest friend?
“Was that Master Hong Dao’s final wish?”
“Later. Every moment counts right now.”
Just as Jeok Cheongang finished speaking, dozens of presences rapidly approached from the distance. At the head of the group, the Thunderbolt Saber King stared wide-eyed at the scene before him.
“H-Hong Dao!”
“There’s no time to be shocked. Listen carefully.”
Jeok Cheongang continued without pause.
“I’m heading straight to Shaolin. Inform everyone and gather them together. Not a single moment can be wasted.”
“Do you intend to cast a net over heaven and earth to capture Jongni Chu?”
“The opposite.”
“What?”
“The Myriad-Mile Pursuit is tracking him, but he is certain to fail. Once everyone is assembled, bring them straight to Shaolin.”
“Did you say Shaolin?”
“Yes.”
Jeok Cheongang nodded gravely.
“If Hong Dao’s final words are true... a storm of blood will soon descend upon Shaolin. It may have already begun.”
The shocking declaration plunged everyone into silence. Even the Thunderbolt Saber King stood there gaping, and I was no different.
Shaolin Temple?
What kind of place was Shaolin Temple?
It was a temple and martial sect of such stature that it was only natural to call it the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of the Murim. Shaolin had stood for a thousand years.
Some even claimed that the Murim itself had begun with the arrival of Bodhidharma.
It was the holy ground of Buddhism and the central seat of martial arts. Even if Shaolin’s power waned, its deep-rooted history and the respect of the people remained unshaken.
And now a storm of blood was going to descend upon Shaolin Temple.
“W-What do you mean? Hong Dao’s final words? And who would dare to—”
“Hah!”
Kwoooong!
Jeok Cheongang’s roar jolted everyone back to their senses. The Thunderbolt Saber King stopped rambling and clamped his mouth shut.
“Dark Heaven. They’ve begun to move. If this old man’s guess is correct, we’ll eventually see Jongni Chu—that bastard who deserves to be torn apart—in Shaolin as well.”
“Dark Heaven...!”
Several leaders, including the Thunderbolt Saber King, opened their eyes wide. Judging by their reactions, they had clearly received at least some warning already.
“Do you understand now why every moment counts?”
Jeok Cheongang turned away from the Thunderbolt Saber King and swept his deeply sunken gaze across the gathering.
“Do exactly as I have said. That is Hong Dao’s final will.”
There was no time left to waste. Jeok Cheongang and I exchanged a glance, unleashed our movement techniques, and left the area simultaneously.
Whoooosh!
As I raced through the fierce wind, something cold touched my cheek.
The sky was clear and cloudless. There was no sign of rain.
But the eyes of someone running after losing a friend and postponing his revenge must have been brimming with tears.
No. It’s rainwater.
I’ll call it rainwater.
Damn it.
I clenched my teeth as I thought of Jongni Chu.
I have a feeling today is going to be a long day.
Shrill whistles pierced the air.
“Find the culprit!”
“He may still be hiding nearby!”
“Everyone, remain calm! Nothing is going to happen!”
The Murim Alliance buzzed like a kicked hornet’s nest.

The countless martial artists attending the Star-Array Grand Banquet were scouring the surrounding area for Jongni Chu with fire in their eyes, while anxious commoners followed the orders of those directing them.
They’re wasting their time.

It would only add to the confusion.

“Not long before his death, Hong Dao told me he had entrusted the Green Jade Buddha Staff to his Disciple.”
I frowned slightly, and Jeok Cheongang continued.

“Ah!”
The exclamation escaped me before I could stop it. A realization flashed through my mind.
Hong Dao’s final words, wrung from him with the last of his strength.
The reason Jeok Cheongang had turned toward Shaolin, postponing even the revenge for his dearest friend.
“The Green Jade Buddha Staff!”
“Exactly.”
Jeok Cheongang’s low voice continued.
“Dark Heaven’s true objective is not Hong Dao’s death. It is the seizure of the Green Jade Buddha Staff.”
Now everything was clear.
Jongni Chu—or rather, Dark Heaven—clearly wanted Shaolin’s sacred treasure.
Hong Dao had squeezed out the last of his strength to leave those final words and reveal that fact.
Now that Dark Heaven knew the Green Jade Buddha Staff was not in Hong Dao’s possession, even a three-year-old could tell where they would go next.
A storm of blood will descend upon Shaolin.
As I recalled Jeok Cheongang’s warning to the Thunderbolt Saber King, my thoughts went cold.
“Huff, hoo...”
Tap-tap-tap-tap!
Ragged breaths. Feet pounding without pause.
An aged voice brought the middle-aged man racing along the mountain path to a halt.
“You seem to have urgent business, young friend.”
The speaker was an old man with a beard that hung to his chest.
Tall, with his hair neatly arranged, he looked at first glance like a retired scholar.
“The weather is lovely. Why not slow down and enjoy the scenery?”
The middle-aged man’s throat bobbed heavily.
His voice emerged taut with tension.
“Who are you?”
“Just an old man out for a stroll. I heard the scenery on Mount Song was splendid, so I came to pass the time.”
“Pass the time?”
The middle-aged man shouted through clenched teeth.
“Enough bullshit! You must be another vile fiend!”
“Hm?”
The old man’s eyes widened before he let out a quiet laugh.
“You have quite a fiery temper, young friend. Still, you’re much better than the people I met earlier. They were far too busy lying.”
“You met people earlier... Don’t tell me?”

“A woodcutter, an herb gatherer. Why are there so many kinds of gatherers around here? Ah, the pair who disguised themselves as husband and wife to pray for a child were at least convincing. I almost fell for them myself.”
“So I killed every last one of them, martial artists and commoners alike. It seemed much easier that way.”
The middle-aged man trembled as if struck by lightning.
There could be no doubt. His companions, who had scattered in every direction to deliver the urgent report, were already dead.
He would probably suffer the same fate soon.
At least I should be grateful that my death will not be meaningless.
Those on the ground had been caught in the net.
The sky was another matter.
He found a sliver of comfort in the sight of a messenger eagle flying powerfully across the distant plain.
Screeeeech!
A strange, piercing cry rang out as something black swooped down upon the messenger eagle.
It was three or four times larger at a glance. The battle between the two birds that collided in midair ended far too quickly to leave any hope.
Kreeee!
The messenger eagle plummeted with a final shriek. Blood seeped between the middle-aged man’s tightly clenched teeth.
“Dark Heaven...”
“Oh? You know us?”
“How could I not? You old bastard who has outraged heaven and man!”
“Most of the Beggars’ Sect beggars knew nothing about us. Your martial arts are too respectable for you to be Lower District Sect riffraff... Ah, that’s it. You’re from the Hidden Shadow Pavilion.”
The old man stroked his beard and raised the corners of his mouth.
“But I find that ‘outraged heaven and man’ remark rather unpleasant. What do you think?”
“You dare do something like this and still—”
The middle-aged man opened his bloodshot eyes wide and was about to shout when the old man shook his head.
“No, not you.”
He raised one withered finger and pointed over the middle-aged man’s shoulder.
“I was asking that fellow.”
Crack!
The middle-aged man could not turn his head.
Heaven and earth flipped, and his vision shook.
Only one sensation remained at the end.
Hot.
Fwoosh. Thud.
His charred corpse crumpled.
A foot came down upon the middle-aged man’s head, crushing the lump of charcoal beneath it.
“Han Su, you bastard. What kind of bullshit are you pulling? Wasting your time playing with trash like this.”
The rough voice belonged to a thickset old man. His beard had grown wild and, strangely enough, was red.
At the appearance of an old friend who had been with him for decades, the old man who looked like a scholar smiled faintly.
“I was just about to wrap things up and leave. How are things up the mountain?”
“They’re busy having their fun. Oh, apparently that Disciple of his has the Green Jade Buddha Staff.”
“Is that so? Then let’s go together, Flame Tiger.”
The two exchanged faint smiles and began walking at a leisurely pace.
With each step, the screams coming from Shaolin Temple drew closer.

paragraphs: “Young Hero Cheong. Young Hero Cheong, wake up.”
Smack! Smack!
Cheongpung opened his eyes with a groan.
Someone was slapping him hard across the face. It was his first time being slapped, so the experience was fascinating in a way, but for some strange reason, it also felt rather unpleasant.
Ah. So this is why people don’t like being slapped.
With that small insight, Cheongpung opened his mouth.
“Excuse me.”
Smack! Smack!
“I’m aw—”
Smack! Smack!
“I’m awake...”
Smack!
Only after landing one last slap did the hand finally stop.
A familiar-looking young man spoke with a stiff expression.
“You’re awake. Do you remember who I am?”
“It’s been a while, Warrior Hyuk Mujin.”
Hyuk Mujin sighed.
“So you do remember me.”
“Of course. I just never expected we’d meet like this.”
Cheongpung remembered Hyuk Mujin as a good person.
But when a good person he had not seen in a year was slapping him across the face, even Cheongpung could not help but feel hurt.
“I apologize if I offended you. I suddenly remembered the money I lost.”
“What?”
“No, the situation was so urgent that I forgot my manners.”
If that was the reason, Cheongpung could understand.
He nodded and looked around. Shouts rang out from every direction, and people were running everywhere.
“Is this a festival?”
“...Does this look like a festival?”
“It isn’t?”
“No.”
Hyuk Mujin answered firmly, then gave him a brief account of the situation.
Dharma King Hong Dao had been found dead, and the culprit was none other than...
“Jongni Chu?”
“Yes. The Always-Victorious Sword, Jongni Chu. That bastard. His exact identity remains unknown, but most believe he was an assassin sent by the Demonic Cult.”
“The Demonic Cult...”
It was a name Cheongpung had heard countless times from his grandfather, the Sword Saint. A place where fiends and vicious killers who had once stained the entire world with blood had gathered.
And Jongni Chu was an assassin from that very Demonic Cult.
Cheongpung shook his head without realizing it.
“No.”
“What do you mean...?”
Hyuk Mujin continued with an incredulous expression.
“You suffered at his hands yourself, and you still don’t understand? The shock must have been so great that you can’t remember, but you nearly died at his hands.”
No. Cheongpung remembered everything clearly.
The helplessness and fear he had felt before a master against whom nothing worked. Even that final moment, when he had contemplated death for the first time in his life.
I was scared. Truly scared.
The mere thought made the fine hairs on his body stand on end and his palms turn clammy.
But why?
Why did Jongni Chu’s face keep appearing before his eyes—that bright smile he had worn when asking Cheongpung to be his friend?
Cheongpung’s lips remained pressed tightly together for a moment before finally parting.
“He’s my friend.”
“...What?”
“That man is my friend. He couldn’t have done it.”
“Young Hero Cheong!”
Startled, Hyuk Mujin hurriedly glanced around.
Only after confirming that no one was paying attention to them did he lower his voice.
“Are you insane? Jongni Chu is already as good as an enemy of the entire Murim. How can you call someone like that your friend...?”
He was an assassin who had murdered the Abbot of Shaolin Temple and fled. Simply being acquainted with Jongni Chu could be enough to earn Cheongpung a brutal beating.
Even if he was the disciple the Sword Saint had raised like his own flesh and blood, people would still glare at him.
“Never mention him out loud again. Do you understand?”
Cheongpung was about to say something, but he closed his mouth at the look in Hyuk Mujin’s eyes.
“He’s a demonic fiend. I don’t know what kind of underhanded trick he used to win your favor, but it was all a disguise meant to help him assassinate Master Hong Dao.”
“Are you certain? Did anyone see him kill him?”
“All the circumstances point to it. The pursuit party formed to capture him and the thousands of heroes who gathered to save Shaolin have finished preparing to depart.”
“Shaolin...”
“The Demonic Cult’s vile scheme has placed Shaolin in danger. Great Hero Jeok and the Captain have already gone on ahead.”
Cheongpung slowly closed his eyes.
In the pitch-black darkness, the faces of Jin Taekyung and Jongni Chu flashed before him in turn.
He did not deliberate for long.
“I’ll go ahead.”
“What?”
By the time Hyuk Mujin asked back with a dazed expression, Cheongpung had already shot far into the distance.
His feet carried him toward Mount Song.
Mount Song was beautiful and peaceful enough to be counted among the Five Sacred Mountains.
But the place that should have been green and lovely was stained with blood and filled with screams.
“Aaaaaagh!”
“Kill every last one of them.”
Slash! Shhhhhhk!
Blood spurted from every direction whenever a flash of sword light gleamed.
In broad daylight on the peaceful day of Baekjung, hundreds of masked men had appeared without warning and begun slaughtering people with emotionless eyes.
“Protect the pilgrims! Do not retreat!”
Shaolin martial monks with Buddhist precept seals carved into their foreheads stood against them, but the situation showed no sign of improving.

The masked men were all exceptional masters and difficult enough to fight on their own. On top of that, the martial monks had to protect the scholarly monks who had never learned martial arts, the young novices, and the countless pilgrims.
“Wh-what is this?”
“Kraaagh!”
No one had expected anything like this to happen today.
Who would dare invade the grounds of Shaolin Temple, the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of the Murim, in the very heart of the Central Plains?
The monks were being swept aside by the cruel, treacherous masked men when—
“You bastards! Do you even know where you are?”
A short old monk barely five feet tall appeared with a thunderous shout.
He glared at the masked men staining Shaolin Temple’s grounds with blood, cold blue sparks blazing in his eyes.
“Demonic martial arts! So you’re the demonic fiends of Tianshan!”
Palm force erupted from the old monk’s hands and swept across the grounds.
Kwoooong!
The masked men rushed him after noticing his presence too late, only to be swallowed by the palm force and killed.
It was an overwhelming sight. More than ten masters were crushed by a single attack.
However...
“The Lord of Heaven has commanded us. Kill the enemy.”
“Follow Heaven’s command. Kill them all.”
The hundreds of masked men did not stop.
They possessed neither agitation nor hesitation. They merely muttered as though possessed by ghosts and swung their swords.
Slash. Slash. Slash.
The old monk’s expression hardened at the sight.
How ruthless...
Even when their limbs were severed and their intestines spilled out, they did not so much as twitch an eyebrow.
They slaughtered without feeling pain or fear, then dropped like puppets with their strings cut. The sight sent a chill through him.
These things aren’t human. They’re Fiends incarnate.
If even an old monk who had fought his way through the Great Faction War felt that way, how much worse must it have been for everyone else?
The more experienced middle-aged martial monks were struggling valiantly, but the young monks witnessing such carnage for the first time trembled with fear.
Yet they did not retreat.
Perhaps it was the sense of duty that came with being disciples of Buddhism standing face-to-face with Fiends.
I never thought this day would come.
The old monk lamented inwardly.
During the last Great Faction War, Shaolin had been at the forefront more than anyone and shed more blood than anyone.
It had been a noble sacrifice that saved the Murim, but Shaolin had lost many elders and much martial knowledge. And the sacrifices of that era had returned today as tragedy.
Of all times, this had to happen while my Senior Brother, the Abbot, was away!
There was no helping it. He was the only one who could defend Shaolin now.
The old monk, Hongcheon, gritted his teeth and unleashed a lion’s roar.
“This is Shaolin!”
His name might have been overshadowed by that of his Senior Brother, Hong Dao, but he too was a master who had reached the Supreme Peak realm.
Though the outside world knew nothing of his abilities, his ceaseless devotion to martial arts had already carried him beyond Hong Dao.
“Come at me, all of you!”
Kwoooong!
Palm force imbued with mighty Buddhist internal energy swept out in every direction.
At that moment—
“Oh-ho. The Hundred-Step Divine Fist?”
“We get to see that damned martial art again.”
Two voices pierced Hongcheon’s ears.
Two men slowly entered the temple grounds. As soon as they appeared, the masked men lowered their swords and withdrew in perfect unison.
“Was it you bastards?”
At Hongcheon’s snarled question, the red-bearded old man picked his nose and answered.
“That’s right. This old man right here.”
“You’re the vile demonic fiends of Tianshan.”
“The demonic fiends of Tianshan? Well, that’s half right and half wrong. But I’ll let it pass.”
Hongcheon paused.
“You’re not from the Demonic Cult?”
“What does that matter? All you need to know is that I’m the one who’ll grab your shiny pate and rip it off.”
The old man with the air of a great scholar answered with a quiet smile.
“Flame Tiger, are you going to handle him?”
“Naturally. Now that I’ve seen the Hundred-Step Divine Fist, I can’t just let it go.”
“I keep telling you to rein in that temper of yours.”
“I’ll think about it later. Right now, I want to kill that bald monk more than I care about my temper.”

The name Flame Tiger.
The immense auras radiating from the two old men, who could not have seemed more different.
“Could you two be...?”
Flame Tiger gave a ferocious laugh and nodded.
“You’re only realizing it now? You must still be a youngster. All those damned monks of the Beom generation have been dead for ages... Are you the Dharma King’s youngest Junior Brother?”
“Judging by that reaction, I guess I’m right. Han Su, what was the name of that old monk you killed at the end?”
“Beomgong.”

There’s no doubt. It’s them.
How could he not know the names Flame Tiger and Han Su?
Or the epithet shared by the villains who had killed countless Shaolin disciples?
“The Yin-Yang Twin Freaks.”
It was a story from the distant past.

They had emerged into the Central Plains and stained the world with blood, while the orthodox faction’s net over heaven and earth, spread to hunt them down, had been torn apart by the Demonic Cult’s invasion.
The two fiends had escaped death by the narrowest margin, entered the Demonic Cult’s service, and earned a terrifying reputation during the Great Faction War.
“The Yin-Yang Twin Freaks... It has been a long time since I heard that name from someone else’s lips.”
“Those were good times. Few things have ever been as enjoyable.”
Flame Tiger fondly reminisced about that horrific past, then shook his head.
“No, that’s not right. I still prefer things as they are now.”
“Of course. We couldn’t even set foot in Henan back then.”
“It was all because of that damned Martial God.”
“But the Martial God is gone now.”
“Hardly any of those so-called Ten Kings and Three Saints are left, either.”

“Ah, come to think of it, I’d forgotten for a moment. Please accept my condolences.”

“On our way up, we heard that someone had died. Dharma King Hong Dao—your Senior Brother.”
Shock struck him, making the world before his eyes seem to go dim.
His Senior Brother, who should have been at the Murim Alliance, was dead?
That was impossible.
“Nonsense!”
Han Su gave a short laugh as he looked at the shaken Hongcheon.
“Whether it’s true or not is for you to decide. And...”
Flame Tiger continued in a heated voice.
“All the monks here, including you, will die. That’s our judgment.”
Rustle.
As if they had sensed their leader’s aura, the masked men took a step forward with emotionless eyes.
A deadly edge rising from hundreds of sword blades filled Shaolin Temple.
Hongcheon’s eyelids trembled at the sight.
Senior Brother... Is it true?
But the trembling soon subsided, and light returned to his eyes.
The old monk, who had devoted eighty years to martial arts, clenched his fists.
“I never thought I’d have to face the Yin-Yang Twin Freaks at the same time. Come, you damned old monsters.”
“Wahahaha! You’ve got quite a foul mouth for a monk. I like that you’re still so full of youthful vigor.”
Flame Tiger burst into hearty laughter and stepped forward.
“Unfortunately, one old man is enough for you. Han Su has a more pressing matter to attend to.”
“Very urgent business.”
Han Su smiled faintly and continued.
“So will you step aside? I have to go to the Face-Wall Cave.”
The Face-Wall Cave.
The moment those words left Han Su’s mouth, Hongcheon felt his heart plummet.
Unnamed was there. His Senior Brother’s only Disciple.
And...
The Green Jade Buddha Staff.
At last realizing the enemies’ objective, Hongcheon let out a lion’s roar.
“Stop them by whatever means necessary!”
“Stop us? That won’t be enough.”
The Yin-Yang Twin Freaks flicked their hands, dark smiles spreading across their faces.
As though they had returned to the days of fifty years ago, horrifying killing intent surged from their entire bodies.
“Kill them all.”
Fwoooooosh!

Smack!
Smack!
Cheongpung opened his eyes with a groan.
Someone was slapping him hard across the face.

Ah.

With that small insight, Cheongpung opened his mouth.
“Excuse me.”
Smack!
Smack!

Smack!
Smack!

Smack!
Only after landing one last slap did the hand finally stop.
A familiar-looking young man spoke with a stiff expression.

Hyuk Mujin sighed.

Cheongpung remembered Hyuk Mujin as a good person.

I suddenly remembered the money I lost.”
“What?”

If that was the reason, Cheongpung could understand.

Shouts rang out from every direction, and people were running everywhere.

Dharma King Hong Dao had been found dead, and the culprit was none other than...

That bastard.

A place where fiends and vicious killers who had once stained the entire world with blood had gathered.
And Jongni Chu was an assassin from that very Demonic Cult.
Cheongpung shook his head without realizing it.

Hyuk Mujin continued with an incredulous expression.

No.
Cheongpung remembered everything clearly.
The helplessness and fear he had felt before a master against whom nothing worked.
Even that final moment, when he had contemplated death for the first time in his life.
I was scared.
Truly scared.
The mere thought made the fine hairs on his body stand on end and his palms turn clammy.
But why?
Why did Jongni Chu’s face keep appearing before his eyes—that bright smile he had worn when asking Cheongpung to be his friend?
Cheongpung’s lips remained pressed tightly together for a moment before finally parting.
“He’s my friend.”
“...What?”
“That man is my friend.
He couldn’t have done it.”
“Young Hero Cheong!”
Startled, Hyuk Mujin hurriedly glanced around.
Only after confirming that no one was paying attention to them did he lower his voice.
“Are you insane?
Jongni Chu is already as good as an enemy of the entire Murim.
How can you call someone like that your friend...?”
He was an assassin who had murdered the Abbot of Shaolin Temple and fled.
Simply being acquainted with Jongni Chu could be enough to earn Cheongpung a brutal beating.
Even if he was the disciple the Sword Saint had raised like his own flesh and blood, people would still glare at him.
“Never mention him out loud again.
Do you understand?”
Cheongpung was about to say something, but he closed his mouth at the look in Hyuk Mujin’s eyes.
“He’s a demonic fiend.

“Are you certain?
Did anyone see him kill him?”
“All the circumstances point to it.

“Shaolin...”

Great Hero Jeok and the Captain have already gone on ahead.”
Cheongpung slowly closed his eyes.
In the pitch-black darkness, the faces of Jin Taekyung and Jongni Chu flashed before him in turn.
He did not deliberate for long.
“I’ll go ahead.”
“What?”
By the time Hyuk Mujin asked back with a dazed expression, Cheongpung had already shot far into the distance.
His feet carried him toward Mount Song.
Mount Song was beautiful and peaceful enough to be counted among the Five Sacred Mountains.
But the place that should have been green and lovely was stained with blood and filled with screams.
“Aaaaaagh!”
“Kill every last one of them.”
Slash!
Shhhhhhk!
Blood spurted from every direction whenever a flash of sword light gleamed.
In broad daylight on the peaceful day of Baekjung, hundreds of masked men had appeared without warning and begun slaughtering people with emotionless eyes.
“Protect the pilgrims!
Do not retreat!”
Shaolin martial monks with Buddhist precept seals carved into their foreheads stood against them, but the situation showed no sign of improving.
The masked men were all exceptional masters and difficult enough to fight on their own.
On top of that, the martial monks had to protect the scholarly monks who had never learned martial arts, the young novices, and the countless pilgrims.
“Wh-what is this?”
“Kraaagh!”
No one had expected anything like this to happen today.
Who would dare invade the grounds of Shaolin Temple, the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of the Murim, in the very heart of the Central Plains?
The monks were being swept aside by the cruel, treacherous masked men when—
“You bastards!
Do you even know where you are?”
A short old monk barely five feet tall appeared with a thunderous shout.
He glared at the masked men staining Shaolin Temple’s grounds with blood, cold blue sparks blazing in his eyes.
“Demonic martial arts!
So you’re the demonic fiends of Tianshan!”
Palm force erupted from the old monk’s hands and swept across the grounds.
Kwoooong!
The masked men rushed him after noticing his presence too late, only to be swallowed by the palm force and killed.
It was an overwhelming sight.
More than ten masters were crushed by a single attack.
However...
“The Lord of Heaven has commanded us.
Kill the enemy.”
“Follow Heaven’s command.
Kill them all.”
The hundreds of masked men did not stop.
They possessed neither agitation nor hesitation.
They merely muttered as though possessed by ghosts and swung their swords.
Slash.
Slash.
Slash.
The old monk’s expression hardened at the sight.
How ruthless...
Even when their limbs were severed and their intestines spilled out, they did not so much as twitch an eyebrow.
They slaughtered without feeling pain or fear, then dropped like puppets with their strings cut.
The sight sent a chill through him.
These things aren’t human.
They’re Fiends incarnate.
If even an old monk who had fought his way through the Great Faction War felt that way, how much worse must it have been for everyone else?
The more experienced middle-aged martial monks were struggling valiantly, but the young monks witnessing such carnage for the first time trembled with fear.
Yet they did not retreat.
Perhaps it was the sense of duty that came with being disciples of Buddhism standing face-to-face with Fiends.
I never thought this day would come.

Of all times, this had to happen while my Senior Brother, the Abbot, was away!
There was no helping it.
He was the only one who could defend Shaolin now.
