paragraphs: Blood gushed up.
The middle-aged monk’s beard, streaked here and there with white, was soaked in blood. He forced out the words in a broken voice.
“D-Demon. You’re a demon.”
A calm voice slipped into his ear.
“Shakyamuni drove away the demons’ temptations and attained enlightenment beneath the Bodhi tree, or so they say. But...”
Shaaak!
A hand wreathed in bitterly cold blue Force pulled free of the monk’s chest.
The gaping wound had already frozen over, and frost-covered drops of blood fell to the ground like shards of ice.
“No enlightenment can endure in the face of death.”
The monk trembled as a chill swept through his entire body.
He did not know whether it came from the extreme Yin-Cold Technique that had frozen even his internal organs or the aura of death looming before his eyes.
No. He could not know.
Ssslip. Thud.
Yin Ghost Han Su looked down at the monk, who had died with his eyes wide open. His gaze darkened.
That was dangerous. More dangerous than I expected.
He looked around. Four corpses lay sprawled before the collapsed entrance to the Face-Wall Cave, including the middle-aged monk who had just fallen.
The Four Great Vajras.
As martial monks counted among Shaolin’s finest, each of them possessed formidable martial arts.
The last bald monk in particular had been a master at the threshold of Supreme Peak. If Han Su had not traded flesh for bone, he might have lost his life to the Four Great Vajras’ combined assault.
Persistent bastards. Somehow, they’ve managed to keep their lineage alive.
Shaolin had suffered losses approaching ninety percent during the last Great Faction War.

The damage had been so catastrophic that it could no longer compare to the days when it had been called the greatest sect under heaven. Even so, the strength Shaolin had accumulated over a thousand years still remained.
But that ends today.
Every part of the plan was proceeding smoothly. Dharma King Hong Dao was dead, the Four Great Vajras had fallen, and Hongcheon would soon meet his end at Flame Tiger’s hands.
The hundreds of killers stripped of every sensation would drench Mount Song in blood and withdraw only after burning the martial arts manuals in the Scripture Depository.
If Shaolin lost both its leading masters and its martial arts, its decline would be certain.
And one mission took priority over everything else.
The Green Jade Buddha Staff.
Han Su could not guess why Shaolin’s sacred treasure mattered so much, but he had to complete his task.
Because it was none other than the Lord of Heaven’s command.
Was that not why he, the man who enjoyed the Lord of Heaven’s absolute trust, had come with them?
“I’ll take care of Hong Dao. You bastards take care of Shaolin. If you fail to find the Green Jade Buddha Staff... I’ll leave what happens next to your imagination.”
Han Su’s face stiffened as he recalled the last thing he had said.
There could not be a single mistake. If Han Su failed, he would pay dearly for it.
Boom!
Han Su flicked his sleeve, clearing the blocked entrance to the Face-Wall Cave.
Even the massive stone gate revealed beyond it could not halt his advance.
Rumble!
The stone gate collapsed with a deafening roar. Beyond the billowing cloud of dust and powdered stone, a pair of eyes gleamed with piercing light.
“Benefactor. What brings you here?”
Han Su curled his lips as the young monk, Unnamed, unfolded his crossed legs and slowly rose.
“Are you Hong Dao’s Disciple?”
“And what will you do if I am?”
“I’ve come to collect something.”
“I have nothing to give you, Benefactor.”
“Then let me correct myself. I’ve come to take it.”
“I cannot surrender so much as a single grain of rice to someone reeking of blood.”
“Don’t trouble yourself over it. I’ll take your life along with it.”
“Amitabha.”
Unnamed brought his palms together, his prayer beads wrapped around one hand. Determination gleamed in his eyes.
“It won’t be easy.”
The battle between Hongcheon and Flame Tiger, two fist masters who had reached Supreme Peak, was fierce.
Screeeech! Boom!
Every thrust, swing, and rising kick carried tremendous power.
It was a clash between superhumans who had stepped into the lofty realm of Supreme Peak—a battle no one dared interfere with.
But as time passed, the scales began to tip.
Boom!
The instant their Force-wreathed fists collided, a line of crimson blood trickled from one man’s mouth.
“Cough.”
The monk’s gray robes turned bright red.
Flame Tiger bared his yellow teeth as Hongcheon was driven back a dozen steps, as if swept away by an invisible wind.
“Brat. When you were still suckling at your mother’s breast, this old man was rampaging through Nanman. You’re thirty years too early to challenge me.”
Hongcheon wiped his mouth with his sleeve. Despite his pallid complexion, the old monk’s eyes burned fiercely.
“You truly are an old monster. How about climbing into your coffin already?”
“Even when the orthodox faction cast a net over heaven and earth, they couldn’t catch this old man. A bald monk like you doesn’t stand a chance.”
Hongcheon bit his lip as Flame Tiger’s aura blazed even more fiercely.
He knew those words were not mere confidence. They were simply the truth.
What kind of monster is he, to still be going this strong?
The Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts had already been over sixty during the Great Faction War.
Yet despite clearly being well over a hundred now, Flame Tiger showed no sign of fatigue.

Internal energy whose depths Hongcheon could not begin to fathom. Experience accumulated through countless acts of slaughter. Even the one weakness Flame Tiger should have possessed—old age—seemed to have passed him by.
Despair closed in around Hongcheon.
But there’s still hope.
His eyes shifted slightly toward the more than one hundred martial monks fighting the masked men.
One hundred and eight, to be exact.
They were the Hundred and Eight Arhats, the face and pride of Shaolin Temple.
The carefully selected elite wielded their precept blades and Zen staffs, steadily driving back the masked men.
“They are the greatest criminals under heaven. Show them no mercy!”
“Open the Killing Gate!”
The Hundred and Eight Arhats displayed their true strength when they deployed the Hundred and Eight Arhats Formation.
Each of them performed his assigned role flawlessly, calmly reproducing in battle what they had practiced thousands of times.
Clang-clang-clang! Slash!
The Hundred and Eight Arhats Formation bore down like the palm of the Tathagata, and the masked men began to fall one after another, spraying blood.
The battle, so one-sided at first, had become evenly matched.
If this continues... we can win.
The Murim Alliance was only a few shichen away. Once reinforcements arrived, the Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts and the masked men would be the ones in danger.
A glimmer of hope crossed Hongcheon’s eyes.
“Wahahaha!”
“Every thought is written all over your face. What an innocent monk you are.”
Hongcheon’s expression stiffened. Something about Flame Tiger’s attitude struck him as strange.
Did he already know this would happen?
But why?
Before he could pursue the question, a deafening explosion left his ears ringing and shook the earth beneath his feet.
Kwooooom!
Hongcheon stared at the sight before him, his mouth hanging open.
The world seemed to slow. Amid the earth thrown more than ten zhang into the air, severed limbs tumbled through a downpour of blood.
One section of the Hundred and Eight Arhats Formation had vanished as though swallowed by a gigantic monster.
“No!”
Time lurched back into motion with Hongcheon’s scream.
The explosion had devastated an area more than ten zhang across. More than twenty Arhat monks had been reduced to chunks of flesh.
The masked men surged into the gap like a wave.
Slash. Slash. Slash!
The Arhat monks were still only human.
Flashing blades filled the vision of those frozen in shock.
The battlefield allowed not a moment of carelessness. The price of hesitation was horrific.
“Aaaaaagh!”
“Junior Brother!”
The Hundred and Eight Arhats Formation, once as solid as an invincible shield, crumbled helplessly. Several old monks belatedly tried to restore it, but their efforts were in vain.
Their opponents were no ordinary men.
They were beings worthy of being called demons.
“The Lord of Heaven has commanded us. Kill the enemy.”
Tss-tss-tss-tss.
As one masked man muttered in a toneless voice, red light seeped from his eyes, ears, nostrils, and mouth.
The Arhat monks stared in stunned disbelief at the bizarre phenomenon they were witnessing for the first time.
“W-What is that?”
“Demonic martial arts! It’s demonic martial arts! Everyone, get away!”
But it was already too late.
The red light swelled until it enveloped the masked man’s entire body, then erupted in every direction, swallowing dozens of Arhat monks and several masked men.
Boom!
An explosion. A deafening roar. Screams.
Severed limbs flew through the sky, and the rain pattering down was red.
Blood vessels spread across Hongcheon’s eyes as he stared blankly at the scene.
“H-How dare you...”
Shaolin was collapsing.
Shaolin Temple, which had stood unshaken even through the Great Faction War, now overflowed with corpses and death.
The young Disciple who had greeted him with a smile every morning lay dead. The Junior Brother with whom he had shared decades of friendship had vanished without a trace.
As the hellscape unfolded before his eyes, blood dripped from his tightly clenched fist.
“This can’t... This can’t be happening.”
Flame Tiger threw back his head and laughed heartily at Hongcheon’s muttering.

“It’s called the Exploding Blood Demonic Art. It’s a damned tricky art, so it’s difficult to master, but it’s perfect for times like this. I brought a couple of them along... and they’re even more useful than I expected.”
“How dare you bastards—!”
Hongcheon shot forward with a cry that was nearly a scream.
A fist wreathed in crimson Force was waiting for him.
Bababoom!
His Body-Protecting Qi shattered, and a barrage of powerful blows hammered Hongcheon’s limbs.
The pain was so intense that his vision went dark. Blood gushed from his mouth, mixed with pieces of his internal organs.
“Gwaaaargh!”
Through his blurred vision, Hongcheon saw Flame Tiger approaching at a leisurely pace.
“You stupid bastard. You spent all those years learning Shaolin’s martial arts, yet you forgot your Unshakable Mind?”
“Cough! Cough!”
It had been an undeniable mistake. No matter what happened, Hongcheon should not have lost his composure. Whatever he witnessed, he should have responded calmly.
His opponent was a monster who had already been considered comparable to the Ten Kings during the Great Faction War.
The best course of action had been to maintain the standoff somehow and buy time.
“You bastard...”
But Hongcheon still forced himself upright, gasping for breath.
Not yet.
If he fell, Shaolin would fall with him. He had to defend this place until his final breath.
For one moment longer. So that even one more person might escape alive.
That was the final duty of an old monk who had devoted his entire life to Shaolin.
“Come.”
Flame Tiger frowned at the fire burning in Hongcheon’s eyes.
“This is why I hate monk bastards. They’re about to die, but they still insist on putting on airs.”
“What would a demonic fiend like you know?”
“I think I know one thing.”
Flame Tiger laughed savagely.
“You’re about to die.”
Whoosh!
Already gravely wounded, Hongcheon could not follow his speed.
In the blink of an eye, Flame Tiger closed the distance and slammed a fist into Hongcheon’s shoulder.
Thud!
The Force behind that single punch tore through flesh and bone.
Hongcheon screamed as everything below his shoulder vanished.
“Aaaaaagh!”
“You damned bald monk. You dare dodge this old man’s fist? Let’s see you dodge this one too.”
Flame Tiger planted a foot on Hongcheon’s head as the old monk writhed in agony.
Even a tenth—no, a hundredth—of his strength would crush Hongcheon’s skull like a watermelon.
“What do people say at a time like this? Ah, right.”
Flame Tiger tapped his forehead theatrically and continued.
“May you be reborn in paradise.”
Grrrrk.
The pressure slowly increased.
Just as death closed in before Hongcheon’s eyes, two voices reached them.
“Take that filthy foot off him. Before I reduce even your filthy spirit to ash.”
“And make your little chili pepper extra crispy.”
The first voice belonged to an old man. The second was young—shockingly young.
Flame Tiger turned toward the voices, and his face stiffened.
“The Fire King...!”

sentences.text: Blood gushed up.
The middle-aged monk’s beard, streaked here and there with white, was soaked in blood.
He forced out the words in a broken voice.
“D-Demon.
You’re a demon.”
A calm voice slipped into his ear.
“Shakyamuni drove away the demons’ temptations and attained enlightenment beneath the Bodhi tree, or so they say.
But...”
Shaaak!
A hand wreathed in bitterly cold blue Force pulled free of the monk’s chest.
The gaping wound had already frozen over, and frost-covered drops of blood fell to the ground like shards of ice.
“No enlightenment can endure in the face of death.”
The monk trembled as a chill swept through his entire body.
He did not know whether it came from the extreme Yin-Cold Technique that had frozen even his internal organs or the aura of death looming before his eyes.
No.
He could not know.
Ssslip.
Thud.
Yin Ghost Han Su looked down at the monk, who had died with his eyes wide open.
His gaze darkened.
That was dangerous.
More dangerous than I expected.
He looked around.
Four corpses lay sprawled before the collapsed entrance to the Face-Wall Cave, including the middle-aged monk who had just fallen.
The Four Great Vajras.
As martial monks counted among Shaolin’s finest, each of them possessed formidable martial arts.
The last bald monk in particular had been a master at the threshold of Supreme Peak.
If Han Su had not traded flesh for bone, he might have lost his life to the Four Great Vajras’ combined assault.
Persistent bastards.
Somehow, they’ve managed to keep their lineage alive.
Shaolin had suffered losses approaching ninety percent during the last Great Faction War.
The damage had been so catastrophic that it could no longer compare to the days when it had been called the greatest sect under heaven.
Even so, the strength Shaolin had accumulated over a thousand years still remained.
But that ends today.
Every part of the plan was proceeding smoothly.
Dharma King Hong Dao was dead, the Four Great Vajras had fallen, and Hongcheon would soon meet his end at Flame Tiger’s hands.
The hundreds of killers stripped of every sensation would drench Mount Song in blood and withdraw only after burning the martial arts manuals in the Scripture Depository.
If Shaolin lost both its leading masters and its martial arts, its decline would be certain.
And one mission took priority over everything else.
The Green Jade Buddha Staff.
Han Su could not guess why Shaolin’s sacred treasure mattered so much, but he had to complete his task.
Because it was none other than the Lord of Heaven’s command.
Was that not why he, the man who enjoyed the Lord of Heaven’s absolute trust, had come with them?
“I’ll take care of Hong Dao.
You bastards take care of Shaolin.
If you fail to find the Green Jade Buddha Staff...
I’ll leave what happens next to your imagination.”
Han Su’s face stiffened as he recalled the last thing he had said.
There could not be a single mistake.
If Han Su failed, he would pay dearly for it.
Boom!
Han Su flicked his sleeve, clearing the blocked entrance to the Face-Wall Cave.
Even the massive stone gate revealed beyond it could not halt his advance.
Rumble!
The stone gate collapsed with a deafening roar.
Beyond the billowing cloud of dust and powdered stone, a pair of eyes gleamed with piercing light.
“Benefactor.
What brings you here?”
Han Su curled his lips as the young monk, Unnamed, unfolded his crossed legs and slowly rose.
“Are you Hong Dao’s Disciple?”
“And what will you do if I am?”
“I’ve come to collect something.”
“I have nothing to give you, Benefactor.”
“Then let me correct myself.
I’ve come to take it.”
“I cannot surrender so much as a single grain of rice to someone reeking of blood.”
“Don’t trouble yourself over it.
I’ll take your life along with it.”
“Amitabha.”
Unnamed brought his palms together, his prayer beads wrapped around one hand.
Determination gleamed in his eyes.
“It won’t be easy.”
The battle between Hongcheon and Flame Tiger, two fist masters who had reached Supreme Peak, was fierce.
Screeeech!
Boom!
Every thrust, swing, and rising kick carried tremendous power.
It was a clash between superhumans who had stepped into the lofty realm of Supreme Peak—a battle no one dared interfere with.
But as time passed, the scales began to tip.
Boom!
The instant their Force-wreathed fists collided, a line of crimson blood trickled from one man’s mouth.
“Cough.”
The monk’s gray robes turned bright red.
Flame Tiger bared his yellow teeth as Hongcheon was driven back a dozen steps, as if swept away by an invisible wind.
“Brat.
When you were still suckling at your mother’s breast, this old man was rampaging through Nanman.
You’re thirty years too early to challenge me.”
Hongcheon wiped his mouth with his sleeve.
Despite his pallid complexion, the old monk’s eyes burned fiercely.
“You truly are an old monster.
How about climbing into your coffin already?”
“Even when the orthodox faction cast a net over heaven and earth, they couldn’t catch this old man.
A bald monk like you doesn’t stand a chance.”
Hongcheon bit his lip as Flame Tiger’s aura blazed even more fiercely.
He knew those words were not mere confidence.
They were simply the truth.
What kind of monster is he, to still be going this strong?
The Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts had already been over sixty during the Great Faction War.
Yet despite clearly being well over a hundred now, Flame Tiger showed no sign of fatigue.
Internal energy whose depths Hongcheon could not begin to fathom.
Experience accumulated through countless acts of slaughter.
Even the one weakness Flame Tiger should have possessed—old age—seemed to have passed him by.
Despair closed in around Hongcheon.
But there’s still hope.
His eyes shifted slightly toward the more than one hundred martial monks fighting the masked men.
One hundred and eight, to be exact.
They were the Hundred and Eight Arhats, the face and pride of Shaolin Temple.
The carefully selected elite wielded their precept blades and Zen staffs, steadily driving back the masked men.
“They are the greatest criminals under heaven.
Show them no mercy!”
“Open the Killing Gate!”
The Hundred and Eight Arhats displayed their true strength when they deployed the Hundred and Eight Arhats Formation.
Each of them performed his assigned role flawlessly, calmly reproducing in battle what they had practiced thousands of times.
Clang-clang-clang!
Slash!
The Hundred and Eight Arhats Formation bore down like the palm of the Tathagata, and the masked men began to fall one after another, spraying blood.
The battle, so one-sided at first, had become evenly matched.
If this continues... we can win.
The Murim Alliance was only a few shichen away.
Once reinforcements arrived, the Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts and the masked men would be the ones in danger.
A glimmer of hope crossed Hongcheon’s eyes.
“Wahahaha!”
“Every thought is written all over your face.
What an innocent monk you are.”
Hongcheon’s expression stiffened.
Something about Flame Tiger’s attitude struck him as strange.
Did he already know this would happen?
But why?
Before he could pursue the question, a deafening explosion left his ears ringing and shook the earth beneath his feet.
Kwooooom!
Hongcheon stared at the sight before him, his mouth hanging open.
The world seemed to slow.
Amid the earth thrown more than ten zhang into the air, severed limbs tumbled through a downpour of blood.
One section of the Hundred and Eight Arhats Formation had vanished as though swallowed by a gigantic monster.
“No!”
Time lurched back into motion with Hongcheon’s scream.
The explosion had devastated an area more than ten zhang across.
More than twenty Arhat monks had been reduced to chunks of flesh.
The masked men surged into the gap like a wave.
Slash.
Slash.
Slash!
The Arhat monks were still only human.
Flashing blades filled the vision of those frozen in shock.
The battlefield allowed not a moment of carelessness.
The price of hesitation was horrific.
“Aaaaaagh!”
“Junior Brother!”
The Hundred and Eight Arhats Formation, once as solid as an invincible shield, crumbled helplessly.
Several old monks belatedly tried to restore it, but their efforts were in vain.
Their opponents were no ordinary men.
They were beings worthy of being called demons.
“The Lord of Heaven has commanded us.
Kill the enemy.”
Tss-tss-tss-tss.
As one masked man muttered in a toneless voice, red light seeped from his eyes, ears, nostrils, and mouth.
The Arhat monks stared in stunned disbelief at the bizarre phenomenon they were witnessing for the first time.
“W-What is that?”
“Demonic martial arts!
It’s demonic martial arts!
Everyone, get away!”
But it was already too late.
The red light swelled until it enveloped the masked man’s entire body, then erupted in every direction, swallowing dozens of Arhat monks and several masked men.
Boom!
An explosion.
A deafening roar.
Screams.
Severed limbs flew through the sky, and the rain pattering down was red.
Blood vessels spread across Hongcheon’s eyes as he stared blankly at the scene.
“H-How dare you...”
Shaolin was collapsing.
Shaolin Temple, which had stood unshaken even through the Great Faction War, now overflowed with corpses and death.
The young Disciple who had greeted him with a smile every morning lay dead.
The Junior Brother with whom he had shared decades of friendship had vanished without a trace.
As the hellscape unfolded before his eyes, blood dripped from his tightly clenched fist.
“This can’t...
This can’t be happening.”
Flame Tiger threw back his head and laughed heartily at Hongcheon’s muttering.
“It’s called the Exploding Blood Demonic Art.
It’s a damned tricky art, so it’s difficult to master, but it’s perfect for times like this.
I brought a couple of them along... and they’re even more useful than I expected.”
“How dare you bastards—!”
Hongcheon shot forward with a cry that was nearly a scream.
A fist wreathed in crimson Force was waiting for him.
Bababoom!
His Body-Protecting Qi shattered, and a barrage of powerful blows hammered Hongcheon’s limbs.
The pain was so intense that his vision went dark.
Blood gushed from his mouth, mixed with pieces of his internal organs.
“Gwaaaargh!”
Through his blurred vision, Hongcheon saw Flame Tiger approaching at a leisurely pace.
“You stupid bastard.
You spent all those years learning Shaolin’s martial arts, yet you forgot your Unshakable Mind?”
“Cough!
Cough!”
It had been an undeniable mistake.
No matter what happened, Hongcheon should not have lost his composure.
Whatever he witnessed, he should have responded calmly.
His opponent was a monster who had already been considered comparable to the Ten Kings during the Great Faction War.
The best course of action had been to maintain the standoff somehow and buy time.
“You bastard...”
But Hongcheon still forced himself upright, gasping for breath.
Not yet.
If he fell, Shaolin would fall with him.

They’re about to die, but they still insist on putting on airs.”

Let’s see you dodge this one too.”

Ah, right.”

Grrrrk.

Before I reduce even your filthy spirit to ash.”
“And make your little chili pepper extra crispy.”
The first voice belonged to an old man.
The second was young—shockingly young.
Flame Tiger turned toward the voices, and his face stiffened.
“The Fire King...!”

chapters.title: Chapter 262
paragraphs: What awaited us when we arrived at full speed was a scene so horrific I could barely look at it.
Corpses. Pools of blood. Ownerless arms and legs...
If the Shaolin Temple I had seen with my own eyes a year ago had been a beautiful painting of a utopian paradise, then what lay before me now was a painting of hell.
These fucking lunatics.
They had clearly been killing civilians and Murim warriors alike, indiscriminately.
Beyond the masked men battling Shaolin’s monks, I spotted a red-bearded old man.
“The Fire King...!”
Without taking my eyes off him, I asked, “Know him?”
“No.”
“What about the monk pinned beneath him?”
“Hongcheon. Hong Dao’s youngest Junior Brother. He’s grown a lot since I last saw him.”
“...He sure has.”
So much that he looked well over seventy.
As I found myself at a loss for words, the old man’s blazing gaze swept over us.
“Are you the only ones?”
Jeok Cheongang answered indifferently.
“What if it is?”
“Heh heh. Looks like you’ve finally found a place to die, old man.”
“Even if your head is empty, you should still speak properly. It isn’t a place to die. It’s a place to kill—and that includes every one of you.”
The old man’s eyebrow twitched.
“Still as arrogant as ever. You haven’t changed.”
“Haven’t changed? Have we met before?”
“I saw you once from a distance. I regretted for years that we never had the chance to see which of us was stronger.”
“What’s your name?”
“Flame Tiger! I am the tiger of Nanman!”
“The Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts? Good. There should be one more, so there’s no need to take you alive. I can kill you.”
Jeok Cheongang clicked his tongue.
“You’re one lucky bastard, though. You turned back with the Sanzu River right before your eyes.”
“Is that so?”
Flames blazed in Flame Tiger’s eyes. At the same time, Fist Force gathered around his rough, rock-hard fist.
I had expected as much, but the old man was also a Supreme Peak master. What was more, he had trained in the same kind of Scorching Yang Qi as we had.
“You arrived much sooner than I’d heard... but that changes nothing.”
Than he’d heard?
For an instant, I wondered how Flame Tiger could have received word so quickly.
Even if he used a messenger pigeon, we should have been faster.
But I had to set the question aside. Flame Tiger was gripping Hongcheon’s head as though he meant to crush it.
Blood trickled from the mouth of the old monk, whose entire body was drenched in red.
“Cough. Cough.”
“Want this monk to live?”
I felt Jeok Cheongang tense.
More than thirty jang separated us from Flame Tiger. Even Jeok Cheongang could not charge in recklessly. If he did, Hongcheon’s head would be crushed like a block of tofu.
“Put him down. Now.”
Beneath Jeok Cheongang’s calm voice, I could feel rage boiling like lava.
Flame Tiger grinned.
“I heard you were close to that bald monk, Dharma King Hong Dao. I suppose it was true. Did he ask you to look after his Junior Brother before he died?”
“Hong Dao was wiser and more virtuous than any monk I knew. His name does not belong in your filthy mouth.”
“He’s dead either way. Maybe he’s crossing the Sanzu River right now.”
Jeok Cheongang stared at Flame Tiger, his gaze dark and still, then parted his lips.
“Go on.”
“What?”
“I said go on. Did you truly think that would be enough to shake this old man?”
“Y-You damned old monster.”
Flame Tiger’s face flushed red as he shook Hongcheon by the head.
“Are you saying you don’t care if this monk dies?”
“I don’t.”
“W-What?”
“It’s regrettable that I can’t save him, but Hong Dao did not ask me to look after his Junior Brother. He entrusted Shaolin to me.”
Tss-tss-tss-tss!
At that moment, an immense amount of internal energy gathered in Jeok Cheongang’s hand. It rapidly took shape, then shot forward like an arrow.
Not toward Flame Tiger, but toward the masked men ceaselessly swinging their swords.
Kwooooooong!
The terrifying mass of internal energy unleashed from Jeok Cheongang’s hand plunged straight into their midst.
Like a starving fire dragon, it rampaged through the masked men, devouring and incinerating everything it touched.
Whoosh!
For the first time, emotion surfaced in their otherwise lifeless eyes.
Fear and pain.
“Aaaaaagh!”
“Aaaaargh!”
Flames soared amid horrific screams.
Dozens staggered away with their bodies ablaze. Dozens more were already dead.
The masked men froze at the sight, and the monks’ precept blades and Zen staffs flew toward them.
“It’s not over yet!”
“Drive out these villains!”
Fwoosh! Slash!
Jeok Cheongang had reversed the situation in an instant. He fixed Flame Tiger with an icy glare.
“If you’re going to kill him, do it. Otherwise, put him down gently. You’re a bear, you bastard. Stop trying to play the fox.”
“Y-You goddamned old bastard!”
Whoosh!
Flame Tiger played the fox to the very end.
He hurled Hongcheon at us and rushed close behind him, plainly intending to use the monk’s body as a shield while he struck at the opening.
—You take Hongcheon.
A thread of Sound Transmission pierced my ear.
Jeok Cheongang and I kicked off the ground at the same instant.
Four figures shot toward one another.
I caught Hongcheon while Jeok Cheongang vaulted over him and attacked the fox—or rather, the bear—hiding behind him.
Kwoooong!
I let the pressure wave from their terrifying collision carry me backward.
After sliding more than twenty jang, I laid Hongcheon in a nearby patch of grass. Then I charged toward the two Supreme Peak masters locked in a vicious exchange.
Of course, Flame Tiger was not going to stand around chuckling while I joined the fight.
“You bastard!”
Fwoosh—thud!
My knee rang with a sharp vibration as it blocked a foot as thick as a log.
But that was all.
Supreme Peak and Peak were separated by a gulf no amount of luck could bridge.
But I had more than mere luck.
I had heaven’s luck.
The System.
I can handle him.
One-on-one would have been impossible, but Flame Tiger was already struggling just to hold off Jeok Cheongang.
His only mistake was underestimating me.
“I’m confiscating your dentures for four months.”
Flame Tiger’s face turned red enough to burst at the sight of my grin.
“You green little brat!”
“You yellow old geezer!”
“Kraaaagh!”
Flame Tiger threw Jeok Cheongang off and charged at me with a roar.
“I’ll kill you first!”
Whoosh!
A devastating punch hurtled toward me. Even I would not walk away unharmed if I took a strike wrapped in Fist Force with my bare body.
I stepped back, grabbed White Flame from my back, and swung.
Clang!
The punch stopped with a deafening crash.
Flame Tiger’s eyes grew as wide as lanterns.
“Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron?”
“Expensive weapons really are the best. Don’t you agree, Old Master?”
Jeok Cheongang did not answer.
Instead, his blue-white fist was already flying toward Flame Tiger.
Kwoong!
The ground shook with the thunderous impact.
The two fists had met perfectly, but one man’s fist had its bones crushed and was charred black.
Flame Tiger muttered with a dazed expression.
“H-How?”
“Did you think all who cultivate Scorching Yang Qi were equal?”
Jeok Cheongang’s voice was indifferent, but lava burned in his eyes.
Heat that made Flame Tiger’s paltry blaze seem insignificant poured from his entire body, pressing down on everything around him.
Flame Tiger groaned.
“The Fire King...”
“That’s right. This old man is Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King and eighteenth-generation successor of the Fire Gate Clan.”
“That’s imposs— Cough!”
As Flame Tiger coughed up blood and tried to flee, I launched myself after him.
“Where do you think you’re going?”
Crack!
My foot came down hard, crushing his instep and driving deep into the ground.
A pained groan escaped through Flame Tiger’s clenched teeth along with a spray of blood.
The next moment, two streaks of light pierced into his abdomen as his upper body staggered.
Whoosh!
The difference in our realms meant a difference in power, but the martial art we used was the same.
Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
Thud!
The Body-Protecting Qi encasing him like armor shattered.
A fountain of blood erupted from Flame Tiger’s gaping mouth.
“Gueeegh!”
Both men were Supreme Peak masters, but the difference between them was vast.
Jeok Cheongang looked down at Flame Tiger, who was panting from his severe Internal Injury.
“Your luck ends here.”
“Cough. W-Wait a moment.”
“I have neither the time nor the reason.”
“I’ll tell you everything! R-Right, Dark Heaven! Everything about Dark Heaven...”
“Didn’t this old man tell you to stop playing the fox?”
Fwoosh—thud!
There was not a trace of hesitation in Jeok Cheongang’s strike.
Flame Tiger’s head vanished. His body swayed for a moment before collapsing into a pool of blood.
I casually wiped the blood splattered across my face and said:
“Wouldn’t it have been better to keep him alive?”
“You don’t reveal important secrets to a bear as stupid as that.”
“Even so...”
“The bear is dead. Now we catch the fox.”
With those cryptic words, Jeok Cheongang turned his head.
More than a hundred jang away, an old man stood rooted to the spot, staring at us.
In his hand was a short staff glowing with green light.
“The Green Jade Buddha Staff!”
“Yin Ghost Han Su. He’s next.”
The next moment, as though he had understood those words, Han Su’s figure shot away at blinding speed.
Whoosh!
Han Su drove his movement technique to its limit.
Behind him, he could feel two auras drawing closer, little by little—ever so slowly.
Damn it!
He had recognized the man at first glance.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
He had never expected that a monster reputed to be among the very first of the Ten Kings would arrive so quickly.
But who is that young man?
The question briefly crossed his mind, then vanished.
The brat’s identity did not matter.
What mattered was that Flame Tiger, whose martial prowess equaled his own, had died at their hands.
What an idiot. He attacked the Fire King instead of the Thunderbolt Saber King.

Han Su had first met Flame Tiger during the Great Faction War and spent decades at his side, but they were not sworn brothers bound by a Peach Garden Oath. He had no intention of dying on the same day and at the same hour as Flame Tiger.
Just a little farther. Just a little more!
His mission was complete.
The Green Jade Buddha Staff in his hand was proof. If he could reach the designated location and rendezvous with him...
He would survive for certain.
Because he was a master beyond even the Fire King’s ability to defeat.
Flame Tiger. If that happens, I’ll avenge you.
Just as Han Su tightened his grip around the Green Jade Buddha Staff, his face hardened.
This is...!
Another aura was approaching in the distance.
This one was not behind him.
It was ahead.
At first, he thought it might be reinforcements from the orthodox faction, but the aura he sensed this time belonged to only one person. Its momentum was not particularly strong, either.
Damn it. This complicates things.
If anything delayed him, even for a moment, the Fire King might catch him.
Han Su bit down hard on his lip and wrung every last ounce of strength from his body. The instant he burst through the undergrowth—
“Ah!”
A short cry escaped him, his face lighting with joy.
No emotion could compare to the relief of returning from the brink of death.
Han Su called out to him, his voice brimming with elation.
“Blood Lord!”
As though by prior agreement, Jeok Cheongang and I stopped at the same time.
Han Su, who had gone from a desperate fugitive to a swaggering predator, stood waiting for us.
“There they are! The Fire King—that goddamned old man—and the young brat killed Flame Tiger!”
No.
Han Su was no predator.
He was merely a fox borrowing a tiger’s might.
The real predator was the man standing quietly beside Han Su.
I could sense nothing from him, which was strange in itself.
And that made him seem all the more dangerous.
Jeok Cheongang’s reaction was different. His face stiffened as he asked, “Who are you?”
“Your enemy.”
The young man smiled faintly.
“The enemy who killed your most precious friend.”
...What?

I suppose it was true.
Did he ask you to look after his Junior Brother before he died?”
“Hong Dao was wiser and more virtuous than any monk I knew.
His name does not belong in your filthy mouth.”
“He’s dead either way.
Maybe he’s crossing the Sanzu River right now.”
Jeok Cheongang stared at Flame Tiger, his gaze dark and still, then parted his lips.
“Go on.”
“What?”
“I said go on.
Did you truly think that would be enough to shake this old man?”
“Y-You damned old monster.”
Flame Tiger’s face flushed red as he shook Hongcheon by the head.
“Are you saying you don’t care if this monk dies?”
“I don’t.”
“W-What?”
“It’s regrettable that I can’t save him, but Hong Dao did not ask me to look after his Junior Brother.
He entrusted Shaolin to me.”
Tss-tss-tss-tss!
At that moment, an immense amount of internal energy gathered in Jeok Cheongang’s hand.
It rapidly took shape, then shot forward like an arrow.
Not toward Flame Tiger, but toward the masked men ceaselessly swinging their swords.
Kwooooooong!
The terrifying mass of internal energy unleashed from Jeok Cheongang’s hand plunged straight into their midst.
Like a starving fire dragon, it rampaged through the masked men, devouring and incinerating everything it touched.
Whoosh!
For the first time, emotion surfaced in their otherwise lifeless eyes.
Fear and pain.
“Aaaaaagh!”
“Aaaaargh!”
Flames soared amid horrific screams.
Dozens staggered away with their bodies ablaze.
Dozens more were already dead.
The masked men froze at the sight, and the monks’ precept blades and Zen staffs flew toward them.
“It’s not over yet!”
“Drive out these villains!”
Fwoosh!
Slash!
Jeok Cheongang had reversed the situation in an instant.
He fixed Flame Tiger with an icy glare.
“If you’re going to kill him, do it.
Otherwise, put him down gently.
You’re a bear, you bastard.
Stop trying to play the fox.”
“Y-You goddamned old bastard!”
Whoosh!
Flame Tiger played the fox to the very end.
He hurled Hongcheon at us and rushed close behind him, plainly intending to use the monk’s body as a shield while he struck at the opening.
—You take Hongcheon.
A thread of Sound Transmission pierced my ear.
Jeok Cheongang and I kicked off the ground at the same instant.
Four figures shot toward one another.
I caught Hongcheon while Jeok Cheongang vaulted over him and attacked the fox—or rather, the bear—hiding behind him.
Kwoooong!
I let the pressure wave from their terrifying collision carry me backward.
After sliding more than twenty jang, I laid Hongcheon in a nearby patch of grass.
Then I charged toward the two Supreme Peak masters locked in a vicious exchange.
Of course, Flame Tiger was not going to stand around chuckling while I joined the fight.
“You bastard!”
Fwoosh—thud!
My knee rang with a sharp vibration as it blocked a foot as thick as a log.
But that was all.
Supreme Peak and Peak were separated by a gulf no amount of luck could bridge.
But I had more than mere luck.
I had heaven’s luck.
The System.
I can handle him.
One-on-one would have been impossible, but Flame Tiger was already struggling just to hold off Jeok Cheongang.
His only mistake was underestimating me.
“I’m confiscating your dentures for four months.”
Flame Tiger’s face turned red enough to burst at the sight of my grin.
“You green little brat!”
“You yellow old geezer!”
“Kraaaagh!”
Flame Tiger threw Jeok Cheongang off and charged at me with a roar.
“I’ll kill you first!”
Whoosh!
A devastating punch hurtled toward me.
Even I would not walk away unharmed if I took a strike wrapped in Fist Force with my bare body.
I stepped back, grabbed White Flame from my back, and swung.
Clang!
The punch stopped with a deafening crash.
Flame Tiger’s eyes grew as wide as lanterns.
“Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron?”
“Expensive weapons really are the best.
Don’t you agree, Old Master?”
Jeok Cheongang did not answer.
Instead, his blue-white fist was already flying toward Flame Tiger.
Kwoong!
The ground shook with the thunderous impact.
The two fists had met perfectly, but one man’s fist had its bones crushed and was charred black.
Flame Tiger muttered with a dazed expression.
“H-How?”
“Did you think all who cultivate Scorching Yang Qi were equal?”
Jeok Cheongang’s voice was indifferent, but lava burned in his eyes.
Heat that made Flame Tiger’s paltry blaze seem insignificant poured from his entire body, pressing down on everything around him.
Flame Tiger groaned.
“The Fire King...”
“That’s right.
This old man is Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King and eighteenth-generation successor of the Fire Gate Clan.”
“That’s imposs— Cough!”
As Flame Tiger coughed up blood and tried to flee, I launched myself after him.
“Where do you think you’re going?”
Crack!
My foot came down hard, crushing his instep and driving deep into the ground.
A pained groan escaped through Flame Tiger’s clenched teeth along with a spray of blood.
The next moment, two streaks of light pierced into his abdomen as his upper body staggered.
Whoosh!
The difference in our realms meant a difference in power, but the martial art we used was the same.
Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
Thud!
The Body-Protecting Qi encasing him like armor shattered.
A fountain of blood erupted from Flame Tiger’s gaping mouth.
“Gueeegh!”
Both men were Supreme Peak masters, but the difference between them was vast.
Jeok Cheongang looked down at Flame Tiger, who was panting from his severe Internal Injury.
“Your luck ends here.”
“Cough.
W-Wait a moment.”
“I have neither the time nor the reason.”
“I’ll tell you everything!
R-Right, Dark Heaven!
Everything about Dark Heaven...”
“Didn’t this old man tell you to stop playing the fox?”
Fwoosh—thud!
There was not a trace of hesitation in Jeok Cheongang’s strike.
Flame Tiger’s head vanished.
His body swayed for a moment before collapsing into a pool of blood.
I casually wiped the blood splattered across my face and said:
“Wouldn’t it have been better to keep him alive?”
“You don’t reveal important secrets to a bear as stupid as that.”
“Even so...”
“The bear is dead.
Now we catch the fox.”
With those cryptic words, Jeok Cheongang turned his head.
More than a hundred jang away, an old man stood rooted to the spot, staring at us.
In his hand was a short staff glowing with green light.
“The Green Jade Buddha Staff!”
“Yin Ghost Han Su.
He’s next.”
The next moment, as though he had understood those words, Han Su’s figure shot away at blinding speed.
Whoosh!
Han Su drove his movement technique to its limit.
Behind him, he could feel two auras drawing closer, little by little—ever so slowly.
Damn it!
He had recognized the man at first glance.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
He had never expected that a monster reputed to be among the very first of the Ten Kings would arrive so quickly.
But who is that young man?
The question briefly crossed his mind, then vanished.
The brat’s identity did not matter.
What mattered was that Flame Tiger, whose martial prowess equaled his own, had died at their hands.
What an idiot.
He attacked the Fire King instead of the Thunderbolt Saber King.
Han Su had first met Flame Tiger during the Great Faction War and spent decades at his side, but they were not sworn brothers bound by a Peach Garden Oath.
He had no intention of dying on the same day and at the same hour as Flame Tiger.
Just a little farther.
Just a little more!
His mission was complete.
The Green Jade Buddha Staff in his hand was proof.
If he could reach the designated location and rendezvous with him...
He would survive for certain.
Because he was a master beyond even the Fire King’s ability to defeat.
Flame Tiger.
If that happens, I’ll avenge you.
Just as Han Su tightened his grip around the Green Jade Buddha Staff, his face hardened.
This is...!
Another aura was approaching in the distance.
This one was not behind him.
It was ahead.
At first, he thought it might be reinforcements from the orthodox faction, but the aura he sensed this time belonged to only one person.
Its momentum was not particularly strong, either.
Damn it.
This complicates things.
If anything delayed him, even for a moment, the Fire King might catch him.
Han Su bit down hard on his lip and wrung every last ounce of strength from his body.
The instant he burst through the undergrowth—
“Ah!”
A short cry escaped him, his face lighting with joy.
No emotion could compare to the relief of returning from the brink of death.
Han Su called out to him, his voice brimming with elation.
“Blood Lord!”
As though by prior agreement, Jeok Cheongang and I stopped at the same time.
Han Su, who had gone from a desperate fugitive to a swaggering predator, stood waiting for us.
“There they are!
The Fire King—that goddamned old man—and the young brat killed Flame Tiger!”
No.
Han Su was no predator.
He was merely a fox borrowing a tiger’s might.
The real predator was the man standing quietly beside Han Su.
I could sense nothing from him, which was strange in itself.
And that made him seem all the more dangerous.
Jeok Cheongang’s reaction was different.
His face stiffened as he asked, “Who are you?”
“Your enemy.”
The young man smiled faintly.
“The enemy who killed your most precious friend.”
...What?

chapters.title: Chapter 263
paragraphs: “That makes me the enemy who killed your most precious friend.”
At those words, I froze.
The same thought must have crossed Jeok Cheongang’s mind.
What did I just hear?
For a moment, I couldn’t make sense of it. The words that had come from the unfamiliar young man’s mouth tangled together in my head.
Wait...
He killed Hong Dao? That bastard?
Memories etched deep into my mind surfaced, then vanished.
Jongni Chu disappearing in the middle of the duel. Hong Dao gasping at death’s door. And the four words he had left behind as his final message.
Jongni Chu. Dark Heaven. Unnamed. Buddhist Staff.
What, exactly, had everything I’d seen and heard until now meant?
Where had it all begun, and how had it unfolded?
I stood frozen like a statue, desperately trying to grasp the thread connecting everything. But before I could put my thoughts in order, a dry voice escaped Jeok Cheongang’s lips.
“You... killed... Hong Dao?”
Each word came out separately, strained with restraint, rage, and disbelief.
The young man smiled faintly at Jeok Cheongang and nodded.
“I told you, didn’t I? It was much easier than I expected. I told him I was going to set off a Heaven-Shaking Thunder in the spectator stands, and he followed me without a fuss.”
“Heaven-Shaking Thunder? Had you planted explosives?”
“Ah, that? Of course it was a lie.”
“...What?”
“Why do people lie? Because every now and then, some idiot falls for it.”
Blood dripped from Jeok Cheongang’s fist as he clenched it hard enough to crush something.
“He wasn’t fooled. He allowed himself to be fooled. That was the kind of man Hong Dao was.”
“He allowed himself to be fooled? I suppose that’s possible. He was the damned Abbot of Shaolin, after all. Saying he wanted to prevent even the slightest chance of a massacre would make sense.”
“You bastard!”
“Don’t give me too much grief. I hadn’t planned anything this shoddy, either. But things went wrong where I least expected them to. Of course, part of that was because of...”
The young man’s gaze suddenly shifted toward me.
“The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung. You played your part.”
My body seemed to stiffen just from meeting his eyes.
I didn’t know whether it was because of my hostility toward him or because I could sense the overwhelming difference in power between us.
Maybe both.
I bit my lip and glared at the young man.
“What the fuck are you talking about?”
“You barged into the duel, forcing me to move the plan forward by a day. The biggest complication was that bastard, the Always-Victorious Sword Jongni Chu.”
That confirmed it.
Jongni Chu had not been the culprit—or even an accomplice.
“Well, everything worked out neatly in the end.”
The young man extended a hand.
Realizing what he wanted, Han Su hurriedly held out an object.
“Shaolin’s sacred treasure—the Green Jade Buddha Staff.”
“So this is the...”
The young man’s long fingers slowly brushed over the softly glowing Green Jade Buddha Staff.
But the next moment, he stared intently at Han Su’s face.
Han Su’s wrinkled hand was still gripping the staff.
“You can let go now.”
Han Su swallowed hard before answering.
“B-Blood Lord, I have one request.”
“A request? Go ahead. You worked hard, so I’ll do my utmost to grant it.”
It was a strange sight—no, a bizarre one.
An old man groveling before a young man who looked young enough to be his grandson.
Even more so when that old man was the infamous demonic fiend who had turned Shaolin Temple into a river of blood.
Who the hell is that bastard?
There were only two possibilities.
Either his status within Dark Heaven was unimaginably high, or he was much older than he looked.
There was also a good chance that both were true.
Whatever the case, Han Su’s face brightened at the answer from the young man called the Blood Lord.
“R-Really?”
The Blood Lord clicked his tongue.

“Have you spent your whole life being deceived? You completed your mission perfectly, so a Reward is only natural. But I wonder what kind of difficult request our Senior Yin Ghost is taking so long to bring up.”
“It is not that difficult a request.”
“But it’s difficult for you to handle yourself?”
“...I am ashamed to admit it, but yes.”
“Ah. I think I know what it is.”
The Blood Lord jerked his chin toward Jeok Cheongang and me.
“You want me to kill those two, don’t you? Am I right?”
Han Su nodded, his eyes filled with killing intent.
The Blood Lord let out a short laugh.
“Well, this is unexpected. I suppose the two of you were closer than I thought.”
“He was at my side for half my life. Nothing less will satisfy me.”
“Loyalty... Well, that’s admirable in its own way.”
“Kill them as cruelly as possible. I will lend a hand.”
“Will that be enough? If the orthodox faction comes swarming in, things will get troublesome. If we want to finish quickly and leave, you’ll have to work up a little sweat too, Senior.”
“Then?”
“You take the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi. I’ll take the Fire King. We should be finished within an ildagyeong at the latest.”
“You want me to take that young brat? Wahahaha! Very well!”
Their conversation was absurd. They spoke of our lives as though they were objects already tucked inside their pockets.
At the same time, a chill ran down my spine.
He means every word.
The Blood Lord had just declared that he could kill the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, within the time it took to drink a cup of tea.
The way Jeok Cheongang’s face had stiffened proved that his words were no empty boast.
—If things turn against us, run.
At the Sound Transmission that suddenly reached my ear, I gave the slightest shake of my head.
A fierce battle was already raging above us. We couldn’t expect help from Shaolin.
If I withdrew, Jeok Cheongang would have no choice but to face the concentrated assault of two Supreme Peak masters.
Our best option is to hold out here until the very end.
Jeok Cheongang knew that too.
And yet he had told me to run because he was warmer and worried more than anyone realized.
This time, we might really be in trouble.
I licked my parched lips and tightened my grip on White Flame.
Han Su sneered at the sight.
“Pathetic fool. Do you think that will change anything? Your attainment is impressive enough, but even if you died and came back to life, you could never defeat this old man.”
“Go fuck yourself.”
I spat a wad of phlegm onto the ground where he could see it.
“Give me a few shichen of solid sleep in this world, and when I wake up, you’ll die by my hand.”
“What kind of bullshit is that?”
“If you don’t believe me, put it to the test.”
“How dare you, you green little brat!”
It was unfortunate.
If I hadn’t been in the middle of a battle, and if time stopped completely when I used Logout instead of merely slowing down, I could have used all the time in the world to escape this crisis.
But those thoughts were nothing more than personal wishful thinking.
Now was the time to face reality, not indulge in delusions.
“I’ll freeze you alive.”
Step. Step. Crack.
Now I understood exactly why that damned old man was called the Yin Ghost.
The ground froze beneath every step he took, and frost settled over the branches.
“What vicious Yin-Cold Qi. But...”
Jeok Cheongang stepped in front of me.
“You dare not lay a hand on my Disciple.”
Whoosh!
If Han Su’s Yin-Cold Qi was an iceberg, Jeok Cheongang’s Scorching Yang Qi was the sun.
If Flame Tiger’s martial arts had truly been equal to Han Su’s, then Jeok Cheongang’s overwhelming victory had been inevitable.
But Han Su looked perfectly at ease.
He knew there was a tiger behind him.
“Blood Lord, I will need you to step in.”
“Of course. It’s about time we got started.”
The Blood Lord tucked the Green Jade Buddha Staff into his robes as carefully as if it were a priceless treasure.
Then he moved.
No—he vanished.
And in the next instant—
Slash! Thump!
A round object flew through the air with a sickening sound and rolled to a stop at my feet.
White hair. Dignified features. A faint smile still lingering around the mouth.
Jeok Cheongang’s eyes widened along with mine.
Han Su, the infamous great demonic fiend and Supreme Peak master known as the Yin Ghost, had been beheaded in a single strike.
By the hand of the ally he had trusted without question.
Unlike us, the Blood Lord—the one responsible for everything—remained perfectly calm.
“Fucking old man. This is why you should never take in rootless trash.”
Clicking his tongue, he casually nudged Han Su’s headless body.
Splash!
The corpse toppled like a dead tree, spraying a fountain of blood across the ground.
“If you’re a sword, act like a sword. Go wherever the person holding you swings you. How dare you...”
Thud! Thud! Crack!
His kicks, loaded with internal energy, tore through flesh and shattered bone.
After repeatedly stamping and grinding Han Su’s lifeless corpse beneath his feet, the Blood Lord swept his fallen hair back.
“There are always people who don’t know their place. They don’t know how strong they are or how far they should stick their necks out. Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, don’t you agree?”
What was I supposed to say?
I hesitated, then answered honestly.
“No. You just look like a crazy bastard to me.”
For a moment, the Blood Lord stared blankly at me.
Then a smile spread across his lips.
“You’re bold for a young one.”
“You’re still a young brat yourself, and you already seem a little unhinged.”
“Thank you for thinking I’m young. I’m older than I look.”
“Not that old.”
“Don’t push it. I’ve lived at least twice as long as you have.”
I looked him up and down in disbelief.
He stood at roughly my eye level, his body perfectly proportioned.
His face made him look like some inexperienced young man in his early to mid-twenties at most.
This went far beyond merely looking young.
But if there was anywhere something like this could happen, it was the Murim.
“What? Surprised I’m so much older than you expected?”
I shook my head.
“No. If that’s true, I was thinking you’re a bastard who really doesn’t act his age.”
“Wahahaha!”
The Blood Lord burst into cheerful laughter.
His behavior, his tone—everything about him was light, almost frivolous.
That only made him feel more dangerous.
Even now, bent over with laughter and his shoulders shaking, he showed not the slightest opening.
Jeok Cheongang, who had been glaring at him as his shoulders shook, suddenly spoke.
“You will regret this.”
“Regret?”
The Blood Lord stopped laughing and frowned.
“Why would I regret it?”
“If you wanted to finish this cleanly, you should not have killed the Yin Ghost.”
“He was a rusty sword. His usefulness had run out, so disposing of him was only natural.”
“A Supreme Peak master is a rusty sword... Then what does that make this old man?”
The Blood Lord stroked his chin.
“You are worth rating highly, Fire King. If the Great Faction War had continued for one more year, you probably would have become one of the Four Saints instead of merely one of the Three Saints.”
“Then it seems my edge has not gone dull yet.”
“You are good enough to be called a fine sword.”
“What would happen if that fine sword were driven into your heart?”
“Who knows... I’m sturdier than I look. I doubt that would draw even a single drop of blood.”
“When Hong Dao died, this old man swore to heaven.”
The Blood Lord smiled faintly as Jeok Cheongang’s gaze grew dark and still.
“Even if his killer were a demon god rather than a human, I would see this vengeance through to the end.”
“That’s touching and all, but...”
The Blood Lord’s smile vanished as he caressed the hilt of the sword at his waist.
“I have a feeling the Fire Gate Clan’s lineage will end today.”
Without taking his eyes off the Blood Lord, Jeok Cheongang asked me:
“What do you think of that?”
“I think his mouth needs a circumcision. It’s been spewing nothing but dickhead bullshit for a while now.”
The smile disappeared from the Blood Lord’s face.
“...You really are an interesting bastard.”
Step.
The Blood Lord took one step toward Jeok Cheongang and me, then suddenly spoke.
“But how long does that little rat over there plan to keep hiding?”
Rustle.
A suspicious-looking figure emerged from the distant grass and scratched the back of his head.
“Benefactor. I’m sorry. I’ve never been this frightened in my life...”
I had never been so happy to see Cheongpung.

If Flame Tiger’s martial arts had truly been equal to Han Su’s, then Jeok Cheongang’s overwhelming victory had been inevitable.
But Han Su looked perfectly at ease.
He knew there was a tiger behind him.
“Blood Lord, I will need you to step in.”
“Of course.
It’s about time we got started.”
The Blood Lord tucked the Green Jade Buddha Staff into his robes as carefully as if it were a priceless treasure.
Then he moved.
No—he vanished.
And in the next instant—
Slash!
Thump!
A round object flew through the air with a sickening sound and rolled to a stop at my feet.
White hair.
Dignified features.
A faint smile still lingering around the mouth.
Jeok Cheongang’s eyes widened along with mine.
Han Su, the infamous great demonic fiend and Supreme Peak master known as the Yin Ghost, had been beheaded in a single strike.
By the hand of the ally he had trusted without question.
Unlike us, the Blood Lord—the one responsible for everything—remained perfectly calm.
“Fucking old man.
This is why you should never take in rootless trash.”
Clicking his tongue, he casually nudged Han Su’s headless body.
Splash!
The corpse toppled like a dead tree, spraying a fountain of blood across the ground.
“If you’re a sword, act like a sword.
Go wherever the person holding you swings you.
How dare you...”
Thud!
Thud!
Crack!
His kicks, loaded with internal energy, tore through flesh and shattered bone.
After repeatedly stamping and grinding Han Su’s lifeless corpse beneath his feet, the Blood Lord swept his fallen hair back.
“There are always people who don’t know their place.
They don’t know how strong they are or how far they should stick their necks out.
Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, don’t you agree?”
What was I supposed to say?
I hesitated, then answered honestly.
“No.
You just look like a crazy bastard to me.”
For a moment, the Blood Lord stared blankly at me.
Then a smile spread across his lips.
“You’re bold for a young one.”
“You’re still a young brat yourself, and you already seem a little unhinged.”
“Thank you for thinking I’m young.
I’m older than I look.”
“Not that old.”
“Don’t push it.
I’ve lived at least twice as long as you have.”
I looked him up and down in disbelief.
He stood at roughly my eye level, his body perfectly proportioned.
His face made him look like some inexperienced young man in his early to mid-twenties at most.
This went far beyond merely looking young.
But if there was anywhere something like this could happen, it was the Murim.
“What?
Surprised I’m so much older than you expected?”
I shook my head.
“No.
If that’s true, I was thinking you’re a bastard who really doesn’t act his age.”
“Wahahaha!”
The Blood Lord burst into cheerful laughter.
His behavior, his tone—everything about him was light, almost frivolous.
That only made him feel more dangerous.
Even now, bent over with laughter and his shoulders shaking, he showed not the slightest opening.
Jeok Cheongang, who had been glaring at him as his shoulders shook, suddenly spoke.
“You will regret this.”
“Regret?”
The Blood Lord stopped laughing and frowned.
“Why would I regret it?”
“If you wanted to finish this cleanly, you should not have killed the Yin Ghost.”
“He was a rusty sword.
His usefulness had run out, so disposing of him was only natural.”
“A Supreme Peak master is a rusty sword...
Then what does that make this old man?”
The Blood Lord stroked his chin.
“You are worth rating highly, Fire King.
If the Great Faction War had continued for one more year, you probably would have become one of the Four Saints instead of merely one of the Three Saints.”
“Then it seems my edge has not gone dull yet.”
“You are good enough to be called a fine sword.”
“What would happen if that fine sword were driven into your heart?”
“Who knows...
I’m sturdier than I look.
I doubt that would draw even a single drop of blood.”
“When Hong Dao died, this old man swore to heaven.”
The Blood Lord smiled faintly as Jeok Cheongang’s gaze grew dark and still.
“Even if his killer were a demon god rather than a human, I would see this vengeance through to the end.”
“That’s touching and all, but...”
The Blood Lord’s smile vanished as he caressed the hilt of the sword at his waist.
“I have a feeling the Fire Gate Clan’s lineage will end today.”
Without taking his eyes off the Blood Lord, Jeok Cheongang asked me:
“What do you think of that?”
“I think his mouth needs a circumcision.
It’s been spewing nothing but dickhead bullshit for a while now.”
The smile disappeared from the Blood Lord’s face.
“...You really are an interesting bastard.”
Step.
The Blood Lord took one step toward Jeok Cheongang and me, then suddenly spoke.
“But how long does that little rat over there plan to keep hiding?”
Rustle.
A suspicious-looking figure emerged from the distant grass and scratched the back of his head.
“Benefactor.
I’m sorry.
I’ve never been this frightened in my life...”
I had never been so happy to see Cheongpung.

chapters.title: Chapter 264
paragraphs: I never expected to be this happy to see that dumpling ghost. At a time when even a cat’s paw would have been welcome, Cheongpung’s arrival could be an enormous help.
A delighted shout burst from my lips before I knew it.
“Cheongpung!”
“Yes, Benefactor.”
As Cheongpung answered hesitantly, the Blood Lord recognized him.
“Oh-ho. I was wondering what kind of rat it was, but aren’t you Huashan’s Invincible Divine Sword?”
I had hoped otherwise, but it was just as I feared. That was all the Blood Lord knew about Cheongpung’s identity.
The duel had revealed that Cheongpung was a disciple of Huashan, but there was no way he knew that Sword Saint Mae Jonghak had raised his youngest disciple like his own flesh and blood.
This was the perfect chance to lull him into carelessness...
“Or should I call you the Sword Saint’s Disciple? Perhaps his grandson?”
Son of a bitch. There was nothing he didn’t know.
Then again, Dark Heaven had recruited the Head Elder and planted him there decades ago. The Blood Lord was clearly one of Dark Heaven’s highest-ranking members.
It would be stranger if he didn’t know.
The Blood Lord gave a quiet laugh at my disappointed expression.
“No need to look so disappointed. That friend of yours joining you won’t change anything.”
Would you look at this bastard...
Although Cheongpung and I had yet to advance beyond the upper reaches of Peak, neither of us could be compared to an ordinary Peak master.
I had overwhelming stats and extensive combat experience. Cheongpung had innate martial talent and a genius for combining dozens of martial arts as the situation demanded.
And on top of that, we had the Fire King Jeok Cheongang—the greatest of the Ten Kings.
I thought we had more than a fair chance.
“You’re underestimating us.”
“I’m only stating a fact.”
“What?”
“If you wanted to kill me, you should have brought the Sword Saint instead of his Disciple.”
“...You little bastard.”
“There’s only one thing left, then.”
The Blood Lord spoke with casual confidence and beckoned to us with one finger.
“Prove it with your martial arts.”
That was the only thing he had said so far that was actually right.
He was correct. A martial artist had to prove himself through martial arts.
Victory would prove our strength. Defeat would prove our weakness.
“When you meet Yama, tell him the Fire King sent you.”
Whoosh!
Along with his dry, ashy voice, Jeok Cheongang’s figure shot forward. At the same time, a familiar alert pierced my ears.
Ding.
System A sudden Quest, Life-or-Death Crisis, has been generated! - You cannot refuse the Quest. The Quest will be forcibly accepted!
Damn it. What a perfect title for the Quest.
I kicked off the ground and charged. Instead of cursing, I remembered to shout one name.
“Cheongpung! Now!”
Cheongpung flinched, bit his lip, and lunged forward. The blue-steel sword in his hand danced gracefully, tracing plum blossoms through the air.
Fwoosh! Shhhhk!
On a secluded mountain path, Scorching Yang Qi heated the cool breeze as spear and sword tore through the burning air.
Watching us charge from the front and rear, the Blood Lord parted his lips.
“Well, then... Let’s see what you can do.”
Crack-crack-crack!
Jeok Cheongang flicked his hand. Palm force brimming with Scorching Yang Qi burst from his wrinkled palm.
The Flame Divine Palm, already at Great Completion.
Just as the Extreme Yang palm technique—said to burn even the soul—was about to engulf the Blood Lord—
Whoosh!
A single gust of wind blew past.
A saber had appeared in the Blood Lord’s hand. Its saber force blazed an ominous red, cleaving the Flame Divine Palm’s force in two.
Whoom! Boom!
The massive trees lining both sides of the path exploded.
Flames surged into the air amid a thunderous roar, while dirt, roots, and splinters of wood poured down like a sudden rainstorm.
Two streaks of light pierced through the debris.
Whoosh! Shhhk!
A spear and sword shot toward him from the front and rear.
The Blood Lord curled his lips and released his saber. At the same time, his newly freed fists struck the empty air.
Boom!
Compressed air exploded outward, unleashing a violent gale. The viciously thrusting spearhead and the plum blossoms blooming from the sword’s tip were both swept away by the wind pressure.
Jin Taekyung and Cheongpung’s eyes widened as their bodies were pushed back against their will.
“...Fuck. He’s insanely strong.”
“H-How can this be?”
Crack.
The Blood Lord rolled his neck and drew his saber back into his hand. He had fended off both men while controlling it with Seizing an Object Through Empty Space.
“Is that all you’ve got?”
Jeok Cheongang’s eyelids trembled.
Who would have thought that a single form of the Flame Divine Palm at Great Completion could be defeated so easily? The Blood Lord had not dodged or deflected it.
He had cut it apart.
Jeok Cheongang’s heart sank as he realized the Blood Lord was an even greater master than he had imagined.
When he said we should have brought the Sword Saint if we wanted to kill him... That was no empty boast.
His opponent was a master who could easily stand beside the Three Saints.
No—perhaps he was even stronger.
Neither his internal energy nor his enlightenment in martial arts fell short of Jeok Cheongang’s own.
And on top of that, the Blood Lord possessed the youthful vigor and strong body needed to unleash both without the slightest loss.
Today, Jeok Cheongang’s wrinkled hands seemed smaller and more wretched than ever.
If only I were thirty years younger... No, even twenty...
When his body had been whole, he had lacked enlightenment. By the time he attained that enlightenment, his body had grown too old.
Water inevitably leaked from an old jar riddled with holes.
That was Jeok Cheongang now.
Perhaps this place will become my grave.
The Blood Lord did not miss the shadow that settled over Jeok Cheongang’s eyes.
His lips twisted into a sneer, and he snickered.
“Old man. Starting to get the picture? Do you understand the situation now?”
Jeok Cheongang calmly shook his head.
He knew that Jin Taekyung and Cheongpung were watching his mouth. He could not destroy their morale with careless words.
“You talk too much. We have only just begun.”
“Maybe you three have. I haven’t even started.”
“What?”
“I heard the orthodox factions like to prattle on about courtesy and have masters yield three forms to their inferiors. I thought I’d give it a try.”
The Blood Lord pointed a long finger at each of them in turn.
All three had unleashed one form apiece, making three in total. Just as he had said, he had yielded three forms without taking a single step.
“Now it’s my turn to go first. Struggle all you like.”
A crimson gleam flared in the Blood Lord’s eyes. His sclera flooded bloodred as a vast and hideously ominous qi erupted from his body.
And then—
Rumble, rumble, rumble!
Mount Song trembled.
Shhhhk! Boom!
Streaks of light filled the air in every direction. Blinding flashes erupted amid the ceaseless thunder of explosions.
Dominating them all was a single saber scattering black-red qi.
Boom!
Powerful saber force swept through the air, leaving a pale trail of light in its wake.
Its destructive arc erased everything in its path, knocking aside every attack sent toward the Blood Lord.
Mine included, of course.
Boom!
The spearhead of White Flame rang sharply. The shaft I gripped with all my strength vibrated violently in my palm.
Even though I had poured an enormous amount of internal energy into it, the force was unbelievable.
It was hard to believe such power belonged to a human being.
What a monster.
Gritting my teeth, I twisted around.
Whoosh!
The black-red blade passed within a hair’s breadth of my head, slicing off several strands of hair.
The wind pressure alone split my skin, sending blood trickling down my face.
I caught the drops running along the bridge of my nose in my mouth and swung my spear.
“Hah!”
Whirrrrrl!
The spearhead spun fiercely toward the Blood Lord’s chest.
Perhaps because I had poured in all the Points I had received as the reward for winning the Star-Array Grand Banquet, my movement and strength had risen another level.
But—
Crack!
The Blood Lord’s free hand snatched the spearhead from the air.
It was a bare hand, but not truly bare. Immense black-red internal energy blazed around it.
“That won’t be enough.”
With those quiet words, he pulled the spearhead toward him with tremendous force.
Then his eyebrows shot upward.
The spearhead that had been trapped in his grip a moment ago was gone.
As if it had never existed.
“You—!”
Before the startled word had fully left his mouth, I had already plunged deep inside his reach.
Inventory Open. Summon.
In the blink of an eye, White Flame—burning hot with Scorching Yang Qi—was back in my hand.
The Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, harder and sharper than anything in the world, tore through his Body-Protecting Qi and pierced the flesh beneath it.
Thud! Boom!
The Blood Lord snapped his sleeve, and a powerful burst of force slammed into my abdomen.
After being driven back ten steps in a row, I saw the Blood Lord’s wide-eyed face—and the fountain of blood erupting from his chest.
I did it.
Only I could have pulled off that attack—and it had worked precisely because I was merely me.
It landed because I had used the System, something no one could possibly have anticipated, and because the Blood Lord had not considered an attack from someone like me worth guarding against.
Now’s my chance.
It was an opportunity that might never come again. Our last lifeline, one I could not afford to let slip away.
I swallowed the blood surging up my throat and shouted.
“Old Master!”
My voice rang across the devastated mountain path. It pierced the air, rode the wind, and reached one man’s ears.
A heated voice slipped between his lips.
“Well done.”
The old man hurtling toward the Blood Lord had transformed into the Fire King.
Fwoooosh!
A colossal blaze erupted from his small body. It burned the air and crushed the wind.
If the Blood Lord’s qi was something so ominous that merely looking at it made one uneasy, then Jeok Cheongang’s was heat itself—as though it could burn the world.
“Son of a bitch...”
The Blood Lord muttered the curse like a groan.
But it was already too late. He might not have known, but I did. I knew what Jeok Cheongang was doing and how much power that martial art possessed.
He had used it only once before and become a legend by killing a thousand members of the Demonic Cult.
Dance of the Fire God and Demon.
At that moment, Jeok Cheongang vanished.
He approached the Blood Lord on light footsteps, as though dancing, while his hands and feet blurred like mist.
Red and blue fire qi filled heaven and earth. It was a beautiful flash of light—and terrifyingly destructive.
“Fire King!”
Whoosh!
At the Blood Lord’s rough shout, black-red saber force mingled with the fire qi. A thunderous roar rang out, as though cliffs were collapsing and the sky itself were being torn apart.
This is...
I could hardly follow the exchange with my eyes. It lasted less than the smallest fraction of a moment, but I still understood.
Hundreds of tremendously powerful attacks had passed between them in that brief instant.
And I knew who had won.
Boom!
A wave of heat swallowed the black-red saber force. Something flashing shot into the sky and plunged deep into the churned-up earth.
A saber.
Its owner was receiving the final blow.
“This old man told you, didn’t he? Even if you were a demon god instead of a human, I would kill you.”
With those quiet words, Jeok Cheongang drove a palm into the Blood Lord’s chest.
Sizzle.
His flesh burned, and his breastbone collapsed. After vomiting a mouthful of blood, the Blood Lord fell to his knees with a hazy look in his eyes.
And... that was all.
Jeok Cheongang gazed down at the Blood Lord’s motionless head. Then his body staggered.
“Old Master!”
“Grandpa Jeok!”
Cheongpung and I rushed over, supported Jeok Cheongang, and carried him to a nearby patch of grass that was still more or less intact.
The Dance of the Fire God and Demon.
No flame burned forever. When the dance ended, the fire went out and the heat faded.
That was why Jeok Cheongang, despite all the long years he had lived, had only ever been able to use it once.
“Well? Wasn’t it just as this old man told you?”
“What are you talking about?”
“The Dance of the Fire God and Demon. Wasn’t it incredible?”
At Jeok Cheongang’s faint smile, I let out a sigh of relief.
Then I smiled with him.
“It was incredible.”
I meant it. Everything about it had been incredible.
Except for the voice that came from behind us the next moment.
“The Dance of the Fire God and Demon... That’s one hell of a name.”
We slowly turned our heads.
The Blood Lord rose to his feet before our eyes, perfectly unscathed.
