Jeok Cheongang gazed down at the Blood Lord’s motionless head.
Then his body staggered.
“Old Master!”
“Grandpa Jeok!”
Cheongpung and I rushed over, supported Jeok Cheongang, and carried him to a nearby patch of grass that was still more or less intact.
The Dance of the Fire God and Demon.
No flame burned forever.
When the dance ended, the fire went out and the heat faded.
That was why Jeok Cheongang, despite all the long years he had lived, had only ever been able to use it once.
“Well?
Wasn’t it just as this old man told you?”
“What are you talking about?”
“The Dance of the Fire God and Demon.
Wasn’t it incredible?”
At Jeok Cheongang’s faint smile, I let out a sigh of relief.
Then I smiled with him.
“It was incredible.”
I meant it.
Everything about it had been incredible.
Except for the voice that came from behind us the next moment.
“The Dance of the Fire God and Demon...
That’s one hell of a name.”
We slowly turned our heads.
The Blood Lord rose to his feet before our eyes, perfectly unscathed.

chapters.title: Chapter 265
paragraphs: I was certain—absolutely certain—that he was dead.
Even if he had not breathed his last, I was convinced he could no longer be called a living human being.
But...
Slither. Crack-crack!
I could hardly believe what I was seeing.
Pale new flesh spread over skin that had been burned black and looked ready to crumble at the slightest touch. Protruding bones slid back into place and disappeared beneath it.
What the hell is this?
What was I supposed to call it? Recovery?
No. This was regeneration.
Regeneration beyond anything human—like something out of a monster.
Cheongpung let out a strangled gasp at the horrifying sight.
Meanwhile, the last of the changes came to an end. The face that had been stripped down to the muscle rapidly regenerated.
Crack.
The Blood Lord rubbed his neck and flashed us a crooked grin.
“You should have crushed my head. Made sure of it.”
Jeok Cheongang had gone rigid as a statue. He barely managed to part his lips.
“How?”
The Blood Lord answered casually.
“For now, let’s just call it demonic martial arts. It’s all the same to orthodox bastards like you anyway, isn’t it?”
“You... Cough!”
“Old Master!”
I was startled and hurried to support Jeok Cheongang. His face had gone pale, and a stream of red blood ran down his chin.
This is bad.
Jeok Cheongang had already exhausted all his strength.
Even the Dance of the Fire God and Demon, unleashed by wringing out the last of his power, had come to nothing. The man in my arms was no longer the Fire King, merely an exhausted old man.
“R-Run...”
Jeok Cheongang could not finish. His head drooped.
I hurriedly checked his pulse. It was faint, but still beating.
He’s all right for now.
But it was far too soon to breathe a sigh of relief.
“From the look of things, even the great Fire King has reached his limit.”
The Blood Lord stepped forward with a delighted expression.
“This was more entertaining than I expected. No, to be honest, it was even frightening. I never imagined things would reach this point.”
“You smell like shit. Shut your mouth.”
I rose to my feet and tightened my grip on White Flame, which I had set down for a moment.
Jeok Cheongang was already out of the fight. If he used any more strength here... something truly irreversible would happen.
“You intend to stop me alone? How admirable.”
“Did you trade one of your eyes for taffy or something? There are two of us.”
The Blood Lord shook his head.
“No. There’s only one. I don’t count terrified little rats as people.”
Terrified little rat?
I turned my head.
Cheongpung stood frozen beside me.
His pupils shook uncontrollably, and the hand clutching his sword hilt trembled violently.
Fear.
That was the only emotion I could sense from him.
“To send a wet-behind-the-ears brat out into the martial world... The Sword Saint spoiled his Disciple far too much.”
Step.
The Blood Lord was still more than fifty paces away. But when he took a single step, Cheongpung flinched as though burned and retreated.
This is...
My heart sank.
I knew exactly what it meant.
The path I had experienced myself, the path countless others had walked—Cheongpung was only now beginning to walk it.
Of all times, why now?
It was a growing pain every martial artist and Hunter had to experience, but for the genius standing before me, the timing was unbearably late.
The Blood Lord read the realization on my face and grinned.
“You know it too, don’t you? He’s already finished. That helplessness he’s feeling for the first time. The fear of death. Once those things take hold of you, they’re not easy to escape.”
“...Jongni Chu.”
There was no doubt.
This was because of Cheongpung’s duel with Jongni Chu.
Jongni Chu was the one who had planted the seed of fear in Cheongpung. And that seed had sprouted after meeting another powerful figure—the Blood Lord.
“Exactly. I have no idea where that fellow came from, but he did quite a job. He drew the attention of the orthodox factions and even neatly disposed of the Sword Saint’s Disciple. Ha-ha!”
My mouth felt gritty, as though I were chewing sand.
Cheongpung was still paralyzed with fear, while the Blood Lord leisurely closed the distance between us.
Damn it.
Fortunately, I still had one final move left.
The problem was that it really was my final move.
Even if it succeeded, there was no guarantee what the outcome would be. If it failed, all that awaited us was death.
But I have no choice.
I slowly drew up what little internal energy remained—not even ten percent.
One Annihilation.
My only hope was to pour everything I had into a single strike and crush his head.
I folded up the question Can I do it? and burned it away.
I have to. Somehow.
I had to choose certainty over doubt, and desperate resolve over certainty. Only by staking my life on every tiny movement would I have even the faintest chance.
“Young sir.”
Click. Clack.
I knew what it was without looking.
Cheongpung’s teeth were chattering.
I shouted with all my might.
“Cheongpung!”
He gasped and jerked his head up.
“I won’t say this twice. Listen carefully and decide for yourself.”
“Y-Yes?”
“You have two choices. First, carry Old Master and run as far away as you can.”
“Benefactor!”
“I’m not finished. Second, stop shaking like a fucking coward and fight that bastard beside me with everything you have.”
His trembling breath betrayed the turmoil inside him.
Then the feet that had retreated several steps began moving forward again.
Step.
We stood side by side in front of the unconscious Jeok Cheongang.
“Your answer. I haven’t heard it yet.”
“This is my answer.”
“Be honest.”
“I’m scared, Benefactor.”
“Fuck. You’re brutally honest.”
“But I really am scared. I’ve never felt anything like this in my life.”
I kept my eyes fixed on the approaching Blood Lord.
“If you’re that scared, why not run?”
“I don’t know. I just feel like if I run away now... I’ll regret it for the rest of my life.”
That regret.
I knew what he meant.
I glanced at Cheongpung. He was still terrified, and his hands still trembled, but the step he had taken forward was firm. His feet were rooted in place, refusing to retreat.
Yes.
For now, that was enough.
I had just given a small nod when—
“Regret? Run away?”
Twenty paces away, the Blood Lord stopped and laughed aloud as though he had heard the greatest joke in the world.
“What audacious nonsense from a pair of fledglings. I’m the one who decides whether you run. That is the right of the strong and the inevitable fate of the weak.”
“Well, you’re partly right...”
I raised my spear and aimed it at him. White Flame’s transparent spearhead shattered the sunlight into countless fragments.
“But why does every word out of your mouth sound so fucking disgusting?”
“The truth is uncomfortable. Especially for the weak.”
“This won’t do. Open wide, patient. It’s time for your circumcision. It might hurt a little—I’ll be using a spear without anesthesia.”
“Puhahaha!”
“You’re laughing? You think it can’t happen to you? That’s how life gets you. I should’ve known something was up when Mom said we were going out for something delicious.”
The Blood Lord’s smile deepened.
“Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi. The more I see of you, the more entertaining you become. Those bizarre martial arts of yours that I can’t identify, that spirit... I like you.”
“And if you like me?”
“Come under me. I might even spare the Fire King.”
“Why don’t you eat a dick, sir? After today, I’ll never have to deal with a bastard like you again.”
“Someone once said that the first meeting is coincidence, the second is a connection, and the third is destiny.”
“Listen to this son of a bitch, writing a goddamn romance novel.”
The Blood Lord shrugged.
“Perhaps. It isn’t a relationship between a man and a woman, but if we’ve crossed paths twice in this vast world, wouldn’t you call that a connection?”
“Twice?”
For a moment, I didn’t understand.
What the hell was this bastard talking about?
“Did you see me at the Star-Array Grand Banquet or something?”
“Of course I saw you.”
His playful voice continued.
“At Eight Spring Gorge.”
“...What?”

“It was quite a spectacle. Corpses piled into mountains, blood flowing like a river... Watching you take Jin Baekyang’s life was especially memorable. Wasn’t that when they started calling you the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi?”
“What are you talking about...”

“Jin Baekyang, the Blade of Flowers. What a useless bastard. At first, he acted as though he would tear out his own liver and gallbladder for us, but as he grew older, he must have developed some pathetic doubts. Ruined the entire job. What incompetent fool recruited such a half-assed bastard? Tsk, tsk.”
I stared blankly at the Blood Lord as he clicked his tongue.
Every word coming from his mouth sounded hollow and alien.

“Oh, what about that Third Rate sect called the Mount Heng Sword Sect? Is it still around? I did hear from one of my subordinates that one of its Sect Leader’s sons had been killed. I lost interest after Eight Spring Gorge, so I haven’t paid much attention.”
A shudder shot along my spine like a bolt of lightning.
“Then... it was you?”
“I told you.”
The Blood Lord’s eyes curved into crescents. His next words came in a gentle voice that did not suit him at all.
“The first meeting is coincidence, the second is a connection, and the third is destiny. What do you think? Wouldn’t you say you and I have a connection?”
My breath caught.
The bastard standing before me was the one who had started that war.
The Blood Lord saw my expression and roared with laughter.

“Why the long face? Things worked out smoothly thanks to me. The Jin Family of Taiyuan is the foremost family in Shanxi. You became the Fire King’s Disciple and even seized victory at the Star-Array Grand Banquet. Shouldn’t you thank me?”
I did not answer.
One thought filled my mind.
How many people died again?
I didn’t know.
A thousand? Two thousand?
Countless people had died in a Great War that had been meaningless from beginning to end. There had been no true victor or loser.
Martial artists who had merely swung their weapons when ordered died. So did innocent commoners who had nothing to do with the conflict. Even more children were left orphaned by the war.
When the Murim of Shanxi began to reel, the mounted bandits of Gaoyuan ran rampant.
The war had barely ended before the same history repeated itself.
And he expects me to thank him.
I licked my dry, cracked lips. My grip around the spear shaft tightened on its own.
An unknown strength filled my exhausted body.
A stat that did not appear in the System window.
Anger.
“Hey.”
“Hmm?”
“That bullshit about once being coincidence and twice being a connection.”
I took a deep breath. Without it, I felt as though fireballs might pour from my mouth.
“You and I are different. Let’s skip all that and go straight to destiny.”
“Destiny?”
“Yeah. The destiny where one of us dies.”
Before I had even finished speaking, I kicked off the ground.
The distance vanished in an instant, and his smiling face appeared before me.
One Annihilation.
Gooooong!
The spearhead cleaved through space.
Crack!
“Gaaaaah!”
The young man’s arm broke, and white bone burst through his skin.
He screamed at the agony, worse than anything he had ever experienced. Spurting blood splattered across his own face.
The foul reek made bile rise in his throat. The instant he bent over to retch, a thick leg slammed into his abdomen.
Thud. Boom!
“You pathetic fool. I pity the Sword Saint for having a half-wit like you as his Disciple.”
The young man—Cheongpung—went flying. He struggled to turn himself over.
It hurt.
He wanted to collapse.
His entire body screamed in pain, and a deep despair weighed upon him.
My body... My body won’t listen to me.
In the end, he could not rise. He collapsed, and the vast sky filled his vision.
The sky above Lotus Peak on Huashan had always been clear and beautiful. By day, the clouds gleamed; by night, the stars glittered. Roe deer and rabbits bounded energetically across the mountain.
But...
Why is the sky here so red?
This sky was different.
Red and bleak.
Cheongpung blinked and realized that the tiny blood vessels in his eyes had burst. It was the first time that had ever happened, but he was not surprised.
I’ve already broken bones for the first time, and I’ve lost so much blood.
Thinking about his condition made his breathing quicken without him realizing it.
As he lay sprawled on the ground, gasping for breath, a chilling sound pierced his ears.
Whoosh—crack!
“Urk!”
“You bastard!”
Cheongpung turned toward the sound. Two figures locked in a bloody struggle came into view through his tilted vision.
No.
It could no longer be called a fight.
Thud! Thud! Thud!
“Hngh!”
“You’re still not dead? Even after this? Even after this?”
Bam-bam-bam! Crash!
His nose collapsed. His ankle broke, and his shoulder was wrenched out of place.
Once. Three times. Ten times...
Yet no matter how badly he was injured or how many times he fell, he rose again.
He would do the same a hundred times.
That was the kind of man Cheongpung knew him to be.
Benefactor.
But reality was merciless.
The outcome had been decided almost immediately.

Cheongpung did not know what martial art Jin Taekyung had used, but the power of that one strike had been unparalleled. It had shattered the Blood Lord’s Red Blade, infused with Sword Force, and wounded him.
Yet in less than a moment, the Blood Lord regenerated and drove them both into a corner.
“You lunatic... I’ve never seen a more tenacious bastard.”
Everything was about to end.
The Blood Lord shook his head, looking thoroughly appalled. His entire body was drenched in blood as well.

Unlike before, however, his wounds no longer healed. The easy smile he had worn throughout the battle was gone, and he breathed raggedly as he pulled Jin Taekyung’s spear from where it stood embedded deep in the ground.
“Huff, huff... Fine. I’ll kill you.”
Kill.
The moment Cheongpung heard that word, his palm pressed against the ground.
The pain from his broken arm and leg faded, along with the smell of blood.
A strange, floating sensation spread through his entire body.
What is this?
He did not know.
At the end of his staggering steps stood the Blood Lord.
“Huh. What’s this now? Do you want to die too?”
His hands trembled when he met the Blood Lord’s ferocious gaze.
But then he saw Jin Taekyung lying behind him, and the trembling slowly subsided.
“Benefactor... Benefactor.”
“What a pair of lunatics...”
The Blood Lord let out an incredulous, hollow laugh and swung the spear.
Slash!
Cheongpung staggered aside, twisting his body. Blood sprayed from his chest.
It hurts.
But he did not stop.
He did not fall.
The sword hilt had slipped from his powerless grip long ago.
“What the...”
The Blood Lord stared at him in disbelief, then seized Cheongpung’s throat with one powerful hand.
“Ghk!”
“What the hell is wrong with you people? Why are you both so desperate to die first?”
His voice held genuine curiosity.
As his consciousness faded, Cheongpung opened his mouth. A strained voice escaped him.
“Because... I think I’d regret it for the rest of my life if I backed down.”
“That’s your reason? A cowardly bastard like you refuses to retreat for such a pathetic reason?”
The Blood Lord’s killing intent grew even more savage.
But something was strange.
Cheongpung was not frightened at all.
It felt as though he had returned to his days on Lotus Peak. Before he knew it, the corners of his mouth had lifted.
“Hehe. Yes.”
The Blood Lord’s face twisted viciously.
Cheongpung had smiled.
He had smiled while standing before him.
It was impossible.
It was something that should never have happened.
“I heard your last words loud and clear.”
The Blood Lord was about to drive the spearhead into Cheongpung’s chest when—
“You’ve broken free of your shell.”
A clear voice rang out.
A voice exactly like the blue sky over Huashan that Cheongpung remembered.
A voice he felt he finally recognized.

But...
Why is the sky here so red?
This sky was different.
Red and bleak.
Cheongpung blinked and realized that the tiny blood vessels in his eyes had burst.
It was the first time that had ever happened, but he was not surprised.
I’ve already broken bones for the first time, and I’ve lost so much blood.
Thinking about his condition made his breathing quicken without him realizing it.
As he lay sprawled on the ground, gasping for breath, a chilling sound pierced his ears.
Whoosh—crack!
“Urk!”
“You bastard!”
Cheongpung turned toward the sound.
Two figures locked in a bloody struggle came into view through his tilted vision.
No.
It could no longer be called a fight.
Thud!
Thud!
Thud!
“Hngh!”
“You’re still not dead?
Even after this?
Even after this?”
Bam-bam-bam!
Crash!
His nose collapsed.
His ankle broke, and his shoulder was wrenched out of place.
Once.
Three times.
Ten times...
Yet no matter how badly he was injured or how many times he fell, he rose again.
He would do the same a hundred times.
That was the kind of man Cheongpung knew him to be.
Benefactor.
But reality was merciless.
The outcome had been decided almost immediately.
Cheongpung did not know what martial art Jin Taekyung had used, but the power of that one strike had been unparalleled.
It had shattered the Blood Lord’s Red Blade, infused with Sword Force, and wounded him.
Yet in less than a moment, the Blood Lord regenerated and drove them both into a corner.
“You lunatic...
I’ve never seen a more tenacious bastard.”
Everything was about to end.
The Blood Lord shook his head, looking thoroughly appalled.
His entire body was drenched in blood as well.
Unlike before, however, his wounds no longer healed.
The easy smile he had worn throughout the battle was gone, and he breathed raggedly as he pulled Jin Taekyung’s spear from where it stood embedded deep in the ground.
“Huff, huff...
Fine.
I’ll kill you.”
Kill.
The moment Cheongpung heard that word, his palm pressed against the ground.
The pain from his broken arm and leg faded, along with the smell of blood.
A strange, floating sensation spread through his entire body.
What is this?
He did not know.
At the end of his staggering steps stood the Blood Lord.
“Huh.
What’s this now?
Do you want to die too?”
His hands trembled when he met the Blood Lord’s ferocious gaze.
But then he saw Jin Taekyung lying behind him, and the trembling slowly subsided.
“Benefactor...
Benefactor.”
“What a pair of lunatics...”
The Blood Lord let out an incredulous, hollow laugh and swung the spear.
Slash!
Cheongpung staggered aside, twisting his body.
Blood sprayed from his chest.
It hurts.
But he did not stop.
He did not fall.
The sword hilt had slipped from his powerless grip long ago.
“What the...”
The Blood Lord stared at him in disbelief, then seized Cheongpung’s throat with one powerful hand.
“Ghk!”
“What the hell is wrong with you people?
Why are you both so desperate to die first?”
His voice held genuine curiosity.
As his consciousness faded, Cheongpung opened his mouth.
A strained voice escaped him.
“Because...
I think I’d regret it for the rest of my life if I backed down.”
“That’s your reason?
A cowardly bastard like you refuses to retreat for such a pathetic reason?”
The Blood Lord’s killing intent grew even more savage.
But something was strange.
Cheongpung was not frightened at all.
It felt as though he had returned to his days on Lotus Peak.
Before he knew it, the corners of his mouth had lifted.
“Hehe.
Yes.”
The Blood Lord’s face twisted viciously.
Cheongpung had smiled.
He had smiled while standing before him.
It was impossible.
It was something that should never have happened.
“I heard your last words loud and clear.”
The Blood Lord was about to drive the spearhead into Cheongpung’s chest when—
“You’ve broken free of your shell.”
A clear voice rang out.
A voice exactly like the blue sky over Huashan that Cheongpung remembered.
A voice he felt he finally recognized.

chapters.title: Chapter 266
paragraphs: “You’ve broken free of your shell.”
A clear voice rang out.
Cheongpung thought of the sunlight and blue sky over Lotus Peak. The Blood Lord felt as though his heart had dropped into his stomach.
He had failed to sense someone barely two hundred feet away. He, of all people.
His eyes narrowed at the man walking up the mountain path.
That bastard...
He had a slender build and an approachable face. He looked to be in his mid-twenties at most.
A sword had been shoved carelessly through his belt without a scabbard, its blade covered entirely in reddish rust.
A dry voice slipped from the Blood Lord’s lips.
“The Always-Victorious Sword?”
The young man, Jongni Chu, smiled faintly.
“I was always worried.”
“What?”
“About what kind of storms a fearless, innocent child would face once he entered the martial world.”
“What the hell are you talking about...?”
The Blood Lord was about to continue when realization struck him.
From the very beginning, Jongni Chu’s every word and action had been directed at one person alone.
“But it’s all right now. You overcame it so well.”
His gaze and voice were warm.
At last, a faint smile touched Cheongpung’s lips as he struggled for breath.
Watching that, the Blood Lord let out a hollow laugh.
“Would you look at these two...”
They were treating him as though he did not even exist.
Him—the man who inspired fear and awe in countless people, even within Dark Heaven.
The blatant disregard of these young pups made his grip tighten.
Crack.
“Ghk!”
With the sound of bones twisting out of place, a gush of blood burst from between Cheongpung’s lips.
As Cheongpung groaned in pain and lost consciousness, Jongni Chu’s quiet voice reached the Blood Lord’s ears.
“That’s enough.”
Seeing the smile vanish from Jongni Chu’s face made the Blood Lord feel considerably better.
He grinned and opened his mouth.
“So now you can finally see me.”
“I saw you from the beginning. I merely lost you while chasing your retreating back.”
The Blood Lord frowned as he listened.
“Was that you? The fearless bastard who interfered with me?”
“I was one step too late. A regrettable thing.”
As Jongni Chu calmly answered, the Blood Lord slowly looked him up and down.
The Always-Victorious Sword, Jongni Chu. He’s the one?
Jongni Chu had intervened just as the Blood Lord was about to finish off Dharma King Hong Dao. The rapidly approaching presence had forced him to turn away before he could deliver the final blow.
From what I sensed then, his aura was at least beyond the Ten Kings.

Even the Blood Lord would be in trouble if he were held back inside the Murim Alliance. After withdrawing and leaving the dying Hong Dao behind, that bastard had continued chasing him for quite some time.
He nearly caught me.
Fortunately, the martial art the Blood Lord practiced transcended all common sense.
And yet that mysterious master had been Jongni Chu. The Blood Lord shot him a suspicious look.
“You’ve already chased me this far. You’re quick on your feet.”
“Not as quick as you. That movement technique of yours was unlike anything I’ve ever seen or heard of.”
The Blood Lord’s eyes narrowed.
His opponent was absurdly young. He also seemed close to Cheongpung, and his realm of martial arts was almost impossible to believe.
“You. What is your relationship with the Martial God?”
Jongni Chu stroked his smooth chin, as was his habit.
“The Martial God... I did receive a few teachings from him.”
“Are you his Disciple?”
“Even a suckling infant can teach us something. Everyone we encounter in life is both teacher and student to one another.”
“Enough with the vague Zen riddles. Answer me before I break this brat’s neck.”
Instead of answering, Jongni Chu merely regarded him with calm eyes.
They were deep enough to draw a man in forever, yet tranquil as a lake on a windless day.
What is this feeling?
It was strange. They had only met each other’s eyes, yet the Blood Lord could not make his hand tighten.
No—it felt as though the strength were slowly draining from his fingers. As if something invisible had seized his wrist and refused to let go.
This is almost like...
The Blood Lord clenched his teeth as the thought surfaced.
No.
That was impossible. How dare he think of that person while looking at some worthless orthodox-faction stray?
It can’t be. All I have to do is cut down a bastard like him in one stroke.
He forced himself to regain his composure, but an inexplicable unease was already growing inside him.
Could he truly defeat this man?
Could he escape this place?
The Blood Lord slowly licked his parched lips.
“You... Who the hell are you?”
Dark Heaven’s information network stretched wide and ran deep throughout the land. Yet it had failed to uncover the identity of one person: Jongni Chu.
A mysterious figure whose face and origins were entirely unknown.
Jongni Chu tilted his head.
“Is that important?”
“What?”
“If a few words could persuade you to stop, I would tell you. But you won’t stop.”
His tranquil voice continued.
“There are people hovering between life and death even now. If you refuse to stop on your own, I have no choice but to stop you by force.”
Shhk.
With that, Jongni Chu drew the sword shoved carelessly through his belt. As the hopelessly rusted blade emerged, a sneer curled the Blood Lord’s lips.
“You’ll stop me? With that thing that barely qualifies as a sword?”
“Well, it still seems more useful than one might think.”
“Have you ever cut anyone with that sword?”
“Countless people. They aren’t memories I take much pride in.”
“Don’t compare me to some pack of nobodies. Who was the last person you cut down? A bandit no better than a slash-and-burn farmer? Or perhaps...”
At that moment, a low voice slipped from Jongni Chu’s lips.
“The Heaven-Poison Demon Lord.”
The Blood Lord went rigid.
The Heaven-Poison Demon Lord.
No martial artist could fail to recognize that title.
During the Great Faction War, he had been the greatest of archfiends, sweeping across the land while worshiping the Heavenly Demon—the Cult Leader of the Heavenly Demon Divine Cult—as a god.
He had been second-in-command of the Demonic Cult, which had once devoured half the world.
That was the Heaven-Poison Demon Lord.
But even he had been unable to escape the fate of a mere martial artist.

One day, after his evil reputation had grown darker with every passing day, he encountered a certain person. The Heaven-Poison Demon Lord met his death that day, and the one who killed him gained a new name.
“The Sword Saint...!”
The Blood Lord trembled as though struck by lightning.
Sword Saint Mae Jonghak.
That name had briefly crossed his mind when he tried to guess Jongni Chu’s identity. But he had soon shaken his head.
It was impossible.
It could not be allowed to be true.
A strained voice finally escaped his lips.
“You... How could you...?”
Jongni Chu—or rather, Sword Saint Mae Jonghak—ran his fingers along the blade as he answered.
“When the Great Faction War ended, I found myself wondering what I should do next. It didn’t take me long to decide. I simply loved martial arts.”
Scrape. Scrape.
Each pass of the violet Palm Force coating his hand stripped away the reddish rust, revealing the clear blade beneath.

“I devoted myself ceaselessly to martial arts. The child I took in late in life, who was like a grandson to me, became my Disciple—and at times, my teacher as well. Just when I thought I had reached Great Completion, I saw another wall before me.”
Sword Saint Mae Jonghak.
The great martial artist, who had already reached an exalted realm decades ago, had once again stepped into a new domain.
For a man already prepared in every way, a higher enlightenment had arrived.

“Even I didn’t expect to be Returned to Youth. In any case, finding myself unexpectedly young again made me curious about the outside world. I also found myself thinking about that aggravating grandson of mine who ran away a year ago.”
And so Sword Saint Mae Jonghak had entered the world and traveled throughout the land under the name Jongni Chu.
He was already a figure from the distant past. No one suspected that Mae Jonghak had returned to the body of a twenty-year-old.
Not even Dark Heaven, whose web stretched across the land.
“It was an enjoyable time. Until you people appeared.”
Shhk!
The last traces of rust peeled away.
At last, his cherished sword regained its true form and gleamed coldly.
Hundreds—perhaps thousands. The sword that had drunk the blood of countless fiends now pointed at the Blood Lord.
“Just as I said, isn’t this sword still useful?”
The next instant, a violet flash erupted.
Slash!
The Blood Lord blinked.
Time seemed to slow as Cheongpung’s body toppled into view.
So did a familiar wrist—the one attached to the hand gripping the unconscious Cheongpung’s throat.
That’s...
My hand.
The next thought was drowned beneath a surge of blood and pain. His mouth dropped open, and a scream tore from it.
“Gaaaaah!”
But it was not over yet.
As the Blood Lord staggered backward, screaming, a cold voice pursued him.
“You’ve accumulated sins that can never be washed away. Shouldn’t you pay the price?”
Whoosh!
Every hair on the Blood Lord’s body stood on end.
It was like a hallucination. The entire landscape vanished, and a single sword aimed at his chest consumed his every sense.
Shhk.
The sword glided through the air. The violet Force of the Zaha Divine Technique transformed into thirty-six plum blossoms that scattered in every direction.
At the beautiful sight, the Blood Lord murmured as though groaning.
“The Thirty-Six Plum Blossom Swords.”
But it was different.
Unmistakably different.
If the Thirty-Six Plum Blossom Swords Cheongpung had used earlier were a supreme technique, what Mae Jonghak now displayed was a divine feat beyond martial arts.
That very divine technique was boring into the vital points throughout the Blood Lord’s body.
I can’t stop this.
Horrified, the Blood Lord tried to throw himself aside.
Grab!
A hand clamped around his ankle.
Jin Taekyung, whom he had thought spent and unconscious, grinned up at him through bloodstained teeth.
“Where do you think you’re going, motherfucker?”
“You—!”
Papapapapat!
The rest of his words never came.
Violet flashes filled his eyes. Blood sprayed, and flesh split apart. The immense agony wiped his mind blank.
“Ghk!”
This was on an entirely different level. There was no way to block the Sword Energy hurtling across more than a hundred feet.
Slash! Slash!
Then, as his consciousness began to fade, the Blood Lord’s eyes suddenly flashed.
No. If I use that—if I use that, I can survive.
His mission was already complete. The Green Jade Buddha Staff in his hand—the only one left—was proof of that.
It was regrettable that he had failed to kill the Fire King, but...
As long as he lived, there would always be another chance.
He glared at Jin Taekyung with a resentful gaze. Even as he vomited clots of blood, Taekyung was smiling.
“Just you wait. I’ll kill you with my own hands.”
“What?”
“Stay alive until then. Make sure of it.”
The Blood Lord’s lips curled upward.
Mae Jonghak, who sensed what he intended, stiffened and sent Sword Energy flying with a rigid expression.
“Stop!”
Shriek! Slash!
The Blood Lord’s one remaining arm was severed cleanly at the shoulder.
“Lord of Heaven!”
Whoosh!
With that shout, he drew upon the last of his strength and shot forward like lightning. His teeth clamped down hard on his own severed arm—or rather, on the Green Jade Buddha Staff it still held.
And then—
Fwoom!
A black radiance, ominous even to behold, swallowed his entire body.
Then it vanished without a trace, taking the Blood Lord with it.
As though it had never existed in the first place.

chapters.title: Chapter 267
paragraphs: Fwoom!
I merely blinked at the black light that exploded like a flash.
That was all...
Where the fuck did that bastard go?
The shock was enough to make me forget the pain. I stared blankly, my mouth hanging open.
He was gone. As though he had been erased with an eraser.
The blood spattered around us and the Blood Lord’s wrist, still gripping Cheongpung’s neck, were the only proof that he had ever existed.
Ding.
System Quest Life-or-Death Crisis has been successfully completed! - You have gained an enormous amount of EXP! - Level Up! - Level Up!
With the System notifications, my body began to recover at a staggering rate.
My broken bones knitted back together, and my cut and mangled flesh healed. My empty dantian filled to the brim, and vitality surged through my muscles.
But one thing remained unchanged: my utter bewilderment.
“What the actual fuck was that?”
The Blood Lord. No matter what it took, I should have killed that bastard.
I was muttering dejectedly while staring at the ground when a familiar voice spoke, and a hand suddenly appeared in front of me.
“Are you all right?”
I was mentally exhausted, but my body was fine. I took Jongni Chu’s hand and rose to my feet.
“Yeah, I’m fine. I owe you my life.”
“That’s a relief. Then help me tend to the injured first... Wait. What did you just say?”
Jongni Chu blinked.
His face clearly said, What did I just hear?
“Why?”
“H-Hm?”
“Is there a problem?”
Jongni Chu stared blankly at me for a moment, then waved it off.
“No, no. What problem could there be? But didn’t you hear... that thing earlier?”
“That thing? What are you talking about? I did pass out for a moment.”
There was a limit to how much punishment I could take. I had been hit, gotten back up, been knocked down again, and gotten back up dozens of times over.
Then, at some point, I took a direct blow to the jaw and briefly lost consciousness.
“When I opened my eyes, it was almost over. I saw that bastard’s ankle, so I grabbed it right away.”
“...I see.”
Jongni Chu’s lips moved as though he wanted to say something, but he ultimately kept his mouth shut.
I wanted to ask how everything had unfolded and who Jongni Chu really was, but I held back too.
What matters is that he’s on our side.
That was enough for now. More urgent matters surrounded us.
“Old Master!”
I was worried about Cheongpung, but Jeok Cheongang was old, and his injuries concerned me even more.
I rushed over and examined him. His pulse was faint and his breathing shallow, but both were still there.
“Would you step aside for a moment?”
After carefully lowering Cheongpung, whose emergency treatment he had finished, Jongni Chu placed a hand over Jeok Cheongang’s Mingmen acupoint.
As internal energy flowed into him, the strain visibly eased from Jeok Cheongang’s face.
“How is he?”
“His injuries aren’t that serious. He expended too much energy all at once, so he probably won’t regain consciousness for a while.”
“What about Cheongpung?”
“The same. He has internal injuries, but he’s young. He should recover soon.”
“Phew...”
“A blessing amid all this misfortune.”
Jongni Chu smiled faintly at my relieved sigh.
That was when—
Shshshshk!
Countless presences rapidly approached from below. Their aura was vicious beyond description.
Don’t tell me there’s another one?
My expression hardened as I tightened my grip around the spear shaft, but Jongni Chu waved a hand.
“Put it down. They’re allies.”
He was right. Hundreds of martial artists soon appeared, with several familiar faces leading them.
Someone from the Nine Sects and One Gang. Someone from the Five Great Families.
They were the people who had occupied the seats of honor during the Star-Array Grand Banquet.
For some reason, however, several key figures—including the Thunderbolt Saber King—were nowhere to be seen.
“Stop.”
The footsteps of the hundreds of martial artists, which had seemed as though they would never stop, came to an abrupt halt in front of us.
The man who had given the order limped toward Jongni Chu and me. Sunlight filtering through the leaves glinted off his steel prosthetic leg.
The Thousand-Faced Fox, Song Ho.
As his piercing gaze swept over Jongni Chu and me, I suddenly remembered something I had forgotten.
They didn’t know Jongni Chu was an ally. To them, he was a public enemy of the Murim who had assassinated Dharma King Hong Dao and brought a bloodbath down upon Shaolin Temple.
Step. Step.
As the Thousand-Faced Fox advanced on his prosthetic leg, hundreds of martial artists moved with him.
This looked like it was about to turn into a bloody clash over a stupid misunderstanding.
“W-Wait a second. I think there’s been a serious misunderstanding...”
I was about to step forward amid the ominous tension when Jongni Chu suddenly spoke.
“Thousand-Faced Fox Song Ho.”
“Gasp.”
Was this bastard insane?
At a time when explaining the situation and clearing up the misunderstanding should have been the bare minimum, he had started by speaking informally.
“Hey, hey!”
I hurriedly jabbed him in the side, but it was already too late. A bombshell burst from Jongni Chu’s mouth.
“How’s your leg?”
Was he actually out of his mind?
I gaped at Jongni Chu.
This time, he had crossed the line completely. First the casual speech, and now he was mocking a disabled person.
I hurriedly stepped forward before the Thousand-Faced Fox could yank off his prosthetic leg and charge at Jongni Chu.
“I’m sorry. He’s not usually like this. Let me explain. So, what happened was—”
“Hm? I can explain it myself.”
“Explain, my ass. What the fuck are you going to explain in this situation? Apologize first, you bastard.”
To hell with him being my lifesaver.
Before things could get any worse, I grabbed Jongni Chu by the back of the neck and forced his head down.
When I raised my own head, I saw the Thousand-Faced Fox’s face, stiff and frozen as though he had seen a ghost.
He’s really pissed.
Of course he was. Anyone who didn’t get angry in this situation wasn’t human. They’d have to be Jesus or Buddha.
But the thoughts racing frantically through my mind as I tried to defuse the situation ground to a halt at the Thousand-Faced Fox’s reply.
“It has been a long time.”
Jongni Chu nodded with a genial chuckle like an old man.
“It’s good to see you doing well. I thought you would be the first to recognize me.”
“It took me quite some time. Until two shichen ago, I thought the Blood Ghost Sword Demon—that damned bastard—had Returned to Youth.”
“My, my. You’ve grown old too.”
“I owe the fact that I lived long enough to grow this old to you, Great Hero. If you hadn’t saved me back then, I wouldn’t be standing here now.”
The Thousand-Faced Fox laughed as he lightly tapped his prosthetic leg, then continued.
“I discovered Shadow Killer two shichen ago. You were playing a mischievous prank.”
“Ah, that fellow. Come to think of it, he should be waking up around now.”
“Someone who should have died was alive. That was when I realized I had been barking up the wrong tree.”
“I didn’t want anyone to find out. I wanted to keep it hidden until the Star-Array Grand Banquet ended, at least.”
Jongni Chu added with a bitter expression,
“I never imagined something like this would happen, though.”
“I feel the same. Despite all our precautions, a bloodbath occurred at Shaolin of all places...”
“You wouldn’t be here unless the situation at Shaolin had been settled. Did the Thunderbolt Saber King go?”
“Yes. As soon as we grasped the situation, we divided our forces and took two separate routes. Great Hero Peng should be handling matters at Shaolin by now.”
“The losses are too great. Something that should never have happened has happened.”
“I have much to tell you about that.”
“As do I.”
A heavy silence settled over us.
I had been listening to their conversation in a half-dazed state, but somehow managed to speak.
“Hey, no. Excuse me.”
Jongni Chu—or rather, he—blinked.
“Are you talking to me?”
“Yes. Um, there’s something I’d like to ask you...”
“Ask me anything.”
Hundreds of pairs of eyes turned toward me. Everyone wore the same expression.
That lunatic has finally come to his senses.
“May I ask your name?”
The answer came without hesitation.
“Mae Jonghak.”
“...Ah. Mae Jonghak.”
Every hair on my body stood on end.
From our first meeting to this moment, every conversation I’d had with him and everything I’d done flashed rapidly before my eyes.
“I think it’s a coincidence, but your name is the same as someone I know.”
“Is that so?”
I drew a deep breath. My heartbeat thundered in my ears.
It’s cold.
A dagger had flown straight into my chest. But don’t worry. There were more people with the same name than you might think.
Maybe he was Fake Jonghak.
Clinging to that final hope, I opened my mouth.
“Do you happen to have an epithet...?”
“The Sword Saint.”
“Ah. Yes.”
Fuck. He’s the real thing.
As darkness swallowed my vision, an amused voice slipped into my ear.
“Let’s remain good friends from now on. Friend.”
I want to die.
An enormous cavern of unknown depth in an unknown location.
At its center, where complex patterns and characters no one could decipher had been carved into the stone, black radiance erupted.
Whoosh!
The deep darkness stretched, dimming even the fiercely burning torches.
When the pitch-black darkness vanished a moment later, unrest spread among the dozens of black-clad figures surrounding the cavern’s center.
“The Blood Lord!”
“What is going on...?”
Their gazes converged on a staggering, bleeding figure.
A young man drenched in blood and breathing heavily.
Sword wounds covered the Blood Lord’s entire body, and blood gushed nonstop from the severed stumps of both arms.
“Call the sorcerers! Bring them here!”
“The Blood Lord is gravely wounded!”
As the desperate shouts echoed through the cavern, the Blood Lord slowly opened his mouth.
The severed arm he had held on to until the very end dropped to the floor with a thud. Its hand still clutched a short staff.
The staff gave off a faint green light even in the darkness, drawing a quiet gasp from someone nearby.
“The Green Jade Buddha Staff...!”
It was none other than the sacred treasure of thousand-year-old Shaolin.
No one had been able to guarantee the mission’s success. Yet despite the wretched state he had returned in, their superior had completed it splendidly.
Just as expected of the Disciple cherished by that person.
“Congratulations!”
“Congratulations?”
A red glow filled the Blood Lord’s eyes as he stared at the subordinate bowing deeply with a fist-and-palm salute.
Whoosh—crack!
The subordinate’s chest shattered, and he slammed into the wall amid a fountain of blood.
His body trembled with a wheezing sound, then went still. There was no need to check. He was dead.
“Throw that bastard to the beasts.”
The moment the Blood Lord’s frigid voice left his lips, one of his subordinates hoisted the corpse over his shoulder and disappeared.

This was hardly the first or second time such a thing had happened. They were merely reminded once more of how terrifying their superior was. Not one of them mourned or showed any agitation over the death of the ignorant newcomer who had stepped forward.
“Blood Lord, you must receive treatment first...”
“I’m dizzy. Begin.”
The Blood Lord surrendered himself to the sorcerers who had just arrived.
He wanted to slaughter everything in sight, but barely managed to suppress his murderous impulse.
He needed to conserve his strength for now. He had to recover as quickly as possible so he could tear those bastards apart and kill them.
The Sword Saint. The Fire King. Cheongpung. And...
The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung.
The memory of that bastard grinning through blood-soaked teeth made his blood boil.
Unable to contain his rage, he smashed a fist into a sorcerer’s head.
Boom. Thud.
The headless body collapsed like a rotten old tree. Feeling the frightened gazes of the remaining sorcerers, the Blood Lord spat through clenched teeth,
“I can’t afford to kill any more valuable sorcerers. Continue.”
The treatment resumed after its brief interruption. It was a bizarre sight that defied explanation. Broken bones knitted together, and flesh grew back.
The Blood Lord clenched his teeth against the pain that accompanied the recovery. As his vision began to turn white, one man’s face appeared before him.
You... I’ll kill you with my own hands. I swear.

chapters.title: Chapter 268
paragraphs: The death of Dharma King Hong Dao. And the mysterious bloodbath at Shaolin Temple, the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of the Murim.
Word travels faster than a galloping horse.
Countless eyewitnesses spread the rumors far and wide.
“Did you all hear the news? About the Star-Array Grand Banquet...”
“Martial artists are surrounding Mount Song. I heard there was a bloodbath at Shaolin Temple.”
Henan Province, which had been swept up in the festive excitement of the Star-Array Grand Banquet, was thrown into an uproar.
The elderly recalled the Demonic Cult’s rampage across the land several decades ago. The young realized that the war they had dismissed as a dusty relic of the past had become a present-day reality.
“The Demonic Cult has appeared? This is terrible. Just terrible.”
“I heard someone else was behind it, not the Demonic Cult.”
“You’re saying there are others besides the Demonic Cult capable of such a thing?”
“I don’t know the details myself. It’s just something I overheard.”
“That can’t be right. They say the terrifying Yin-Yang Twin Freaks led the attack on Shaolin.”
“The Yin-Yang Twin Freaks? I heard the Heavenly Demon of the Demonic Cult personally made a move.”
“T-The Heavenly Demon?”
As one rumor piled onto another, the story snowballed.
With everyone lost in a jumble of truth and lies, it was only natural for their attention to turn toward a single place.
The former site of the Murim Alliance.
The place where the great and small pillars of the orthodox faction stood.
“I heard what happened. About Jongni Chu—or rather, Great Hero Mae Jonghak, the Sword Saint.”
“Keep your chin up. These things happen.”
“I’m completely broke myself now. Whew... Anyway, that’s what happened to me. But when I heard your news, Captain, I felt strength surging through me.”
“Why?”
“Pardon?”
“I asked why that gave you strength.”
“Isn’t it obvious? As the ancient sages said, pain grows lighter when shared...”
Thwack!
“Guh.”
A precise blow to the solar plexus folded Hyuk Mujin at the waist and knocked the wind out of him.
When I saw the back of his head sitting wide open, my hand moved on its own. It just moved.
Smack!
“Feeling stronger now? Huh?”
“W-Wait. You hit me in the solar plexus. The solar plexus.”
“You’re making my blood pressure shoot up, you bastard. You’ve got my blood running backward!”
Smack-smack-smack!
After raining blows down on the back of his head, I finally felt a little better.
I already had enough on my mind. Why did this bastard have to rile me up on top of everything else?
“Things are serious right now, so watch your mouth. Got it?”
Rubbing the back of his head, Hyuk Mujin muttered, “You looked too serious, so I was trying to lighten the mood.”
“Just keep quiet.”
“...Yes, sir.”
Having silenced Hyuk Mujin, I gazed out the window.
Martial artists hurried frantically in every direction. Though none of them openly showed it, tension hung thick in the air.
Yet amid it all, the sky was brilliantly clear.
Hyuk Mujin’s subdued voice reached my ears.
“It feels strange.”
“What does?”
“Everything. None of it feels real. It’s only been one day.”
“I feel the same way.”
Even tumultuous wasn’t enough to describe it. Nothing that had happened the day before felt real. It all seemed like a dream.
Hong Dao breathing his last. Shaolin Temple drenched in blood. The Yin-Yang Twin Freaks, the Blood Lord, and finally Sword Saint Mae Jonghak.
The scenes passed before my eyes like a panorama.
The problem is, this is only the prologue.
If this were a movie theater, it wouldn’t be strange for the end credits to start rolling by now. But this was nothing more than an ominous prelude.
The vague sense of crisis that everyone anticipated was so palpable I could feel it on my skin.
Something is changing.
The world had already become a massive powder keg. The orthodox faction held the fuse, but Dark Heaven had the flint.
And just yesterday, the fuse had been lit.
I didn’t know how all this would end, but I could guess what would happen along the way.
There’s going to be a war.
A war on an entirely different scale from the one in Shanxi Province.
There was no way the people at the top had failed to realize what even I suspected.
The leaders of the orthodox faction were already consumed with handling the aftermath and holding meetings about the incident.
“Come to think of it, Captain, didn’t you attend yesterday’s meeting too?”
I nodded slightly.
The Jin Family of Taiyuan might not compare to the Nine Sects and One Gang or the Five Great Families, but it was still the undisputed hegemon of Shanxi Province.
And since Shanxi Province was where Dark Heaven had first revealed itself, it was only natural that the leaders would take a keen interest in it.
“What did they say?”
“They asked about the Head Elder and the Red Wind Band. I told them everything I knew.”
“The Head Elder is one thing, but why the Red Wind Band?”
“The Temporary Strength Pill used by Pung Yang, the Red Wind Band Leader, is connected to Dark Heaven.”
“Ah.”
Hyuk Mujin was now a high-ranking member of the family, so he had some idea of what was going on. He knew about both the Temporary Strength Pill and Dark Heaven.
“Did they say anything else?”
“I just left. My eldest brother will hear the important news and pass it on anyway...”
My voice sank without me realizing it.
“I didn’t feel comfortable leaving Old Master alone for too long.”
My gaze drifted from the window toward a lone figure.
A small elderly man lay on the bed as though deeply asleep.
When I took his wrinkled hand, I could feel his pulse. The faint rise and fall of his chest told me he was breathing. But even after a full day, he still hadn’t regained consciousness.
“When do you think he’ll wake up?”
“That’s the problem. No one knows.”
“Didn’t some famous physician come by?”
“He said there was nothing he could do. Since Old Master wasn’t gravely wounded like the others, he told us to wait and see.”
The Dance of the Fire God and Demon. The supreme technique of the Fire Gate Clan.
It possessed enough power to contend with a thousand martial artists, but everything came at a price.
A man well over a hundred years old simply didn’t have the stamina or strength left to withstand the aftermath.
Maybe...
I shook my head, driving away the thought that had suddenly surfaced.
There was no point dwelling on the worst.
Both the Sword Saint and the physician had said his life wasn’t in danger. For now, the best thing I could do was stay by Jeok Cheongang’s side and watch over him.
“There weren’t any suspicious people around while I was gone, were there?”
The Abbot of Shaolin had been assassinated inside the Murim Alliance. No one was safe. Just as Jeok Cheongang had protected me from the Blood Lord, I had to protect him.
Hyuk Mujin nodded confidently.
“The Jin Dragon Squad has the pavilion completely surrounded. No one can slip through. Don’t worry.”
“The Jin Dragon Squad? The elite force of the Taiyuan Jin Family?”
“Yes. The Lesser Family Head was concerned for Great Hero Jeok’s safety, so he assigned me here. Who do you think I am? I’m Hyuk Mujin, Vice Squad Leader of the Jin Dragon Squad.”
I looked him up and down, then quietly averted my eyes.
Hyuk Mujin’s confident expression instantly turned sour.
“What was that reaction?”
“Nothing. I just realized I shouldn’t leave again.”
“Don’t tell me you don’t trust the strength of the Jin Dragon Squad, the family’s finest?”
“Come on. I said that’s not it. Let it go.”
Hyuk Mujin glared at me through narrowed eyes, then shot to his feet.
“Fine. I’ll report to the Lesser Family Head and have everyone withdrawn.”
“Hey, why are you taking it that way? Are you going through puberty or something?”
“Because you keep saying such hurtful things, Captain! Is this only the first or second time? Huh?!”
“Keep your voice down. You’ll wake Old Master.”
“It would be nice if he woke up.”
He had a point.
As I found myself momentarily at a loss for words, Hyuk Mujin headed for the door.
One glance told me he was putting on an act because he wanted me to stop him. At times like this, I had to give him what he wanted.
“Hey, where are you going?”
Hyuk Mujin huffed, “Forget it. I can put up with anything else, but I won’t tolerate you insulting the subordinates I care about!”
“Gasp.”
“What now?”
“I never thought I’d hear words like that come out of your mouth. Mujin, you’ve really grown up. Guess your mouth doesn’t need circumcising after all.”
“...I’m really leaving.”
“Fine, fine. Sit down. Calm down and have a glass of water.”
“Hmph. No.”
“Well, well. Our Mujin really has grown up. Making me say it twice now.”
Hyuk Mujin froze, then quietly lowered himself onto the chair.
“I still deserve an apology.”
“Huh? For what?”
“For insulting my subordinates.”
“Why should I apologize? I never insulted them.”
“You just said you didn’t trust them. Wasn’t that because you look down on them for being weaker in martial arts than you?”
I sipped my cold tea.

“Well, we’re not the Nine Sects and One Gang or one of the Five Great Families, so of course there’s a difference in strength. But you said every member of the Jin Dragon Squad is young and talented, didn’t you? They distinguished themselves yesterday too. Weren’t they the ones who saved Unnamed?”
Shaolin was a mighty tree. Yesterday’s tragedy had cost it a great branch called the Dharma King and countless fruits, but its roots remained.
Shaolin’s martial arts. And Unnamed, who had survived.
Those were its roots.
Oh, and hadn’t they said that old monk Hongcheon survived too?
“That’s right. They fought Dark Heaven without giving an inch.”
Hyuk Mujin puffed out his chest, his face filled with pride.
“Exactly. Then what’s the problem? The kids looked sharp to me. They’re fiercely loyal to the family too. There’s only one problem.”
“What’s that?”
“You’re their Vice Squad Leader.”
“Your subordinates are standing at attention down there, while their Vice Squad Leader sits up here shooting the breeze?”
“Th-That’s...”
“You said you cared about them. That you were proud of them.”
“It’s true! Do you have any idea how much I care about those guys...?”
Hyuk Mujin faltered for a moment, then quickly recovered and poured out the words as though he had been waiting for the chance.
“Besides, my current mission is to guard Great Hero Jeok and you, Captain.”
“And before that?”
“Pardon?”
“What was your previous mission?”
“Guarding the Lesser Family Head, obviously.”
“Really?”
I chuckled, pulled that from inside my robes, and tossed it onto the table.
Clatter.
Hyuk Mujin sucked in a breath at the sight of the golden mask gleaming on the table.
“Gasp! W-Where did you get that...?”
“Where do you think? I knew you weren’t usually that kind of guy, but you stuck to me like a bad smell after the preliminaries.”
“Wait. You’ve got it all wrong. I was genuinely so busy with guard duty that I barely had time to open my eyes—”
“A misunderstanding? Fine. Want me to make sure you never open them again?”
Crack!
The golden mask crumpled into a little ball in my hand. Hyuk Mujin’s eyes shook as though caught in an earthquake.

“You were handling an escort at a gambling house, you bastard? You were so famous I didn’t even need to ask around. Apparently, some guy won a hundred thousand silver nyang in one go, then lost a hundred thousand silver nyang right afterward. They were treating him like a legend—no, an absolute legend.”
If the story had reached my ears even in the middle of this crisis, that said everything.
I’d even heard a rumor that one of the servants working at the Murim Alliance had hit the jackpot on Toto—no, Dodo—slapped the Chief Steward across the face, and walked out.

“If you cared about your subordinates that much, you should’ve collected dues and placed the bet with their money. Did you really gobble it down by yourself because you were afraid the payout odds would drop?”
No answer. Nothing to say.
Even if he had ten mouths, he wouldn’t have anything to say. Hyuk Mujin stood there frozen and pale before finally forcing out a few words.
“Life is... all about one big score.”
This bastard still hadn’t come to his senses.
I stared at Hyuk Mujin in disbelief and raised my fist.
That was when—
Swish. Tap.
There had been no noticeable presence. No sound.
As if by magic, a young man—or rather, an old man—had ascended more than ten jang and landed on the windowsill. He grinned and waved.
“Want to talk for a moment, friend?”
Friend, my ass.
I looked at Sword Saint Mae Jonghak and heaved an inward sigh.

It just moved.
Smack!

Smack-smack-smack!

It all seemed like a dream.
Hong Dao breathing his last.
Shaolin Temple drenched in blood.
The Yin-Yang Twin Freaks, the Blood Lord, and finally Sword Saint Mae Jonghak.
The scenes passed before my eyes like a panorama.
The problem is, this is only the prologue.
If this were a movie theater, it wouldn’t be strange for the end credits to start rolling by now.
But this was nothing more than an ominous prelude.
The vague sense of crisis that everyone anticipated was so palpable I could feel it on my skin.
Something is changing.
The world had already become a massive powder keg.
The orthodox faction held the fuse, but Dark Heaven had the flint.
And just yesterday, the fuse had been lit.

There’s going to be a war.

The leaders of the orthodox faction were already consumed with handling the aftermath and holding meetings about the incident.
“Come to think of it, Captain, didn’t you attend yesterday’s meeting too?”
I nodded slightly.

And since Shanxi Province was where Dark Heaven had first revealed itself, it was only natural that the leaders would take a keen interest in it.
“What did they say?”
“They asked about the Head Elder and the Red Wind Band.
I told them everything I knew.”
“The Head Elder is one thing, but why the Red Wind Band?”
“The Temporary Strength Pill used by Pung Yang, the Red Wind Band Leader, is connected to Dark Heaven.”
“Ah.”
Hyuk Mujin was now a high-ranking member of the family, so he had some idea of what was going on.
He knew about both the Temporary Strength Pill and Dark Heaven.
“Did they say anything else?”
“I just left.
My eldest brother will hear the important news and pass it on anyway...”
My voice sank without me realizing it.
“I didn’t feel comfortable leaving Old Master alone for too long.”
My gaze drifted from the window toward a lone figure.
A small elderly man lay on the bed as though deeply asleep.
When I took his wrinkled hand, I could feel his pulse.
The faint rise and fall of his chest told me he was breathing.
But even after a full day, he still hadn’t regained consciousness.
“When do you think he’ll wake up?”
“That’s the problem.
No one knows.”
“Didn’t some famous physician come by?”
“He said there was nothing he could do.

The Dance of the Fire God and Demon.
The supreme technique of the Fire Gate Clan.
It possessed enough power to contend with a thousand martial artists, but everything came at a price.
A man well over a hundred years old simply didn’t have the stamina or strength left to withstand the aftermath.
Maybe...
I shook my head, driving away the thought that had suddenly surfaced.
There was no point dwelling on the worst.
Both the Sword Saint and the physician had said his life wasn’t in danger.
For now, the best thing I could do was stay by Jeok Cheongang’s side and watch over him.
“There weren’t any suspicious people around while I was gone, were there?”
The Abbot of Shaolin had been assassinated inside the Murim Alliance.
No one was safe.
Just as Jeok Cheongang had protected me from the Blood Lord, I had to protect him.
Hyuk Mujin nodded confidently.
“The Jin Dragon Squad has the pavilion completely surrounded.
No one can slip through.
Don’t worry.”

The elite force of the Taiyuan Jin Family?”

The Lesser Family Head was concerned for Great Hero Jeok’s safety, so he assigned me here.
Who do you think I am?
