The Fire Dragon Divine Spear, now at the seventh stage, burned through air and sound alike, carving a path of fire.
Fwoooosh!
Rumble!
The final Iron Golem collapsed with a deafening crash.
It had taken only a few minutes to dispose of more than ten A-rank monsters.
When I looked around, everyone was staring at me in shock.
“This is insane...”
“Did you see that?
Did you just see that?”
“Yes.
I saw it.”
“Wow, he was playing with an A-rank monster.
I couldn’t even see him move.”
“I told you I saw it.”
A voice rang out above the murmuring rookie Guild members.
“Is the raid over already?
After combat, clean up the remains and keep watch over the surrounding area.
Guild Master and Miss Song, please take charge.”
His words were polite, but his tone cracked like a whip.
Team Leader Choi landed lightly, and the rookies flinched before hurrying off to find something to do.
He really does have charisma sometimes.
Maybe it was that unique aura of his.
You had to be born with something like that.
As I was thinking this, Team Leader Choi approached and spoke with a grave expression.
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung.
I’ve been thinking about this for a while, but I can’t hold back any longer.”
“Yes.”
“Where did you buy that spear?”
Right.
This was the kind of person he was.
I’d forgotten for a moment.
Whether he knew what I was thinking or not, Team Leader Choi’s gaze remained fixed on the spear in my hand—White Flame.
“It’s like looking at a work of art.
A classical yet beautiful Chinese-style design.
Don’t tell me it’s made from Magic Gem?”
No.
It’s made from Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.
Of course, telling him the truth would only cause trouble, so I gave him a vague answer.
“I’m not sure.
I don’t know much about it myself.”
Team Leader Choi’s covetous gaze traveled up and down the spear.
“If you don’t mind my asking, would you consider selling it to me...?”
“No.
It’s not for sale.”
Even if I wanted to sell it, I couldn’t.
It was a bound Item that only I could use.
The Item information said so, too.
Perhaps for that reason, it was the only object in my two separate inventories—the ones divided between Murim and the modern world—that could travel between the two worlds.
Team Leader Choi smacked his lips in disappointment, then changed the subject.
“Regardless, I’m truly impressed.
You just keep getting stronger.”
I answered half-jokingly and half-seriously.
“All it takes is training like hell for a year under a Supreme Peak master with dementia.”
“Dementia?
What did you say?”
“A Supreme Peak master.”
“Isn’t that a term from wuxia novels?
Peak master, Supreme Peak master.”
“That’s right.
I’m thinking of writing a novel as a hobby after I retire.
Something like Login Murim.”
“That title isn’t very good.
It won’t be a hit.”
“I’m not actually planning to write it.”
Team Leader Choi let out a short laugh before speaking.
“I know I’ve said this before, but sometimes, when I look at you, Mr.
Jin Taekyung, a certain thought crosses my mind.”
“What thought?”
“Whether you and I are truly the same kind of person.”
His light brown eyes seemed to grow hot and reddish.
“A perennial F-rank Hunter becoming this powerful in only a few months?
If I hadn’t seen you with my own eyes, I never would have believed it.”
It was a reasonable suspicion.
Second-awakened Hunters were uncommon, but not so few that they could be considered exceedingly rare.
In my case, however, I had reached a realm far beyond any ordinary second awakening.
What’s more, Team Leader Choi had watched my transformation from closer than anyone else.
I might fool everyone else, but not Team Leader Choi.
To him, I was no different from a second-, third-, or fourth-awakened Hunter.
I licked my dry lips.
This was a secret I had to take to my grave.
If it ever got out, I might be dragged off by the NIS—or no, NASA—and spend the rest of my life as a test subject.
“Team Leader.
I’m sorry, but that’s...”
Team Leader Choi shook his head slightly and cut me off.
“I know.
I understand that you have secrets you can’t even tell me.
In a way, I’m in a similar position, so I have no intention of pressing you.”
A similar position?
Before the question could fully form in my mind, he continued.
“An unprecedented second-awakened Hunter unlike anything the world has ever seen.
That explanation should be enough, shouldn’t it?
Butler Kim feels the same way I do.”
Song Song and Im Kkeokjeong had joined us later, but Butler Kim had been at Team Leader Choi’s side, watching me grow.
News articles were already pouring out under headlines like The F-Rank Hunter’s Rebellion and A Miracle.
If the two of them kept their mouths shut, I could probably bring things to an end here.
I dipped my head.
“Thank you.
I owe you one.”
“Don’t mention it.”
“But may I ask you one thing?”
“Anything.”
“Why are you going this far for me?”
“Oh, that?”
Team Leader Choi gave a breathy laugh.
“You just said it yourself.
You owe me.”
“I did.”
“And I intend to collect that debt in full—with interest.”
“That’s all you need to know.
Well, then.”
Team Leader Choi turned to leave, then paused.
“That novel you mentioned earlier—if you ever write it, let me read it.
I enjoy novels more than you might think.”
“Then you won’t be able to read mine.”
“Why not?”
Because if I ever write it, it won’t be a novel you’d enjoy.
It’ll be an essay about my own experiences.
Team Leader Choi tilted his head at my silent smile.
The workshop—or rather, the raid—scheduled to last six nights and seven days ended after only three.
I had wandered around alone and beaten down every monster I saw, leaving nothing else to hunt.
“It was supposed to be a raid for team bonding, but somehow it turned out like this.”
I quietly avoided Song Song’s incredulous stare.
Wiping out all the Golems inside the Gate hadn’t been enough.
I’d even soloed the boss monster.
That EXP was so sweet.
“Ahem.”
“The rookies need raid experience, too.
Why are you so desperate to jump in every time you see a monster?”
“Come on, it all worked out.
Let it go.”
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung.”
“Now, now.
Let’s just let it go, Miss Song.”
“And if I just can’t let it go?”
“I’ll punish you by confessing my feelings.”
Song Song pressed her lips shut and slowly backed away with a frightened expression.
I got what I wanted, so why do I feel like crying?
Hah.
I loved you...
I trudged away like the tragic male lead of a romance.
The moment I exited the dungeon, the reporters camped outside the Gate set off a barrage of camera flashes.
I had spent an entire year in Murim, but only a few days had passed in the modern world.
It would take more time for all the interest and excitement surrounding me to die down.
“Please step back, reporters!”
“Only authorized personnel are allowed beyond this point!”
Only after the guards rushed in and held back the press did I escape the barrage of flashes.
Once the shutter sounds finally stopped, the rookie Guild members, their faces flushed with excitement, shouted loudly.
“Thank you for your hard work!”
Their eyes sparkled.
Their gazes were filled with admiration and respect as they looked at us.
Though, of course, most of that attention was focused on me.
Feeling awkward, I turned toward the founding members.
That was when I realized someone was missing.
“Where’s Uncle Kkeokjeong?”
“Huh?
Now that you mention it, he isn’t here.”
Team Leader Choi answered.
“He told me privately on the way here, then slipped away.
Apparently something came up.”
“What could be so urgent that he left without even changing out of his gear?”
“It must be urgent if he left like that.”
What was going on?
Had something happened at home?
An uneasy feeling settled in the back of my mind.
Come to think of it, I didn’t get to talk with him much after returning.
I had spent most of the raid operating alone, so I hadn’t had many chances to talk with the others.
Looking back, Im Kkeokjeong’s expression had seemed a little dark.
At the time, I’d assumed he was simply nervous, but...
Did something really serious happen?
Even after I changed out of my gear and everyone went their separate ways, I couldn’t stop thinking about it.
I debated for a long time whether to call him, but in the end, I sent a quick message to the number saved in my contacts.
It simply said that we should grab a drink together soon.
He probably had his own problems to deal with, and sticking my nose in where it didn’t belong might be rude.
That should be enough.
I was staring at the stubborn number 1 that refused to disappear when—
Bzzzzt.
My smartphone vibrated.
A phone icon appeared on the screen, along with the saved name.
It was a name I had saved several months ago and completely forgotten about.
Garam Middle School Classmate Park Jihoon
I had run into him by chance on the day I went to buy a house, and he hadn’t contacted me once since.
What could he want?
Mildly curious, I answered the call.

chapters.title: Chapter 272
paragraphs: “Hello?”
The voice on the other end of the phone sounded unfamiliar.

The Park Jihoon I remembered from middle school hadn’t even finished going through his voice change, and since then, we’d only exchanged a few words in passing when we ran into each other a few months ago.
Is this really him?
I was still hesitating when he spoke again.
“Is this Jin Taekyung’s number?”
“Oh, yeah, it’s me. I thought you might be someone else.”
“What the hell? You didn’t save my number last time?”
“I did, but for a second I thought you might’ve called the wrong number. I didn’t recognize your voice.”
“Fair enough. That was the first time we’d seen each other since middle school.”
“True. I didn’t even recognize you then.”
“Of course you didn’t. Do you have any idea how much money I poured into this face?”
A low laugh came through the phone. There wasn’t a trace of awkwardness between us; the mood felt warm and familiar.
I laughed along as I climbed into the VIP limousine provided by the Gate Management Agency. The driver met my eyes in the rearview mirror and gave me a polite nod before smoothly pulling away.
“So, what’s up?”
“Nothing much. I called to see if you wanted to grab a drink.”
“Drinks? Out of the blue?”
“Yeah. I said I’d get in touch when we had our class reunion, but I never did.”
Did he?
Thinking back, it seemed like he had. I’d been so busy since then that I’d completely forgotten.
“Something came up at the last minute, and I had to go overseas on business. I couldn’t even make it to the reunion.”
“An overseas business trip?”
“There was a problem at our European branch. I only got back recently.”
I went to Murim, and this guy went to Europe.
I had no idea what he’d done there, but for some reason, I felt cheated. I spoke with as much envy as I could muster.
“You lucky bastard. Must’ve been nice getting to see Europe.”
“You’re jealous of me? You?”
Park Jihoon burst out laughing on the other end of the line.
“That feels really weird coming from you. Are you trying to rub it in?”
“No, that’s not what I meant.”
“I’m kidding. So, are you free tonight?”
I glanced at the time. It was already eight in the evening.
I’d moved out of our family home and into an officetel in Bucheon three days ago, so even if I went home, the only person waiting for me would be Jinho hyung.
I had time. The problem was...
He doesn’t have some other motive, does he?
But I only hesitated for a moment.
I’d been a Hunter for seven years. Even the close friends I’d been inseparable from during my school days had gradually stopped contacting me long ago.
Out of sight, out of mind didn’t apply only to romantic relationships.
And yet here I was, suspecting a friend who had contacted me after all this time without any ulterior motive.
Have I developed trust issues or something?
The aftermath of the Won Myunghoon incident, along with the harassment I’d endured from certain trash reporters, must have left a lasting mark. I was left with a bitter taste in my mouth.
“You must be pretty busy. I guess that makes sense. Then maybe next time...”
“No, I’m free now. Where should we meet?”
A little while later, the limousine gliding down the road changed course.
“You got here faster than I expected.”
Park Jihoon was already outside waiting for me.
The weather was gradually turning toward winter. In his cashmere coat over a crisp white shirt, he looked completely different from me.
“What’s with the outfit? Why are you so dressed up?”
“I have something important to take care of today. And let’s get one thing straight. It’s not that I’m dressed up—you’re dressed down.”
“Hey, what’s wrong with what I’m wearing? Jeans and a sweatshirt are perfectly fine.”
This was me making an effort, too. Hayeon had kept squawking at me to stop wearing tracksuits when so many people were watching.
“Where did all the money you earned go...? Oh, right. You donated it.”
“Don’t bring that up. It still hurts.”
“That’s why I called you. When something’s eating at you, alcohol is the best medicine.”
Park Jihoon grinned and jerked his chin toward the entrance, then started walking.
We passed a uniformed security guard and countless surveillance cameras installed throughout the grounds before finally making it inside.
The sight that greeted me left my mouth hanging open.
What the hell is this?
The marble floor glittered beneath the lights, while paintings that looked as though they had come straight out of the seventeenth century hung in frames along the walls.
I think I saw that one in an art textbook. There’s no way it’s genuine, right? Yeah. It can’t be.
I followed him, gawking like a country bumpkin.
We stopped in front of five elevators lined up side by side.
There weren’t even any buttons, so I had no idea what I was supposed to do. Then Jihoon placed his hand on a black panel, and an elevator descended in the blink of an eye with a mechanical whine.
Bzzzzing.
“What are you doing? Get in.”
“What are you so surprised about?”
“Nothing. I just thought you said this was an officetel.”
“It is. An officetel.”
The officetel he knew and the one I knew seemed to be two entirely different things. I swallowed the words before they could slip out.
Maybe it was because we were in Cheongdam-dong, but the place practically reeked of wealth from the entrance onward.
“You really made it. You even bought a place like this.”
“It came onto the market recently, so I bought it. I thought I could stop by now and then to clear my head.”
Anyone listening to him would think he’d bought a pair of shoes.
As I shook my head in disbelief, the elevator stopped and the doors opened. Instead of a cold, dark hallway, a living room decorated in shades of gray spread out before me.
I didn’t know the exact square footage, but the living room alone was about the same size as our family home.
“Come in.”
I had no idea whether he’d really bought the place just to clear his head, but one thing was certain: I’d never been anywhere like it.
The enormous lounge suite and wine cellar in the living room made it look as though someone had picked up an upscale bar and moved it inside.
Park Jihoon took off his coat and asked, “What do you want to drink?”
“What do you have?”
“Château Cheval Blanc, Screaming Eagle Cabernet Sauvignon, Royal de Maria...”
What the hell is he talking about?
I blinked at the stream of alien words.
“Chateau Shibal, what?”
“Château Cheval Blanc.”
Whether it was château or shatto, every single name was impossibly complicated.
After a brief silence, I asked, “Don’t you have any somaek?”
Park Jihoon let out a short laugh.
We stacked up a crate each of soju and beer and drank without pause.
It had been eleven years since we’d lost touch in our third year of middle school, so we had a mountain of things to talk about.
“Remember that guy No Jaehun from the class next door?”
“Who was No Jaehun?”
“The tall guy who used to brag about working out. Anyway, when he got into a fight with Seon Woongje from our class, you—”
“Wait. Who the hell is Seon Woongje?”
“...Do you have amnesia or something?”
We talked about everything from trivial memories of middle school to what we’d been doing since we lost touch.
The only time either of us stopped talking was to drink.
At some point, I realized the corners of my mouth had been turned up for quite a while.
This is fun.

How could I put it? Drinking with someone you felt comfortable around was always enjoyable, but there was something a little more special about sharing a drink with a friend who shared the same memories.
The atmosphere was so warm and friendly that I felt like an idiot for having suspected him, even briefly, during our phone call.
I also learned a few things about him that I’d never known before.
“You were born with a silver spoon?”
“Silver spoon is a bit much. My father just runs a small business.”
“A Hunter-related business that he’s been running for more than thirty years?”
“Yeah.”
“That makes you a silver-spoon kid, you deceitful bastard. Guys who talk like you always turn out to be the ones who are genuinely rich.”
I looked at him.
It wasn’t that he suddenly looked different now that I knew he was rich. I just found it fascinating.

The neighborhood where we’d lived back then had been perfectly ordinary. If it hadn’t been, someone like me—whose school grades had been determined by rolling a mechanical pencil to guess the answers—would never have gotten in.
The Hunter industry, on the other hand, was practically a gold mine.
If his family had survived for thirty years amid such fierce competition, it wouldn’t have been strange to find gold bars rolling around their house.
“Why are you looking at me like that?”
“It’s just weird. Don’t rich kids usually go to Gangnam’s famous School District 8 or somewhere like that?”
“I guess I’m not a rich kid, then. Besides, I transferred in, remember?”
“You transferred? That’s the first I’ve heard of it.”
“Yeah. In our second year of middle school. There wasn’t any reason to mention it.”
“Wasn’t there?”
“No.”
I tilted my head and took another drink.
Then again, what did it matter that he’d transferred schools in middle school? It had happened more than ten years ago.
“We didn’t meet until our third year, anyway. We’d never crossed paths before then, so it makes sense that I wouldn’t know.”
“But we crossed paths plenty of times.”
“Huh?”
“A week after I transferred, I saw you for the first time in front of the teachers’ office. Then we ran into each other in the hallway. We crossed paths in the bathroom, too.”
Memories from more than ten years ago, already blurred into an indistinct mosaic, flowed from Park Jihoon’s lips.
“Wow... How do you remember all that?”
His perfectly smooth lips curved into a smile.
“I have a better memory than you’d think. Unlike some people.”
I topped off his empty glass and chuckled.
“Hey, my memory might be terrible, but there’s one thing I remember.”
“What?”
“You never did your homework. Every time we had a test, you guessed all the answers, put your head down, and went to sleep.”
“Oh, that.”
“If your memory was so good, why were your grades in memorization-heavy subjects so awful? Did you even go to college—ah, is that rude to ask?”
“What’s rude about it? I don’t care.”
“Then that’s a relief.”
“And I did go to college. Business Administration at Hankuk University. I awakened out of nowhere, so I still haven’t graduated.”
“Wait, where? Hankuk University?”
“My parents wanted me to go.”
“...You crazy bastard. Are there parents who don’t want their kid to get into Hankuk University?”
Hankuk University was the most prestigious university in the country. Only the brightest students from across Korea could get in.
Park Jihoon laughed lightly at my incredulous stare.
“When I actually tried, I got in. It wasn’t as hard as I expected.”
“Huh.”
How could I put it? The more I heard about his life, the more it sounded like a wide-open highway.
A wealthy family, a sharp mind, admission to the university everyone dreamed of, and then becoming an A-rank Awakened in one shot.
Unlike me, who’d been forced to provide for my family, becoming a Hunter had been just one of countless options available to him.
“Why?”
“Huh?”
“You were looking at me strangely.”
“Was it that obvious?”
“Very. Taekyung, are you perhaps...”
Park Jihoon propped his chin on one hand.
His alcohol-soaked voice continued in a low murmur.
“Are you jealous of me?”
Jealous?
The question was so unexpected that I stared blankly for a moment. Then I burst out laughing.
“Yeah. I guess that’s what it is.”
“...You’re honest.”
“It’s true. Longing for something I never had? Envy, maybe. Something like that. I don’t regret anything, though. I worked hard enough.”
Park Jihoon stared at me, his eyes widening slightly as though he hadn’t expected that answer.
“So you get jealous of people, too.”
“Hey, what am I, some kind of big shot?”
“You are. Look at yourself now. You’re a Hunter drawing attention from the foreign media as well as the domestic press. Before long, you might even become one of Korea’s five S-rank Hunters.”
“That sounds impressive—except I’m also the guy who made a donation and still trembles every time he thinks about the money.”
I let out a short laugh and emptied my glass. Park Jihoon gazed at me in silence, his lips parting as though he were about to say something.
That was when—
Bzzzt.
The smartphone on the table began to vibrate. Park Jihoon stared intently at the screen and licked his lips.
“Who is it?”
“My Guild Team Leader.”
“At this hour? Does the Myeongdong Guild have some kind of twenty-four-hour standby team?”
“Nothing like that. It’s about something important.”
“Then...”
“Sorry, but I think we’ll have to call it a night.”
“Don’t apologize. It’s not like we don’t understand each other’s circumstances.”
I set down my glass and stood. Then I gave Park Jihoon, who was looking at me apologetically, a light tap on the shoulder.
I had a good time tonight.
I meant it. Now that I had become famous in the modern world, there weren’t many people left with whom I could have an ulterior-motive-free conversation like this.
I stopped him when he tried to follow me into the elevator.
“I’m heading out. Don’t bother coming down just to see me off. Take care of your problem.”
A faint smile touched Park Jihoon’s lips.
“Okay. Let’s meet again. Definitely.”
With those final words, the elevator doors closed.
Park Jihoon stood before the window and looked down.
A lone figure was leaving the officetel entrance below, swallowed by the darkness.
“Hello? Mr. Jihoon? Mr. Jihoon?”
“Go ahead.”
“Ah, we finally connected. You were listening, so why didn’t you say anything...?”
“I think you’ve misunderstood something, Team Leader.”
The other person’s breathing faltered at the dry voice.
Park Jihoon lifted a crystal tumbler to his lips. Instead of the somaek he’d been drinking moments ago, amber whiskey rippled inside.
“From now on, wait until I speak. And stop trying to play boss with me.”
Park Jihoon, Hunter of Team 1 in the Myeongdong Guild.
That was the affiliation printed on his business card.
But the Team Leader of Team 1 in the Myeongdong Guild remained silent on the other end of the phone.
They both knew the truth. That title was nothing more than a hollow position.
“You’re not answering.”
“...Understood.”
“So what is it? This important report of yours?”
The Team Leader of Team 1 answered carefully.
“You know Team Leader Jung Hyunwoo, right? The one in charge of Team 8.”
“Of course. He’s skilled, but his flexibility isn’t even half as impressive as his ability. That’s the problem.”
“It seems he’s caught the scent.”
“Really? He’s more perceptive than I expected.”
“Yes. But I wasn’t sure how we should handle it...”
“What is there to think about? Schedule a raid for the earliest possible date. An A-rank one.”
“You mean...”
“Team Leader, do you know how many Gate accidents happen every year? I don’t. Neither does anyone else. Nobody cares.”
Park Jihoon clicked his tongue.
“You’re not answering again.”
“Ah. Understood.”
“And regarding the Peace Guild—or rather, the Jin Taekyung matter...”
Park Jihoon trailed off.
The face of the man who had smiled and tapped him on the shoulder came to mind.
I had a good time tonight.
It had been a sincere statement.
That only made Park Jihoon even less willing to stop.
“Mr. Jihoon?”
Park Jihoon tossed back the rest of his whiskey.
The crystal tumbler crumpled in his hand like a sheet of paper.
“I finished speaking with the higher-ups today. They find him irritating.”
That was all. A single passing remark over dinner with that person. The matter had been as good as settled from that moment on.
“What? But this isn’t really the right time for something like that...”
Park Jihoon’s cold voice cut off the Team Leader’s startled protest.
“Isn’t it only natural for a gardener to pull weeds from the lawn? Your Guild Master has probably already heard the news. I’m hanging up.”
Click.
The call ended.
In the silence that followed, Park Jihoon stared through the spotless window at the view outside.
Jin Taekyung was long gone.

Park Jihoon grinned and jerked his chin toward the entrance, then started walking.
We passed a uniformed security guard and countless surveillance cameras installed throughout the grounds before finally making it inside.
The sight that greeted me left my mouth hanging open.
What the hell is this?
The marble floor glittered beneath the lights, while paintings that looked as though they had come straight out of the seventeenth century hung in frames along the walls.
I think I saw that one in an art textbook.
There’s no way it’s genuine, right?
Yeah.
It can’t be.
I followed him, gawking like a country bumpkin.
We stopped in front of five elevators lined up side by side.
There weren’t even any buttons, so I had no idea what I was supposed to do.
Then Jihoon placed his hand on a black panel, and an elevator descended in the blink of an eye with a mechanical whine.
Bzzzzing.
“What are you doing?
Get in.”
“What are you so surprised about?”
“Nothing.
I just thought you said this was an officetel.”
“It is.
An officetel.”
The officetel he knew and the one I knew seemed to be two entirely different things.
I swallowed the words before they could slip out.
Maybe it was because we were in Cheongdam-dong, but the place practically reeked of wealth from the entrance onward.
“You really made it.
You even bought a place like this.”
“It came onto the market recently, so I bought it.
I thought I could stop by now and then to clear my head.”
Anyone listening to him would think he’d bought a pair of shoes.
As I shook my head in disbelief, the elevator stopped and the doors opened.
Instead of a cold, dark hallway, a living room decorated in shades of gray spread out before me.
I didn’t know the exact square footage, but the living room alone was about the same size as our family home.
“Come in.”
I had no idea whether he’d really bought the place just to clear his head, but one thing was certain: I’d never been anywhere like it.
The enormous lounge suite and wine cellar in the living room made it look as though someone had picked up an upscale bar and moved it inside.
Park Jihoon took off his coat and asked, “What do you want to drink?”
“What do you have?”
“Château Cheval Blanc, Screaming Eagle Cabernet Sauvignon, Royal de Maria...”
What the hell is he talking about?
I blinked at the stream of alien words.
“Chateau Shibal, what?”
“Château Cheval Blanc.”
Whether it was château or shatto, every single name was impossibly complicated.
After a brief silence, I asked, “Don’t you have any somaek?”
Park Jihoon let out a short laugh.
We stacked up a crate each of soju and beer and drank without pause.
It had been eleven years since we’d lost touch in our third year of middle school, so we had a mountain of things to talk about.
“Remember that guy No Jaehun from the class next door?”
“Who was No Jaehun?”
“The tall guy who used to brag about working out.
Anyway, when he got into a fight with Seon Woongje from our class, you—”
“Wait.
Who the hell is Seon Woongje?”
“...Do you have amnesia or something?”
We talked about everything from trivial memories of middle school to what we’d been doing since we lost touch.
The only time either of us stopped talking was to drink.
At some point, I realized the corners of my mouth had been turned up for quite a while.
This is fun.
How could I put it?
Drinking with someone you felt comfortable around was always enjoyable, but there was something a little more special about sharing a drink with a friend who shared the same memories.
The atmosphere was so warm and friendly that I felt like an idiot for having suspected him, even briefly, during our phone call.
I also learned a few things about him that I’d never known before.
“You were born with a silver spoon?”
“Silver spoon is a bit much.
My father just runs a small business.”
“A Hunter-related business that he’s been running for more than thirty years?”
“Yeah.”
“That makes you a silver-spoon kid, you deceitful bastard.
Guys who talk like you always turn out to be the ones who are genuinely rich.”
I looked at him.
It wasn’t that he suddenly looked different now that I knew he was rich.
I just found it fascinating.
The neighborhood where we’d lived back then had been perfectly ordinary.
If it hadn’t been, someone like me—whose school grades had been determined by rolling a mechanical pencil to guess the answers—would never have gotten in.
The Hunter industry, on the other hand, was practically a gold mine.
If his family had survived for thirty years amid such fierce competition, it wouldn’t have been strange to find gold bars rolling around their house.
“Why are you looking at me like that?”
“It’s just weird.
Don’t rich kids usually go to Gangnam’s famous School District 8 or somewhere like that?”
“I guess I’m not a rich kid, then.
Besides, I transferred in, remember?”
“You transferred?
That’s the first I’ve heard of it.”
“Yeah.
In our second year of middle school.
There wasn’t any reason to mention it.”
“Wasn’t there?”
“No.”
I tilted my head and took another drink.
Then again, what did it matter that he’d transferred schools in middle school?
It had happened more than ten years ago.
“We didn’t meet until our third year, anyway.
We’d never crossed paths before then, so it makes sense that I wouldn’t know.”
“But we crossed paths plenty of times.”
“Huh?”
“A week after I transferred, I saw you for the first time in front of the teachers’ office.
Then we ran into each other in the hallway.
We crossed paths in the bathroom, too.”
Memories from more than ten years ago, already blurred into an indistinct mosaic, flowed from Park Jihoon’s lips.
“Wow...
How do you remember all that?”
His perfectly smooth lips curved into a smile.
“I have a better memory than you’d think.
Unlike some people.”
I topped off his empty glass and chuckled.
“Hey, my memory might be terrible, but there’s one thing I remember.”
“What?”
“You never did your homework.
Every time we had a test, you guessed all the answers, put your head down, and went to sleep.”
“Oh, that.”
“If your memory was so good, why were your grades in memorization-heavy subjects so awful?
Did you even go to college—ah, is that rude to ask?”
“What’s rude about it?
I don’t care.”
“Then that’s a relief.”
“And I did go to college.
Business Administration at Hankuk University.
I awakened out of nowhere, so I still haven’t graduated.”
“Wait, where?
Hankuk University?”
“My parents wanted me to go.”
“...You crazy bastard.
Are there parents who don’t want their kid to get into Hankuk University?”
Hankuk University was the most prestigious university in the country.
Only the brightest students from across Korea could get in.
Park Jihoon laughed lightly at my incredulous stare.
“When I actually tried, I got in.
It wasn’t as hard as I expected.”
“Huh.”
How could I put it?
The more I heard about his life, the more it sounded like a wide-open highway.
A wealthy family, a sharp mind, admission to the university everyone dreamed of, and then becoming an A-rank Awakened in one shot.
Unlike me, who’d been forced to provide for my family, becoming a Hunter had been just one of countless options available to him.
“Why?”
“Huh?”
“You were looking at me strangely.”
“Was it that obvious?”
“Very.
Taekyung, are you perhaps...”
Park Jihoon propped his chin on one hand.
His alcohol-soaked voice continued in a low murmur.
“Are you jealous of me?”
Jealous?
The question was so unexpected that I stared blankly for a moment.
Then I burst out laughing.
“Yeah.
I guess that’s what it is.”
“...You’re honest.”
“It’s true.
Longing for something I never had?
Envy, maybe.
Something like that.
I don’t regret anything, though.
I worked hard enough.”
Park Jihoon stared at me, his eyes widening slightly as though he hadn’t expected that answer.
“So you get jealous of people, too.”
“Hey, what am I, some kind of big shot?”
“You are.
Look at yourself now.
You’re a Hunter drawing attention from the foreign media as well as the domestic press.
Before long, you might even become one of Korea’s five S-rank Hunters.”
“That sounds impressive—except I’m also the guy who made a donation and still trembles every time he thinks about the money.”
I let out a short laugh and emptied my glass.
Park Jihoon gazed at me in silence, his lips parting as though he were about to say something.
That was when—
Bzzzt.
The smartphone on the table began to vibrate.
Park Jihoon stared intently at the screen and licked his lips.
“Who is it?”
“My Guild Team Leader.”
“At this hour?
Does the Myeongdong Guild have some kind of twenty-four-hour standby team?”
“Nothing like that.
It’s about something important.”
“Then...”
“Sorry, but I think we’ll have to call it a night.”
“Don’t apologize.
It’s not like we don’t understand each other’s circumstances.”
I set down my glass and stood.
Then I gave Park Jihoon, who was looking at me apologetically, a light tap on the shoulder.
I had a good time tonight.
I meant it.
Now that I had become famous in the modern world, there weren’t many people left with whom I could have an ulterior-motive-free conversation like this.
I stopped him when he tried to follow me into the elevator.
“I’m heading out.
Don’t bother coming down just to see me off.
Take care of your problem.”
A faint smile touched Park Jihoon’s lips.
“Okay.
Let’s meet again.
Definitely.”
With those final words, the elevator doors closed.
Park Jihoon stood before the window and looked down.
A lone figure was leaving the officetel entrance below, swallowed by the darkness.
“Hello?
Mr.
Jihoon?
Mr.
Jihoon?”
“Go ahead.”
“Ah, we finally connected.
You were listening, so why didn’t you say anything...?”
“I think you’ve misunderstood something, Team Leader.”
The other person’s breathing faltered at the dry voice.
Park Jihoon lifted a crystal tumbler to his lips.
Instead of the somaek he’d been drinking moments ago, amber whiskey rippled inside.
“From now on, wait until I speak.
And stop trying to play boss with me.”
Park Jihoon, Hunter of Team 1 in the Myeongdong Guild.
That was the affiliation printed on his business card.
But the Team Leader of Team 1 in the Myeongdong Guild remained silent on the other end of the phone.
They both knew the truth.
That title was nothing more than a hollow position.
“You’re not answering.”
“...Understood.”
“So what is it?
This important report of yours?”
The Team Leader of Team 1 answered carefully.
“You know Team Leader Jung Hyunwoo, right?
The one in charge of Team 8.”
“Of course.
He’s skilled, but his flexibility isn’t even half as impressive as his ability.
That’s the problem.”
“It seems he’s caught the scent.”
“Really?
He’s more perceptive than I expected.”
“Yes.
But I wasn’t sure how we should handle it...”
“What is there to think about?
Schedule a raid for the earliest possible date.
An A-rank one.”
“You mean...”
“Team Leader, do you know how many Gate accidents happen every year?
I don’t.
Neither does anyone else.
Nobody cares.”
Park Jihoon clicked his tongue.
“You’re not answering again.”
“Ah.
Understood.”
“And regarding the Peace Guild—or rather, the Jin Taekyung matter...”
Park Jihoon trailed off.
The face of the man who had smiled and tapped him on the shoulder came to mind.
I had a good time tonight.
It had been a sincere statement.
That only made Park Jihoon even less willing to stop.
“Mr.
Jihoon?”
Park Jihoon tossed back the rest of his whiskey.
The crystal tumbler crumpled in his hand like a sheet of paper.
“I finished speaking with the higher-ups today.
They find him irritating.”
That was all.
A single passing remark over dinner with that person.
The matter had been as good as settled from that moment on.
“What?
But this isn’t really the right time for something like that...”
Park Jihoon’s cold voice cut off the Team Leader’s startled protest.
“Isn’t it only natural for a gardener to pull weeds from the lawn?
Your Guild Master has probably already heard the news.
I’m hanging up.”
Click.
The call ended.
In the silence that followed, Park Jihoon stared through the spotless window at the view outside.
Jin Taekyung was long gone.

chapters.title: Chapter 273
paragraphs: “Good morning!”
“Good morning!”
I felt like a mob boss. Every time I took a step, rookie Guild members bowed ninety degrees and greeted me from every direction.
They were fresh out of training camp, still wet behind the ears. In terms of years on the job, I was certainly their senior by a wide margin.
This industry does take seniority and junior status pretty seriously.
The problem was that some of the rookie Guild members were late-blooming Hunters older than me.
“It’s an honor to meet you!”
A rookie who looked well into his mid-thirties bowed, his eyes sparkling.
Then I saw the top of his head shining even brighter, and my heart ached.
“Right. Good luck...”
“Thank you!”
“Thank you!”
What are you, an echo?
And I wasn’t talking to you guys. You thick-haired bastards.
I clicked my tongue inwardly as I studied the rookies, then stopped when my gaze reached one young man.
That one might actually be useful.
He was the most promising of the new recruits. His aura was impressive, and every movement he made was as controlled as a martial artist’s.
Noticing my gaze, the young man grinned.
“Good morning, Senior.”
He was definitely different. Unlike the other rookies, he wasn’t nervous or obsequious.
In my experience, guys like him fell into one of two categories.
Either they had absolutely nothing to back up their pride, or they were confident in their own abilities.
The guy in front of me belonged to the latter.
“You there. What’s your name?”
“My name is Kim Jinsoo. I graduated at the top of the training camp’s B-rank course. I was also the first person to destroy a Golem’s core during this raid.”
“Really?”
“Yes. It was my first A-rank Gate, but it wasn’t as difficult as I expected.”
What an interesting guy.
He had no hesitation about gilding his own face. He was the type who would always make sure he got his share wherever he went.
When I stared at him, Kim Jinsoo gave me an easygoing smile.
“And you don’t need to speak so formally with me, Senior.”
“We just met. I’ll speak casually once we know each other better. The same goes for everyone else, so I’d appreciate it if you skipped the loud greetings from now on.”
“Yes!”
“I’ll keep that in mind, Senior!”
He hadn’t listened to a word I said.
The deafening noise echoed through the hallway, and the office door at the far end slowly opened.
A crisp white dress shirt and neatly pressed black slacks. There was only one Hunter in our Guild who came to work dressed like that.
“You’re all lively this morning.”
“Too lively, if you ask me.”
Like a scene from a commercial, Team Leader Choi held a coffee cup and jerked his chin toward the office.
“Come in and have some coffee. Let’s calm things down.”
The office was spacious and comfortable. Perhaps because it had been decorated to suit Team Leader Choi’s tastes, expensive furniture stood everywhere, and a silver nameplate sat on the desk.
Team Leader Choi Minwoo
Even the nameplate looks expensive.

Moving the Guild House and recruiting all those new Guild members must have cost a fortune. Apparently, it was true that the Peace Guild had extracted an astronomical settlement from the Star Guild, where Won Myunghoon had been Guild Master.
As I admired the nameplate, a cup of black coffee suddenly appeared in front of me.
Team Leader Choi followed my gaze.
“Would you like me to have one made for you? A nameplate.”
“I’m fine. I don’t have a position to put on it.”
“We can always create one. General Team Leader. Division Head. Whatever you want.”
“Anything?”
“Yes.”
“Then I’ll keep it modest. Guild Master.”
“I’m joking. If I became Guild Master, I’d run the Guild into the ground.”
Besides, even if I did become Guild Master, I’d obviously be nothing but a mascot—a puppet Guild Master. What would be the point?
I accepted the coffee and sat on the sofa. More than twenty newspapers were stacked on the glass table.
They ranged from major domestic dailies to foreign newspapers filled with writing I couldn’t even begin to decipher. Just looking at them made my eyes spin.
“You actually read all of these?”
“I read them to keep track of overseas developments and collect industry information. It’s nothing special. Knowing around five languages is enough to read them.”
That was extremely special. Five languages? What kind of life had this man led?
Shaking my head in amazement, I glanced at one of the open newspapers.
A clear color photograph of a man who looked to be in his thirties caught my eye, along with several headlines in bold print.
- The Late Hunter Jung Hyunwoo (pictured) - Accidents Continue: Gates Remain Deadly Even for A-Rank Hunters - Myeongdong Guild Expresses Regret over Unexpected Death...
It looked like there had been another accident.
The Myeongdong Guild? That’s Jihoon’s Guild.
Just as I was about to take a closer look, Team Leader Choi elegantly tilted his coffee cup and continued.
“The Peace Guild will continue to grow. We’ve already recruited twenty B-rank Hunters and thirty C-rank or lower Hunters. That kind of growth is unprecedented in Korea’s long-stagnant market.”
Just as he said, the Peace Guild was growing at a terrifying rate.
Only about four months had passed since the Guild was founded, but if we maintained this momentum, we could easily call ourselves a mid-sized Guild.
Of course, we still have far fewer Hunters than other mid-sized Guilds.
That was because we hadn’t recruited more yet, not because we couldn’t.
The Guild website had already gone down from excessive traffic. I’d heard that hundreds of job inquiries poured in every day.
“And I played a major role in that. I’m the number one contributor.”
“That’s true.”
Team Leader Choi continued smoothly.
“It is true, but I’m not giving you a bonus.”
“...You’re quick to catch on.”
I’d tested the waters just in case, but he hadn’t taken the bait.
As he watched me silently smack my lips, Team Leader Choi smiled.
“However, I’ll consider it favorably if you do me one favor.”
“What favor?”
“I’d like you to take charge of the rookie Guild members for a while.”
“...The rookies?”
“Yes. We were very selective when we recruited them, and they’re all talented, but they’re still rough around the edges.”
“Of course they are. They’re beginners.”
No matter how much training someone went through, a real battle felt completely different from the training camp.
There was a reason people said a lower-rank Hunter with ten years of experience was better than a higher-rank Hunter fresh out of training camp.
“But why ask me? There are other people here.”
“I already spoke to Butler Kim and Song-i this morning. I suggested that we take turns teaching the rookies.”
“What did they say?”
“They agreed. Gladly, without the slightest hesitation.”
“...What about Uncle Kkeokjeong?”
“I haven’t been able to ask him yet. It’s long past his usual arrival time, and he isn’t answering his phone.”
Team Leader Choi checked the time and continued.
“Wouldn’t it be a good idea? The rookie Guild members are hoping that Mr. Jin Taekyung will teach them, too. Most of them applied to our Guild because of you.”
“I appreciate the flattery, but...”
I scratched the back of my head.
Dark Heaven had revealed its fangs in Murim, and Jeok Cheongang was still unconscious.

Even if I spent thirty days in the modern world, only three hours would pass in Murim. I had time to spare, but with A-rank Gates to clear, teaching a bunch of greenhorns wasn’t exactly the most rewarding use of it.
If I was going to spend that time on something else, I’d be a hundred times better off with my family.
“Leave me out of it. From the Guild’s perspective, wouldn’t it be more efficient for me to clear another A-rank Gate instead of teaching those guys?”
“More efficient...”
“Yes. Efficiency.”
“Then I suppose it can’t be helped.”
A sinister smile curled Team Leader Choi’s lips.
“I’ll be counting on you with our rookie Guild members.”
“What?”
“All the A-rank Gates are booked solid. You won’t get into one for at least a week.”
“Don’t lie to me! You scam artist!”
“If you don’t believe me, see for yourself.”
I snatched the paper Team Leader Choi held out. It was densely packed with the reservation schedules for A-rank Gates across the country.
Damn it. He was telling the truth.
“I’ll give you a two-hundred-percent performance bonus this month. You get to go on raids and teach your juniors. How wholesome.”
“Or you can stay home and do nothing.”
The corners of Team Leader Choi’s mouth rose in an infuriating smile.
I was just about to shout, I’m not doing it!, when a System notification rang.
Ding.
System The Quest It Was Too Much Money to Say “I’m Not Doing It!” has been generated! Will you accept the Quest? Y / N
“What do you say?”
“I’ll take that as a yes and get the rookies ready. I’ve already reserved several B-rank Gates.”
Ding.
System You have tacitly agreed. - You have accepted the Quest!
Goddamn it.
—Grrrrr.
The monsters’ harsh breathing closed in from every direction. Twenty pairs of anxious eyes swept their surroundings.
Huff. Huff.
Their breathing grew ragged, and their hands turned white around their shields and weapons.
Perched on a branch high above the ground, I watched the scene unfold.
My face was expressionless, but my mind was occupied by a serious dilemma.
What should I have for dinner?
Galbi, or whole boiled duck for the first time in ages?
Both were too good to pass up...
“Hold the line!”
“What are the damage dealers doing? Damage dealers!”
The shrill screams drew my attention back to the chaos below.
More than a dozen Lycanthropes were charging the shield wall and hammering against it. The pale-faced tanks were being driven steadily backward.
Of course they’re getting pushed back. They’re trying to overpower the monsters head-on.
It wasn’t entirely the tanks’ fault, though. The damage dealers were so flustered that they weren’t doing their jobs, either.
If they had launched suppressive attacks at the right moments, this situation would never have happened.
I’d warned them several times before the raid began, but they were still making the same mistakes.
That line is about to break.
The moment I thought it, the shield wall collapsed amid a chorus of screams.
A gap opened in an instant. One of the most agile-looking Lycanthropes charged through with a characteristic roar.
Its bright yellow predator’s eyes fixed on the healers sheltering behind the shield wall.
—Graaaargh!
—Awoooooo!
To me, it sounded no different from a dog barking, but these rookie Hunters, who were only beginning their second raid, were terrified.
“Aaaah!”
“Eeeek!”
The mage and healer’s screams shook the dark forest.
It’s already noisy enough. Those screams are going to draw another twenty or so over here.
I memorized the faces of the two people who had screamed.
From now on, their nickname is the Pied Pipers.
“Senior! Senior Jin Taekyung!”
“Please help us, Senior!”
Several round faces looked up at me and cried out desperately.
The front line had already collapsed, and the rookies had nothing behind them but an enormous boulder.
The Lycanthropes closed in triumphantly, tightening their encirclement.
How did the monsters end up being better at forming ranks than they are?
I rubbed the sleep from the corner of my eye and answered.
“I told you. If I help, your skills won’t improve.”
“We don’t care if they improve!”
“Well, I do. You know what happens if you make a habit of getting help? You’ll make a habit of shitting the bed during raids, too.”
“We still don’t want to die like this!”
“But... nobody wants to die, you know?”
“Please help us!”
“Don’t give up. Keep fighting. You can do it!”
“Please save us!”
“By the way, what should I have for dinner—galbi or boiled duck?”
“Hey, you fucking bastard!”
It was the balding rookie from that morning. The admiring light that had shone as brightly as his crown was gone, replaced by a gaze full of fury.
“Get down here, you young bastard...”
Thud!
A tank came flying in from somewhere and crashed into him, sending them both sailing into the distance.
The momentum had effectively shifted to the monsters. I was wondering whether it was time to step in when—
Shhk!
—Kauuugh...
A flash of light streaked through the air, and one of the Lycanthropes groaned. Blood gushed from its gaping throat before it crumpled to the ground.
The young man who had landed the precise, powerful strike shouted at the top of his lungs.
“Formation Three!”
His booming voice snapped the others back to their senses one by one.
Soon, the twenty Hunters had re-formed their ranks and begun advancing slowly.
At their head stood Kim Jinsoo.
“Keep pushing! Archers, get your skills ready!”
That kid has potential.
I let out a quiet laugh and jumped down from the tree. Then I swung my spear at the dozens of Lycanthropes drawn by the sound of battle.
Whoooosh!
“You did well.”
“Thank you, Senior!”
Kim Jinsoo grinned and bowed. Behind him, I saw three people with their heads pressed into the ground.
Two were the Pied Pipers, and the other was the balding rookie.
I’d given the balding rookie the special privilege of holding the push-up position.
I had to help him protect what little hair he had left...
“Keep it up next time. You’ll improve quickly.”
“Yes. I won’t disappoint you, Senior.”
“Then go get some rest, Jinsoo. We have another raid in two hours.”
Team Leader Choi had really gone all out. He’d scheduled three raids in a single day.
I was grinding my teeth inwardly when the phone in my pocket began to vibrate.
Designer-Brand Junkie
What was this? Had we developed telepathy?
Still baffled, I answered the call. Team Leader Choi’s urgent voice struck my ear.
“Taekyung. Come to the hospital in Ilsan right now!”
Hospital?

“Then I’ll keep it modest.
Guild Master.”
“I’m joking.
If I became Guild Master, I’d run the Guild into the ground.”
Besides, even if I did become Guild Master, I’d obviously be nothing but a mascot—a puppet Guild Master.
What would be the point?
I accepted the coffee and sat on the sofa.
More than twenty newspapers were stacked on the glass table.
They ranged from major domestic dailies to foreign newspapers filled with writing I couldn’t even begin to decipher.
Just looking at them made my eyes spin.
“You actually read all of these?”
“I read them to keep track of overseas developments and collect industry information.
It’s nothing special.
Knowing around five languages is enough to read them.”
That was extremely special.
Five languages?
What kind of life had this man led?
Shaking my head in amazement, I glanced at one of the open newspapers.
A clear color photograph of a man who looked to be in his thirties caught my eye, along with several headlines in bold print.
- The Late Hunter Jung Hyunwoo (pictured) - Accidents Continue: Gates Remain Deadly Even for A-Rank Hunters - Myeongdong Guild Expresses Regret over Unexpected Death...
It looked like there had been another accident.
The Myeongdong Guild?
That’s Jihoon’s Guild.
Just as I was about to take a closer look, Team Leader Choi elegantly tilted his coffee cup and continued.
“The Peace Guild will continue to grow.
We’ve already recruited twenty B-rank Hunters and thirty C-rank or lower Hunters.
That kind of growth is unprecedented in Korea’s long-stagnant market.”
Just as he said, the Peace Guild was growing at a terrifying rate.
Only about four months had passed since the Guild was founded, but if we maintained this momentum, we could easily call ourselves a mid-sized Guild.
Of course, we still have far fewer Hunters than other mid-sized Guilds.
That was because we hadn’t recruited more yet, not because we couldn’t.
The Guild website had already gone down from excessive traffic.
I’d heard that hundreds of job inquiries poured in every day.
“And I played a major role in that.
I’m the number one contributor.”
“That’s true.”
Team Leader Choi continued smoothly.
“It is true, but I’m not giving you a bonus.”
“...You’re quick to catch on.”
I’d tested the waters just in case, but he hadn’t taken the bait.
As he watched me silently smack my lips, Team Leader Choi smiled.
“However, I’ll consider it favorably if you do me one favor.”
“What favor?”
“I’d like you to take charge of the rookie Guild members for a while.”
“...The rookies?”
“Yes.
We were very selective when we recruited them, and they’re all talented, but they’re still rough around the edges.”
“Of course they are.
They’re beginners.”
No matter how much training someone went through, a real battle felt completely different from the training camp.
There was a reason people said a lower-rank Hunter with ten years of experience was better than a higher-rank Hunter fresh out of training camp.
“But why ask me?
There are other people here.”
“I already spoke to Butler Kim and Song-i this morning.
I suggested that we take turns teaching the rookies.”
“What did they say?”
“They agreed.
Gladly, without the slightest hesitation.”
“...What about Uncle Kkeokjeong?”
“I haven’t been able to ask him yet.
It’s long past his usual arrival time, and he isn’t answering his phone.”
Team Leader Choi checked the time and continued.
“Wouldn’t it be a good idea?
The rookie Guild members are hoping that Mr.
Jin Taekyung will teach them, too.
Most of them applied to our Guild because of you.”
“I appreciate the flattery, but...”
I scratched the back of my head.
Dark Heaven had revealed its fangs in Murim, and Jeok Cheongang was still unconscious.
Even if I spent thirty days in the modern world, only three hours would pass in Murim.
I had time to spare, but with A-rank Gates to clear, teaching a bunch of greenhorns wasn’t exactly the most rewarding use of it.
If I was going to spend that time on something else, I’d be a hundred times better off with my family.
“Leave me out of it.
From the Guild’s perspective, wouldn’t it be more efficient for me to clear another A-rank Gate instead of teaching those guys?”
“More efficient...”
“Yes.
Efficiency.”
“Then I suppose it can’t be helped.”
A sinister smile curled Team Leader Choi’s lips.
“I’ll be counting on you with our rookie Guild members.”
“What?”
“All the A-rank Gates are booked solid.
You won’t get into one for at least a week.”
“Don’t lie to me!
You scam artist!”
“If you don’t believe me, see for yourself.”
I snatched the paper Team Leader Choi held out.
It was densely packed with the reservation schedules for A-rank Gates across the country.
Damn it.
He was telling the truth.
“I’ll give you a two-hundred-percent performance bonus this month.
You get to go on raids and teach your juniors.
How wholesome.”
“Or you can stay home and do nothing.”
The corners of Team Leader Choi’s mouth rose in an infuriating smile.
I was just about to shout, I’m not doing it!, when a System notification rang.
Ding.
System The Quest It Was Too Much Money to Say “I’m Not Doing It!” has been generated!
Will you accept the Quest?
Y / N
“What do you say?”
“I’ll take that as a yes and get the rookies ready.
I’ve already reserved several B-rank Gates.”
Ding.
System You have tacitly agreed. - You have accepted the Quest!
Goddamn it.
—Grrrrr.
The monsters’ harsh breathing closed in from every direction.
Twenty pairs of anxious eyes swept their surroundings.
Huff.
Huff.
Their breathing grew ragged, and their hands turned white around their shields and weapons.
Perched on a branch high above the ground, I watched the scene unfold.
My face was expressionless, but my mind was occupied by a serious dilemma.
What should I have for dinner?
Galbi, or whole boiled duck for the first time in ages?
Both were too good to pass up...
“Hold the line!”
“What are the damage dealers doing?
Damage dealers!”
The shrill screams drew my attention back to the chaos below.
More than a dozen Lycanthropes were charging the shield wall and hammering against it.
The pale-faced tanks were being driven steadily backward.
Of course they’re getting pushed back.
They’re trying to overpower the monsters head-on.
It wasn’t entirely the tanks’ fault, though.
The damage dealers were so flustered that they weren’t doing their jobs, either.
If they had launched suppressive attacks at the right moments, this situation would never have happened.
I’d warned them several times before the raid began, but they were still making the same mistakes.
That line is about to break.
The moment I thought it, the shield wall collapsed amid a chorus of screams.
A gap opened in an instant.
One of the most agile-looking Lycanthropes charged through with a characteristic roar.
Its bright yellow predator’s eyes fixed on the healers sheltering behind the shield wall.
—Graaaargh!
—Awoooooo!
To me, it sounded no different from a dog barking, but these rookie Hunters, who were only beginning their second raid, were terrified.
“Aaaah!”
“Eeeek!”
The mage and healer’s screams shook the dark forest.
It’s already noisy enough.
Those screams are going to draw another twenty or so over here.
I memorized the faces of the two people who had screamed.
From now on, their nickname is the Pied Pipers.
“Senior!
Senior Jin Taekyung!”
“Please help us, Senior!”
Several round faces looked up at me and cried out desperately.
The front line had already collapsed, and the rookies had nothing behind them but an enormous boulder.
The Lycanthropes closed in triumphantly, tightening their encirclement.
How did the monsters end up being better at forming ranks than they are?
I rubbed the sleep from the corner of my eye and answered.
“I told you.
If I help, your skills won’t improve.”
“We don’t care if they improve!”
“Well, I do.
You know what happens if you make a habit of getting help?
You’ll make a habit of shitting the bed during raids, too.”
“We still don’t want to die like this!”
“But... nobody wants to die, you know?”
“Please help us!”
“Don’t give up.
Keep fighting.
You can do it!”
“Please save us!”
“By the way, what should I have for dinner—galbi or boiled duck?”
“Hey, you fucking bastard!”
It was the balding rookie from that morning.
The admiring light that had shone as brightly as his crown was gone, replaced by a gaze full of fury.
“Get down here, you young bastard...”
Thud!
A tank came flying in from somewhere and crashed into him, sending them both sailing into the distance.
The momentum had effectively shifted to the monsters.
I was wondering whether it was time to step in when—
Shhk!
—Kauuugh...
A flash of light streaked through the air, and one of the Lycanthropes groaned.
Blood gushed from its gaping throat before it crumpled to the ground.
The young man who had landed the precise, powerful strike shouted at the top of his lungs.
“Formation Three!”
His booming voice snapped the others back to their senses one by one.
Soon, the twenty Hunters had re-formed their ranks and begun advancing slowly.
At their head stood Kim Jinsoo.
“Keep pushing!
Archers, get your skills ready!”
That kid has potential.
I let out a quiet laugh and jumped down from the tree.
Then I swung my spear at the dozens of Lycanthropes drawn by the sound of battle.
Whoooosh!
“You did well.”
“Thank you, Senior!”
Kim Jinsoo grinned and bowed.
Behind him, I saw three people with their heads pressed into the ground.
Two were the Pied Pipers, and the other was the balding rookie.
I’d given the balding rookie the special privilege of holding the push-up position.
I had to help him protect what little hair he had left...
“Keep it up next time.
You’ll improve quickly.”
“Yes.
I won’t disappoint you, Senior.”
“Then go get some rest, Jinsoo.
We have another raid in two hours.”
Team Leader Choi had really gone all out.
He’d scheduled three raids in a single day.
I was grinding my teeth inwardly when the phone in my pocket began to vibrate.
Designer-Brand Junkie
What was this?
Had we developed telepathy?
Still baffled, I answered the call.
Team Leader Choi’s urgent voice struck my ear.
“Taekyung.
Come to the hospital in Ilsan right now!”
Hospital?

chapters.title: Chapter 274
paragraphs: Hospital? Why so suddenly?
I was just about to ask what had happened when the call ended amid the sound of hurried footsteps.
I tried calling back two or three times, but it was no use.
—The number you have dialed cannot be reached. After the beep, you will be connected to voicemail...
I hung up when the automated message began repeating. Unease crept into my chest.
This was a first. Team Leader Choi was always calm, but he had sounded frantic.
Could it be...?
No. Don’t jump to conclusions already.
This wasn’t the time to think. It was time to move.
Ilsan Hospital. He said Ilsan Hospital.
I grabbed my things and left the changing room. The rookies waiting outside turned their heads when I appeared.
Kim Jinsoo, who had been chatting animatedly in the middle of the group, sprang to his feet.
“Ah, Senior. Are we leaving right away?”
“No. Something urgent has come up.”
The timing could have been worse. There were two hours until the next raid, and thankfully, the next Gate was nearby. It wouldn’t take long to get there.
“Mr. Kim Jinsoo.”
“Yes.”
“You’re the acting team leader for the next two hours.”
“What?”
“Take the others to the next Gate. And don’t start the raid under any circumstances until I get there.”
Kim Jinsoo nodded, looking dazed. I gave him a light tap on the shoulder, then hurried out of the building.
I climbed into a taxi waiting for a passenger, told the driver where to go, and immediately started making calls.
Pick up. Please pick up.
Ring. Ring.
The longer the phone rang, the more anxious I became.
Just as I was about to hang up and try again—
Click.
“Hey, son.”
“What? Is that my brother?”
“Be quiet. Don’t play with the phone while you’re eating.”
“Seriously? Is what Mom’s holding a brick instead of a phone?”
“You little brat!”
“Whew.”
Thank God. It wasn’t them.
The tension left me all at once when I heard my family’s voices on the other end of the line.
Mom asked what was going on, so I gave her a vague excuse and hung up.
Then it must be a problem with the Guild.
Who was in trouble?
If Team Leader Choi wasn’t answering, Butler Kim would have the clearest picture of the situation.
But then someone else’s face flashed through my mind—how quiet he had become lately, and the heavy expression he’d been wearing.
Uncle Kkeokjeong.
My guess was right.
When I called the number saved in my phone, I was greeted not by Im Kkeokjeong’s gruff voice, but by a cold automated message.
—The phone is turned off. After the beep...
I raced to the hospital. Song Song, who had apparently been contacted in advance, was waiting outside with an anxious look on her face.
“You’re here?”
“Tell me while we walk.”
The hospital’s distinctive smell hit me as soon as we passed through the revolving doors.
Civilians, Hunters, hospital staff—the place was packed. We pushed our way through the crowd.
A few people who recognized me pulled out their phones and started taking pictures.
“Hey, hey. Look over there.”
“That’s Jin Taekyung.”
“Jin Taekyung? Lord Fuck?”
“Wow, he looks incredible in person.”
I forced down the stress surging inside me.
As the crowd parted before us like the Red Sea, I whispered to Song Song.
“What happened?”
“I don’t know all the details, either...”
“Just tell me what you do know.”
She bit her lip.
“He seemed to have a lot on his mind lately.”
“On his mind?”
“You know how things are. The Guild keeps growing, and talented young rookies keep joining...”
“That’s enough. I get it.”
Im Kkeokjeong had been with the Peace Guild since its earliest days. But he was also the only D-rank Hunter among us.
Once the Peace Guild began drawing media attention because of me, people had started talking about him, too.
They called him the Guild’s only weak link. Some even left hateful comments telling him to quit instead of trying to ride our coattails.
Im Kkeokjeong had laughed heartily and stopped the rest of us from getting angry over it.
But...
“Whew.”
My chest felt tight.
I had promised myself that I would always look after my people, yet I had failed to pay enough attention to someone so close to me.
“So what happened after yesterday’s raid?”
“Apparently, he went out drinking alone and got into an argument.”
“Go on.”
“I heard he was completely drunk when the fight started... He was badly injured.”
My heart dropped.
Strangers could run their mouths about him being a low-rank Hunter or whatever else they wanted, but Im Kkeokjeong was a D-rank Hunter with twenty years of experience.
Even ten grown men attacking at once wouldn’t be able to bring him down.
“So the other side were Hunters.”
Song Song gave a small nod.
“How badly was he hurt? Is it serious?”
“His treatment is finished for now, but...”
Unable to continue, Song Song hesitated and came to a stop.
A sign reading Special Treatment Ward swayed above her head.
This wasn’t a ward where doctors treated patients. It was staffed by practitioners known as healers.
That alone showed how severe his injuries were.
“You’d better see for yourself.”
The words left Song Song like a sigh as she slid open the hospital-room door.
Rattle.
A harsh medicinal smell washed over me, and I saw three people pacing around the bed.
Team Leader Choi. Butler Kim. And a middle-aged woman I assumed was Im Kkeokjeong’s wife.
My heart pounded as I approached the bed.
“...Uncle?”
Hhhk. Hhk.
Only faint, ragged breathing answered me. Im Kkeokjeong lay beneath the stark white sheets with an oxygen mask over his face.
And then...
The hairy arm he always wrapped around me in a crushing hug had been cleanly severed below the elbow.
The silence stretched on.
Even after leaving the hospital room and climbing to the rooftop, I couldn’t figure out what I should say first.
I listened quietly as Team Leader Choi and Butler Kim explained what had happened. At last, I opened my mouth.
“Where are those bastards now?”
Everyone there knew exactly who I meant.
Team Leader Choi’s lips moved. Then he silently shook his head.
No way.
“You didn’t catch them?”
“No. All three fled the scene.”
“What about the CCTV footage? They were drinking at a store. Their faces should have been recorded.”
“The investigators have already examined it. They have the results.”
Security cameras these days offered practically the same image quality as regular cameras. If the bastards’ faces had been captured clearly, catching them should only be a matter of time.
Hunters and Awakened people were few enough in number to make them easy to track down.
“Then that’s fine. We’ll find those bastards right away and—”
“They say their identities are unknown.”
“What?”
Had I heard him wrong?
When I stared at him in confusion, Team Leader Choi continued with a sigh.
“Their identities are unknown. Apparently, they aren’t any Awakened or Hunters registered as existing in this country.”
“...Could they be ethnic Koreans from China? Or Chinese or Japanese?”
“No. According to the witnesses, the suspects were definitely Korean. They were also the ones who started the argument.”
“Then what the hell is going on...?”
Butler Kim, who had been silently listening to my conversation with Team Leader Choi, suddenly spoke.
“They may be Black Hunters.”
Black Hunters?
Even the name sounded filthy. Butler Kim continued in a low voice.
“Not every Awakened person is registered with the Gate Management Agency and the Association.”
So that was what this unfamiliar term meant?
I rubbed my throbbing temple.
“Aren’t those just unregistered Awakened people?”
In modern society, Awakened people were both powerful shields against Gates and dangerous blades that had to be handled with care.
Even the lowest-rank Hunter possessed strength far beyond that of an average person.
That was why Awakened people were always kept under strict supervision.
Even if they had no intention of becoming Hunters, their names were still placed on the list of Awakened people.
The only way off that list was to die.
An unregistered Awakened person was someone who had failed to register with the Association within the designated period.
Of course, they were sometimes called something else.
Madman.
There was a reason unregistered Awakened people were treated like lunatics.
If they didn’t voluntarily report their Awakening within a month, they stopped being Awakened people and became inmates instead.

To hell with suspended sentences or any other bullshit. They were thrown straight into a prison for Awakened criminals, and when they got out, they even received an electronic ankle monitor as a free gift.
Who would be insane enough to gamble their entire life like that?
“Are there still lunatics like that these days?”
“There always have been, and there still are. Why else do you think crime continues to exist?”
“So the people who attacked Uncle Kkeokjeong were unregistered Awakened people. Then how do we find them...?”
Butler Kim gently cut me off.
“They’re Black Hunters.”
“Yes. In other words, unregistered Awakened people.”
“They’re different.”
Butler Kim stroked his neatly trimmed beard and continued.
“Hunter Jin Taekyung, what do you think is the greatest difference between an Awakened person and a Hunter?”
The question came out of nowhere. I felt like we were going around in circles.
If the person asking hadn’t been Butler Kim, I might have said something.
Suppressing the anger boiling inside me, I answered.
“Training. Just because someone owns a gun doesn’t make them a hunter.”
“The same distinction applies to unregistered Awakened people and Black Hunters.”
“So what you’re saying is...”
Butler Kim nodded.
“Exactly. An unregistered Awakened person who has received the same systematic training as a Hunter. That is a Black Hunter.”
For a moment, my mind went blank.
It was a very simple concept when you thought about it, but I had never considered it before.
And for good reason.
“How is that possible?”
Unregistered Awakened people were felons. Where would they get weapons, and who would provide them with systematic training?
“Are criminal organizations training Black Hunters or something?”
“Criminal organizations... That’s half right and half wrong.”
“Then what is it?”
The answer burst tersely from Team Leader Choi’s mouth.
“Guilds.”
“...What?”

“Money gathers wherever people gather. And wherever money piles up, conflict inevitably follows. Do you really believe today’s Guilds exist purely to protect the world from the monsters inside Gates?”
I couldn’t answer.
I hadn’t become a Hunter to protect the world, either.
The Great Cataclysm was already a thing of the past. When people thought of Hunters, they no longer imagined noble duty or a spirit of self-sacrifice.
They envied the money and fame Hunters possessed, and the people who grew up watching that became Hunters themselves.
Guilds were nothing more than collections of those Hunters.

“Do you know the country’s corporate rankings? From first to tenth place? On the surface, they’re all private companies, but in reality, they’re little more than puppets of massive Guilds. Things aren’t much different overseas.”
Team Leader Choi let out a cold laugh.
Only then did I finally begin to recover from the shock.
“Is... is all of that really true?”
“You once asked me why I left Ares Guild.”
Team Leader Choi said nothing more, but I understood what he meant.
They were all pieces of shit in the same cesspool.
To them, Black Hunters were like daggers concealed up their sleeves. No one knew they existed.
No, they might know and simply pretend not to.
While I was still reeling, another unanswered question came to mind.
“Fine. Let’s say all of that is true.”
I took a deep breath, cooling my head.
“But why did those Black Hunters specifically target Uncle Kkeokjeong? Why go this far just to keep a Guild so far beneath them in check?”
“Taekyung.”
Team Leader Choi cut me off and licked his parched lips.
There was something strange in his eyes. He was looking at me as if I were a greenhorn.
It felt as though I had gone back to the day I first became a Hunter.
“You’re naive.”
Before I could answer, he continued.
“This place is crawling with monsters. It’s the kind of place where one bothersome person—or even an entire Guild—can simply be erased. Get rid of that half-baked common sense.”
That cold sentence pierced my chest.

Butler Kim, who had been silently listening to my conversation with Team Leader Choi, suddenly spoke.
“They may be Black Hunters.”
Black Hunters?
Even the name sounded filthy.
Butler Kim continued in a low voice.
“Not every Awakened person is registered with the Gate Management Agency and the Association.”
So that was what this unfamiliar term meant?
I rubbed my throbbing temple.
“Aren’t those just unregistered Awakened people?”
In modern society, Awakened people were both powerful shields against Gates and dangerous blades that had to be handled with care.
Even the lowest-rank Hunter possessed strength far beyond that of an average person.
That was why Awakened people were always kept under strict supervision.
Even if they had no intention of becoming Hunters, their names were still placed on the list of Awakened people.
The only way off that list was to die.
An unregistered Awakened person was someone who had failed to register with the Association within the designated period.
Of course, they were sometimes called something else.
Madman.
There was a reason unregistered Awakened people were treated like lunatics.
If they didn’t voluntarily report their Awakening within a month, they stopped being Awakened people and became inmates instead.
To hell with suspended sentences or any other bullshit.
They were thrown straight into a prison for Awakened criminals, and when they got out, they even received an electronic ankle monitor as a free gift.
Who would be insane enough to gamble their entire life like that?
“Are there still lunatics like that these days?”
“There always have been, and there still are.
Why else do you think crime continues to exist?”
“So the people who attacked Uncle Kkeokjeong were unregistered Awakened people.
Then how do we find them...?”
Butler Kim gently cut me off.
“They’re Black Hunters.”
“Yes.
In other words, unregistered Awakened people.”
“They’re different.”
Butler Kim stroked his neatly trimmed beard and continued.
“Hunter Jin Taekyung, what do you think is the greatest difference between an Awakened person and a Hunter?”
The question came out of nowhere.
I felt like we were going around in circles.
If the person asking hadn’t been Butler Kim, I might have said something.
Suppressing the anger boiling inside me, I answered.
“Training.
Just because someone owns a gun doesn’t make them a hunter.”
“The same distinction applies to unregistered Awakened people and Black Hunters.”
“So what you’re saying is...”
Butler Kim nodded.
“Exactly.
An unregistered Awakened person who has received the same systematic training as a Hunter.
That is a Black Hunter.”
For a moment, my mind went blank.
It was a very simple concept when you thought about it, but I had never considered it before.
And for good reason.
“How is that possible?”
Unregistered Awakened people were felons.
Where would they get weapons, and who would provide them with systematic training?
“Are criminal organizations training Black Hunters or something?”
“Criminal organizations...
That’s half right and half wrong.”
“Then what is it?”
The answer burst tersely from Team Leader Choi’s mouth.
“Guilds.”
“...What?”
“Money gathers wherever people gather.
And wherever money piles up, conflict inevitably follows.
Do you really believe today’s Guilds exist purely to protect the world from the monsters inside Gates?”
I couldn’t answer.
I hadn’t become a Hunter to protect the world, either.
The Great Cataclysm was already a thing of the past.
When people thought of Hunters, they no longer imagined noble duty or a spirit of self-sacrifice.
They envied the money and fame Hunters possessed, and the people who grew up watching that became Hunters themselves.
Guilds were nothing more than collections of those Hunters.
“Do you know the country’s corporate rankings?
From first to tenth place?
On the surface, they’re all private companies, but in reality, they’re little more than puppets of massive Guilds.
Things aren’t much different overseas.”
Team Leader Choi let out a cold laugh.
Only then did I finally begin to recover from the shock.
“Is... is all of that really true?”
“You once asked me why I left Ares Guild.”
Team Leader Choi said nothing more, but I understood what he meant.
They were all pieces of shit in the same cesspool.
To them, Black Hunters were like daggers concealed up their sleeves.
No one knew they existed.
No, they might know and simply pretend not to.
While I was still reeling, another unanswered question came to mind.
“Fine.
Let’s say all of that is true.”
I took a deep breath, cooling my head.
“But why did those Black Hunters specifically target Uncle Kkeokjeong?
Why go this far just to keep a Guild so far beneath them in check?”
“Taekyung.”
Team Leader Choi cut me off and licked his parched lips.
There was something strange in his eyes.
He was looking at me as if I were a greenhorn.
It felt as though I had gone back to the day I first became a Hunter.
“You’re naive.”
Before I could answer, he continued.
“This place is crawling with monsters.
It’s the kind of place where one bothersome person—or even an entire Guild—can simply be erased.
Get rid of that half-baked common sense.”
That cold sentence pierced my chest.
