paragraphs: You’re naive.
That one sentence I’d heard the day before wouldn’t leave my mind.
I sat in the caregiver’s chair beside the bed, staring blankly at the humidifier spraying mist. Then a thought suddenly occurred to me, and I said it aloud.
“No. It wasn’t naivety.”
Murim was a world that lived up to the phrase a mountain of sabers and a forest of swords.
Bloodshed was commonplace, and death was part of daily life. Might made right, and whoever survived was the winner.
Whenever I witnessed Murim’s cruelty, I thought of the modern world.
An organized welfare system and laws. People’s sense of ethics. A civilization incomparably more advanced than Murim.
But I had been wrong.
“It wasn’t that I was naive. I was just stupid.”
Murim people wore swords at their waists, but modern people hid daggers up their sleeves.
Monsters weren’t confined to Gates. They existed outside them, too.

People wrapped in expensive clothes and wholesome public images who ruled over the concrete jungle. The moment those bastards began drawing the daggers hidden in their sleeves, they revealed themselves as the monsters outside the Gates.
Like Won Myunghoon.
I’d been too soft in my thinking. Even though I knew the world was unfair and fucked-up, I hadn’t been able to let go of my complacency.
This is the modern world. A democratic society in the twenty-first century.
There might be a vicious struggle to prove one’s abilities, but I’d believed something like this could never happen here.
And this is what that got me.
I stared at Im Kkeokjeong sleeping on the bed. Both arms, severed below the elbows, had been treated with recovery magic from a high-ranking healer and advanced potions.
He probably wouldn’t have much trouble with daily life, but there was no guarantee he could return as a Hunter. Potions weren’t a cure-all.
Which bastard was behind this?
Various thoughts swam through my cold mind.
Who had sent the Black Hunter, and why? What were they after?
Cutting off Im Kkeokjeong’s arms could have been a warning to stop here. Or it could have been the opening shot.
I’ll find out what they meant soon enough.
Until then, I had no intention of sitting around and waiting.
Neither did Team Leader Choi.
“Get some rest, Uncle.”
I had just pulled the rumpled blanket over Im Kkeokjeong when—
Bzzzz.
A vibration broke the silence, and my smartphone lit up the darkness.
A short text message from Team Leader Choi.
Team Leader Choi: Come to the Guild House.
I left the hospital as soon as I read the message. It was the dead of night, and two people were waiting for me at the Guild House after everyone else had gone home.
“Ah, Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
“Welcome.”
Team Leader Choi and Song Song.
Butler Kim, whom I’d naturally expected to be there, was nowhere to be seen.
Team Leader Choi noticed my gaze and spoke first.
“He stepped out for a moment.”
“Really?”
It was unusual for Butler Kim to leave Team Leader Choi’s side when he usually followed him like a shadow, but that wasn’t important right now.
I got straight to the point.
“What happened?”
“I should offer you a cup of coffee before I explain, but... take a look at this first.”
Instead of a coffee cup, Team Leader Choi held out his smartphone. The screen displayed the country’s largest online portal.
His long finger tapped an internet article, and a stream of articles divided into different categories appeared.
Among them, I skimmed the article at the very top.

[The Judiciary Bows Before the Fame the Public Has Created. Where Is the Fairness?] [United Party Supreme Council Member Assemblywoman Yoon Seoyoon: “A Death Brought About by One Individual’s Rash Actions. Won Myunghoon Should Have Faced the Judgment of the Law.” Strong Condemnation...] [Self-Defense or Murder?]
The articles dominated the politics and society sections. They didn’t mention my name, but it was obvious who they were talking about.
“When was this posted?”
“An hour ago. And it already has over a hundred thousand views and more than five thousand comments.”
“An hour ago? That would’ve been around four in the morning.”
“Apparently, netizens are more diligent than we thought. Or perhaps I should say the paid commenters are.”
“Interesting.”
Team Leader Choi took a sip of coffee that had gone as cold as the smile on my lips.
“There’s an even more interesting article.”
“More interesting than this?”
“Scroll down a little. It’ll be more than you expected, Taekyung.”
He was right. My finger stopped moving before I realized it.
I stared silently at the bold headline.
[Exclusive Preview of Interview with Former Colleague K: “Famous Hunter J Is a Vile Human Being.”]

When I tapped the article, a preview video of an interview lasting just over three minutes appeared. After a fifteen-second advertisement for a cosmetics brand, the screen filled with the image of a potbellied man in a sharp suit.
His face had been lightly pixelated, but I recognized him at a glance.
“Ha.”
The moment I realized who the middle-aged man—or rather, “former colleague K”—was, a hollow laugh escaped me.
That face was all too familiar. Someone I’d thought I would never see again was right there on the screen.
“I didn’t expect to see him again like this.”
Song Song, looking at the phone over my shoulder, asked, “You really know him?”
“Of course. How could I not?”
“If things were bad enough for him to give this shitty interview, you obviously didn’t get along.”
“No.”
“Then were you close?”
“It’s not that...”
What word could describe the relationship between that man and me? I thought about it for a moment before answering.
“It was fucking awful.”
“Oh.”
No matter how I thought about it, those words fit perfectly.
Our relationship had been that terrible. Considering everything we had been through together, it was almost strange that we had never crossed blades.
I stared at the face that had somehow grown even fatter since the last time I’d seen him.
Mr. Common Sense. Long time no see.
Kim Sangshik, Team Leader of the Sopung Guild.
Back when I was an F-Grade Hunter, he had been the one who goaded the Guild Master into firing me.
The last time I’d seen him was when I ran into him at the Association while getting my Grade reassessed. And now, here he was again.
I heard he got fired from the Guild afterward.

Kim Sangshik was short on ability and overflowing with greed. Despite his name, he was short on common sense, too. He’d gone around doing every idiotic thing imaginable until the Guild finally fired him.
He was the very definition of a petty little man, so there was no doubt he’d been grinding his teeth at the thought of me ever since.
That was probably why he had even filmed an interview like this.
Let’s hear what kind of bullshit he’s spouting.
Right on cue, the reporter began asking questions.
“I hear you have something to say about the recently famous Hunter J. First, is it true that you were his former colleague?”
Kim Sangshik nodded with an uncharacteristically serious expression.
“That is absolutely true. I was Jin Tae... No, I was J’s direct supervisor.”
“More specifically?”
“He was on my team. I became team leader after the Gate accident two years ago. I was also the one who informed J of his dismissal this summer.”
“Oh dear. Was there a reason?”
“There wasn’t just one reason.”
Kim Sangshik then launched into an indignant tirade about why he had fired me.
Every single excuse was a gem of bullshit, but his final exchange with the reporter was the crowning touch.
“I was falsely accused of employment corruption and driven out of the Guild where I had worked for more than twenty years. But I did not fire J for personal gain.”
“Are you saying there was another reason?”
“Yes.”
There had been a reason they had released only a three-minute preview. Kim Sangshik ended it with the solemn expression of a martyr for the nation.
“During the mutated Gate accident two years ago, J threw his teammates to the monsters as prey and fled. He is the kind of man who won’t hesitate to do any ugly and dirty thing to survive...”
I couldn’t properly hear what came after that.
Even after the video ended with a caption promising that the full interview would be released soon, I continued staring silently at the screen.
As if Kim Sangshik might leap out of it if I stared long enough.
Team Leader Choi broke the heavy silence.
“What did you think?”
Ah, what did I think?
Well. I felt like I’d been clubbed in the back of the head, but part of me wanted to laugh. At the same time, something was boiling in my gut.
“Very interesting. Just like you said, Team Leader.”
“I laughed when I first saw it, too. I have a rough idea of what K—or rather, Kim Sangshik—is like. The problem is...”
“The public won’t find it very funny.”
“Exactly.”
The comments section was already on the verge of exploding.
There were more than ten thousand comments now, and I didn’t need to read them all. The most upvoted comment caught my eye.
└ (Best comment): I knew it. I heard it through the grapevine and thought, No way, but I always had a feeling this would blow up someday.
What vine? And what the hell is supposed to blow up?
I didn’t know what kind of asshole had written it, but it was a relief he wasn’t standing in front of me.
If he had been, I would have made sure that at the very least, he heard the next rumor from the overpass to the Yellow Springs.
“Well, I don’t think there’s any need to read more.”
I closed the comments with a hollow laugh.
Team Leader Choi took back his smartphone, loosely folded his arms, and spoke.
“This is organized. It’s clear now that they planned to send the Black Hunter from the very beginning.”
“And they’re the ones creating the hostile public opinion, too.”
“That’s how people are. Once someone starts muddying the waters in earnest, it’s hard to keep your bearings.”
“And I doubt there will be even a single line in the news about Uncle Kkeokjeong being attacked in the middle of all this.”
“You understand the situation well.”
“If I didn’t, I’d be a fucking idiot. Has the investigation team handling the case said anything?”
Team Leader Choi shook his head slightly.
“Don’t tell me they’re in on it, too.”
“There seems to be outside pressure. The CCTV footage is in the other side’s hands, too.”
“Didn’t you say there were witnesses?”
“We’ve lost contact with all three.”
That’s just fantastic.
My fist clenched without me realizing it, and my knuckles cracked.
“They’re really coming at us with a plan.”
“They seem intent on isolating you completely. The interview with Mr. Kim Sangshik is part of that.”
We weren’t dealing with some Third Rate media company that made its money selling gossip.
This was one of the country’s ten largest media outlets.
They would wrap even the most ludicrous bullshit in glossy packaging and present it as credible. Then they would use money and power to lend it even more weight.
For example... testimony from people who knew me well.
“Looks like I’ll get to see my old coworkers again. Though I guess they’ll be hard to recognize once their faces are pixelated.”
I asked Team Leader Choi, who was looking at me with an unreadable expression,
“Why are you looking at me like that?”
“As I recall, Jin Taekyung had a good reputation within the Sopung Guild.”
“I got along with everyone. It was such a dinky little Guild.”
“Then why did you think that?”
“Because there’s one thing that works on everyone. This. And this.”
I brought my thumb and index finger together and wiggled them.
In the end, it all came down to cash. Money was everything.
And for Hunters who risked their lives to make money, the temptation would be even stronger.
“Maybe it’s because I’ve been stabbed in the back so many times in a row, but... these are people I spent seven years laughing and joking around with, and I still can’t trust them.”
If this had happened a few days ago, I might have naively believed in my old coworkers.
But not anymore. The world where dreams, friendship, and common sense meant anything had already vanished from my mind.

“Looking at how the article made it into the politics and society section, it seems like they greased some lawmaker’s palm, too. You think they couldn’t buy off a few low-Grade Hunters who are struggling to make ends meet?”
“It’s obvious. I’ll become the worst bastard alive and get carved up all over the internet. The image I’ve built up until now will come crashing down, and our Guild will come crashing down with it.”
Team Leader Choi, who had been wearing that strange expression the entire time, let out a quiet laugh.
“You’ve improved a little. You can think like a jaded adult now.”
“Are you taking back what you said yesterday about me being naive?”
“I’ll decide after I see what you do from here.”
“What?”
“We can’t just stand by and let them do this to us.”
As he spoke, he tapped his smartphone screen. The phone rang, and someone answered.
“I found it. The tail.”
Butler Kim’s low, smooth voice flowed through the speaker.

“You’ve improved a little.
You can think like a jaded adult now.”
“Are you taking back what you said yesterday about me being naive?”
“I’ll decide after I see what you do from here.”
“What?”
“We can’t just stand by and let them do this to us.”
As he spoke, he tapped his smartphone screen.
The phone rang, and someone answered.
“I found it.
The tail.”
Butler Kim’s low, smooth voice flowed through the speaker.

chapters.title: Chapter 276
paragraphs: The middle-aged man looked like any other ordinary guy from the neighborhood.
A bluish shadow of stubble ran from his sideburns to his chin. His practical hiking clothes bulged around his belly.
At the crack of dawn, he finished stretching with sleep still heavy in his eyes, then began jogging slowly along a path between the rice paddies.
“One-two, one-two,” he chanted in the hearty rhythm peculiar to middle-aged men everywhere.
He was the “tail” Butler Kim had found.
“Are you sure this is the man?”
Inside an equally ordinary minivan, Song Song watched the footage Butler Kim had recorded with magic and muttered doubtfully.
“He looks normal.”
“Wouldn’t it be stranger if he looked extraordinary? It’s not like you can recognize a Black Hunter the way you can a ninth-grade civil servant.”
“Still, that man looks way too normal. Is there something only combat Hunters can recognize?”
“There is.”
I stared intently at the middle-aged man as he finished his jog and entered the mansion.
All I was looking at was a recording, so I couldn’t sense his internal energy. But no matter how talented an actor was, some tiny movement would always give them away.
And I had the eye to see through an act.
“A Peak master...”
“Hm?”
Song Song wasn’t the only one who reacted to my mutter.
Team Leader Choi and Butler Kim looked at me as if to ask what I meant, so I continued.
“...I mean, an A-rank Hunter.”
“You seemed to say something else. Did you say ‘Peak master’?”
“Nope. You must have misheard.”
At times like this, the only answer was absolute denial. If I said I hadn’t said it, what could they do?
Their doubtful looks lasted only a moment before Team Leader Choi and Butler Kim nodded in agreement with my assessment.
“I also believe he is an A-rank Hunter.”
“From what I observed, he ranks fairly high even among A-rank Hunters. I had no choice but to keep my distance because I thought he might detect the surveillance magic.”
Butler Kim’s assessment made sense. He was a battle-hardened veteran of the Great Cataclysm and had observed the man in person.
But Team Leader Choi had a far keener eye than I’d expected.
This wasn’t something just anyone could recognize.
Well, that isn’t important right now.
I asked what I was most curious about.
“But how did you find him? I heard the investigation team had collected all the nearby CCTV footage.”
“We went and retrieved it again.”
No, I meant, how did you manage that?
Before I could ask, Team Leader Choi pressed his thumb and index finger together to form a circle.
“You said this works on just about everyone, Taekyung.”
“It’s an immutable truth. I’ve made frequent use of it myself for some time.”
So he had bribed someone on the investigation team.
Considering Team Leader Choi’s generosity, whoever it was must have made quite a haul.
“Didn’t you say there was outside pressure?”
“When there’s outside pressure, you give them enough money to withstand it.”
Impressive.
But judging by what he said next, even money had its limits.

“It appears that someone fairly powerful has gotten involved. Normally, they should have told us everything without much resistance, but perhaps they were frightened. No matter how much money we fed them, they refused to talk. The CCTV footage was the best we could get.”
“And that man was caught on it?”
“Yes. There were slight discrepancies, possibly because he used an artifact enchanted with Illusion magic, but there’s no doubt it was him.”
I had expected as much, but it seemed the people pulling the strings wielded considerable power.

They had greased the palm of a supreme council member from a political party and manipulated public opinion online as easily as breathing. Even the police and prosecutors—corrupt enough to accept bribes—were afraid to make a move.
It has to be one of the major Guilds.
A major Guild ranked among the top twenty could pull this off. They were effectively corporate giants operating under the name of a Guild.
They had even cultivated an illegal private army of Black Hunters. That told me everything I needed to know.
“So what does that bastard do?”
“He’s a city dweller who fulfilled his dream of moving to the countryside and becoming a farmer.”
Butler Kim smoothly added one more sentence as he handed me a tablet.
“On the surface.”
The tablet contained everything about the “tail.”

He was now in his mid-forties. He had amassed a considerable fortune in the stock market over a decade ago, but after repeatedly collapsing from a chronic illness, he had decided to move to the countryside.
“A chronic illness?”
“We even have the hospital records.”
What kind of chronic illness could an A-rank Hunter have?
I snorted and flicked through the medical records.
“I’ll bet my left wrist that all of this is bullshit.”
Team Leader Choi nodded as if that went without saying.
“Then I’ll bet Jin Taekyung’s right wrist.”
Was this lunatic serious? Why was he betting my wrist?
Casually ignoring my incredulous stare, Team Leader Choi continued.

“In any case, on paper, he’s a perfectly ordinary citizen. Apparently, he was sociable from the day he first settled there. He throws a village feast once every two weeks, so the villagers stopped treating him like an outsider long ago.”
“And no one suspects him in a remote mountain village?”
“He’s a rich, good-natured man.”
“It’s the perfect place to hide and do things. For example, train Black Hunters.”
I examined the final image closely.
A picturesque two-story house. The building itself looked relatively small compared to the spacious yard.
A luxury SUV and a sedan were parked beside the gray stone wall.
How many people are inside?
There had been three men in the group that attacked Im Kkeokjeong. They had no reason to scatter like the Dragon Balls, so I had to assume they were all inside that house.
Ah, wait. Hold on.
“You said he throws a village feast once every two weeks.”
“Yes. Each time, he orders a large quantity of food from outside, but... Ah!”
The village feasts were probably a cover for procuring food.
There might be a lot more of them than I thought.
Did he keep the rest crammed into a basement to train?
Or were they hidden somewhere in the dense forest surrounding the house?
Personally, I hoped they were all huddled together in the basement.
That would make things easier.
“Approaching carelessly could backfire. So for today, we should stop here and—”
“Yes. It’s about time we got started.”
I pulled my hood low and opened the car door.
“I’ll be back.”
“Pardon?”
“The three of you can follow in twenty minutes. It should be almost over by then.”
All three of them stared at me in bewilderment.
Butler Kim, the most experienced among them, spoke first.
“Hunter Jin Taekyung. There is nothing more frightening than an enemy whose capabilities you have not assessed.”
“Yes. I know.”
“I understand that your skills are exceptional, but...”
Butler Kim continued in a grave voice.
“There could be dozens of A-rank Hunters like the man I observed waiting for you.”
“It’s fine. Honestly, the Three Idiots looked stronger than that guy.”
“Don’t worry about it. He just reminded me of some people I know.”
Song Song asked incredulously, “You’re thinking about people you know at a time like this?”
“No. I’m always thinking about you.”
“Eek.”
“Be quiet before I punish you with a confession.”
“Aah!”
Whew. I’m fucking cool. No wonder women run screaming.
I was about to step out of the minivan after chalking up another easy win when Team Leader Choi spoke.
“I want to stop you, but I can’t.”
His expression was impossible to describe.
“Every crazy thing you’ve done has always succeeded.”
“You’ve got me figured out. Then move exactly as I said. It’ll all be over within an hour at most.”
“Black Hunters... Those men have been trained to hunt humans, not monsters. Be careful.”
I couldn’t hold back a short laugh.
“Good. That happens to be my specialty, too.”
“Pardon?”
Leaving the wide-eyed Team Leader Choi behind, I stepped outside.
Beneath a rural night sky strewn with stars, I drew the cool air deep into my lungs and stretched.
As I walked toward the Black Hunters’ base, shrouded in darkness in the distance, I was no longer Hunter Jin Taekyung.
I had become Jin Taekyung, a man of Murim.
Grrrrr.
A beast’s eyes flashed in the pitch-black darkness.
I directed my killing intent at the two Tosa mastiffs baring their teeth at me from behind the iron bars.
“If I hear you bark, you’re becoming dog-meat soup.”
Unless the dogs had attended a Korean language academy, there was no way they could understand me.
But killing intent was another matter.
Killing intent, honed through countless battles and brushes with death, awakened a primal fear.
Even a person with exceptional nerve could wet themselves from it. Dogs, which were even more sensitive to such things, were no exception.
Whine. Whimper.

The Tosa mastiffs sensed my killing intent, hid their teeth, tucked their tails beneath their bellies, and flattened themselves against the ground. Their anxious eyes trembled, and they dared not look my way.
“That’s right. Good dogs.”
Slice.
The moment I cut through the iron bars with Palm Force gathered around my hand and stepped into the yard, I felt as though I had passed through a soft membrane.
Then a blaring siren rang out.
Wheeeeeeeeng!
Ding.
System Alarm Magic has activated! Sound-Blocking Magic has activated! No noise will escape the mansion! Vision-Blocking Magic has activated! The scene inside cannot be seen from outside!
They had taken some precautions.
Even better.
The instant the magic activated, the lights inside the mansion blazed to life.
I sensed dozens of people moving hurriedly inside. A moment later, the steel front door burst outward as if it had exploded.
Bang!
Five men emerged first. The “tail” stood at their center.
The ordinary-looking middle-aged man’s eyes now belonged to a killer.
System Lv. 95 Im Yeongjun
His face twisted, and his eyes trembled. He had clearly recognized me.
I gave him a broad smile.
“I’m with the village youth association.”
“Jin Taekyung!”
“Nope. This is Patrick.”
“How did you find this place?”
“We have a rich Young Master in our Guild. Whatever else you say about him, he knows how to get things done.”
Im Yeongjun’s sharp gaze swept our surroundings.
“Don’t tell me you came alone.”
“What if I did?”
“Looks like you did.”
His mouth twisted.
“Fucking idiot. There’s a limit to how ignorant you can be of the way the world works.”
“That’s what I wanted to say to you. You should’ve chosen your target more carefully.”
“That D-rank nobody who barely qualifies as a Hunter? Did they reattach his arm?”
“They did, but... Apparently, he has some lingering aftereffects. So I came to collect a little compensation.”
“I was going to kill him, but I held back. Be grateful that it ended there. If you don’t want to suffer something worse, lie flat and quiet as a dead mouse.”
“I’ve already seen something worse, and lying flat like a dead mouse isn’t my style. I’m not particularly grateful, either, so isn’t that why I came here?”
Im Yeongjun gave a short laugh.
“Kid, I know you’re excited because everyone around you treats you like a big shot, but don’t make the mistake of thinking we’re ordinary Hunters.”
Just as he said, the aura and killing intent emanating from the Black Hunters were far denser and stronger than those of ordinary Hunters.
I swept my gaze over the mansion.
I could feel them—the presences hiding inside, waiting for orders.
“One, five, ten... Twenty-eight in all. You’ve gathered quite a crowd.”
“I’m not an ordinary Hunter, either.”
Watching his face stiffen, I continued.
“Three. Hand over the three who took part in the attack two days ago, including you. The rest of you, disarm yourselves and tell me everything you know. Then I’ll spare your lives.”
“You crazy bastard.”
“Good. I was worried you might accept.”
That was my first and last offer.
There wouldn’t be another.
Open Inventory. Equip White Flame.
The moment the cool spear shaft filled my grasp, Im Yeongjun shouted, his voice rising almost to a scream.
“Kill him!”
That was the signal.
Dozens of Black Hunters who had been waiting in breathless silence smashed through the walls and windows and surged toward me.
Crash! Shhhhk!
A rain of countless blades and arrowheads poured in from every direction.
My eyes had already gone cold as I watched them.
“You picked the wrong person to mess with.”
Fwoooosh!

chapters.title: Chapter 277
paragraphs: An endless rain of blades and arrowheads poured in from every direction.
I didn’t need to think about how to move. A picture formed naturally in my mind, and my hands moved at the same time as my thoughts.
Fwoosh!
Blue flames wrapped around the spearhead and traced a semicircle.
KRAAASH!
The arrows and weapons caught in its path split apart like tofu.
Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron was hard and sharp enough to destroy Body-Protecting Qi on its own. With Spear Energy added to it, the result was only natural.
Though perhaps not to them.
“Gasp!”
The closest Black Hunter gasped as he stared at his sword, melted by the fiery qi of the Fire Gate Divine Technique.
He was my first target.
Crack!
My grip could crush stone and rebar. When I tightened my fingers around his forearm, his flesh was mangled and bone burst through.
“Gyaaaaaah!”
I had memorized the descriptions of every man who had attacked Im Kkeokjeong. I stared intently at the Black Hunter’s face as he screamed in agony.
“You’re not one of them.”
“Die!”
With a venomous shout, he drove a dagger up beneath my chin. Even in that much pain, his hand didn’t hesitate.
This wasn’t how someone moved in a raid.
These were the movements of a skilled killer.
And I tried to reason with people like these.
Once again, I reflected on what a fucking idiot I’d been.
I let out a hollow laugh and dodged the dagger. At the same time, I seized his other arm and pulled with all my strength.
No, I tore it off.
Crack-crack-crack!
“Urrrrgh...!”
His mouth gaped wide, but the pain was too great for him to scream.
I kicked him in the back as his whole body convulsed. He gasped raggedly, barely clinging to life, while blood gushed from the torn stumps.
I tossed both arms onto the lawn.
“One down.”
A heavy silence descended over the yard.
The Black Hunters faltered after seeing a comrade on their level taken apart in an instant. Behind them, Im Yeongjun’s eyebrows twitched as he watched.
“So you had something to rely on.”
“Yeah. That’s why I came. You don’t seem to have anything, though.”
“You fucking bastard, Jin Taekyung...”
“You should’ve listened while I was asking nicely. Because of you and the other two, this bastard can’t even jerk off by himself anymore.”
My voice remained flat as I swept my gaze around. Wherever my eyes passed, anger and confusion churned across their faces.
Sensing the shift in the atmosphere, Im Yeongjun glared and roared.
“What are you waiting for, you bastards?! I’ll save every last one of you even if I have to bathe you in potions! Don’t be afraid—beat him to death!”
I blinked. For a moment, I wondered if I had heard him correctly.
Ah, right. Potions.
“If you lose an arm or a leg, you’d need at least a high-grade potion. You guys must be loaded.”
“If that’s what it costs to remove one major obstacle, it’s worth every penny. We should’ve eliminated you from the start... I never liked the order we were given.”
“Should you really be blabbing about having someone powerful behind you? Aren’t you worried they’ll kill you to silence you?”
“Kill me to silence me?”
A sneer spread across Im Yeongjun’s lips.
“We’re the ones who silence witnesses. Besides, you’re going to die here anyway.”
“Sure, let’s put that aside for now. There’s something I’ve been wondering.”
I asked with complete sincerity.
“Those potions of yours—can they bring the dead back to life? Or do you carry three or four spare lives around?”
“What?”
Slice!
The spear answered for him. The Black Hunter groaning at my feet lost his head.
I gave the severed head a light kick, sending it rolling toward the others.
“Go on. Save him.”
“Oh, right. Even potions can’t save you if your heart bursts or your head comes off.”
Shhk!
Without hesitation, I flicked my hand.
Two daggers shot out with terrifying speed, becoming flashes of light.
Thwack!
Two Black Hunters staggered, then collapsed.
Their bodies had been unable to withstand the internal energy carried by the daggers. Half of each man’s head was gone.
“Ah. I was trying to plant them neatly between the eyebrows, but I couldn’t control my strength.”
The air around us seemed to vibrate.
The sneer had vanished from Im Yeongjun’s lips. A tempest now raged in the eyes of the remaining twenty-five Black Hunters.
“What the fuck...?”
Suppressed groans rose from here and there. It was something they had never experienced before.
Hunters hunted monsters.
Black Hunters had been created to hunt those Hunters.
Murder, kidnapping, blackmail, and every other filthy job—they had served as enforcers for a major Guild.
But they had clearly never imagined that they might be hunted themselves.
Much less that it would be this one-sided.
I spat phlegm onto the headless corpse.
“You bastards are like dark-path knife fighters.”
No. In terms of their mindset, dark-path knife fighters were actually better.
At least those men accepted that they might someday be stabbed to death in a back alley.
“What... exactly are you?”
His voice was bone-dry, reflecting the turmoil inside him.
I grinned at Im Yeongjun as he stared at me.
“You already know. Why bother asking?”
His gaze turned cold.
“You fooled everyone completely. That’s not the skill of a man who’s only killed once or twice.”
“Killing beasts doesn’t count as murder. Usually, it’s called slaughter.”
Step. Step.
Every time I advanced slowly, the Black Hunters surrounding me in a semicircle took a step backward.
Even the dullest among them must have realized by now that I wasn’t merely an A-rank Hunter.
They could feel the qualitatively different killing intent and the thick scent of blood clinging to me.
“Jin Taekyung.”
Im Yeongjun spoke, his face rigid.
“Taking out that D-rank Hunter was a warning. The order came from above.”
“I didn’t like the way you delivered that warning. Not one bit.”
“I understand your position. Stop here.”
“And if I don’t?”
“The next warning could be worse.”
“Worse?”
“Aren’t you worried about your mother and younger sibling?”
The words caught in my throat.
My slow but steady advance came to an abrupt stop, and strength returned to Im Yeongjun’s voice.
“I can negotiate with the people above us. I’ll act as the stepping stone between you.”
“A stepping stone...”
“You only have to give up one thing. Stop living as A-rank Hunter Jin Taekyung and live as the civilian Jin Taekyung instead. Of course, you’ll be generously compensated.”
I gazed into Im Yeongjun’s eyes.
They held wariness toward me, but they were also the eyes of a wolf constantly searching for an opening.
After a brief silence, a dry voice escaped my lips.
“A stepping stone. That sounds good.”
The corners of Im Yeongjun’s mouth began to rise slightly. I continued smoothly.
“Since you’re a stepping stone, I can just step lightly on you and pass over. I’ll find out who’s on the other side of the stream when I get there.”
There would be no compromise.
They had crossed the line. They were already my enemies.
The modern way and the way of Murim. I had weighed the two against each other and agonized over the choice until the very end...
But today, I would choose the latter.
“And listen, asshole. When you make an offer like that, try doing it with a more trustworthy look in your eyes.”
“Jin Taekyung!”
I heard his shout as I kicked off the ground.
The Black Hunters charged at me with gritted teeth, and I brought my spear down upon them.
Slice!
Boom!
A single punch infused with three-tenths of my internal energy.
The enhancement magic shattered, and the Tower Shield broke apart.
The tank hiding behind it stared at me in shock.
Thrust!
White Flame’s spearhead pierced his chest and burst out through his back.
The mage behind the sturdy shield hurriedly stepped backward.
Thwack!
I flicked my hand, and a dagger buried itself in the back of his head.
But it wasn’t over yet.
“Die!”
Shhhhhk!
Neck, chest, shoulder.
Three blades hurtled toward me with a fierce rush of air. Faint Sword Energy shimmered along their edges, marking their wielders as A-rank Hunters.
Slice!
I pulled the spear from the dead tank’s chest and swung it.
The three swords shattered beneath that lightning-fast strike, and one of the men collapsed clutching his throat.
Blood sprayed over me like a fountain. I released my spear and thrust both palms toward the other two men as they tried to cut me down with their broken swords.
Crack—BOOM!
Compressed air exploded outward.
The Flame Divine Palm struck them squarely in the chest, and they sank to their knees as blood poured from all seven orifices.
Their melted magical armor clung to their upper bodies and burned into their flesh, but they were dead before they could feel the pain.
“Goodbye.”
I had just wiped the blood from my face with my sleeve when—
Shhk! Shhhhhk!
I tilted my head slightly.
An iron arrow thick and heavy enough to pass for a small spear flew past me and buried itself in the stone wall behind me.
Boom!
A cloud of dirt erupted as the arrow drove deep into the solid rock.
Its power was tremendous.
They’ve been getting on my nerves for a while.
Like ordinary Hunters, these men had a balanced distribution of roles.
They had tanks, mages, and melee damage dealers. Naturally, they also had ranged damage dealers.
Three archers had remained inside the mansion from the beginning, loosing arrow after arrow from the second-floor windows.
Shhk-shhk-shhk!
I clicked my tongue and was about to knock the arrows aside with my spear shaft when the air rippled.
A black silhouette burst from empty space and brought a dagger down to cleave my skull.
Shrrrkk!
Fast and precise.
He was clearly a melee damage dealer with an exceptional stealth-type Skill.
How many people had he killed this way?
I didn’t know, but one thing was certain.
Today, he picked the wrong target.
Bang-bang-bang!
I twisted the spearhead with a deft motion.
The iron arrows, which should have been swept aside like fallen leaves, changed course and pierced the Black Hunter who had been trying to bury a dagger in my crown.
Thwack-thwack-thwack!
“Urgh!”
Struck by arrows out of nowhere in midair, the Black Hunter fell with a heavy thud.
I pulled an iron arrow from his upper body. His body convulsed, then went still. At the same moment, I hurled the arrow back in the direction it had come from.
Shhhhhk! Thwack!
The iron arrow infused with internal energy did its job perfectly.
It flew back toward its original owners twice as fast and with twice the force it had carried when first fired.
The three archers, who had been nocking their next arrows, died almost simultaneously.
“This is fucking insane...”
The men who had been about to charge stopped in their tracks. Their hands trembled around their weapons.
They had just watched more than ten of their comrades die in the blink of an eye.
But I had no intention of stopping there.
Shrrrkk! Slice!
I charged straight into them, cutting, stabbing, and smashing.
A mist of blood formed, and someone’s arms, legs, or head flew in every direction.
“Gyaaaaaah!”
“Argh!”
Screams erupted all around me.
From among the terrified enemies, a knuckle wrapped in Fist Energy shot out and slammed into my spear shaft.
Boom!
“Retreat into the mansion!”
I let out a short laugh at Im Yeongjun’s shout. He had bought them a brief moment.
“Did you set up some magic circles as traps?”
“Shut up!”
Whoosh!
He was their leader for a reason. As expected, he was the best of them.
No, at this level, he could even be called a Peak master in Murim.
He knows how to use qi.
One reason Hunters seemed so inferior to martial artists was the way they handled qi.
But Im Yeongjun and the other Black Hunters moved far more efficiently than ordinary Hunters.
Even so, this is as far as they go.
No matter how high someone flew or how low they crawled, there were walls they could never cross.
I drove my fist toward the knuckle.
Refusing to back down, Im Yeongjun gritted his teeth and met my punch head-on.
Boom!
One Strike.
The knuckle shattered.
Boom!
Two Strike.
Im Yeongjun’s fist was crushed.
KRA-BOOM!
Three Strike.
The first move of the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist slammed into his shoulder.
His flesh melted, and his bones were pulverized.
It was as though a fire dragon had devoured his entire shoulder.
Im Yeongjun spat blood and flew backward.
“Team Leader!”
But he still had subordinates left.
The Black Hunters who had waited until the last moment quickly hoisted Im Yeongjun onto their backs and rushed into the mansion.
Thud!
The door had barely closed when layer upon layer of transparent barriers wrapped around the mansion.
A defensive spell?
It had to be an extremely powerful one. It felt even sturdier than the defensive magic Butler Kim had once shown me.
But I didn’t stop walking.
One step carried me to the door. I punched the dozens of defensive barriers.
Four Strike.
The Heaven-Destroying Divine Fist, unleashed with all my strength, hammered into them.
Just as it had shattered an unnamed cliff on Mount Song, the Heaven-Destroying Divine Fist broke and crushed everything blocking its path.
KRAAAAAASH!
With a roar like the sky splitting apart, the defensive barriers were torn to shreds.
The roof flew off, and the walls turned to ash.
Beyond the melted front door, I saw the enemies frozen in place.
Im Yeongjun stood at their center.
His jaw trembled. A single word, sounding almost like a groan, escaped between his lips soaked in blood.
“What... what the hell are you?”
I gladly answered him.
“A monster. Same as you.”
Team Leader Choi had said it before.
This world was teeming with monsters.
So I had decided that, every once in a while, I would become a monster myself.
Just like today.
“Have you ever heard of Tendon-Splitting and Bone-Twisting?”
It didn’t take long for Im Yeongjun to open his mouth.

I tossed both arms onto the lawn.

You guys must be loaded.”

chapters.title: Chapter 278
paragraphs: The beautiful two-story house had been transformed into a haunted ruin.
If the dozens of layers of defensive barriers hadn’t absorbed part of the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist’s impact, the entire place would have been reduced to ash.
Just then, I sensed someone approaching from behind, and a quiet voice sounded in my ear.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
I had been sitting on a half-charred sofa. Turning my head, I answered,
“Yes.”
Team Leader Choi, Butler Kim, and Song Song stood behind me.
Their expressions were complicated as they looked at me. Considering they had seen the bodies strewn miserably across the garden, it was only natural.
Being drenched from head to toe in blood probably didn’t help my appearance, either.
Song Song cautiously asked, “Did you... kill all of them?”
“Yeah.”
“I’m kidding. I spared the ones who surrendered.”
Then I added gently, “For now.”
The answer was for Song Song, but the warning was meant for Team Leader Choi and Butler Kim.
Team Leader Choi asked with concern, “Are you hurt anywhere?”
“As you can see, I’m fine.”
“What about the survivors?”
“I gathered them in one place.”
“Without taking any other measures?”
“Of course I did. For the next few hours, they’ll be no different from corpses that can still breathe, so don’t worry.”
The personal measure I had taken was a Pressure-Point Strike.
After striking their Mute Acupoints, Paralysis Acupoints, and Sleep Acupoints, I had stacked the Black Hunters neatly inside the only room left standing.
I had used force to subdue them, but I wasn’t some blood-crazed murderer who intended to kill even those who surrendered.
More importantly, they might prove useful later.
“You did well. But...”
Team Leader Choi’s gaze shifted to the man sprawled at my feet.
“Who is that?”
“The owner of this house.”
I rolled him over with my foot, revealing a man in his forties.
Im Yeongjun, the homeowner and leader of the Black Hunters.
His entire body was so drenched in blood that he could easily have been mistaken for a corpse, but he was very much alive. In fact, there wasn’t a single wound left on him.
Butler Kim examined him and muttered knowingly, “You used potions. Several times, at that.”
“Yes.”
“Did you torture him?”
“You have sharp eyes.”
“It was common during the Great Cataclysm. There were plenty of people worse than Black Hunters.”
Song Song’s expression darkened at the word torture. But after a faint sigh, she placed a hand on my shoulder.
“That couldn’t have been easy.”
It was only natural for her to be repulsed. Even I, accustomed as I was to the ways of Murim, didn’t feel comfortable about what I had done.
But Im Yeongjun had been far more tight-lipped than I had expected. Ordinary threats would never have made him talk.
“These aren’t ordinary opponents. Someone had to do it,” Team Leader Choi said.
“If you hadn’t, Hunter Jin Taekyung, I would have,” Butler Kim added. “Don’t take it too much to heart.”
They were right. Someone had to do it. My hands were already stained with blood, so there was no reason to balk at torture now.
I shook my head to clear away my troubled thoughts, then opened my mouth.
“There’s no physical evidence. Apparently, they deleted all the relevant information the moment I broke in and the alarm magic went off.”
“All of it?”
“Yes. There weren’t even any computers in the house. Only two people, including Im Yeongjun, had cell phones. Even those were burner phones with no identifiable source.”
I showed them the remains of the cell phone I had collected beforehand.
Even someone as hopeless with technology as me could tell that recovering anything from it would be impossible. Every component had been crushed, and they had burned the SD card.
Team Leader Choi clicked his tongue when he saw the wreckage.
“Thorough. At this point, there’s no way any documents would have been left behind.”
“They didn’t.”
“What about the other Black Hunters?”
“Ten survived, but none of them knows anything. I killed the one who was effectively their deputy. Im Yeongjun personally recruited and trained everyone here.”
From what I had gathered, they operated as a thoroughly compartmentalized organization.
Everything involving the Black Hunters—from laundering their identities to paying them—had gone through Im Yeongjun.
“It’s fortunate that Im Yeongjun survived, at least. What did he tell you?”
“That...”
I suddenly stopped speaking.
The one sentence he had screamed like a howl after experiencing Tendon-Splitting and Bone-Twisting three times still echoed in my ears.
“M-Myeongdong Guild! I said Myeongdong Guild!”
A major Guild that might not rank among the country’s top ten, but easily placed within the top twenty.
And...
Jihoon.
It was also the Guild where an old friend I had met again recently belonged.
After some thought, I spoke again.
“Could you give me a little time?”
“There’s something I need to check personally.”
Team Leader Choi studied me for a moment, then nodded.
“We’ll start cleaning up the scene. Look into it and let us know.”
“I will.”
“Let’s get started right away.”
At Team Leader Choi’s words, Butler Kim swung the staff he had been using like a cane.
The tightly shut door opened. The ten Black Hunters whose acupoints I had struck floated into the air and filed out of the house one after another.
Im Yeongjun was among them, of course.
“Everyone, stand back.”
After delivering the warning in a low voice, Butler Kim began chanting.
Mana surged. Enormous flames engulfed the two-story house, which had barely managed to retain its shape.
The fire swept through the garden and would not stop until it had erased everything.
Fwoooosh!
A cloud of acrid smoke billowed up with the flames.
Yet the quiet rural village surrounding the mansion remained peaceful.
With magic blocking all sight and sound, the mansion wouldn’t be discovered until much later.
“Will this be enough?”
“More than enough. Even if we left it alone, they would step in and erase every trace of this place themselves.”
People had vanished overnight, and a house had burned down. But that was all.
The villagers would talk about it for a while, but nothing would come of it.
That was how monsters with power and authority operated.
There was only one thing I wanted to know.
Garam Middle School Classmate Park Jihoon
Which side did the owner of the number saved in my phone actually belong to?
The darkness had yet to lift when Park Jihoon dressed and left his house at dawn.
A uniformed chauffeur was waiting for him at the entrance with a limousine.
“You’re here, sir.”
“What’s going on? Why am I being picked up out of the blue at this hour?”
“I’m afraid I don’t know. The Guild Master only instructed me to collect you from your home.”
Fair enough. What would a mere driver know?
Clicking his tongue softly, Park Jihoon climbed into the car. Perhaps because of the early hour, the roads were deserted.
Some time later, the limousine glided to a stop in a part of Hannam-dong lined with luxury apartments and villas.
Before them stood a massive mansion.
One of the guards stationed along the stone wall ran over and bowed to Park Jihoon.
“He’s waiting inside.”
Park Jihoon passed through iron gates reminiscent of a European nobleman’s estate and crossed a garden larger than an athletic field before finally meeting the man who had summoned him.
“Have you eaten breakfast?”
The man was in his fifties, with hair that had gone half gray. His age belied his imposing physique, and well-developed chest muscles showed beneath his white robe.
Park Jihoon bowed his head.
“Not yet.”
“Then come eat. The beef-and-radish soup turned out especially well today.”
It was barely six in the morning. No one would welcome breakfast this early, especially after being dragged out of bed.
Nevertheless, Park Jihoon thanked him and picked up his spoon without complaint.
“Aren’t you eating, Guild Master?”
“I’ve already eaten. Don’t mind me. Finish your meal.”
The man casually unfolded a copy of that morning’s newspaper.
The front page featured a photograph of a middle-aged man in a suit bowing his head solemnly.
Park Tae Seop, Guild Master of Myeongdong Guild, visits the wake of the late Hunter Jung Hyunwoo. “My heart is filled with grief. I bow my head and apologize to the bereaved family.”
Only then did Park Jihoon understand why he had been summoned.
The old geezer’s pissed.
The man, identical to the one in the color photograph, asked without looking up from the newspaper, “How’s the picture? Did I come out well?”
“Yes. You’re naturally handsome.”
“That’s your problem. No matter what you say, it always sounds like empty flattery.”
“I mean it.”
At the unhesitating answer, the middle-aged man—Park Tae Seop, Guild Master of Myeongdong Guild—raised his eyebrows.
It was a sign that his patience had run out.
“Jung Hyunwoo. Why did you kill him?”
Here it comes.
Park Jihoon quietly set down his spoon.
“I caught a whiff.”
“Then you should have stopped at covering your nose.”
“That was Myeongdong Guild’s job. Mine is to wring the necks of anyone who catches the stink before they can go blabbing about it.”
“Without my permission?”
“Do I need permission, too?”
Bang!
Park Tae Seop slammed his fist into the dining table. The table shattered with a splintering crack, sending glass and food flying in every direction.
“Guild Master!”
The guards who came rushing in were met by a furious roar.
“Get the hell out, all of you! Don’t take another step inside until I give the order!”
They froze for a moment, then bowed and withdrew.
Park Jihoon calmly pulled out a handkerchief and wiped the soup splashed across his face.
“What a shame. It was delicious.”
“You insolent brat, still stinking of your mother’s milk...”
“We both reek of something rotten anyway. A little milk on top won’t make any difference.”
“I built this Guild with my own blood! And a little shit like you kills one of my Guild members without even telling me?”
“Come now, Guild Master.”
Park Jihoon’s smooth, unlined brow furrowed.
The handkerchief in his hand dropped onto the shattered remains of the table.
“What else was I supposed to do?”
“What did you say?”

“Don’t you know how troublesome it gets when people who catch the stink start talking? One spark, and the whole house burns down. If it were only your house at risk, I wouldn’t have said a word. But the fire would spread to our side, so I stepped in.”
“Even so, you—!”

“And I’d appreciate it if you got one thing straight. You’re a war hero who fought and bled during the Great Cataclysm? I’ll give you that. But claiming that Myeongdong Guild belongs to you is a bit...”
Park Jihoon let out a short laugh and rose from his seat.
“Thank you for breakfast. Though I barely managed a few spoonfuls.”
Park Tae Seop trembled as he watched him.
“Sit down.”
“If you have anything else to say, call me. If you keep this up, I’m going to lose my respect for a great senior like you.”
“I said sit down.”
The air around them churned violently.
Park Tae Seop, Guild Master of Myeongdong Guild, was a hero forged by the Great Cataclysm and one of the country’s highest-ranking rankers.
But Park Jihoon knew the man couldn’t lay a hand on him.
“I’ll see you next time.”
He bowed politely and was about to turn away when Park Tae Seop spoke again.
“The sparks you scattered are about to burn the whole house down. You didn’t know that?”
“What are you talking about? I handled Team Leader Jung’s matter thoroughly enough to prevent any loose talk.”
“The Black Hunters. I heard they recently went after a D-rank Hunter from the Peace Guild.”
Park Jihoon’s face stiffened.
He instinctively realized that something had gone seriously wrong.
“...What is it? What happened?”
At that moment, the phone inside Park Jihoon’s coat pocket began to vibrate.
As though possessed, he pulled it out and stared at the name filling the screen, his eyes darkening.
Jin Taekyung

The personal measure I had taken was a Pressure-Point Strike.
After striking their Mute Acupoints, Paralysis Acupoints, and Sleep Acupoints, I had stacked the Black Hunters neatly inside the only room left standing.
I had used force to subdue them, but I wasn’t some blood-crazed murderer who intended to kill even those who surrendered.
More importantly, they might prove useful later.

“The owner of this house.”
I rolled him over with my foot, revealing a man in his forties.
Im Yeongjun, the homeowner and leader of the Black Hunters.
His entire body was so drenched in blood that he could easily have been mistaken for a corpse, but he was very much alive.
In fact, there wasn’t a single wound left on him.
Butler Kim examined him and muttered knowingly, “You used potions.
Several times, at that.”
“Yes.”
“Did you torture him?”
“You have sharp eyes.”
“It was common during the Great Cataclysm.

Song Song’s expression darkened at the word torture.
But after a faint sigh, she placed a hand on my shoulder.
“That couldn’t have been easy.”
It was only natural for her to be repulsed.
Even I, accustomed as I was to the ways of Murim, didn’t feel comfortable about what I had done.
But Im Yeongjun had been far more tight-lipped than I had expected.
Ordinary threats would never have made him talk.
“These aren’t ordinary opponents.
Someone had to do it,” Team Leader Choi said.
“If you hadn’t, Hunter Jin Taekyung, I would have,” Butler Kim added.
“Don’t take it too much to heart.”
They were right.
Someone had to do it.
My hands were already stained with blood, so there was no reason to balk at torture now.
I shook my head to clear away my troubled thoughts, then opened my mouth.
“There’s no physical evidence.
Apparently, they deleted all the relevant information the moment I broke in and the alarm magic went off.”
“All of it?”
“Yes.
There weren’t even any computers in the house.
Only two people, including Im Yeongjun, had cell phones.
Even those were burner phones with no identifiable source.”
I showed them the remains of the cell phone I had collected beforehand.
Even someone as hopeless with technology as me could tell that recovering anything from it would be impossible.
Every component had been crushed, and they had burned the SD card.
Team Leader Choi clicked his tongue when he saw the wreckage.
“Thorough.
At this point, there’s no way any documents would have been left behind.”
“They didn’t.”
“What about the other Black Hunters?”
“Ten survived, but none of them knows anything.
I killed the one who was effectively their deputy.
Im Yeongjun personally recruited and trained everyone here.”
From what I had gathered, they operated as a thoroughly compartmentalized organization.
Everything involving the Black Hunters—from laundering their identities to paying them—had gone through Im Yeongjun.
“It’s fortunate that Im Yeongjun survived, at least.
What did he tell you?”
“That...”
I suddenly stopped speaking.
The one sentence he had screamed like a howl after experiencing Tendon-Splitting and Bone-Twisting three times still echoed in my ears.
“M-Myeongdong Guild!
I said Myeongdong Guild!”
A major Guild that might not rank among the country’s top ten, but easily placed within the top twenty.
And...
Jihoon.
It was also the Guild where an old friend I had met again recently belonged.
After some thought, I spoke again.
“Could you give me a little time?”
“There’s something I need to check personally.”
Team Leader Choi studied me for a moment, then nodded.
“We’ll start cleaning up the scene.
Look into it and let us know.”
“I will.”
“Let’s get started right away.”
At Team Leader Choi’s words, Butler Kim swung the staff he had been using like a cane.
The tightly shut door opened.
The ten Black Hunters whose acupoints I had struck floated into the air and filed out of the house one after another.
Im Yeongjun was among them, of course.
“Everyone, stand back.”
After delivering the warning in a low voice, Butler Kim began chanting.
Mana surged.
Enormous flames engulfed the two-story house, which had barely managed to retain its shape.
The fire swept through the garden and would not stop until it had erased everything.
Fwoooosh!
A cloud of acrid smoke billowed up with the flames.
Yet the quiet rural village surrounding the mansion remained peaceful.
With magic blocking all sight and sound, the mansion wouldn’t be discovered until much later.
“Will this be enough?”
“More than enough.
Even if we left it alone, they would step in and erase every trace of this place themselves.”
People had vanished overnight, and a house had burned down.
But that was all.
The villagers would talk about it for a while, but nothing would come of it.
That was how monsters with power and authority operated.
There was only one thing I wanted to know.
Garam Middle School Classmate Park Jihoon

chapters.title: Chapter 279
paragraphs: Jin Taekyung.
The three-syllable name stood out clearly on the screen.
Park Jihoon was about to press the call icon without thinking when a thunderous shout stopped him.
“I’m not finished talking. Put that damn phone away and sit down right now!”
“Are you deaf?”
“...No, sir. Go ahead.”
Park Jihoon turned off the screen and dropped heavily into a chair. Park Tae Seop glared at him with blazing eyes.
“Was killing a Team Leader-level Hunter without permission not enough for you?”
“I was under the impression that matter had already been discussed. ‘That person’ said they had personally contacted you to ask for your understanding.”
“Understanding? You mean threaten me?”
“They’d be hurt if they heard you say that.”
“What the hell do you have against Jin Taekyung and the Peace Guild that you’d go so far as to send Black Hunters...?”
“That’s enough.”
Park Jihoon cut him off, his voice hard.
“There’s no need for you to know things you’re better off not knowing.”
“Isn’t it important that the Guild Master accepted the proposal? One way or another, the result matters more than the process.”
“Yeah. So is that why you turned that important result into this mess?”
Park Jihoon frowned. Park Tae Seop’s complaints were nothing new, but this was the first time he had been so openly hostile.
What the hell happened?
“That’s enough bickering. What went wrong?”
Park Tae Seop, breathing hard with anger, tossed out a single sentence.
“Two hours ago, Team 11 sent an emergency message.”
To the outside world, Myeongdong Guild had ten teams.
But that was merely its public face. Team 11, the team Park Tae Seop had mentioned, did not officially exist. It was made up entirely of Black Hunters.
“Did you say an emergency message?”
“If you have eyes, see for yourself.”
Park Tae Seop pulled something from his robe pocket and tossed it over. Park Jihoon caught an old-fashioned cell phone so outdated that he couldn’t even guess when it had been made.
The call history had been wiped clean. The inbox held only a single text message, received two hours earlier.
Intruder detected.
One short line.
But its contents were anything but ordinary.
Park Jihoon closed the phone and asked, “Where was it?”
“Far away. A backwater hole beside some nameless mountain. It’s outside the safe zone, and there aren’t any Gates nearby, so no one has any reason to go there.”
“Any word after that?”
“If there had been, would I be bringing this up?”
“So they’re out of contact.”
“I sent people to check, but... I have a bad feeling about this.”
Park Jihoon felt the same.
Seven years ago, as soon as he had been assigned to Myeongdong Guild, his first task had involved Team 11.
Park Tae Seop, the Guild Master of Myeongdong Guild, had strongly objected to hiding and training criminals. But he had been unable to defy the orders of that person.
That was how they had gathered roughly thirty Black Hunters.
Three A-rank Hunters. And twenty-five B-rank Hunters.
They were a force powerful enough to rival—or even surpass—Team 1, Myeongdong Guild’s elite.
And now they had lost contact after an intruder appeared.
Just as unease began creeping through Park Jihoon’s chest—
Brrrrr.
The phone in his inner coat pocket began to vibrate again. The longer it continued, the more his unease grew.
Ring. Ring...
The call went unanswered and ended in voicemail, just like every time before.
This was already my tenth call. I’d sent him a text ages ago, too, but he hadn’t replied.
He should be at work by now.
The entrance of the high-rise building towering over the heart of Seoul was crowded with people. I was watching them absently when someone spoke to me.
“Excuse me.”
The man addressing me was dressed in a suit.
His face was angular, and his eyes were sharp. I could sense the solid build beneath his clothes and the energy coiled inside him. The man beside him, apparently his colleague, was much the same.
I put away my phone and answered,
“Yes, excuse me.”
The suited man hesitated, then opened his mouth. The name tag on his chest clearly displayed both his name and his affiliation: Myeongdong Guild.
“We’re from the Security Team. We received a report about you.”
“I’m not a sir. What kind of report?”
“We checked the CCTV footage and saw you loitering in front of our building for quite a while... Is there something you need?”
Their eyes were full of suspicion and wariness.
I was wearing track pants and a hoodie, with a cap pulled low over my face and sunglasses on top of that. A guy dressed like this peering into the building was bound to attract a report.
“Sir, would you mind moving somewhere else for a moment?”
“No, I’d rather not. And I told you, I’m not a sir.”
“It’ll only take a moment.”
Despite his fairly polite tone, his actions were anything but.
Whoosh!
With a short rush of wind, both men reached for me at the same time.
In the next instant, question marks appeared on their once-confident faces.
Tap. Grab.
“Huh?”
“What?”
I casually caught both their wrists and put on a stern expression.
“Y-You rude punks. How dare you lay hands on your teacher?”
“W-Wait a second.”
“Who the hell are you? Let go!”
The two C-rank Hunters from the Security Team were visibly flustered. No matter how hard they strained, they couldn’t move an inch, and their mouths fell open.
Should I break them?
I considered it for a moment, but the time wasn’t right yet. I released their wrists before the commotion could grow any larger.
“Let’s not go around putting our hands on people.”
Rubbing their reddened wrists, the two men cautiously asked, “Were you... a Hunter?”
“Excuse me, but could we have your name and affiliation?”
“I’m Jin Taekyung of the Peace Guild.”
“What?”
“Could you be the Lord Fuck I’ve heard about?”
“...You must have seen that internet broadcast.”
I’d rather be the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi. What the hell is Lord Fuck supposed to mean?
I sighed and lowered my sunglasses slightly. The two men gasped and immediately bowed deeply.
“It’s an honor to meet you.”
“You’re much more handsome in person.”
Their eyes sparkled like high school students who had just spotted their favorite idol. Judging by their reaction, they clearly knew nothing about what was really going on.
Of course. Anything involving the Black Hunters would be top secret. If an ordinary Security Team Hunter knew about it, the secret would have leaked long ago.
“But what brings you to our Guild...?”
“I came to see someone I know.”
“Someone you know?”
I pulled a thin piece of paper from my wallet and held it out. It was Park Jihoon’s business card, which I’d received a while back and kept.
“Hunter Park Jihoon of Team 1?”
The Security Team Hunter tilted his head at the card, then turned to his colleague.
“Senior, do you know who this is?”
“Who?”
“He’s supposedly Hunter Park Jihoon from Team 1. I know all the Team 1 Hunters, but I can’t quite place him...”
“Park Jihoon, Park Jihoon... Oh, him. You know. That guy.”
He elbowed his colleague in the side, and only then did the other man let out an “Oh!”
The two of them looked back and forth between me and the business card with fascinated expressions.
What’s with that reaction?
My eyes narrowed. Unable to see my expression behind my sunglasses, the Security Team Hunter asked, “Are you close with Hunter Park Jihoon?”
“We went to middle school together.”
“Ohhh, so you’re friends.”
I gave him a gentle smile.
“Well, for now.”
“Huh?”
“I’m joking.”
Maybe.
Oblivious to my thoughts, the Security Team Hunters laughed and kept asking questions.
“So you came to see Hunter Park Jihoon?”
“Yes. He wasn’t answering his phone, and he wasn’t at home, either. I thought I might find him at work.”
“We’re sorry. We had no idea.”
“You were just doing your job, so don’t worry about it. More importantly, is Jihoon inside?”
The senior Security Team Hunter answered, “He probably won’t come in today, either.”
“Today, too?”
“Yes. He hardly ever comes to work. Maybe once a month? I’ve been here almost a year and have only seen him a few times. This guy’s barely been here a month, so...”
“Sounds like Myeongdong Guild’s Hunters don’t come to work very often.”
“Of course they do. I don’t know why, but everyone just accepts that he doesn’t.”
Yeah. Why is that?
I’d never heard of a Guild Hunter who showed up for work once a month.
The question that had taken root in one corner of my mind grew deeper.
Without letting it show, I said, “Could you try contacting Jihoon for me? I understand there’s a separate phone for Guild summons.”
“Uh, that’s...”
The two men hesitated, so I made them an offer they couldn’t refuse.
“I came to discuss a cooperative raid. If I put in a word, I think I could get another person or two added...”
“Whoa.”
“Are you serious?”
Of course not.
It was all a lie from beginning to end. But I kept a perfectly straight face and continued.
“You’re both C-rank, right?”
“Yes, sir.”
“How did you know?”
“I can tell at a glance. But you two seem too good to waste away in the Security Team.”
Strictly speaking, a Guild’s Security Team was little more than a backwater department.
If a Hunter were truly skilled, why would the Guild waste him on guard duty? From the Guild’s perspective, sending him on raids would be far more profitable.
There was no way the two Security Team Hunters didn’t know that. Their eyes lit up.
“I’ll contact him right away!”
“I’d appreciate that.”
“Is there anything else you need?”
“Would it be all right if I looked around the Guild for a bit? I can wait for Jihoon inside.”
“Yes. Yes, of course.”
Unlike the senior, who was bowing obsequiously, the junior Hunter’s face had gone stiff.
He’d only joined a month ago. His sense of duty and loyalty to the company were probably still burning bright.
“Senior, I don’t think that’s right.”
“What? You little punk.”
“I really respect Hunter Jin Taekyung, too, but doesn’t this violate the Guild’s internal regulations?”
“Hey, you idiot!”
The senior seemed to realize he’d slipped up as soon as he shouted. He glanced at me, then lowered his voice to a whisper.
“Are you crazy? It’s an A-Rank Gate. You could rot in the Security Team for three years and never get another opportunity like this.”
“Then we should report it to the Team Leader first...”
“God, you’re so damn rigid. Why do we need to report that he wants to look around for a moment? It’s not like he’s just anybody. He’s Hunter Jin Taekyung.”
“No, even so...”
“Please. Try to live with a little yutori, okay?”
“Yutori?”
The junior Hunter’s expression suddenly turned grave.
“In the current climate, please refrain from carelessly using words like that. It makes me uncomfortable.”
“You’re out of your mind. Do you want your life at the Guild to get uncomfortable?”
What a complete circus.
Clicking my tongue, I stepped forward. The junior Hunter flinched, then thrust out his chest.
“D-Do you have something to say?”
“No. I was just moved by what I heard.”
“What?”
“You’re a true patriot, and your loyalty to the company goes without saying. I’ll be sure to mention it when I meet the Guild Master of Myeongdong Guild later.”
“T-The Guild Master?”
“Yes. Jihoon said he’d speak to the Guild Master, too. I should make sure to mention that there’s an excellent talent here.”
I glanced at the name tag on the junior Hunter’s chest and added, “Hunter Kim Cheol Soo.”
The eyes of Kim Cheol Soo, devoted company man, trembled with emotion.
With my most amiable smile, I asked, “Can I go in now?”
Kim Cheol Soo shouted at the top of his lungs, “Irasshaimase!”
“...Ah, yes. Arigato.”
The luxurious twenty-story building belonged to Myeongdong Guild.
The senior Hunter had pulled rank to ditch his junior and come with me. He chattered away as we walked.
“The first through ninth floors house the civilian departments—tax, accounting, corporate affairs, and so on. From the tenth through the nineteenth floors, each floor belongs to a raid team.”
“What about the twentieth?”
“The Guild Master and the board of directors, obviously.”
“I see.”
“Team 1 is the Guild’s elite team, so they’re on the nineteenth floor.”
Ding.
The elevator arrived as he finished speaking. I pressed the button for the nineteenth floor and was waiting for the doors to close when—
“Hey, hey! Wait!”
The senior Hunter hurriedly pressed the open button.
The doors slid open, and a middle-aged man with a receding hairline stepped inside.
He gave us a sidelong glance, then covered the receiver with one hand as he spoke.
“Yes, yes. No, it’s nothing. Just the elevator. Yes.”
The energy coming from him as he continued his important call was formidable.
An A-rank Hunter?
The senior Hunter had gone rigid at the man’s appearance. I gave him a questioning look, and he discreetly raised one finger while mouthing the answer.
Team 1 Leader.
No wonder he hadn’t pressed a button.
As Team 1 Leader, he was naturally headed for the nineteenth floor. I listened to his call.
And in the next instant, a familiar voice pierced my ears.
“How does it make any sense that all twenty-eight of them were wiped out? Hurry up and—”
My body trembled as if I’d been electrocuted.
That familiar voice.
And the number twenty-eight.
So it was you.
My hand moved the instant the thought struck me.
Grab!
“Ghk! Who the hell are you...?”
I clamped a hand around the Team 1 Leader’s throat like a shackle and whispered into the receiver.
“Park Jihoon. You fucking bastard.”

sentences.text: Jin Taekyung.
The three-syllable name stood out clearly on the screen.
Park Jihoon was about to press the call icon without thinking when a thunderous shout stopped him.
“I’m not finished talking.
Put that damn phone away and sit down right now!”
“Are you deaf?”
“...No, sir.
Go ahead.”
Park Jihoon turned off the screen and dropped heavily into a chair.
Park Tae Seop glared at him with blazing eyes.
“Was killing a Team Leader-level Hunter without permission not enough for you?”
“I was under the impression that matter had already been discussed.
‘That person’ said they had personally contacted you to ask for your understanding.”
“Understanding?
You mean threaten me?”
“They’d be hurt if they heard you say that.”
“What the hell do you have against Jin Taekyung and the Peace Guild that you’d go so far as to send Black Hunters...?”
“That’s enough.”
Park Jihoon cut him off, his voice hard.
“There’s no need for you to know things you’re better off not knowing.”
“Isn’t it important that the Guild Master accepted the proposal?
One way or another, the result matters more than the process.”
“Yeah.
So is that why you turned that important result into this mess?”
Park Jihoon frowned.
Park Tae Seop’s complaints were nothing new, but this was the first time he had been so openly hostile.
What the hell happened?
“That’s enough bickering.
What went wrong?”
Park Tae Seop, breathing hard with anger, tossed out a single sentence.
“Two hours ago, Team 11 sent an emergency message.”
To the outside world, Myeongdong Guild had ten teams.
But that was merely its public face.
Team 11, the team Park Tae Seop had mentioned, did not officially exist.
It was made up entirely of Black Hunters.
“Did you say an emergency message?”
“If you have eyes, see for yourself.”
Park Tae Seop pulled something from his robe pocket and tossed it over.
Park Jihoon caught an old-fashioned cell phone so outdated that he couldn’t even guess when it had been made.
The call history had been wiped clean.
The inbox held only a single text message, received two hours earlier.
Intruder detected.
One short line.
But its contents were anything but ordinary.
Park Jihoon closed the phone and asked, “Where was it?”
“Far away.
A backwater hole beside some nameless mountain.
It’s outside the safe zone, and there aren’t any Gates nearby, so no one has any reason to go there.”
“Any word after that?”
“If there had been, would I be bringing this up?”
“So they’re out of contact.”
“I sent people to check, but...
I have a bad feeling about this.”
Park Jihoon felt the same.
Seven years ago, as soon as he had been assigned to Myeongdong Guild, his first task had involved Team 11.
Park Tae Seop, the Guild Master of Myeongdong Guild, had strongly objected to hiding and training criminals.
But he had been unable to defy the orders of that person.
That was how they had gathered roughly thirty Black Hunters.
Three A-rank Hunters.
And twenty-five B-rank Hunters.
They were a force powerful enough to rival—or even surpass—Team 1, Myeongdong Guild’s elite.
And now they had lost contact after an intruder appeared.
Just as unease began creeping through Park Jihoon’s chest—
Brrrrr.
The phone in his inner coat pocket began to vibrate again.
The longer it continued, the more his unease grew.
Ring.
Ring...
The call went unanswered and ended in voicemail, just like every time before.
This was already my tenth call.
I’d sent him a text ages ago, too, but he hadn’t replied.
He should be at work by now.
The entrance of the high-rise building towering over the heart of Seoul was crowded with people.
I was watching them absently when someone spoke to me.
“Excuse me.”
The man addressing me was dressed in a suit.
His face was angular, and his eyes were sharp.
I could sense the solid build beneath his clothes and the energy coiled inside him.
The man beside him, apparently his colleague, was much the same.
I put away my phone and answered,
“Yes, excuse me.”
The suited man hesitated, then opened his mouth.
The name tag on his chest clearly displayed both his name and his affiliation: Myeongdong Guild.
“We’re from the Security Team.
We received a report about you.”
“I’m not a sir.
What kind of report?”
“We checked the CCTV footage and saw you loitering in front of our building for quite a while...
Is there something you need?”
Their eyes were full of suspicion and wariness.
I was wearing track pants and a hoodie, with a cap pulled low over my face and sunglasses on top of that.
A guy dressed like this peering into the building was bound to attract a report.
“Sir, would you mind moving somewhere else for a moment?”
“No, I’d rather not.
And I told you, I’m not a sir.”
“It’ll only take a moment.”
Despite his fairly polite tone, his actions were anything but.
Whoosh!
With a short rush of wind, both men reached for me at the same time.
In the next instant, question marks appeared on their once-confident faces.
Tap.
Grab.
“Huh?”
“What?”
I casually caught both their wrists and put on a stern expression.
“Y-You rude punks.
How dare you lay hands on your teacher?”
“W-Wait a second.”
“Who the hell are you?
Let go!”
The two C-rank Hunters from the Security Team were visibly flustered.
No matter how hard they strained, they couldn’t move an inch, and their mouths fell open.
Should I break them?
I considered it for a moment, but the time wasn’t right yet.
I released their wrists before the commotion could grow any larger.
“Let’s not go around putting our hands on people.”
Rubbing their reddened wrists, the two men cautiously asked, “Were you... a Hunter?”
“Excuse me, but could we have your name and affiliation?”
“I’m Jin Taekyung of the Peace Guild.”
“What?”
“Could you be the Lord Fuck I’ve heard about?”
“...You must have seen that internet broadcast.”
I’d rather be the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi.
What the hell is Lord Fuck supposed to mean?
I sighed and lowered my sunglasses slightly.
The two men gasped and immediately bowed deeply.
“It’s an honor to meet you.”
“You’re much more handsome in person.”
Their eyes sparkled like high school students who had just spotted their favorite idol.
Judging by their reaction, they clearly knew nothing about what was really going on.
Of course.
Anything involving the Black Hunters would be top secret.
If an ordinary Security Team Hunter knew about it, the secret would have leaked long ago.
“But what brings you to our Guild...?”
“I came to see someone I know.”
“Someone you know?”
I pulled a thin piece of paper from my wallet and held it out.
It was Park Jihoon’s business card, which I’d received a while back and kept.
“Hunter Park Jihoon of Team 1?”
The Security Team Hunter tilted his head at the card, then turned to his colleague.
“Senior, do you know who this is?”
“Who?”
“He’s supposedly Hunter Park Jihoon from Team 1.
I know all the Team 1 Hunters, but I can’t quite place him...”
“Park Jihoon, Park Jihoon...
Oh, him.
You know.
That guy.”
He elbowed his colleague in the side, and only then did the other man let out an “Oh!”
The two of them looked back and forth between me and the business card with fascinated expressions.
What’s with that reaction?
My eyes narrowed.
Unable to see my expression behind my sunglasses, the Security Team Hunter asked, “Are you close with Hunter Park Jihoon?”
“We went to middle school together.”
“Ohhh, so you’re friends.”
I gave him a gentle smile.
“Well, for now.”
“Huh?”
“I’m joking.”
Maybe.
Oblivious to my thoughts, the Security Team Hunters laughed and kept asking questions.
“So you came to see Hunter Park Jihoon?”
“Yes.
He wasn’t answering his phone, and he wasn’t at home, either.
I thought I might find him at work.”
“We’re sorry.
We had no idea.”
“You were just doing your job, so don’t worry about it.
More importantly, is Jihoon inside?”
The senior Security Team Hunter answered, “He probably won’t come in today, either.”
“Today, too?”
“Yes.
He hardly ever comes to work.
Maybe once a month?
I’ve been here almost a year and have only seen him a few times.
This guy’s barely been here a month, so...”
“Sounds like Myeongdong Guild’s Hunters don’t come to work very often.”
“Of course they do.
I don’t know why, but everyone just accepts that he doesn’t.”
Yeah.
Why is that?
I’d never heard of a Guild Hunter who showed up for work once a month.
The question that had taken root in one corner of my mind grew deeper.
Without letting it show, I said, “Could you try contacting Jihoon for me?
I understand there’s a separate phone for Guild summons.”
“Uh, that’s...”
The two men hesitated, so I made them an offer they couldn’t refuse.
“I came to discuss a cooperative raid.
If I put in a word, I think I could get another person or two added...”
“Whoa.”
“Are you serious?”
Of course not.
It was all a lie from beginning to end.
But I kept a perfectly straight face and continued.
“You’re both C-rank, right?”
“Yes, sir.”
“How did you know?”
“I can tell at a glance.
But you two seem too good to waste away in the Security Team.”
Strictly speaking, a Guild’s Security Team was little more than a backwater department.
If a Hunter were truly skilled, why would the Guild waste him on guard duty?
From the Guild’s perspective, sending him on raids would be far more profitable.
There was no way the two Security Team Hunters didn’t know that.
Their eyes lit up.
“I’ll contact him right away!”
“I’d appreciate that.”
“Is there anything else you need?”
“Would it be all right if I looked around the Guild for a bit?
I can wait for Jihoon inside.”
“Yes.
Yes, of course.”
Unlike the senior, who was bowing obsequiously, the junior Hunter’s face had gone stiff.
He’d only joined a month ago.
His sense of duty and loyalty to the company were probably still burning bright.
“Senior, I don’t think that’s right.”

You little punk.”

You could rot in the Security Team for three years and never get another opportunity like this.”

“God, you’re so damn rigid.
Why do we need to report that he wants to look around for a moment?
It’s not like he’s just anybody.
He’s Hunter Jin Taekyung.”

What a complete circus.

The eyes of Kim Cheol Soo, devoted company man, trembled with emotion.
With my most amiable smile, I asked, “Can I go in now?”
Kim Cheol Soo shouted at the top of his lungs, “Irasshaimase!”

Arigato.”
The luxurious twenty-story building belonged to Myeongdong Guild.
The senior Hunter had pulled rank to ditch his junior and come with me.
He chattered away as we walked.

From the tenth through the nineteenth floors, each floor belongs to a raid team.”
