chapters.title: Chapter 280
paragraphs: “Park Jihoon, you fucking bastard.”
The voice on the other end cut off mid-sentence.
I couldn’t see him, but his confusion and agitation at that moment came through clearly enough.
“What’s the matter? If someone calls you, you should answer.”
After a moment, he replied.
“Is that you?”
“Yeah, it’s me, you bastard.”
My voice came out heated. Blood raced through my veins, and my heart hammered in my chest.
But my head was as cold as if I’d been doused with ice water.
Maybe some part of me had already seen this coming.
I kept thinking, surely not. Surely not.
But the number twenty-eight falling from his lips had been enough to turn a faint suspicion into certainty.
What I wanted to know was whose orders they were acting on—and how deeply he was involved.
“Did you send those bastards?”
A low, smooth baritone answered.
“Who knows? If that’s what happened, then I suppose I did.”
“What? Did you think I’d deny it?”
Well, look at this guy.
His attitude—as if he had nothing whatsoever to be ashamed of—drew a hollow laugh from me.
“Who told you? Im Yeongjun? Of course. He’s the only one it could’ve been. I thought he knew how to keep his mouth shut...but I misjudged him.”
Park Jihoon clicked his tongue and continued.
“Fucking idiot. I never should’ve left it to him.”
“What did the shit do wrong? The asshole who dropped his pants and started straining in public is the one to blame. But you...”
Crack.
The Team 1 Leader, still struggling with his neck trapped in my grip, turned blue.
“Did you think about how you were going to clean up after taking that dump?”
“It’s unexpected that things turned out this way...but do you really think I’d have done my business without considering the cleanup?”
“Yeah. That’s exactly what it looks like.”
“What?”
“Can you handle me?”
Silence followed.
One second. Two. Three.
Then, at the end of that brief silence, came a cold, razor-edged voice unlike any I had ever heard from him.
“Take one more step, and both you and the Peace Guild are finished.”
“So?”
“It’s not too late. Don’t make this any bigger. Come out. Let’s end it here.”
Hearing that, it suddenly occurred to me that the way the world worked wasn’t so different from a fight.
The one who seized the advantage pressed forward without mercy. The one who was afraid took the first step back.
And I knew exactly what Park Jihoon feared.
Black Hunters.
The existence of the Black Hunters—the illegal private armies maintained by major Guilds.
The thought that they were holding Park Jihoon back made the corners of my mouth curl upward.
“End it?”
“Yes.”
“Who says?”
“You people started this. I’ll decide where it ends.”
On the other end of the phone, Park Jihoon’s breathing grew ragged.
“Well, this is something. I knew you were stupid, but you’re even worse than I thought.”
“The result will be beyond anything you imagined, too. Please fucking look forward to it, you son of a bitch.”
That was when it happened.
Ding.
“Nineteenth floor.”
With the mechanical announcement, the tightly closed elevator doors slowly slid open.
A broad hallway with a high ceiling came into view. Dozens of people moved through it.
Several naturally glanced in our direction. A moment later, their mouths dropped open.
“T-Team Leader?”
“You there! Who the hell are you...?”
Instead of answering, I hurled the Team 1 Leader at them. A Hunter approaching with an accusing finger outstretched went crashing into the wall along with him.
At the same time, an employee sitting at the desk screamed and pressed the emergency button.
WEEEEEE!
“Emergency! Emergency!”
“Intruder! Team 1, arm yourselves!”
Amid the piercing alarm, Park Jihoon’s final words reached my ears.
“Go ahead, then. Let’s see you try.”
Beep. Beep. Beep...
I shoved the Team 1 Leader’s phone, now disconnected, into my inner pocket.
When my hand emerged again, it held two daggers instead.
Let’s see me try?
I’d been planning to.
“Who are you?!”
“Drop your weapons! Now, unless you want to die!”
Myeongdong Guild’s elite Hunters armed themselves with astonishing speed and surrounded me in a semicircle.
The elevator was behind me. The only other person there stood frozen like a plaster statue, muttering to himself.
“This is a dream. It has to be.”
I glanced at him, half out of his mind, and asked,
“What phone do you use?”
“Gasp!”
“Your phone. What kind?”
“I-I use an AdultPhone 25.”
“Ah. The apple you bit into and spat out.”
“Y-Yes, yes. That’s right.”
“Take it out and start recording.”
“Yes, sir!”
He answered at the top of his lungs, then froze halfway through pulling out his phone.
“Y-Yes, sir? I’m sorry, but what did you just say?”
“You said you have an AdultPhone 25. Its camera’s much better than mine, so I figured you should do the filming.”
“F-Film what?”
“Everything.”
Just then, the fallen Team 1 Leader sprang to his feet and roared.
“What are you waiting for, you bastards? Beat the shit out of him!”
“Team Leader, isn’t that Hunter Jin Taekyung? What is going on all of a sudden...?”
“I’ll take responsibility.”
In any Guild, Team 1 was both its symbol and its elite force.
For Myeongdong Guild, consistently ranked among Korea’s top ten, that went without saying. Its Team 1 members were consummate professionals—living combat machines.
“This is an order from above. Don’t think of him as a person. Think of him as a monster and fight.”
The moment their Team Leader gave them a firm order, dozens of gazes sank into cold focus.
Five tower shields at the front slammed into the marble floor in perfect unison.
Boom!
“Formation—!”
In the middle of their peaceful daily lives, the downtown building became a battlefield.
What am I looking at?
Lee Minsu, a C-rank Hunter assigned to Myeongdong Guild’s Security Team, blinked.
The scene unfolding before him was simply too unreal.
Krrr-crack! Boom!
A tower shield as sturdy as an armored vehicle shattered, and a massive tank flew far away as if it had been struck by a giant’s hammer.
For the briefest instant, a gap opened—barely wide enough for one person.
A pale figure slipped through it.
And then—
Shriiiik! Slash! Slash!
“Gaaah!”
“Gasp!”
The shield wall collapsed in a flash of light.
The tanks pitched forward in an undignified heap, the tendons in their calves cleanly severed.
How did he...?
He couldn’t even see the strikes properly.
Blink once, and two people fell. Blink twice, and three or four went down.
Every time the young man in the gray hoodie, Jin Taekyung, took a step, blood spurted and screams overflowed.
“S-Stop him!”
“Damage dealer!”
The front line where the tanks had been holding had already collapsed the moment the battle began. Five blades swung powerfully toward Jin Taekyung as he advanced one step at a time.
Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!
Both shoulders. His chest. Both legs.
Three attacks targeted his upper body, while two went for his lower body. There was no way to evade them without retreating.
“We got him!”
At the instant someone cried out in delight, the dagger in Jin Taekyung’s hand blurred like mist.
Clang-clang-clang-clang-clang!
All five blades, which everyone had been certain would connect, shot into the air.
The Hunters who had wielded them stared at Jin Taekyung in shock. The force of the deflection had torn their palms open, leaving them drenched in blood.
“W-What the...?”
“That’s impossible!”
Jin Taekyung answered their cries in a flat voice.
“Looks possible to me.”
Slash!
A single line swept horizontally through the air.
An attack that could neither be seen nor avoided.
Directly in its path stood the five Hunters who had just attacked him.
Fwoosh!
As the Hunters fell, spraying fountains of blood from their chests, a streak of light pierced between them.
Whooosh! Thunk!
The arrowhead stopped just short of Jin Taekyung’s chest.
An A-rank Hunter had fired it with perfect accuracy, mana coursing through the shaft.
But what stopped it was neither a shield coated in various magics nor a sharp weapon.
Crack.
Jin Taekyung snapped the arrow shaft between two fingers and flicked his hand.
With a terrifying whistle, the arrow shot back along its original path, shattered three defensive spells, and buried itself in its owner’s shoulders.
Thud!
“Ghk!”
“Fire one more arrow, and I’ll make sure you end up with an odd number of balls.”
“The rest of you, back off unless you want your balls lopsided too. It’s annoying having to hold back.”
He had been holding back?

The Hunters of Team 1 felt as if they had been possessed by ghosts. It was hard enough to believe that he had rendered more than a dozen people unable to fight in the time it took to drink a glass of cold water.
And he had been holding back while doing it?
The same thought flashed through every mind.
What kind of monster is this?
Who were they?
They were Myeongdong Guild’s elite, battle-hardened veteran Hunters. Even the least experienced had eight years under their belt, while the most senior had been Hunters for more than twenty.
They had earned their positions through skills far surpassing those of other Hunters at the same rank, and they had taken immense pride in that fact.
At least, they had—until they faced Jin Taekyung here today.
“Please move aside while I’m still speaking politely, Seniors. I’d really like to smash every one of your faces in, but you don’t seem to be directly involved, so this is all I’m doing.”
Loose track pants and a gray hoodie. He looked as if he had stepped out to visit the café down the street.
Yet no one dared dismiss his words.
He had already displayed his strength and seared it into their minds.
“So clear a path.”
An overwhelming aura crushed the corridor, leaving even veterans of countless brutal battles inside Gates struggling to breathe.
It awakened a primal terror unlike anything they had ever felt from a monster.
Monster. That bastard is a real monster.
Step. Step.
The monster walked straight toward them.
The Hunters unconsciously moved aside to let him pass.
That was when—
“Burning Hands!”
Whoosh!
A hand wreathed in flame came crashing down on Jin Taekyung amid fierce heat.
The fire spell could melt solid rock, but the enormous hand of mana vanished without a trace the instant it struck Jin Taekyung’s palm.
“M-Magic?”
“It’s called the Flame Divine Palm. Pretty useful, right?”
The Team 1 Leader’s eyes widened at the sight of his palm engulfed in blue flame.
Jin Taekyung stared at him and ran his tongue over his dry lips.
He looked like a predator that had just discovered prey it had forgotten about.
“Ah. You’re the one exception to what I said earlier.”
“Gasp.”
Whoosh!
Jin Taekyung’s form scattered like a ghost.
But the Team 1 Leader was an exceptional battle mage in his own right, accomplished enough to command Myeongdong Guild’s elite team. Even in his panic, he reacted quickly.
“Blink!”
It was a teleportation spell that allowed him to move anywhere within ten meters, provided he could see the destination.
If I move behind him and unleash my attack spells all at once, even someone as skilled as him...
The Team 1 Leader used Blink to move behind Jin Taekyung.
For an instant, it felt as though the world had stopped.
Jin Taekyung’s clear, deep-black eyes were right in front of his face.
Thud.
A palm still radiating heat pressed down on his shoulder.
“Why are you so surprised?”
“You practically advertised where you were going with your eyes.”
Had he predicted the direction from the movement of his gaze?
No. That wasn’t all.
The Team 1 Leader’s body trembled as though he had been struck by lightning.
His movement was faster than my Blink.
What kind of monster was he?
And what kind of monster had Park Jihoon—and Myeongdong Guild—provoked?
With a trembling voice, the Team 1 Leader recited the final spell he had prepared.
“P-Poison.”
Whoosh.
A cloud of green poisonous fog burst forth and enveloped Jin Taekyung’s face.
But just as the Team 1 Leader’s instincts had warned him, the monster proved once again that he truly was a monster.
“Ugh. Smells like a fart.”
His handsome brow furrowed.
That was his entire reaction to the Poison spell.
Having reached Peak and attained the realm of Unaffected by a Hundred Poisons, Jin Taekyung blew on the frozen Team 1 Leader.
“Hoo.”
“Gasp.”
The Team 1 Leader inhaled the poisonous fog, and his face turned blue.
Jin Taekyung grabbed him by the nape as the paralyzing poison stiffened his entire body, then looked around and asked,
“Where’s that bastard Park Jihoon’s office?”
Ssssk!
Ten fingers pointed toward a single door.

He’s the only one it could’ve been.
I thought he knew how to keep his mouth shut...but I misjudged him.”
Park Jihoon clicked his tongue and continued.
“Fucking idiot.
I never should’ve left it to him.”
“What did the shit do wrong?
The asshole who dropped his pants and started straining in public is the one to blame.
But you...”
Crack.
The Team 1 Leader, still struggling with his neck trapped in my grip, turned blue.
“Did you think about how you were going to clean up after taking that dump?”
“It’s unexpected that things turned out this way...but do you really think I’d have done my business without considering the cleanup?”
“Yeah.
That’s exactly what it looks like.”
“What?”
“Can you handle me?”
Silence followed.
One second.
Two.
Three.
Then, at the end of that brief silence, came a cold, razor-edged voice unlike any I had ever heard from him.
“Take one more step, and both you and the Peace Guild are finished.”
“So?”
“It’s not too late.
Don’t make this any bigger.
Come out.
Let’s end it here.”
Hearing that, it suddenly occurred to me that the way the world worked wasn’t so different from a fight.
The one who seized the advantage pressed forward without mercy.
The one who was afraid took the first step back.
And I knew exactly what Park Jihoon feared.
Black Hunters.
The existence of the Black Hunters—the illegal private armies maintained by major Guilds.
The thought that they were holding Park Jihoon back made the corners of my mouth curl upward.
“End it?”
“Yes.”
“Who says?”
“You people started this.
I’ll decide where it ends.”
On the other end of the phone, Park Jihoon’s breathing grew ragged.
“Well, this is something.
I knew you were stupid, but you’re even worse than I thought.”
“The result will be beyond anything you imagined, too.
Please fucking look forward to it, you son of a bitch.”
That was when it happened.
Ding.
“Nineteenth floor.”
With the mechanical announcement, the tightly closed elevator doors slowly slid open.
A broad hallway with a high ceiling came into view.
Dozens of people moved through it.
Several naturally glanced in our direction.
A moment later, their mouths dropped open.
“T-Team Leader?”
“You there!
Who the hell are you...?”
Instead of answering, I hurled the Team 1 Leader at them.
A Hunter approaching with an accusing finger outstretched went crashing into the wall along with him.
At the same time, an employee sitting at the desk screamed and pressed the emergency button.
WEEEEEE!
“Emergency!
Emergency!”
“Intruder!
Team 1, arm yourselves!”
Amid the piercing alarm, Park Jihoon’s final words reached my ears.
“Go ahead, then.
Let’s see you try.”
Beep.
Beep.
Beep...
I shoved the Team 1 Leader’s phone, now disconnected, into my inner pocket.
When my hand emerged again, it held two daggers instead.
Let’s see me try?
I’d been planning to.
“Who are you?!”
“Drop your weapons!
Now, unless you want to die!”
Myeongdong Guild’s elite Hunters armed themselves with astonishing speed and surrounded me in a semicircle.
The elevator was behind me.
The only other person there stood frozen like a plaster statue, muttering to himself.
“This is a dream.
It has to be.”
I glanced at him, half out of his mind, and asked,
“What phone do you use?”
“Gasp!”
“Your phone.
What kind?”
“I-I use an AdultPhone 25.”
“Ah.
The apple you bit into and spat out.”
“Y-Yes, yes.
That’s right.”
“Take it out and start recording.”
“Yes, sir!”
He answered at the top of his lungs, then froze halfway through pulling out his phone.
“Y-Yes, sir?
I’m sorry, but what did you just say?”
“You said you have an AdultPhone 25.
Its camera’s much better than mine, so I figured you should do the filming.”
“F-Film what?”
“Everything.”
Just then, the fallen Team 1 Leader sprang to his feet and roared.
“What are you waiting for, you bastards?
Beat the shit out of him!”
“Team Leader, isn’t that Hunter Jin Taekyung?
What is going on all of a sudden...?”
“I’ll take responsibility.”
In any Guild, Team 1 was both its symbol and its elite force.
For Myeongdong Guild, consistently ranked among Korea’s top ten, that went without saying.
Its Team 1 members were consummate professionals—living combat machines.
“This is an order from above.
Don’t think of him as a person.
Think of him as a monster and fight.”
The moment their Team Leader gave them a firm order, dozens of gazes sank into cold focus.
Five tower shields at the front slammed into the marble floor in perfect unison.
Boom!
“Formation—!”
In the middle of their peaceful daily lives, the downtown building became a battlefield.
What am I looking at?
Lee Minsu, a C-rank Hunter assigned to Myeongdong Guild’s Security Team, blinked.
The scene unfolding before him was simply too unreal.
Krrr-crack!
Boom!
A tower shield as sturdy as an armored vehicle shattered, and a massive tank flew far away as if it had been struck by a giant’s hammer.
For the briefest instant, a gap opened—barely wide enough for one person.
A pale figure slipped through it.
And then—
Shriiiik!
Slash!
Slash!
“Gaaah!”
“Gasp!”
The shield wall collapsed in a flash of light.
The tanks pitched forward in an undignified heap, the tendons in their calves cleanly severed.
How did he...?
He couldn’t even see the strikes properly.
Blink once, and two people fell.
Blink twice, and three or four went down.
Every time the young man in the gray hoodie, Jin Taekyung, took a step, blood spurted and screams overflowed.
“S-Stop him!”
“Damage dealer!”
The front line where the tanks had been holding had already collapsed the moment the battle began.
Five blades swung powerfully toward Jin Taekyung as he advanced one step at a time.
Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!
Both shoulders.
His chest.
Both legs.
Three attacks targeted his upper body, while two went for his lower body.
There was no way to evade them without retreating.
“We got him!”
At the instant someone cried out in delight, the dagger in Jin Taekyung’s hand blurred like mist.
Clang-clang-clang-clang-clang!
All five blades, which everyone had been certain would connect, shot into the air.
The Hunters who had wielded them stared at Jin Taekyung in shock.
The force of the deflection had torn their palms open, leaving them drenched in blood.
“W-What the...?”
“That’s impossible!”
Jin Taekyung answered their cries in a flat voice.
“Looks possible to me.”
Slash!
A single line swept horizontally through the air.
An attack that could neither be seen nor avoided.
Directly in its path stood the five Hunters who had just attacked him.
Fwoosh!
As the Hunters fell, spraying fountains of blood from their chests, a streak of light pierced between them.
Whooosh!
Thunk!
The arrowhead stopped just short of Jin Taekyung’s chest.
An A-rank Hunter had fired it with perfect accuracy, mana coursing through the shaft.
But what stopped it was neither a shield coated in various magics nor a sharp weapon.
Crack.
Jin Taekyung snapped the arrow shaft between two fingers and flicked his hand.
With a terrifying whistle, the arrow shot back along its original path, shattered three defensive spells, and buried itself in its owner’s shoulders.
Thud!
“Ghk!”
“Fire one more arrow, and I’ll make sure you end up with an odd number of balls.”
“The rest of you, back off unless you want your balls lopsided too.
It’s annoying having to hold back.”
He had been holding back?
The Hunters of Team 1 felt as if they had been possessed by ghosts.
It was hard enough to believe that he had rendered more than a dozen people unable to fight in the time it took to drink a glass of cold water.
And he had been holding back while doing it?
The same thought flashed through every mind.
What kind of monster is this?
Who were they?
They were Myeongdong Guild’s elite, battle-hardened veteran Hunters.
Even the least experienced had eight years under their belt, while the most senior had been Hunters for more than twenty.
They had earned their positions through skills far surpassing those of other Hunters at the same rank, and they had taken immense pride in that fact.
At least, they had—until they faced Jin Taekyung here today.
“Please move aside while I’m still speaking politely, Seniors.
I’d really like to smash every one of your faces in, but you don’t seem to be directly involved, so this is all I’m doing.”
Loose track pants and a gray hoodie.
He looked as if he had stepped out to visit the café down the street.
Yet no one dared dismiss his words.
He had already displayed his strength and seared it into their minds.
“So clear a path.”
An overwhelming aura crushed the corridor, leaving even veterans of countless brutal battles inside Gates struggling to breathe.
It awakened a primal terror unlike anything they had ever felt from a monster.
Monster.
That bastard is a real monster.
Step.
Step.
The monster walked straight toward them.
The Hunters unconsciously moved aside to let him pass.
That was when—
“Burning Hands!”
Whoosh!
A hand wreathed in flame came crashing down on Jin Taekyung amid fierce heat.
The fire spell could melt solid rock, but the enormous hand of mana vanished without a trace the instant it struck Jin Taekyung’s palm.
“M-Magic?”
“It’s called the Flame Divine Palm.
Pretty useful, right?”
The Team 1 Leader’s eyes widened at the sight of his palm engulfed in blue flame.
Jin Taekyung stared at him and ran his tongue over his dry lips.
He looked like a predator that had just discovered prey it had forgotten about.
“Ah.
You’re the one exception to what I said earlier.”
“Gasp.”
Whoosh!
Jin Taekyung’s form scattered like a ghost.
But the Team 1 Leader was an exceptional battle mage in his own right, accomplished enough to command Myeongdong Guild’s elite team.
Even in his panic, he reacted quickly.
“Blink!”
It was a teleportation spell that allowed him to move anywhere within ten meters, provided he could see the destination.
If I move behind him and unleash my attack spells all at once, even someone as skilled as him...
The Team 1 Leader used Blink to move behind Jin Taekyung.
For an instant, it felt as though the world had stopped.
Jin Taekyung’s clear, deep-black eyes were right in front of his face.
Thud.
A palm still radiating heat pressed down on his shoulder.
“Why are you so surprised?”
“You practically advertised where you were going with your eyes.”
Had he predicted the direction from the movement of his gaze?
No.
That wasn’t all.
The Team 1 Leader’s body trembled as though he had been struck by lightning.
His movement was faster than my Blink.
What kind of monster was he?
And what kind of monster had Park Jihoon—and Myeongdong Guild—provoked?
With a trembling voice, the Team 1 Leader recited the final spell he had prepared.
“P-Poison.”
Whoosh.
A cloud of green poisonous fog burst forth and enveloped Jin Taekyung’s face.
But just as the Team 1 Leader’s instincts had warned him, the monster proved once again that he truly was a monster.
“Ugh.
Smells like a fart.”
His handsome brow furrowed.
That was his entire reaction to the Poison spell.
Having reached Peak and attained the realm of Unaffected by a Hundred Poisons, Jin Taekyung blew on the frozen Team 1 Leader.
“Hoo.”
“Gasp.”
The Team 1 Leader inhaled the poisonous fog, and his face turned blue.
Jin Taekyung grabbed him by the nape as the paralyzing poison stiffened his entire body, then looked around and asked,
“Where’s that bastard Park Jihoon’s office?”
Ssssk!
Ten fingers pointed toward a single door.

chapters.title: Chapter 281
paragraphs: The limousine sped down the road without so much as a jolt.
Park Jihoon took a bottle of water from the refrigerator and offered it to the middle-aged man sitting across from him.
“Would you like some?”
“At a time like this? And where did you learn to offer someone else’s things as if they were your own?”
“Then I suppose it’s all right if I drink only half. I have at least that much of a stake in bringing Myeongdong Guild to where it is today.”
Myeongdong Guild Master Park Tae Seop glared silently as Park Jihoon tipped back the bottle.
“You’re awfully calm.”
After drinking exactly half, Park Jihoon leaned back against the plush seat.
“Is there some reason I should be worried?”
“This whole mess has erupted, and you’re acting as though nothing’s wrong?”
“It’s nothing more than a minor incident.”
“A single drop of water can bring down a tower of sand.”
“Because it’s made of sand.”
“You’re saying Myeongdong Guild is different?”
“Five hundred Hunters under its banner. Twenty of them A-rank. At this point, it wouldn’t be wrong to call it an iron tower instead of a tower of sand. And...”
The corners of Park Jihoon’s mouth curved gently upward.
“Myeongdong Guild shouldn’t even be part of the comparison. We have ‘that person,’ after all.”
“...That’s true.”
Park Tae Seop nodded reluctantly, though his expression remained displeased. Park Jihoon studied him.
“What is it? What has you so anxious you can’t sit still?”
After a brief silence, Park Tae Seop spoke.
“A feeling.”
“What?”
“When you reach my age, you develop instincts you can’t explain.”
Ha.
Park Jihoon suppressed a laugh. He had wondered what the man was going to say, but in the end, it was nothing more than the grumbling of an old man past sixty.
Just a feeling? What a load of nonsense.
The thought showed plainly on his face, and Park Tae Seop had lived too long not to notice.
“You may think it’s nonsense. I understand. It’s beyond greenhorns like you.”
“Ah, I’m sorry if you took it that way.”
“And only a greenhorn could apologize in a tone without a shred of sincerity.”
“I simply don’t understand. What exactly is bothering you so much?”
After a short silence, a name slipped out.
“Jin Taekyung.”
He breathed the name like a sigh. It had haunted his thoughts ever since they lost contact with Team 11.
For a moment, he had dismissed it as lingering unease over the operation going awry.
But that wasn’t it.
His intuition, which had even endured the Great Cataclysm, had given him the answer to what troubled him.
“He’s a siege cannon. One capable of cracking not just a tower of sand, but an iron one.”
Without waiting for a reply, Park Tae Seop reached out. He picked up the bottle of water Park Jihoon had left behind and drained it in large gulps.
His throat had become unbearably dry as soon as he finished speaking.
Park Jihoon watched with a deep frown.
Has the old man gone senile?
He could admit that the operation had not gone entirely smoothly. There had been unexpected complications, particularly with the Black Hunters and Team 11.
But even taking that into account, Park Tae Seop’s reaction was far too extreme.
It was only natural that Park Jihoon, who absolutely worshiped “that person,” should feel displeased.
“I didn’t realize you held Jin Taekyung in such high regard.”
“He’s proven himself.”
“Jin Taekyung only began attracting attention recently.”
“And he’s shown us a great deal in that short time.”
“Shown us?”
A mocking smile touched Park Jihoon’s lips.

“Won Myunghoon was trash. He was at the very bottom of the rankers, and even then, they only put his name on the list once as an act of charity during all that Korean Wave hype. You know that too, Guild Master.”
“I heard he was stupid and greedy, and that his fame made him look more skilled than he really was.”

“And the Named Monster? They called it a Named Monster, but that Black Drake was the weakest one to appear in nearly twenty years. The Magic Gem recovered from its corpse wasn’t much different from one taken from an A-rank monster.”
“Then could you kill that weak Named Monster by yourself?”
“I don’t see why not.”
Park Jihoon answered without hesitation.
He took pride in his own abilities.

His natural talent had earned him the honor of being chosen by “that person.” It was why, despite not yet being thirty, he could sit across from the Guild Master of Myeongdong Guild and look him in the eye.
But the next question made him falter.
“Then what if you fought Jin Taekyung? Are you certain you could defeat him?”
“...Of course.”
His answer came half a beat late. Realizing it, Park Jihoon pressed his lips together.
“That hesitation just now seems to say something about what kind of person Jin Taekyung is.”
Park Jihoon replied coldly, “I was merely reminded of the past.”
“Ah. You said you two were friends, didn’t you?”
“I don’t want to discuss that. My point is that this incident isn’t as serious as you think, Guild Master.”
“We don’t even know whether Team 11 is alive or dead, and the most talked-about public figure in the country has stormed Myeongdong Guild headquarters. Yet you’re saying this isn’t serious?”
“He’s an idiot. He couldn’t control his temper, so he recklessly barged into Myeongdong Guild headquarters.”
About ten minutes earlier, Park Jihoon had been speaking with the Team 1 Leader when Jin Taekyung’s voice suddenly came over the phone.
He had been startled.
And relieved.
This will make things easy.
Myeongdong Guild had more than five hundred Hunters. Even if half were away on raids, an enormous number remained at headquarters.
Among them was Team 1, the Guild’s elite force.
“Jin Taekyung walked straight into the tiger’s den. All we have to do is keep him there while we sort everything out.”
Even if reporters caught the scent of the story and swarmed in, there was nothing to fear.
He had—no, “that person” had—the power to render cameras and microphones useless.
“I’ll have everything cleaned up by the end of the day.”
Park Tae Seop’s face suddenly looked much older as he muttered, “This feels wrong. Maybe it’s my age, but I’m starting to feel the strain.”
“It’s only a passing breeze. It wouldn’t do for the legs of a man who survived the Great Cataclysm to start trembling now.”
The remark held more reproach than encouragement. Park Tae Seop recognized that and fell silent.
Just then, the dull chime of a phone notification sounded.
“That isn’t mine.”
“It’s mine.”
“Who is it?”
“Manager Kim, the man in charge of my security. I sent him to find out what happened to Team 11. It seems he’s just arrived.”
“Good. Tell him to erase every trace of Team 11 first.”
“Are you giving me orders now?”
Frowning, Park Tae Seop answered the phone.
“It’s me. What happened? Hm? Ah, I see.”
His brow furrowed, then smoothed. His pupils dilated and contracted.
As his expression grew increasingly strange, Park Tae Seop pulled the phone away from his ear.
“What happened?”
“Take it.”
Park Tae Seop thrust the phone toward him, a vein bulging on his forehead.
“What?”
“Hurry!”
Bewildered, Park Jihoon took the phone and pressed it to his ear.
A voice as soft as a cat’s paw slipped into his ear.
“Hunter Park Jihoon of Myeongdong Guild Team 1?”
Park Jihoon knew the instant he heard it.
The caller was not Manager Kim, whom he had encountered in passing several times.
The voice was young and polite, yet carried an air that discouraged familiarity.
“This is Park Jihoon. Who am I speaking to?”
Something felt wrong.
The unfamiliar voice answered the unease in his question.
“My name is Choi Minwoo.”
“Who?”
“Ah, I’m with the Peace Guild. I’m a Team Leader there.”
“...The Peace Guild?”
“Yes.”
Fuck.
Park Jihoon’s lips twitched.
Those few words were enough for him to understand what had happened. Myeongdong Guild’s people had walked straight into the Peace Guild’s trap.
There was no need to see what had happened to Manager Kim, the phone’s owner. He was obviously either bound tightly and unconscious or helplessly watching someone else use his phone.
Myeongdong Guild, you fucking idiots.
Team Leader Choi’s voice drifted leisurely through the receiver, as relaxed as a victor’s.
“I called because I’d like to have a conversation.”
“Well, the thing is...”
Park Jihoon clenched his teeth, his mind racing.
Then he felt a vibration against his chest.
It had not come from Park Tae Seop’s phone.
“Hunter Park Jihoon?”
“Wait. Just a moment.”
With his free hand, Park Jihoon pulled his own phone from the inner pocket of his suit.
A text message had arrived. The sender was...
[Team 1 Leader]
It’s done.
Relief spread across Park Jihoon’s lips in a smile. Jin Taekyung, who had entered the tiger’s den known as Myeongdong Guild, had finally been forced to his knees.
The scales that had tipped against him were balanced again.
But then—
The smile vanished from his lips.
Filling the six-inch screen was not a report that the Team 1 Leader had captured Jin Taekyung, but a single photograph.
What is this?
He recognized the faces.
A young man grinned broadly at the camera, blood spattered across his face. Beside him, caught firmly in his grasp, was a middle-aged man whose complexion had turned as blue as a drug addict’s.
Jin Taekyung...and the Team 1 Leader?
That wasn’t all.
The background was familiar too.
The nameplate reading Hunter Park Jihoon, Myeongdong Guild Team 1 made it unmistakably clear where they were.
And there was one more thing.
No way... Did no one stop him? That one Jin Taekyung?
A reality he did not want to believe.
Park Jihoon’s eyes darted helplessly around as they began to tremble.
Bzzz.
Another text arrived. Its contents were brief but devastating.
Five Korean characters were enough to shatter Park Jihoon’s composure.
Team 1 Leader └ Team 1 Leader: Bring Melona when you come.
“This—this fucking...!”
Crack.
The phone in Park Jihoon’s hand crumpled like a sheet of paper.
Watching him, Myeongdong Guild Master Park Tae Seop muttered quietly,
“We’re fucked.”
Team Leader Choi └ Team Leader Choi: We’ve captured the people dispatched by Myeongdong Guild.
The text was from Team Leader Choi.
A few hours earlier, after burning down the safe house used by the Black Hunters, we had split up.
Team Leader Choi and the others would lie in ambush to secure solid evidence, while I had insisted on acting alone.
It was because Team Leader Choi had argued that we absolutely had to capture something that could serve as evidence or a witness.
He was right.

Every Black Hunter, including Im Yeongjun, had been managed so meticulously that their identities had already been laundered clean. There wasn’t even the slightest link connecting them to Myeongdong Guild.
Team Leader Choi had identified that problem exactly.
He’s always calm and composed.
Looking back, he had never once lost sight of the right path.
Having Butler Kim as both an excellent mage and a wise adviser probably helped, but at this point, Choi had to be a natural.
Now we have solid leverage.
On top of the captured Black Hunters, we had official Myeongdong Guild employees in our hands.
That should make an excellent shield.
Or a dagger.
I sent him a message thanking him for his hard work, along with the photograph I’d taken earlier.
Maybe it was because it was an AdultPhone, but even a picture taken with my foot came out great.
“Maybe I should replace my phone while I’m at it.”
Someone flinched at my mutter. It was the Security Team Hunter I’d hired as my personal cameraman for the day.
Of course, I wasn’t paying him.
“What’s wrong?”
“N-Nothing, sir!”
“Make yourself comfortable. Don’t just stand there. Sit on the sofa or something.”
“I’m comfortable like this!”
“You look pretty uncomfortable to me.”
“I’m fiiiine!”
Was it my imagination, or was there a sob mixed into his shout?
As an ordinary Security Team Hunter, he’d just watched me beat the living shit out of Team 1, the Guild’s elite—people he normally wouldn’t even dare look in the eye.
His reaction was understandable.
The ones who came later weren’t much different.
The other Myeongdong Guild Hunters who arrived afterward didn’t dare attack me after seeing the scene before them.
Of course, quite a few of them were armed with fierce devotion to their Guild.
Unfortunately, they didn’t have the skills to back it up. Everyone who charged me got beaten to a pulp and carried away.
After I had knocked down around fifty of them, no one else tried to attack me. Park Jihoon’s office became forbidden territory that no one could enter.
I sank into his chair.
He must be racing here like a madman by now.
Just thinking about him made my heart turn cold.
A middle-school classmate I had happened to run into on the street after ten long years.
How much of what I saw was the real Park Jihoon?
Hurry up and get here. Before I get any angrier.
Crack.
The armrest snapped beneath my grip.
“H-He’s here!”
“Guild Master!”
Murmurs spread beyond the office door like a wildfire.
At the same time, I sensed two immense presences approaching without hesitation.
He’s here.
And in the next moment, the door blew apart with a thunderous roar.
BOOM!

His natural talent had earned him the honor of being chosen by “that person.” It was why, despite not yet being thirty, he could sit across from the Guild Master of Myeongdong Guild and look him in the eye.
But the next question made him falter.
“Then what if you fought Jin Taekyung?
Are you certain you could defeat him?”
“...Of course.”
His answer came half a beat late.
Realizing it, Park Jihoon pressed his lips together.
“That hesitation just now seems to say something about what kind of person Jin Taekyung is.”
Park Jihoon replied coldly, “I was merely reminded of the past.”
“Ah.
You said you two were friends, didn’t you?”
“I don’t want to discuss that.
My point is that this incident isn’t as serious as you think, Guild Master.”
“We don’t even know whether Team 11 is alive or dead, and the most talked-about public figure in the country has stormed Myeongdong Guild headquarters.
Yet you’re saying this isn’t serious?”
“He’s an idiot.
He couldn’t control his temper, so he recklessly barged into Myeongdong Guild headquarters.”
About ten minutes earlier, Park Jihoon had been speaking with the Team 1 Leader when Jin Taekyung’s voice suddenly came over the phone.
He had been startled.
And relieved.
This will make things easy.
Myeongdong Guild had more than five hundred Hunters.
Even if half were away on raids, an enormous number remained at headquarters.
Among them was Team 1, the Guild’s elite force.
“Jin Taekyung walked straight into the tiger’s den.
All we have to do is keep him there while we sort everything out.”
Even if reporters caught the scent of the story and swarmed in, there was nothing to fear.
He had—no, “that person” had—the power to render cameras and microphones useless.
“I’ll have everything cleaned up by the end of the day.”
Park Tae Seop’s face suddenly looked much older as he muttered, “This feels wrong.
Maybe it’s my age, but I’m starting to feel the strain.”
“It’s only a passing breeze.
It wouldn’t do for the legs of a man who survived the Great Cataclysm to start trembling now.”
The remark held more reproach than encouragement.
Park Tae Seop recognized that and fell silent.
Just then, the dull chime of a phone notification sounded.
“That isn’t mine.”
“It’s mine.”
“Who is it?”
“Manager Kim, the man in charge of my security.
I sent him to find out what happened to Team 11.
It seems he’s just arrived.”
“Good.
Tell him to erase every trace of Team 11 first.”
“Are you giving me orders now?”
Frowning, Park Tae Seop answered the phone.
“It’s me.
What happened?
Hm?
Ah, I see.”
His brow furrowed, then smoothed.
His pupils dilated and contracted.
As his expression grew increasingly strange, Park Tae Seop pulled the phone away from his ear.
“What happened?”
“Take it.”
Park Tae Seop thrust the phone toward him, a vein bulging on his forehead.
“What?”
“Hurry!”
Bewildered, Park Jihoon took the phone and pressed it to his ear.
A voice as soft as a cat’s paw slipped into his ear.
“Hunter Park Jihoon of Myeongdong Guild Team 1?”
Park Jihoon knew the instant he heard it.
The caller was not Manager Kim, whom he had encountered in passing several times.
The voice was young and polite, yet carried an air that discouraged familiarity.
“This is Park Jihoon.
Who am I speaking to?”
Something felt wrong.
The unfamiliar voice answered the unease in his question.
“My name is Choi Minwoo.”
“Who?”
“Ah, I’m with the Peace Guild.
I’m a Team Leader there.”
“...The Peace Guild?”
“Yes.”
Fuck.
Park Jihoon’s lips twitched.
Those few words were enough for him to understand what had happened.
Myeongdong Guild’s people had walked straight into the Peace Guild’s trap.
There was no need to see what had happened to Manager Kim, the phone’s owner.
He was obviously either bound tightly and unconscious or helplessly watching someone else use his phone.
Myeongdong Guild, you fucking idiots.
Team Leader Choi’s voice drifted leisurely through the receiver, as relaxed as a victor’s.
“I called because I’d like to have a conversation.”
“Well, the thing is...”
Park Jihoon clenched his teeth, his mind racing.
Then he felt a vibration against his chest.
It had not come from Park Tae Seop’s phone.
“Hunter Park Jihoon?”
“Wait.
Just a moment.”
With his free hand, Park Jihoon pulled his own phone from the inner pocket of his suit.
A text message had arrived.
The sender was...
[Team 1 Leader]
It’s done.
Relief spread across Park Jihoon’s lips in a smile.
Jin Taekyung, who had entered the tiger’s den known as Myeongdong Guild, had finally been forced to his knees.
The scales that had tipped against him were balanced again.
But then—
The smile vanished from his lips.
Filling the six-inch screen was not a report that the Team 1 Leader had captured Jin Taekyung, but a single photograph.
What is this?
He recognized the faces.
A young man grinned broadly at the camera, blood spattered across his face.
Beside him, caught firmly in his grasp, was a middle-aged man whose complexion had turned as blue as a drug addict’s.
Jin Taekyung...and the Team 1 Leader?
That wasn’t all.
The background was familiar too.
The nameplate reading Hunter Park Jihoon, Myeongdong Guild Team 1 made it unmistakably clear where they were.
And there was one more thing.
No way...
Did no one stop him?
That one Jin Taekyung?
A reality he did not want to believe.
Park Jihoon’s eyes darted helplessly around as they began to tremble.
Bzzz.
Another text arrived.
Its contents were brief but devastating.
Five Korean characters were enough to shatter Park Jihoon’s composure.
Team 1 Leader └ Team 1 Leader: Bring Melona when you come.
“This—this fucking...!”
Crack.
The phone in Park Jihoon’s hand crumpled like a sheet of paper.
Watching him, Myeongdong Guild Master Park Tae Seop muttered quietly,
“We’re fucked.”
Team Leader Choi └ Team Leader Choi: We’ve captured the people dispatched by Myeongdong Guild.
The text was from Team Leader Choi.
A few hours earlier, after burning down the safe house used by the Black Hunters, we had split up.
Team Leader Choi and the others would lie in ambush to secure solid evidence, while I had insisted on acting alone.
It was because Team Leader Choi had argued that we absolutely had to capture something that could serve as evidence or a witness.
He was right.
Every Black Hunter, including Im Yeongjun, had been managed so meticulously that their identities had already been laundered clean.
There wasn’t even the slightest link connecting them to Myeongdong Guild.
Team Leader Choi had identified that problem exactly.
He’s always calm and composed.
Looking back, he had never once lost sight of the right path.
Having Butler Kim as both an excellent mage and a wise adviser probably helped, but at this point, Choi had to be a natural.
Now we have solid leverage.
On top of the captured Black Hunters, we had official Myeongdong Guild employees in our hands.
That should make an excellent shield.
Or a dagger.
I sent him a message thanking him for his hard work, along with the photograph I’d taken earlier.
Maybe it was because it was an AdultPhone, but even a picture taken with my foot came out great.
“Maybe I should replace my phone while I’m at it.”
Someone flinched at my mutter.
It was the Security Team Hunter I’d hired as my personal cameraman for the day.
Of course, I wasn’t paying him.
“What’s wrong?”
“N-Nothing, sir!”
“Make yourself comfortable.
Don’t just stand there.
Sit on the sofa or something.”
“I’m comfortable like this!”
“You look pretty uncomfortable to me.”
“I’m fiiiine!”
Was it my imagination, or was there a sob mixed into his shout?
As an ordinary Security Team Hunter, he’d just watched me beat the living shit out of Team 1, the Guild’s elite—people he normally wouldn’t even dare look in the eye.
His reaction was understandable.
The ones who came later weren’t much different.
The other Myeongdong Guild Hunters who arrived afterward didn’t dare attack me after seeing the scene before them.
Of course, quite a few of them were armed with fierce devotion to their Guild.
Unfortunately, they didn’t have the skills to back it up.
Everyone who charged me got beaten to a pulp and carried away.
After I had knocked down around fifty of them, no one else tried to attack me.
Park Jihoon’s office became forbidden territory that no one could enter.
I sank into his chair.
He must be racing here like a madman by now.
Just thinking about him made my heart turn cold.
A middle-school classmate I had happened to run into on the street after ten long years.
How much of what I saw was the real Park Jihoon?
Hurry up and get here.
Before I get any angrier.
Crack.
The armrest snapped beneath my grip.
“H-He’s here!”
“Guild Master!”
Murmurs spread beyond the office door like a wildfire.
At the same time, I sensed two immense presences approaching without hesitation.
He’s here.
And in the next moment, the door blew apart with a thunderous roar.
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 282
paragraphs: BOOM!
Two people appeared amid the thunderous roar.
I waved at the familiar face among them.
“Well, look who’s here. You fucking bastard.”
I’d been planning to punch him in the mouth the moment I saw him, but the sight of his face twisting with rage drew a quiet laugh from me instead.
Eyeing Park Jihoon’s tightly clenched fist, I put on a disappointed expression.
“You didn’t bring it?”
“What?”
“Melona.”
“You little—”
A huge hand closed around his shoulder as his face flushed red.
“There are still too many eyes on us.”
Biting his lip, Park Jihoon took a step back.
I watched in amusement as the middle-aged man beside him cleared everyone from the immediate area, then addressed me.
“Do you know who I am?”
I nodded. There was no way I wouldn’t recognize that face.
His name carried plenty of weight, and he appeared often enough in newspapers, magazines, and other media.
Park Tae Seop, Guild Master of Myeongdong Guild.
A war hero who had distinguished himself during the Great Cataclysm, and one of Korea’s top rankers.
He had survived countless brutal struggles to become the master of a major Guild. To Hunters, he was both an inspiration and a respected elder.
I used to respect him too.
Not anymore.
My good memories of Park Tae Seop had expired two days ago.
What you thought tended to show in your attitude. Reading the undisguised hostility in my gaze, Park Tae Seop spoke.
“You... consider me your enemy.”
“I can’t exactly consider you a friend. We both know what’s going on.”
“Don’t be so quick to decide. Live long enough, and you’ll realize there are no eternal friends or enemies.”
“I don’t know about the part where there are no eternal enemies.”
I looked at Park Jihoon beside him.
“But the part about there being no eternal friends makes a lot of sense.”
Park Jihoon replied coldly.
“Your premise is wrong from the start. We were never friends.”
“We were never friends.”
I sank deeper into the chair and repeated his words under my breath.
One thing I still couldn’t understand was Park Jihoon’s sudden change in attitude.
But...
“Then again, what does that matter now? Whatever we had was already over the moment you sent those Black Hunters.”
At the mention of that sensitive term, Park Tae Seop waved a hand.
At the Guild Master’s command, the hundred or so Hunters filling the hallway receded like the tide.
Listening to their footsteps fade into the distance, I curled my lips.
“You’re not exactly being open about it.”
“It’s a disgrace.”
“And you’re irritatingly honest.”
“I’m personally ashamed of it.”
“For someone who considers himself ashamed, you gave a pretty damn despicable order.”
“Why?”
Discomfort flickered across Park Tae Seop’s face, but it wasn’t directed at me.
For the briefest instant, his gaze touched Park Jihoon beside him before darting away.
Well, well...
That reaction hadn’t been deliberate.
If it had slipped out unconsciously, he was definitely hiding something.
I thought back over everything that hadn’t quite added up.
Something stinks to high heaven. It reeks.
As I muttered to myself, Park Jihoon abruptly spoke.
“To keep you and the Peace Guild in check.”
“Keep us in check?”
“A new powerhouse emerging means a smaller slice of the pie for someone else. I’m sure the other Guilds feel the same way we do.”
On the surface, it made sense.
Korea’s Guild market was already oversaturated. Its tiers had been divided and its pecking order established. The old powers had no desire to see a new competitor emerge.
“The Peace Guild is dangerous. For now, you’re confined to Bucheon, but soon you’ll grow at a frightening pace and expand your influence.”
“So you sent the Black Hunters?”
“We did. But didn’t I already tell you? It was only a warning.”
“And I believe I already told you that your pathetic warning left someone crippled.”
“Crippled? They reattached his two severed arms without any problems. His daily life won’t be affected at all. Is that what people call crippled these days?”
“He might as well be. His career as a Hunter is over.”
“Better his career than the entire Guild.”
“What?”
Park Jihoon snorted.
“This is only the beginning. Every high-rank Gate worth entering has already been closed off to your Guild. With the surrounding Guilds shutting you out, you’ll slowly wither away and die.”
Something Team Leader Choi had told me a few days ago suddenly came to mind.
The other Guilds had snapped up every A-rank Gate.
Because of that, I’d been forced to drag the rookies from one C-rank or B-rank Gate to another, unable to gain any meaningful EXP.
“Don’t tell me that was—”
“You’re slow. Did you think it was a coincidence?”
The corners of Park Jihoon’s mouth rose. He had not only fully regained his composure, but was even relaxed enough to lean back against the sofa.

“I heard you recruited a lot of Guild members recently. What are you going to do now? At this rate, you’ll have to let them all go within a year. You’ll be lucky if they don’t sue when you can’t pay their allowances.”
I slowly relaxed my folded arms.
“You’re good at this. No wonder you’re a major Guild.”
“Well, I suppose we are.”

“But... we’ve got a pretty decent card too. I think it’d be interesting if everything Myeongdong Guild did behind the scenes after scraping together a bunch of criminal bastards came to light. What do you think?”
I continued without waiting for Park Jihoon to respond.
“Judging by how things work around here, you’d just snatch them away if we handed them over to the police. So I figured we could play a little truth game on an iTube livestream instead.”
“...iTube? A livestream?”
“Oh, right. You don’t know we opened a Guild channel, do you? Subscribe and hit Like. Don’t forget to turn on notifications.”
“Wow, we’re already at three hundred thousand subscribers. If this blows up, we might break ten million. Half the country will probably tune in.”
The smile vanished from Park Jihoon’s lips without a trace.
“You shouldn’t start something you can’t handle.”
“I’ll handle it.”
“Do you want to make every major Guild your enemy?”
“If I raise hell here, can you handle the fallout?”
Park Jihoon’s mouth snapped shut as though it had been glued.
After glaring at me with burning eyes for a while, he spat out a single sentence.
“Tell me what you want.”
“What I want?”
“We’ll accommodate your demands as much as possible. Don’t make this any bigger. Let’s negotiate and end it here.”
“Negotiate.”
“If we take this all the way, we’ll both come out wounded. You know that as well as I do.”
He was right.
If I were the only one who had to bear the consequences, I would have taken this all the way.
But the lives of countless people connected to the Peace Guild were at stake.
Someone’s friend, lover, family...
Their futures too.
I quietly licked my dry lips.
“What can you give me?”
“Money and power. And all kinds of benefits that will help the Peace Guild grow.”
“Didn’t you say the Peace Guild’s growth bothered you enough to send the Black Hunters?”
“Which is why we need to set boundaries.”
“You’re telling us not to stray outside the fence you build?”
“That’s right.”
The longer I listened to Park Jihoon’s proposal, the clearer the picture became.
What we stood to gain in exchange for handing over the Peace Guild’s prisoners and keeping quiet about the incident was substantial.
No, it was enormous.
Buildings and land. Exclusive rights to high-rank Gates currently controlled by Myeongdong Guild. Even a staggering amount of cash.
The overall deal looked good.
But...
“You left out the most important part.”
“Those terms are already more than generous enough—what?”
Park Jihoon frowned.
“What did you just say?”
“I said you left out the most important part.”
“You’re insane. You’re demanding even more?”
“To be honest, there’s no point explaining all this to me. I understand that it’s valuable, but our Guild Master and Team Leader Choi are the experts on which terms are good or bad for us.”
“Then what exactly did I leave out?”
I stared at Park Jihoon.
“An apology.”
“...What?”
“If you did something wrong, you should apologize. But the most important thing—an apology—is missing.”
His offer was packed with extravagant terms, but there was no apology.
The one thing that should have come before everything else was nowhere to be found.
“Ha.”
Park Jihoon let out an incredulous laugh. The way he looked me up and down made his anger and disbelief plain.
“Fine. I’m sorry. Happy now?”
“That’s not how you apologize.”
Crack.
The bones in Park Jihoon’s tightly clenched fist shifted with an ugly pop.
A moment later, he drew a deep breath, looked me in the eye, and enunciated each word.
“I’m sorry.”
“That’s a little better.”
“Are you satisfied now?”
I gave a small nod.
“But next time you do it in person, try putting a little more sincerity into it. Bow your head politely, too.”
“...What the hell are you talking about now?”
“What good does apologizing to me do? You need to apologize to the victim and his family.”
Park Jihoon’s eyelids trembled.
“You want me to apologize to that D-rank Hunter?”
“Why? Can’t do it?”
“I already told you we’d pay him compensation. It’s more money than most Hunters will ever see in their lives.”
“That works out nicely, then. A heartfelt apology accompanied by a massive compensation payment as a token of remorse should be even more effective.”
I gently added one more remark as Park Jihoon glared daggers at me.
“If it hurts your pride, bring someone else along and apologize together.”
Myeongdong Guild Master Park Tae Seop, who had listened in silence until now, finally spoke.
“I’ll visit him in person and apologize. Sincerely.”
“At least you understand the basics, Guild Master. I suppose that makes you a slightly cleaner piece of shit.”
Cleaner shit.
At that moment, I couldn’t think of a more fitting—or more paradoxical—description.
But Park Tae Seop wasn’t the other suspect I had in mind.
I leaned forward in my chair and stared into Park Jihoon’s eyes.
“Bring the person who gave you your orders. Make that person apologize too.”
A violent storm churned in his eyes.
It lasted only an instant, but that brief flash of agitation was more than enough to turn my suspicion into certainty.
“Fine. Guild Master Park Tae Seop just agreed, anyway.”
Park Jihoon continued in the calmest voice he could manage.
“We’ll go together and apologize.”
“Cut the bullshit. Bring that person here.”
“I don’t know what you’re talking about.”
I rose with a quiet laugh and walked toward the reception sofa where Park Jihoon sat.
“No matter how much I thought about it, I just couldn’t make sense of it.”
I dropped into the seat across from him.
With the large solid-wood table between us, I slowly studied him as he pretended to remain calm.
His solid build. The muscles visible beneath his shirt.
And the power lurking within him.
It was immense and powerful.
Even without checking his Level, I could tell how wide the gap was between him and the Team 1 Leader.
“What couldn’t you make sense of?”
“How someone strong enough to chew up that Team Leader lying over there with one hand isn’t even a deputy team leader. He’s just an ordinary Hunter.”
“Not to mention you show up for work so rarely that you might come in once a month. And from the way you spoke to the Team 1 Leader over the phone, you were practically his superior.”
There were too many suspicious details to count.
And as our conversation continued, those suspicions had gradually hardened into certainty.

“We’re discussing terms on this scale, but the man supposedly in charge stays silent while an ordinary team member with no position does all the talking... How am I supposed to interpret that, Guild Master Park Tae Seop?”
Myeongdong Guild Master Park Tae Seop held my gaze, then slowly closed his eyes.
That was answer enough.
I laughed quietly and looked at Park Jihoon.
“So bring that person here. I don’t know who it is, but bring them here and make them apologize first.”
Park Jihoon’s tightly sealed lips finally parted.
“And if I refuse?”
“Then we take this all the way.”
“You crazy bastard. Do you even know who that person is?”
“No. I don’t particularly want to know, either. But I do want to see that bastard come here, slam his head down, and apologize. Then I’ll be satisfied.”
Swish!
At that same instant, I shot out a hand at blinding speed.
Park Jihoon cried out in alarm.
“You bastard!”
Pap-pap-pap!
Our hands collided and tangled in an instant.
Five exchanges passed in the blink of an eye.
Crunch.
His wrist broke, and his eyes flew wide.
I seized his neatly waxed hair and slammed his head into the table.
BANG!
“Like this.”

“What did you just say?”
“I said you left out the most important part.”
“You’re insane.
You’re demanding even more?”
“To be honest, there’s no point explaining all this to me.
I understand that it’s valuable, but our Guild Master and Team Leader Choi are the experts on which terms are good or bad for us.”
“Then what exactly did I leave out?”
I stared at Park Jihoon.
“An apology.”
“...What?”
“If you did something wrong, you should apologize.
But the most important thing—an apology—is missing.”
His offer was packed with extravagant terms, but there was no apology.
The one thing that should have come before everything else was nowhere to be found.
“Ha.”
Park Jihoon let out an incredulous laugh.
The way he looked me up and down made his anger and disbelief plain.
“Fine.
I’m sorry.
Happy now?”
“That’s not how you apologize.”
Crack.
The bones in Park Jihoon’s tightly clenched fist shifted with an ugly pop.
A moment later, he drew a deep breath, looked me in the eye, and enunciated each word.
“I’m sorry.”
“That’s a little better.”
“Are you satisfied now?”
I gave a small nod.
“But next time you do it in person, try putting a little more sincerity into it.
Bow your head politely, too.”
“...What the hell are you talking about now?”
“What good does apologizing to me do?
You need to apologize to the victim and his family.”
Park Jihoon’s eyelids trembled.
“You want me to apologize to that D-rank Hunter?”
“Why?
Can’t do it?”
“I already told you we’d pay him compensation.
It’s more money than most Hunters will ever see in their lives.”
“That works out nicely, then.
A heartfelt apology accompanied by a massive compensation payment as a token of remorse should be even more effective.”
I gently added one more remark as Park Jihoon glared daggers at me.
“If it hurts your pride, bring someone else along and apologize together.”
Myeongdong Guild Master Park Tae Seop, who had listened in silence until now, finally spoke.
“I’ll visit him in person and apologize.
Sincerely.”
“At least you understand the basics, Guild Master.
I suppose that makes you a slightly cleaner piece of shit.”
Cleaner shit.
At that moment, I couldn’t think of a more fitting—or more paradoxical—description.
But Park Tae Seop wasn’t the other suspect I had in mind.
I leaned forward in my chair and stared into Park Jihoon’s eyes.
“Bring the person who gave you your orders.
Make that person apologize too.”
A violent storm churned in his eyes.
It lasted only an instant, but that brief flash of agitation was more than enough to turn my suspicion into certainty.
“Fine.
Guild Master Park Tae Seop just agreed, anyway.”
Park Jihoon continued in the calmest voice he could manage.
“We’ll go together and apologize.”
“Cut the bullshit.
Bring that person here.”
“I don’t know what you’re talking about.”
I rose with a quiet laugh and walked toward the reception sofa where Park Jihoon sat.
“No matter how much I thought about it, I just couldn’t make sense of it.”
I dropped into the seat across from him.
With the large solid-wood table between us, I slowly studied him as he pretended to remain calm.
His solid build.
The muscles visible beneath his shirt.
And the power lurking within him.
It was immense and powerful.
Even without checking his Level, I could tell how wide the gap was between him and the Team 1 Leader.
“What couldn’t you make sense of?”
“How someone strong enough to chew up that Team Leader lying over there with one hand isn’t even a deputy team leader.
He’s just an ordinary Hunter.”
“Not to mention you show up for work so rarely that you might come in once a month.
And from the way you spoke to the Team 1 Leader over the phone, you were practically his superior.”
There were too many suspicious details to count.
And as our conversation continued, those suspicions had gradually hardened into certainty.
“We’re discussing terms on this scale, but the man supposedly in charge stays silent while an ordinary team member with no position does all the talking...
How am I supposed to interpret that, Guild Master Park Tae Seop?”
Myeongdong Guild Master Park Tae Seop held my gaze, then slowly closed his eyes.
That was answer enough.
I laughed quietly and looked at Park Jihoon.
“So bring that person here.
I don’t know who it is, but bring them here and make them apologize first.”
Park Jihoon’s tightly sealed lips finally parted.
“And if I refuse?”
“Then we take this all the way.”
“You crazy bastard.
Do you even know who that person is?”
“No.
I don’t particularly want to know, either.
But I do want to see that bastard come here, slam his head down, and apologize.
Then I’ll be satisfied.”
Swish!
At that same instant, I shot out a hand at blinding speed.
Park Jihoon cried out in alarm.
“You bastard!”
Pap-pap-pap!
Our hands collided and tangled in an instant.
Five exchanges passed in the blink of an eye.
Crunch.
His wrist broke, and his eyes flew wide.
I seized his neatly waxed hair and slammed his head into the table.
BANG!
“Like this.”

chapters.title: Chapter 283
paragraphs: BANG!
The air in the office vibrated with a sharp hum.
Park Jihoon’s forehead smashed through the table and slammed into the floor. With a sharp crack, spiderweb fractures spread across the ground.
“Guh.”
I pressed my knee into his back, applying the principles of the Thousand-Catty Drop.
I stared at the back of his head in surprise.
Huh. Look at this bastard.
Modern Hunters had no concept of martial arts.
Even among close-combat types, it was extremely rare to find someone like Im Yeongjun, a Black Hunter who focused primarily on hand-to-hand combat. Most concentrated on weapons.
Because that was the better way to improve their survival rate.
But Park Jihoon was different. Though it had lasted only an instant, the movements he had shown were comparable to those of a Peak master from Murim.
It was a little clumsy, but it was almost like a grappling technique wielded by someone who had reached a higher realm.

I had underestimated him and been caught off guard. The fight had ended almost immediately, but the fact that he had exchanged moves with me five times already put his ability far beyond what I had expected.
Has this level of hand-to-hand combat survived into the modern era? Why hasn’t anyone heard of it?
With those questions in mind, I asked.
“You. Where did you learn that just now?”
Park Jihoon answered in a strained voice.
“Let go right now, before you regret it.”
“I see. Still full of energy, are you?”
BANG! BANG! BANG!
Once. Twice. Three times.
Every time I grabbed his hair and slammed his head down, a muffled groan escaped him. Blood spattered across the office floor, which had been spotless only moments ago.
As his body went limp, Park Tae Seop, who had been observing the situation, suddenly spoke.
“That’s enough.”
“Is this bastard your son, Guild Master?”
“Would he be my son?”
“Then is he your daughter?”
“Obviously not that, either.”
“Then this isn’t your problem. If you cross the line here, I can’t guarantee what I’ll do.”
Park Tae Seop’s eyebrow twitched.
“You’ve got quite a spicy tongue.”
“My hands are even spicier. My old nickname was the Haengsin-dong Fire-Chicken Stir-Fried Hand... Want a taste?”
“I have a reputation to uphold. I have no intention of fighting someone as young and green as you.”
Park Tae Seop uncrossed his arms and continued.
“But if that fellow is seriously injured, it will put me in a difficult position. He’s an important business partner.”

“He’s a manager sent by your business partner, isn’t he? No, seeing how he pushes you around, it’s embarrassing to even call you partners. You’re practically a figurehead. Does he have something on you?”
I must have struck a nerve, because he made a show of frowning.
“You’re more perceptive than I expected. Though I heard you weren’t very bright.”
I didn’t need to ask which bastard had said that.
I grabbed Park Jihoon’s wax-stiffened hair even more roughly and answered.
“I’m a slow learner. But once I learn something, I don’t forget it.”
“He learned his lesson properly this time, so let him go now.”
“I was planning to do that anyway.”
As I lifted Park Jihoon by the hair, Park Tae Seop gave a small nod.
“Good thinking...”
I drove the fistful of hair back down with all my strength.
BANG!
One more time.
CRUNCH!
The floor shattered beneath the deafening impact. As Park Jihoon flopped around like a raw fish, I drove my toe into his solar plexus.
THUD!
He flew backward and slid all the way to the door.
“Ghk!”
The impact jolted him awake. He trembled violently and spat out a mouthful of blood.
Park Tae Seop was unable to continue speaking, so I addressed him.
“I let him go. There. Happy?”
“You... You’re quite something.”
“Am I really as bad as the bastard who cuts people’s arms off and calls it a warning?”
“I don’t particularly like that fellow myself, but you would’ve been better off taking my advice.”
His expression and voice had turned rigid.
He was serious.
Rather than feeling afraid, I became curious. Who was this person that even Park Tae Seop—a war hero of the Great Cataclysm and one of Korea’s top rankers—was wary of?
I asked with a questioning look.
“Who is it? That bastard only called him ‘that person.’”
“I can’t tell you. Even if I did, you’d only resent me later.”
“Why make such a big deal out of it? Is that person Asmodeus or something?”
“If you made him your enemy, you’d be better off facing the Demon King. At least then, the whole world would fight alongside you... But what are you doing right now?”
Park Tae Seop stared at me wide-eyed.
Or, to be precise, at the phone in my hand.
“I’m looking at this phone.”
“Suddenly?”
“Yes.”
He had the exact expression of a man wondering what kind of lunatic he was dealing with.
Completely baffled, Park Tae Seop asked, “What are you doing with it?”
“What do you think? Since you won’t tell me, I’m trying to find his number myself.”
“His number?”
“Yes. That person’s number.”
“Wait. Is that...?”
“That’s right. I took it from that bastard’s pocket earlier.”
Park Tae Seop’s eyes widened. Park Jihoon, who had been coughing up blood, shouted as though he had forgotten his pain.
“Give it back right now!”
“Nope. Can’t.”
I toyed with the mysterious phone, whose make I couldn’t identify.

It looked completely different from the phone I had seen when I visited his officetel last time. There was no way he had replaced it in the past few days, so it was probably a separate phone he kept for secret communications.
It wasn’t that strange. Even people secretly cheating on their partners carried two or three phones.
He has so many secrets, after all.
When I touched the screen, two messages appeared alongside a lock icon. One asked for a fingerprint, and the other for an iris scan.
I could understand the fingerprint part, but what the hell was with the iris scan?
I beckoned to Park Jihoon, who was staggering to his feet.
“Hey. Come here. Let it scan your fingerprint and iris.”
“Jin Taekyung, you crazy bastard. Do you even know what you’re doing?”
“Yeah, I know. So get over here and put your eye and finger against it before I rip them out.”
“Don’t rush me. I was planning to do that without you telling me.”
Park Jihoon ground his teeth with a crunch and wiped at the corner of his mouth.
But unlike before, when he had been gasping for breath, he was now brimming with strength.
Aside from the blood covering him here and there, his cracked forehead and broken nose had already healed completely. His stamina was as good as new.
Only then did I notice a small reinforced-glass vial rolling around by his feet.
“A potion?”
“When there’s an enemy in front of you, never let your attention wander until the very end. Didn’t they teach you that at the training center?”
He must have taken out the hidden potion and gulped it down during the brief moment I was looking at my phone. I shrugged.
“That only matters when the two sides are evenly matched. That’s not the case here, is it?”
“What?”
“I don’t know where you learned that or who taught you, but...”
As I circulated my qi according to the formula of the Fire Gate Divine Technique, the fire dragon coiled within my dantian awakened.
I fixed Park Jihoon with glowing, reddish eyes.
“You and I are in different classes, you fucking scrub.”

The next moment, the fire dragon formed from a jiazi’s worth of Scorching Yang Qi scattered into hundreds of streams. As they dispersed, they awakened my acupoints and raced forward without restraint.
The internal energy met again at a single destination and merged into one.
Disperse, compress. And...
Release.
WHOOSH!

Early winter was already setting in, but the frigid office transformed into the sweltering heat of midsummer beneath a blazing sun. An enormous burst of fiery qi erupted in an instant and surged through the room.
“Hah.”
I exhaled a scorching breath.
Beyond the wavering heat haze, I saw a man whose face was filled with shock. His expression had gone rigid, and turbulent waves churned in his eyes.
“You... You...”
Park Jihoon’s voice emerged as a groan.
“How?”
“I told you. We’re different.”
As though someone had doused him in ice water, he shuddered and bit down on his lip. He bit so hard that the flesh split at once and blood began to flow.
“This... This is impossible. How could you...?”
The man muttered with a twisted expression, then abruptly opened his mouth.
“I’m going to need your help.”
There was no question who he was addressing.
Park Tae Seop, Guild Master of Myeongdong Guild, had been watching me with astonishment. He answered in a heavy voice.
“Is there any way for me to refuse that proposal?”
“No.”
“And if I refuse anyway?”
“Guaranteed rewards and punishments according to the choice you make. You know how ‘that person’ operates, Guild Master.”
“...I’m sick to death of this.”
Park Tae Seop sighed and pulled a sixty-centimeter-long rod from his waist. When he stroked the Magic Gem attached to its end, a snow-white blade surged upward.
HSSSSSS!
“Don’t blame me.”
With that bitter remark, he pointed the sword at me. Blue aura engulfed its blade.
My opponent was a hero of the Great Cataclysm and one of Korea’s top ten rankers. An immense aura rose from his body to confront my Scorching Yang Qi.
With a powerful ally at his side, Park Jihoon smiled coldly.
“You’re finished.”
“Finished?”
I laughed aloud.
Since I had heard he went to Hankuk University, I had assumed he was at least somewhat intelligent. But it seemed he had completely forgotten what I’d told him last time.
“I’m the one who decides whether this ends, you fucking idiot.”
Park Jihoon had forced me onto the starting line and pulled the trigger to signal the beginning of the race. But he had failed to anticipate the most important thing.
This race had no finish line.
And that wherever I stopped was the finish line.
Open Inventory.
Summon White Flame.
FWOOSH!
I stepped forward amid the flames.
Blue fire streamed along the spearhead, scorching everything around it as it surged toward the enemy.
“Haah!”
With a powerful battle cry, a massive greatsword came flying at me. The blue aura gathered at its tip was denser and longer than anything I had ever seen in reality.
As expected of one of Korea’s top rankers.
Internal energy and mana.
The names were different, but their essence was the same. In that sense, the energy Park Tae Seop possessed exceeded mine.
But...
That’s as far as it goes.
At the thought, I sprang upward.
My hair narrowly grazed the ceiling as the blade sweeping toward my waist cut through empty air.
WHOOM! CLANG-CLANG-CLANG!
The tremendous pressure wave swept everything away. The reinforced glass covering one side of the office shattered and plummeted toward the ground.
Before the screams from below could reach me, I brought the spearhead down toward the crown of Park Tae Seop’s head.
WHOOSH! BANG!
With a deafening roar, Park Tae Seop’s knee struck the floor.
His eyes widened in shock as he hurriedly blocked the attack with the shield in his other hand.
“What is this?”
By now, he must have felt as though a massive boulder weighing ten thousand geun was crushing him.
That was partly the difference in our physical abilities and partly the gap created by the way we used our energy.
Hunters really aren’t very efficient.

In contrast, Murim cultivation techniques explosively increased the efficiency of internal energy. That was why renowned great powers like the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families were so strong.
Superior internal cultivation techniques formed the heart of the martial arts they wielded.
Only when all those tiny gears meshed together with perfect precision could an art truly be called divine.
Disperse, compress, release.
Internal energy was like a scarce resource. You had to draw it out only when absolutely necessary and use it to maximum effect.
Even Park Tae Seop, one of Korea’s top rankers, had not completely escaped that limitation.
BANG! BANG! BOOM!
The instant Park Tae Seop’s shield split in half after blocking a total of four attacks, a flash streaked toward my side.
“Die!”
The wielder of the thin, sharp rapier could only be Park Jihoon.
Just as I thought I had dodged it, the aura extending from the blade’s tip suddenly lengthened and grazed my side.
SIZZLE!
Disappointment flashed across Park Jihoon’s face.
His aura had only cut through my clothes and passed by.
I checked my uninjured side and licked my lips.
“...This is pretty interesting.”
“Interesting? You’re not afraid?”
“Did the guy you call ‘that person’ or whatever teach you?”
“Shut your mouth. You’re not worthy of even speaking of that person.”
“Huh. So I was right. This isn’t some kind of cult, is it?”
“You son of a—!”
WHOOM! SHH-SHH-SHHK!
Park Tae Seop’s greatsword came from the right, while Park Jihoon’s rapier flew in from the left.
Watching the two men tear through the space between us, I thrust out both arms.
BANG! BOOM!
I blocked Park Tae Seop’s greatsword with White Flame and Park Jihoon’s rapier with the dagger I had just summoned, then smoothly rotated my wrists.
KRRRANG!
The four blades, locked in a tense clash, tangled around one another.
I remembered my duel with Sword Saint Mae Jonghak.
His sword, which had let everything flow past.
His movements.
And I put them into practice.
Flow.
Sliiide.
The spearhead and dagger slipped forward like snakes. Neither the massive greatsword nor the slender rapier could block their path.
A moment later, the keen edges of my two weapons touched their throats.
Swish.
“Drop your weapons.”
Two shocked gazes turned toward me.
Park Jihoon spoke in a voice filled with rage and despair.
“How could you...?”
“You didn’t hear me, did you?”
CRACK!
There was no hesitation.
I raised my foot and drove it down onto his knee. Cartilage shattered, and a scream burst from him.
“Aaaaargh!”
“We’re down two arms on our side. One leg doesn’t balance the books.”
I was about to crush his remaining knee when—
“I think that should be enough.”
An unfamiliar voice pierced my ears.
It was impossibly deep and low. A chill ran down my spine, and every fine hair on my body stood on end.
This was...
A Supreme Peak master?
