I stepped forward amid the flames.
Blue fire streamed along the spearhead, scorching everything around it as it surged toward the enemy.
“Haah!”
With a powerful battle cry, a massive greatsword came flying at me.
The blue aura gathered at its tip was denser and longer than anything I had ever seen in reality.
As expected of one of Korea’s top rankers.
Internal energy and mana.
The names were different, but their essence was the same.
In that sense, the energy Park Tae Seop possessed exceeded mine.
But...
That’s as far as it goes.
At the thought, I sprang upward.
My hair narrowly grazed the ceiling as the blade sweeping toward my waist cut through empty air.
WHOOM!
CLANG-CLANG-CLANG!
The tremendous pressure wave swept everything away.
The reinforced glass covering one side of the office shattered and plummeted toward the ground.
Before the screams from below could reach me, I brought the spearhead down toward the crown of Park Tae Seop’s head.
WHOOSH!
BANG!
With a deafening roar, Park Tae Seop’s knee struck the floor.
His eyes widened in shock as he hurriedly blocked the attack with the shield in his other hand.
“What is this?”
By now, he must have felt as though a massive boulder weighing ten thousand geun was crushing him.
That was partly the difference in our physical abilities and partly the gap created by the way we used our energy.
Hunters really aren’t very efficient.
In contrast, Murim cultivation techniques explosively increased the efficiency of internal energy.
That was why renowned great powers like the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families were so strong.
Superior internal cultivation techniques formed the heart of the martial arts they wielded.
Only when all those tiny gears meshed together with perfect precision could an art truly be called divine.
Disperse, compress, release.
Internal energy was like a scarce resource.
You had to draw it out only when absolutely necessary and use it to maximum effect.
Even Park Tae Seop, one of Korea’s top rankers, had not completely escaped that limitation.
BANG!
BANG!
BOOM!
The instant Park Tae Seop’s shield split in half after blocking a total of four attacks, a flash streaked toward my side.
“Die!”
The wielder of the thin, sharp rapier could only be Park Jihoon.
Just as I thought I had dodged it, the aura extending from the blade’s tip suddenly lengthened and grazed my side.
SIZZLE!
Disappointment flashed across Park Jihoon’s face.
His aura had only cut through my clothes and passed by.
I checked my uninjured side and licked my lips.
“...This is pretty interesting.”
“Interesting?
You’re not afraid?”
“Did the guy you call ‘that person’ or whatever teach you?”
“Shut your mouth.
You’re not worthy of even speaking of that person.”
“Huh.
So I was right.
This isn’t some kind of cult, is it?”
“You son of a—!”
WHOOM!
SHH-SHH-SHHK!
Park Tae Seop’s greatsword came from the right, while Park Jihoon’s rapier flew in from the left.
Watching the two men tear through the space between us, I thrust out both arms.
BANG!
BOOM!
I blocked Park Tae Seop’s greatsword with White Flame and Park Jihoon’s rapier with the dagger I had just summoned, then smoothly rotated my wrists.
KRRRANG!
The four blades, locked in a tense clash, tangled around one another.
I remembered my duel with Sword Saint Mae Jonghak.
His sword, which had let everything flow past.
His movements.
And I put them into practice.
Flow.
Sliiide.
The spearhead and dagger slipped forward like snakes.
Neither the massive greatsword nor the slender rapier could block their path.
A moment later, the keen edges of my two weapons touched their throats.
Swish.
“Drop your weapons.”
Two shocked gazes turned toward me.
Park Jihoon spoke in a voice filled with rage and despair.
“How could you...?”
“You didn’t hear me, did you?”
CRACK!
There was no hesitation.
I raised my foot and drove it down onto his knee.
Cartilage shattered, and a scream burst from him.
“Aaaaargh!”
“We’re down two arms on our side.
One leg doesn’t balance the books.”
I was about to crush his remaining knee when—
“I think that should be enough.”
An unfamiliar voice pierced my ears.
It was impossibly deep and low.
A chill ran down my spine, and every fine hair on my body stood on end.
This was...
A Supreme Peak master?

chapters.title: Chapter 284
paragraphs: “I think that’s enough.”
I hadn’t expected that.
The voice from behind me sent a chill through my mind, as though someone had dumped ice water over my head.
When did he get there?
I hadn’t sensed his presence. Even considering that I’d been in the middle of a fight, that should have been impossible.
If he had slipped past senses honed to the very edge of Peak, there was only one answer.
A Supreme Peak master.
I slowly turned around. A man stood amid the rubble of a wall brought down in the fighting, gazing steadily at me.
“Nice to meet you.”
He was a middle-aged man who looked to be in his early forties, with bold features drawn in strong brushstrokes and a solid build that even his clothes couldn’t conceal.
And...
He’s strong.
The moment I sensed the qi coiled within him, my heart sank. At the same time, all my accumulated experience and keenly honed instincts whispered a warning.
The middle-aged man before me was a Supreme Peak master beyond anything I could handle in my current state.
“Young man, you’ve got good instincts. Better than I expected.”
The middle-aged man looked me over with interest, then suddenly tilted his head.
“Or is it because you recognize my face?”
“Both.”
His appearance had shaken me badly.
I tried my best to look calm, but I couldn’t hide the crack in my voice or the tremor in my eyes.
“Well, it’s not as if my face has only been plastered around once or twice.”
The middle-aged man nodded as if it were nothing and strode forward.
He crossed the wrecked office and held out his hand.
“Nice to meet you. I’m Lee Jungryong.”
A short, simple introduction.
But the meaning and influence carried by the three characters of Lee Jungryong’s name were anything but short or simple.
He was the kind of man who could use his face and name as identification anywhere in the world, not just in Korea.
The second-in-command of Ares Guild. And one of Korea’s two S-rank Hunters.
That was Lee Jungryong.
A powerful man who wielded absolute authority over Ares Guild in place of its Guild Master, the other S-rank Hunter.
Ares Guild was said to rank among the top five Guilds in the world. Its influence over Hunters was immense, to say nothing of politics and the economy.
People even said that Korea had two Blue Houses.
Why had someone so powerful appeared here of all places, at this exact moment?
Fuck. It’s obvious.
Suddenly, the conversation I’d had with Park Tae Seop flashed through my mind.
“Who is he? That bastard earlier only called him ‘that person.’”
I can’t tell you. Even if I did, you’d only resent me later.
Why make such a big deal out of it? Is that person Asmodeus or something?
If you made him your enemy, it would be better if he were the Demon King. At least then, the whole world would fight alongside you.
The answer had already formed in my mind.
If Lee Jungryong was the “that person” Park Jihoon had mentioned, and Ares Guild was behind this whole affair, every piece fell perfectly into place.
This is turning into a real goddamn mess.
The unexpected arrival of such a major figure made my blood run cold.
Unlike me, frozen stiff, Lee Jungryong smiled gently and spoke.
“I’ve heard a great deal about you. You look much better in person than you do on television.”
“Thank you.”
“You don’t look happy to see me at all.”
“How could that be? You’re an S-rank Hunter recognized throughout the world.”
“It’s an empty reputation. I’m nowhere near the Guild Master. Anyway...”
Still wearing his distinctive smile, Lee Jungryong opened and closed his outstretched hand.
“When are you going to shake my hand? This is starting to get embarrassing.”
Watching his good-natured smile and listening to the easy joke, I had one thought.
This man has at least a hundred snakes coiled in his belly.
And I hated snakes.
“I’m sorry, but I don’t have a hand free right now.”
“Is that really a problem? Just put down whatever you’re holding and it’ll be easily resolved.”
“I can’t drop a problem that needs to be dealt with right now just for a handshake.”
I tightened my grip on the weapons in each hand.
Swish.
With a faint sound, thin lines of blood appeared across Park Tae Seop’s and Park Jihoon’s throats.
The two men had closed their eyes and pressed their lips tightly together the moment Lee Jungryong appeared. Even so, I could sense something like resolve from them.
“I hear you’re quite close with these two gentlemen. Why don’t you at least say hello?”
“Close? Me?”
Lee Jungryong let out a hearty laugh.
“I’ve known Guild Master Park since the Great Cataclysm, so we’re at least acquainted. Isn’t that right?”
Park Tae Seop, Guild Master of Myeongdong Guild, bit his lip before answering.
“It’s been a long time, Vice Guild Master Lee Jungryong.”
“Yes, it has. But what happened here?”
“There was an unpleasant incident... I apologize for letting you see me in such a sorry state.”
“I don’t know what sort of misunderstanding there has been, but surely it can be settled through conversation. And who is that young man beside you?”
“He’s a member of my Guild. He’s been with us ever since he completed his training center course.”
Park Jihoon spoke in a trembling voice.
“Nice to meet you. I’m Park Jihoon of Myeongdong Guild’s Team 1.”
I wasn’t surprised that Lee Jungryong spoke down to Park Tae Seop despite looking at least ten years younger than him.
I was surprised by their shamelessness.
Everyone here knew that Lee Jungryong was the one who had given Park Jihoon his first orders.
Yet the exchange I had just witnessed between the three men could mean only one thing.
The lizard’s tail.
The old lizard, already prepared to cut off its tail, smiled gently at me.
“See? I’ve never even met that young man before, and Guild Master Park and I merely exchange the occasional greeting.”
I let out a hollow laugh.
“By ‘exchanging greetings,’ do you mean secretly sending Black Hunters to cut off the arm of some innocent person?”
“Black Hunters? Enough. Your delusions are getting out of hand. In any case, regarding Guild Master Park...”
He shook his head and continued.
“I think I may be able to help a little with that problem.”
“Help?”
“Yes, help. The problem needs to be resolved, doesn’t it?”
My earlier thought had been only half right. The lizard wasn’t planning to cut off its tail just yet. He wanted to clean up the mess.
Lee Jungryong’s gaze met mine. A bead of cold sweat that had formed at some point trickled down my neck.
This was both an offer and a warning.
Let these men go.
But...
“It’s a personal matter, so I don’t think that’ll be possible.”
I would decide whether I stopped here or kept going.
I had already made up my mind.
“Hmm? Ha ha.”
Lee Jungryong laughed aloud and regarded me with amusement.
“Young man, you’ve got quite a bit of grit. Plenty of nerve, too.”
“I hear that fairly often.”
“What about arrogant?”
“I hear that even more.”
“High-spirited young men are often misunderstood.”
“I think so too.”
“Yes. I’m glad you understand, but...”
An unreadable light flashed in Lee Jungryong’s eyes.
“Don’t you think it’s time you changed?”
“How?”
“You’re a well-known public figure, and you’re nearing thirty. It would be best to avoid those sorts of misunderstandings.”
“I appreciate the advice, but I’m not planning to change yet.”
“Why not?”
“Because the people who tell me that are always fucking idiots whose only achievement is getting older. There’s no reason to run away just because a few neighborhood mutts are blocking the road.”
“You wouldn’t enjoy being bitten by a vicious dog.”
“No matter how vicious it is, a dog is still a dog. No offense, but I consider myself at least a wolf.”
“A wolf... Then what would you do if the creature blocking your path wasn’t a dog, but a tiger?”
The corners of Lee Jungryong’s mouth curved gently upward.
He was the tiger.
A tiger blocking my path. A predator with teeth and claws capable of killing a wolf.
“I’d run. A wolf can’t beat a tiger.”
“Exactly.”
“But add a few details to the setup, and the wolf might still attack.”
“Details?”
“Yes. For example...”
I continued slowly as I looked at Lee Jungryong.
“What if that tiger was the bastard who badly hurt the wolf’s friend? Something like that.”
He studied me with a peculiar expression.
“It seems the wolf’s friend was badly hurt.”
“Both his legs were cut off. How could he not be? He has a young child, too.”
“That’s an awfully detailed setup.”
“I came up with it while trying to make the setup plausible. It’s only hypothetical, so don’t worry about it.”
“If that’s all it is.”
Lee Jungryong shrugged.
“Still, a wolf taking on a tiger for his friend... He’s certainly loyal.”
“You’d understand if you watched a documentary about wolves. Their loyalty is no joke.”
“But it would be reckless.”
“Why?”
“Because attacking a tiger would get him killed.”
I let out a quiet laugh.
“You never know. Maybe a young, strong wolf could beat an old tiger.”
“...A tiger losing to a wolf? That doesn’t sound like a very well-made documentary.”
“I enjoyed it. The part where every animal in the mountains came running to feast on the tiger’s corpse after the wolf won was especially memorable.”
For the first time, the smile vanished from Lee Jungryong’s face.
Naturally. He had understood the meaning behind my words.
Watching his face stiffen felt like finally dislodging the formula that had been stuck in my throat since infancy.
“You’re irritating. More than I expected.”
After a brief silence, he spoke again.
Lee Jungryong slowly withdrew the hand he had kept extended until now.
“What do you want?”
I answered without hesitation.
“An apology and compensation. And one person’s life.”
“A life?”
“Yes. I want one person’s life.”
Park Jihoon’s neck twitched.
A tremor traveled through the dagger pressed against his throat. He hadn’t made a sound since Lee Jungryong appeared, but now he was trembling with fear of death.
“That’s out of the question. I can’t allow it.”
“I’m not asking for permission. I’m making a demand.”
“Learn to distinguish courage from recklessness. I’m a patient man, but I’m also quite fickle.”
“I’m short on basic decency, so I can’t rest until I’ve paid back at least as much as I received.”
“Your demand is excessive. The compensation should already be more than enough.”
“Who settles for getting back the principal? I want the interest too—compound interest.”
“And if I refuse?”
“Do you remember the documentary I mentioned?”
“Tiger hide or not, do you really think a wolf’s teeth won’t sink into it?”
Lee Jungryong’s gaze sank heavily as he looked at me.
In the strangely tranquil silence, his mouth slowly opened.
“You truly don’t know how frightening a tiger can be.”
WHOOSH!
Before he had even finished speaking, a palm wreathed in red aura shot toward my chest.
Only five steps separated us. I made my decision in an instant.
White Flame. Unequip.
As White Flame was stored in my Inventory, I thrust out my freed right hand.
Disperse, compress, release.
The fire dragon that had been waiting for its chance to awaken transformed into blue flames and settled into my palm.
Flame Divine Palm, with everything I had.
Our palms collided.
BOOOOOOM!
A deafening roar left my ears ringing as the entire building shook like it had been struck by an earthquake.
I took the brunt of the impact.
I danced three steps backward and coughed up a mouthful of blood surging from deep within my lungs.
“Cough!”
Through the pale dust falling from the ceiling, I saw Lee Jungryong standing firmly in place.
His eyes were filled with surprise.
But I was just as shocked.
I had felt him manipulate qi in a way I never could have encountered in the modern world.
He’s different. He’s no ordinary Hunter.
We had exchanged only a single blow, but that was enough.
Lee Jungryong’s strike had resembled the palm technique of a Supreme Peak master. He didn’t merely know how to use his qi properly. He could do far more than that.
So this is an S-rank Hunter.
The power I had felt in that brief instant rivaled the great fiends I had encountered at Shaolin, the Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts.
What kind of monster is this?
I had never expected to experience anything like this in the modern world.
Lee Jungryong stared wide-eyed at me as I swallowed the blood in my mouth, gripping Park Jihoon in one hand and the dagger in the other.
“How could someone as young as you know that method...?”
That method?
He was probably referring to an internal energy cultivation technique in those terms.
I was about to answer, but instead I bared my bloodstained teeth in a grin.
“I’m taking what I demanded.”
At the same time, I plunged the dagger into Park Jihoon’s chest.
Shnk. Shnk-shnk-shnk!
A scream burst from his mouth along with a spray of blood.
“Aaaaargh! Master!”
I’d wondered how this bastard knew about it. Now I saw—they were master and Disciple.
“Stop!”
Even as he shouted, Lee Jungryong couldn’t easily take a step forward.
Every time he tried, I pressed the dagger tight against Park Jihoon’s throat.
“Now, now. If you want to save your adorable Disciple, you’d better stay right there.”
Shnk! Shnk-shnk!
Without hesitation, I drove the dagger down again and again. I hacked indiscriminately at his upper body, avoiding his heart, then tore through the muscles of his thigh.
Slash!
I cut down along his calf and severed the tendons in his ankle. Then I straightened my back, which I had briefly bent, and slashed diagonally upward through his shoulder.
Slash! SPLASH!
“Aaaaaaargh!”
A horrific scream.
Uncle Kkeokjeong must have screamed like that too. He must have passed out from the unbearable pain and woken again, over and over, screaming each time.
And that wasn’t all. The wife who saw her husband return without both arms had her heart butchered as well.
“Save your screams. There’s still one left.”
Slash! Thud!
Park Jihoon’s body, now missing both arms, trembled violently.
“Ghk... guh...”
He had screamed so much that his voice had gone completely hoarse. Only strange noises escaped his throat.
I seized him by the hair. His once-neat, waxed hair was drenched in blood.
“P-please... spare me...”
My blood was boiling hotter than ever, but the voice that slipped through my lips was colder than ice.
“Jihoon.”
“Please. I’m sorry...”
“I had to move away so suddenly back then that I never got to say this.”
I stared into his bloodshot eyes and delivered a congratulatory message ten years past its expiration date.
“Congratulations on graduating, you fucking bastard.”
I hurled him aside.
Thud.
Lee Jungryong picked up the sprawled man in his arms. His eyes burned fiercely.
“You bastard!”
“I left him alive. Whether he’ll ever be a Hunter again, I can’t promise.”
“Do you truly want to die?”
“How about we keep going? Bring down this entire building and let half of Korea find out what happened here. That doesn’t sound so bad to me.”
Lee Jungryong’s face twisted hideously.

“That’s out of the question.
I can’t allow it.”
“I’m not asking for permission.
I’m making a demand.”
“Learn to distinguish courage from recklessness.
I’m a patient man, but I’m also quite fickle.”
“I’m short on basic decency, so I can’t rest until I’ve paid back at least as much as I received.”
“Your demand is excessive.
The compensation should already be more than enough.”
“Who settles for getting back the principal?
I want the interest too—compound interest.”
“And if I refuse?”
“Do you remember the documentary I mentioned?”
“Tiger hide or not, do you really think a wolf’s teeth won’t sink into it?”
Lee Jungryong’s gaze sank heavily as he looked at me.
In the strangely tranquil silence, his mouth slowly opened.
“You truly don’t know how frightening a tiger can be.”
WHOOSH!
Before he had even finished speaking, a palm wreathed in red aura shot toward my chest.
Only five steps separated us.
I made my decision in an instant.
White Flame.
Unequip.
As White Flame was stored in my Inventory, I thrust out my freed right hand.
Disperse, compress, release.
The fire dragon that had been waiting for its chance to awaken transformed into blue flames and settled into my palm.
Flame Divine Palm, with everything I had.
Our palms collided.
BOOOOOOM!
A deafening roar left my ears ringing as the entire building shook like it had been struck by an earthquake.
I took the brunt of the impact.
I danced three steps backward and coughed up a mouthful of blood surging from deep within my lungs.
“Cough!”
Through the pale dust falling from the ceiling, I saw Lee Jungryong standing firmly in place.
His eyes were filled with surprise.
But I was just as shocked.
I had felt him manipulate qi in a way I never could have encountered in the modern world.
He’s different.
He’s no ordinary Hunter.
We had exchanged only a single blow, but that was enough.
Lee Jungryong’s strike had resembled the palm technique of a Supreme Peak master.
He didn’t merely know how to use his qi properly.
He could do far more than that.
So this is an S-rank Hunter.
The power I had felt in that brief instant rivaled the great fiends I had encountered at Shaolin, the Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts.
What kind of monster is this?
I had never expected to experience anything like this in the modern world.
Lee Jungryong stared wide-eyed at me as I swallowed the blood in my mouth, gripping Park Jihoon in one hand and the dagger in the other.
“How could someone as young as you know that method...?”
That method?
He was probably referring to an internal energy cultivation technique in those terms.
I was about to answer, but instead I bared my bloodstained teeth in a grin.
“I’m taking what I demanded.”
At the same time, I plunged the dagger into Park Jihoon’s chest.
Shnk.
Shnk-shnk-shnk!
A scream burst from his mouth along with a spray of blood.
“Aaaaargh!
Master!”
I’d wondered how this bastard knew about it.
Now I saw—they were master and Disciple.
“Stop!”
Even as he shouted, Lee Jungryong couldn’t easily take a step forward.
Every time he tried, I pressed the dagger tight against Park Jihoon’s throat.
“Now, now.
If you want to save your adorable Disciple, you’d better stay right there.”
Shnk!
Shnk-shnk!
Without hesitation, I drove the dagger down again and again.
I hacked indiscriminately at his upper body, avoiding his heart, then tore through the muscles of his thigh.
Slash!
I cut down along his calf and severed the tendons in his ankle.
Then I straightened my back, which I had briefly bent, and slashed diagonally upward through his shoulder.
Slash!
SPLASH!
“Aaaaaaargh!”
A horrific scream.
Uncle Kkeokjeong must have screamed like that too.
He must have passed out from the unbearable pain and woken again, over and over, screaming each time.
And that wasn’t all.
The wife who saw her husband return without both arms had her heart butchered as well.
“Save your screams.
There’s still one left.”
Slash!
Thud!
Park Jihoon’s body, now missing both arms, trembled violently.
“Ghk... guh...”
He had screamed so much that his voice had gone completely hoarse.
Only strange noises escaped his throat.
I seized him by the hair.
His once-neat, waxed hair was drenched in blood.
“P-please... spare me...”
My blood was boiling hotter than ever, but the voice that slipped through my lips was colder than ice.
“Jihoon.”
“Please.
I’m sorry...”
“I had to move away so suddenly back then that I never got to say this.”
I stared into his bloodshot eyes and delivered a congratulatory message ten years past its expiration date.
“Congratulations on graduating, you fucking bastard.”
I hurled him aside.
Thud.
Lee Jungryong picked up the sprawled man in his arms.
His eyes burned fiercely.
“You bastard!”
“I left him alive.
Whether he’ll ever be a Hunter again, I can’t promise.”
“Do you truly want to die?”
“How about we keep going?
Bring down this entire building and let half of Korea find out what happened here.
That doesn’t sound so bad to me.”
Lee Jungryong’s face twisted hideously.

chapters.title: Chapter 285
paragraphs: How dare you do this to my Disciple!
I only paid him back in kind. That settles the principal, so consult your Guild’s leadership about the remaining compound interest.
...You bastard.
I’ll take that as your agreement.
I will never forget what happened today.
That was the conversation we’d had only a few minutes ago.
Lee Jungryong had left after delivering that final line, every word dripping with killing intent.

He had administered emergency treatment with a potion, but Park Jihoon’s wounds were too severe for potions alone to heal. With his Disciple in that condition, he must have been in a hurry to get him treated.
“Phew.”
Once Lee Jungryong’s presence, which I could still sense in the distance, disappeared completely, a sigh of relief escaped me.
“Man, that was exhausting.”
The moment I released the tension I’d held on to until the very end, all the strength drained from my body.
I was tired. My clash with Lee Jungryong had left me with a slight Internal Injury, but the mental exhaustion was even worse.
I really caused one hell of a mess today.
Today, I had made an S-rank Hunter recognized throughout the world and a colossal Guild my enemies.
It had been a precarious tightrope walk with a sheer, bottomless cliff as the stage.
Lee Jungryong and I had met in the middle of that tightrope, and in the end, he had been the one to back down.
He had no choice. I hit him exactly where it mattered.
People with a lot to lose were bound to fear danger.

If the tiger known as Lee Jungryong—or the tiger known as Ares Guild—were to fall, the mountain lord’s honor would hit the ground, and its carcass would become an excellent meal for the animals of the forest—in other words, its competitors.
Of course, the cleanest solution would’ve been Silencing the Witnesses, but...
Lee Jungryong knew I wasn’t an easy opponent.
A single clash had confirmed that he held the upper hand, but it had also been enough for him to realize that the wolf before him posed a genuine threat.
I wiped the blood from the corner of my mouth and thought.
Three steps.
Today, I had taken three steps back against Lee Jungryong.
But today’s three steps would soon become two, and before long, two would become one.
And after that...
I’ll surpass you.
I had never seen any documentary where a wolf defeated a tiger one-on-one, despite what I’d told Lee Jungryong.
But I had the potential to grow without end. Just like my epithet, the Hidden Dragon.
By then, my Guild and I will both be stronger than you ever imagined.
Revenge for Im Kkeokjeong wasn’t the only thing I had gained from this incident. I had also secured a golden opportunity for the Peace Guild to grow.

If we had been frightened into backing down when the Black Hunter first attacked, the Peace Guild would have remained just another mid-sized Guild. But because we had fought back, we had won both revenge and compensation. What came next would depend on Team Leader Choi.
He’ll handle it well.
A conversation I’d had with Team Leader Choi several hours earlier suddenly came to mind.
“What are you planning to do?”
“Hard to say. If my hunch is right, I might see red, and even I don’t know what I’ll do.”
“Are you thinking of storming Myeongdong Guild?”
“I can’t promise I’m not.”
Song Song had called me crazy after hearing that, while Butler Kim had only stared at me in silence.
But Team Leader Choi had reacted differently.
What he said went far beyond anything I’d expected.
“Then go.”
“Excuse me?”

“To Myeongdong Guild. Go smash the place up and turn it upside down. Ah, I’m not telling you to collapse a building in the middle of Seoul and kill people. If you go too far, we might end up using a prison as our Guild house.”
“...I thought you’d try to stop me.”
“I would have, if you weren’t Jin Taekyung. I would’ve racked my brain for some other solution.”
“Then why?”
“You may look reckless at first glance, Mr. Jin, but you always act with the worst possible outcome in mind. And you always bring back the best possible result.”
“Are you really sure about this?”
“I intend to make the Peace Guild the greatest Guild in the world. If we back down when one of our Guild members has been attacked, we can never become the best in the world.”
“Then you really want me to...”
“Do it. Whatever happens, I’ll take responsibility.”
Team Leader Choi’s final words still seemed to echo vividly in my ears.
“I trust you, Mr. Jin. Perhaps even more than I trust myself.”
I had repaid the boundless trust he’d placed in me.
I had given Park Jihoon more than Im Kkeokjeong had suffered, and I had tacitly secured apologies and compensation from enemies no one could dare approach.
The greatest Guild in the world, huh?
Remembering Team Leader Choi’s bold ambition, I let out a quiet laugh.
I took out my phone and made a call.
Someone answered almost before it had begun ringing.
“Yes. This is Choi Minwoo.”
Team Leader Choi. The man himself.
“I have a lot to tell you. Where should I go?”
“Mr. Jin! You’re alive!”
“I thought you were dead. Is this really Jin Taekyung?”
You said you trusted me more than yourself, you son of a bitch...
“Jihoon! Wake up!”
A master’s anguished cry for his young Disciple rang out alongside hurried footsteps.
Park Tae Seop, the Guild Master of Myeongdong Guild, followed close behind Lee Jungryong and stared at his back in surprise.
Did Lee Jungryong have this side to him?
Park Tae Seop had watched Lee Jungryong for many years.
During the Great Cataclysm, he had merely thought of him as someone who was strangely difficult to approach.
But after the war ended and Ares Guild was established, Lee Jungryong seized real power within it. Only then did Park Tae Seop come to understand his true nature.
Hard as steel. Sly as a viper. A man who committed acts that would make others shudder without the slightest hesitation.
That was Lee Jungryong in Park Tae Seop’s eyes—a man he never wanted to face as either an enemy or an ally.
So he’s human after all.
But the strange impression Park Tae Seop had felt vanished without a trace the moment they emerged from the long corridor and entered the hall.
“Welcome.”
The speaker was a middle-aged man. His movements were as crisp and disciplined as a soldier’s, and even his black suit couldn’t conceal his supremely trained physique.
The same was true of the twenty men and women standing behind him like iron towers. Each wore the emblem of Ares Guild over their chest.
I didn’t sense any of them.
That wasn’t the only shock awaiting Park Tae Seop.
He looked past the middle-aged man and spotted roughly a hundred Myeongdong Guild members sprawled across the floor. His eyes widened.
“What is the meaning of this...?”
The middle-aged man answered in a dry voice.
“We merely put them to sleep with sleep magic. For now.”
For now.
The words carried a clear implication. At the moment, they were merely asleep under the influence of magic.
But they could just as easily be put to sleep forever.
Park Tae Seop was about to shout in fury when—
“Is there a problem?”
Lee Jungryong slowly turned around.
The instant Park Tae Seop saw his face, he realized how gravely mistaken he had been.
It was all an act.
Lee Jungryong’s face was devoid of emotion, his eyes deep and cold. There was no trace of his hurried footsteps or the anguished cries of a master fearing for his Disciple’s life.
An icy chill crept up Park Tae Seop’s spine.
“Guild Master Park.”
There was a blade hidden in Lee Jungryong’s gentle voice. It was as though venom dripped from the viper’s tongue every time it moved.
“Was it about twenty years ago? One day, you came to me and dropped to your knees without warning.”
“Do you still remember?”
“...Of course.”
Park Tae Seop clenched his teeth.
How could he possibly forget? Nearly twenty years had passed, but the desperation he’d felt then remained etched into his bones.
A string of massive business failures, debts totaling an enormous sum, and the looks people gave him as though they were staring at a failure...
To Park Tae Seop, it had been a living hell worse than the Great Cataclysm.
After being turned away by countless acquaintances, he had finally sought out Lee Jungryong.
Lee Jungryong had gazed down at the kneeling Park Tae Seop and asked him a single question.
If I help you, what can you do for me?
Park Tae Seop had answered without hesitation.
Anything.
I like that answer.
What would have happened if he hadn’t said those words?
He had asked himself that question hundreds, even thousands of times over the past twenty years, but it was meaningless. He had already come too far to turn back.
No favor came without a price, and he had been forced to commit every manner of crime for Lee Jungryong.
By the time he came to his senses, he was already being dragged along by a leash around his neck.
“Whenever I look at you these days, Guild Master Park, I can’t help thinking about that day. Everything you said when you came to me back then is beginning to sound hollow.”
“How could that be?”

“No, that’s simply human nature. No matter how much someone owes you, they soon forget their gratitude and begin piling up complaints. Save a man from freezing to death, and he changes his tune the moment he warms himself by the fire. What can you do? Ha ha.”
Despite the upward curl of his lips, Lee Jungryong’s eyes were as cold as ice.
When Park Tae Seop lowered his head, his expression rigid, Lee Jungryong continued in a gentler voice.
“I only brought it up because I hope we’ll continue working well together. Your Guild members will be perfectly safe, so don’t worry. Isn’t that right, Team Leader Seok?”
The middle-aged man responsible for Lee Jungryong’s security, Team Leader Seok, answered in a flat voice.
“Of course.”
“Well, I should be on my way. I’ll see you again.”
Pat, pat.
Park Tae Seop stood frozen as Lee Jungryong patted him on the shoulder and walked away.
Inside the descending elevator, Team Leader Seok spoke.
“Shall I take care of him?”
“Who? Ah, Park Tae Seop.”
“Yes. His expression looked rather uneasy.”
“That man’s every thought shows on his face. He was obedient enough for the first few years, but once he got warm and well-fed, he began entertaining other ideas.”
“He knows too much. He also handled this incident so poorly that the fallout reached you, Vice Guild Master.”
For the first time, emotion entered Team Leader Seok’s voice.
Anger.
Seeing the man’s unwavering loyalty, Lee Jungryong smiled faintly.
“Leave him alone for now. We’ve only just started tasting the dish. Of course it’s still bland.”
“Excuse me?”
At that moment, the elevator doors opened with a ding.
Lee Jungryong continued as he walked.
“I’m saying I only gave them a little prod. I wanted to see how they would react.”
“Then...?”
“You occasionally underestimate me. If I had truly set my mind to it, would I have entrusted the job to half-baked fools like them?”
Team Leader Seok let out a low exclamation.
“You anticipated all of this.”
“I’ve barely taken a single spoonful to taste it. If it doesn’t suit my palate, I can always add some salt and pepper.”
“As expected of you, Vice Guild Master.”
Lee Jungryong smiled gently at the admiration in Team Leader Seok’s eyes.
But his true thoughts were different. There was something he couldn’t reveal even to Team Leader Seok, his right-hand man.
Jin Taekyung is no ordinary bastard.
From the beginning, it had been the Peace Guild that bothered Lee Jungryong, not Jin Taekyung.

Even if he had personally intervened, he couldn’t guarantee that something like this wouldn’t have happened. After all, he wasn’t the sort of man who used a cleaver meant for cattle to kill a chicken.
It was certainly efficient, but if an unforeseen variable appeared, the entire plan could go awry.
Who would’ve thought there was a wolf hiding among the chickens?
Lee Jungryong rubbed his tingling wrist.
For a moment, he had felt tremendous heat and power radiating from the young man. It was far too strong to dismiss as some fresh-faced brat’s cute little display.
He knew how to control mana properly. Where could a man who was only an F-rank Hunter until recently have learned...?
He did have a fairly good idea.
After finishing that thought, Lee Jungryong addressed Team Leader Seok.
“Keep a close eye on Jin Taekyung.”
“Don’t worry. If he becomes a nuisance, I’ll deal with him personally.”

Team Leader Seok had always been reliable. He was a born fighting prodigy and the finest of all the youths Lee Jungryong had personally selected and trained. His skill was beyond question. Even a high-level ranker like Park Tae Seop was no match for him.
But a question suddenly occurred to Lee Jungryong.
Was Team Leader Seok really superior to Jin Taekyung?
“Team Leader Seok. No, Go Jun.”
His form of address had shifted from the man’s position to his name.
Team Leader Seok understood the meaning immediately. If he had lacked even that much perception, he could never have become Lee Jungryong’s prized Disciple.
“Yes, Master.”
“Hmm. It’s nothing. I entertained an absurd thought for a moment.”
Lee Jungryong clicked his tongue softly and walked out through the main entrance.
Five men and women were waiting outside the building, dressed in robes covered with elaborate patterns and carrying staffs.
“We greet the Vice Guild Master.”
“Those outfits are certainly gaudy. Can’t you dress a little more ordinarily?”
“They’ll look ordinary to everyone else.”
They were A-rank mages under Lee Jungryong’s direct command.
Just as the oldest-looking mage had said, not one of the hundreds of people hurrying along the sidewalk paid them any attention.
None of those people even knew that an incredible battle had taken place directly above them—one that had nearly brought down a high-rise building.
“This is why magic is so convenient.”

The mages had used brute force to blanket everything within a radius of roughly two hundred meters with illusion magic. Only the handpicked A-rank mages of Ares Guild could pull off something on that scale.
They would remain there and maintain the illusion until the entire aftermath had been dealt with.
“Good. Use that convenient magic of yours to make sure no rumors get out. If anyone looks dangerous, use mental magic to tamper with their memories.”
“Yes, sir. Understood. But that man is badly injured.”
“Ah, him?”
Lee Jungryong glanced at Park Jihoon, who was being carried on the back of a Hunter from his security team, and casually tossed out an order.
“Treat him just enough, then dump him somewhere.”
If he died, so be it. Even if he recovered, he would not be able to properly use even half of the skill he currently possessed.
Lee Jungryong had no interest in collecting spent batteries. He already had countless others. All he had to do was replace this one.
Still, he was useful at the end.
Through Park Jihoon, Lee Jungryong had confirmed the extent of Jin Taekyung’s ruthlessness.
Once blood had been drawn, he should have killed him. If Lee Jungryong himself had been in that position, he would have done so without fail.
You couldn’t take that one step.
What did it matter if he cut off both arms and carved the man’s body to pieces? As long as his enemy still drew breath, it wasn’t complete revenge.
It was nothing more than venting his anger.
That half-measure will come back to poison you someday.
Lee Jungryong let out a derisive chuckle and climbed into the waiting car.

Isn’t that right, Team Leader Seok?”
The middle-aged man responsible for Lee Jungryong’s security, Team Leader Seok, answered in a flat voice.
“Of course.”
“Well, I should be on my way.
I’ll see you again.”
Pat, pat.
Park Tae Seop stood frozen as Lee Jungryong patted him on the shoulder and walked away.
Inside the descending elevator, Team Leader Seok spoke.
“Shall I take care of him?”
“Who?
Ah, Park Tae Seop.”
“Yes.
His expression looked rather uneasy.”
“That man’s every thought shows on his face.
He was obedient enough for the first few years, but once he got warm and well-fed, he began entertaining other ideas.”
“He knows too much.
He also handled this incident so poorly that the fallout reached you, Vice Guild Master.”
For the first time, emotion entered Team Leader Seok’s voice.
Anger.
Seeing the man’s unwavering loyalty, Lee Jungryong smiled faintly.
“Leave him alone for now.
We’ve only just started tasting the dish.
Of course it’s still bland.”
“Excuse me?”
At that moment, the elevator doors opened with a ding.
Lee Jungryong continued as he walked.
“I’m saying I only gave them a little prod.
I wanted to see how they would react.”
“Then...?”
“You occasionally underestimate me.
If I had truly set my mind to it, would I have entrusted the job to half-baked fools like them?”
Team Leader Seok let out a low exclamation.
“You anticipated all of this.”
“I’ve barely taken a single spoonful to taste it.
If it doesn’t suit my palate, I can always add some salt and pepper.”
“As expected of you, Vice Guild Master.”
Lee Jungryong smiled gently at the admiration in Team Leader Seok’s eyes.
But his true thoughts were different.
There was something he couldn’t reveal even to Team Leader Seok, his right-hand man.
Jin Taekyung is no ordinary bastard.
From the beginning, it had been the Peace Guild that bothered Lee Jungryong, not Jin Taekyung.
Even if he had personally intervened, he couldn’t guarantee that something like this wouldn’t have happened.
After all, he wasn’t the sort of man who used a cleaver meant for cattle to kill a chicken.
It was certainly efficient, but if an unforeseen variable appeared, the entire plan could go awry.
Who would’ve thought there was a wolf hiding among the chickens?
Lee Jungryong rubbed his tingling wrist.
For a moment, he had felt tremendous heat and power radiating from the young man.
It was far too strong to dismiss as some fresh-faced brat’s cute little display.
He knew how to control mana properly.
Where could a man who was only an F-rank Hunter until recently have learned...?
He did have a fairly good idea.
After finishing that thought, Lee Jungryong addressed Team Leader Seok.
“Keep a close eye on Jin Taekyung.”
“Don’t worry.
If he becomes a nuisance, I’ll deal with him personally.”
Team Leader Seok had always been reliable.
He was a born fighting prodigy and the finest of all the youths Lee Jungryong had personally selected and trained.
His skill was beyond question.
Even a high-level ranker like Park Tae Seop was no match for him.
But a question suddenly occurred to Lee Jungryong.
Was Team Leader Seok really superior to Jin Taekyung?
“Team Leader Seok.
No, Go Jun.”
His form of address had shifted from the man’s position to his name.
Team Leader Seok understood the meaning immediately.
If he had lacked even that much perception, he could never have become Lee Jungryong’s prized Disciple.
“Yes, Master.”
“Hmm.
It’s nothing.
I entertained an absurd thought for a moment.”
Lee Jungryong clicked his tongue softly and walked out through the main entrance.
Five men and women were waiting outside the building, dressed in robes covered with elaborate patterns and carrying staffs.
“We greet the Vice Guild Master.”
“Those outfits are certainly gaudy.
Can’t you dress a little more ordinarily?”
“They’ll look ordinary to everyone else.”
They were A-rank mages under Lee Jungryong’s direct command.
Just as the oldest-looking mage had said, not one of the hundreds of people hurrying along the sidewalk paid them any attention.
None of those people even knew that an incredible battle had taken place directly above them—one that had nearly brought down a high-rise building.
“This is why magic is so convenient.”
The mages had used brute force to blanket everything within a radius of roughly two hundred meters with illusion magic.
Only the handpicked A-rank mages of Ares Guild could pull off something on that scale.
They would remain there and maintain the illusion until the entire aftermath had been dealt with.
“Good.
Use that convenient magic of yours to make sure no rumors get out.
If anyone looks dangerous, use mental magic to tamper with their memories.”
“Yes, sir.
Understood.
But that man is badly injured.”
“Ah, him?”
Lee Jungryong glanced at Park Jihoon, who was being carried on the back of a Hunter from his security team, and casually tossed out an order.
“Treat him just enough, then dump him somewhere.”
If he died, so be it.
Even if he recovered, he would not be able to properly use even half of the skill he currently possessed.
Lee Jungryong had no interest in collecting spent batteries.
He already had countless others.
All he had to do was replace this one.
Still, he was useful at the end.
Through Park Jihoon, Lee Jungryong had confirmed the extent of Jin Taekyung’s ruthlessness.
Once blood had been drawn, he should have killed him.
If Lee Jungryong himself had been in that position, he would have done so without fail.
You couldn’t take that one step.
What did it matter if he cut off both arms and carved the man’s body to pieces?
As long as his enemy still drew breath, it wasn’t complete revenge.
It was nothing more than venting his anger.
That half-measure will come back to poison you someday.
Lee Jungryong let out a derisive chuckle and climbed into the waiting car.

paragraphs: In the early hours of that morning, a short post appeared on a popular forum frequented by Hunters.

Guys, I had a weird dream. Can someone interpret it for me? I can’t reveal the specifics, but I’m a member of the Security Team of a major Guild with some clout. Anyway, that part isn’t important. I was working as usual when I nodded off for a moment. Then Lord Fuck appeared in my dream. My senior said some weird guy kept hanging around, so we went to catch him together. (My senior’s a traitorous bastard. I think his real name is Yamamoto, but he’s hiding it.) Anyway, the weird guy turned out to be Lord Fuck. But that’s all I remember clearly. After that, my senior did yutori, and I did irasshaimase.

└ Best comment: Before we interpret the dream, can someone translate this post? I have no idea what the hell this guy is talking about. └ Same. └ Forget everything else. What are “yutori” and “irasshaimase”? There’s no way to figure out the context. └ Why is his senior a traitor? Did he buy Heattech from Uniqlo? └ OP: Because he keeps using Japanese in this climate. He’s always saying stuff like yutori and gensei. └ But you said you did irasshaimase. └ OP: Yeah. └ What a lunatic. “Yeah,” my ass. LOL. └ I can smell the problem child from here. Poor senior. └ OP: But when I told my senior about the dream, he said he’d had a similar one. Lord Fuck beat up a hundred of our Guild members and went toe-to-toe with Ares Guild’s Vice Guild Master. └ I want to beat the OP’s ass. └ OP: I’m serious Then he started yelling at me because his phone was gone;; He was probably pissed because it was the latest-model AdultPhone. └ Hello. I’m a practicing shaman. I sense an unusual energy from your post. Could you tell me more about it? └ OP: Whoa, are you really a shaman? └ No. I’m lying. └ OP: Whoa. Are you a crazy bastard?
The post was deleted less than ten minutes later.
The people who had seen it didn’t give much thought to one attention-seeking lunatic disappearing, and no one suspected that Ares Guild had intervened in the whole affair.
Well, no one except me.
They must have tampered with everyone’s memories using mental magic.
It was obviously illegal, but expecting people who raised Black Hunters to care about the law would have been even more ridiculous.
Judging by the comment about the AdultPhone disappearing, it seemed they had thoroughly checked everyone’s phones as well.
That was decisive evidence.
My personal cameraman had bolted outside the moment Park Tae Seop and Park Jihoon appeared, only to fall straight into Ares Guild’s hands.
Not that I was particularly disappointed. They had searched me before letting me leave the building anyway. They even checked my shared cloud folder before returning my phone.
They had also been considerate enough to add a warning.
“Just in case you’re hiding anything, delete it now. If we catch you concealing something, it won’t be pleasant.”
I was already in a foul mood because they had found the porn on my phone, and the guy’s tone was beyond obnoxious.
If the situation had been any different, I would have given him a good one.
I memorized your face, you square-headed bastard.
He had an angular face and a crew cut. He had been put in charge of the cleanup, and everyone else kept calling him “Team Leader,” so he was probably Lee Jungryong’s right-hand man.
Qi Sense had revealed his name as Go Jun. His skill was part of the reason I’d bothered to find out.
That bastard seemed to have learned something resembling martial arts, too.
Once suspicion took root, I could see things more clearly than before.
Every Ares Guild member Lee Jungryong had left behind was exceptional. Any one of them could easily take down two ordinary A-rank Hunters alone.
But the impression Go Jun had given me was... honestly, enough to surprise even me.
His obnoxious manner came from confidence in his own ability.
How did Lee Jungryong train people like this?
Could it really be martial arts? Or perhaps a martial art developed independently within Ares Guild.
One question led to another.
I was mulling all this over when a nurse shouted from the hallway.
“Mr. Lee! Patient Im Hyeokjun is conscious!”
I sprang to my feet.
Im Hyeokjun. Im Kkeokjeong’s real name, though hardly anyone ever used it.
After three long days, he had finally regained consciousness.
“Darling! Jun’s dad!”
“Daddy!”
I forced myself to resist the urge to throw open the door to his hospital room. This was time for his family.
The sobs of a wife and children reunited with their husband and father after three days of unconsciousness drifted through the crack around the door.
Only after a wave of weeping had swept through the room and quite some time had passed did our turn finally come.
“Oh, you’re all here?”
Damn it. My throat closed up at his very first words.
Im Kkeokjeong spread his arms with a bright smile, then scrunched up his nose.
“Ugh.”
“Your arm! Be careful with your arm!”
“I thought it would be fine, but it aches a little when I move it.”
“They reattached a severed arm. Did you think it would be fine right away? What are you, a transforming robot?”
Song Song scolded him while casting a healing spell. Once the pain subsided, Im Kkeokjeong’s expression relaxed considerably.
“Thank you, Miss Song.”
“If you’re grateful, please be careful. Didn’t you hear the healer? You need to rest and avoid overexerting yourself for at least two weeks.”
“And thank you for saying that, too.”
“Uncle!”
“Ow, there go my eardrums.”
I never would have imagined how happy it could make me to see him laughing heartily like a bandit.
After letting out the same boisterous laugh as before, Im Kkeokjeong turned to the others.
“Hyung Kim—no, Guild Master. Thank you so much. The kids’ mother told me how well you looked after me while I was unconscious.”
Butler Kim shook his head slightly.
“There’s no need to thank me. It was only natural. When one of our Guild members suffers something like this, of course we step up.”
“I heard you spent quite a lot of money, too...”
A famous healer had been brought in to treat Im Kkeokjeong, and high-grade potions that casually cost hundreds of millions of won per bottle had been poured into him without restraint.
It might have been the same in the past, but this was a world where even a human life had a price. Who would go this far for a D-rank Hunter with nothing to his name but years of experience?
Butler Kim chuckled softly at the emotion thickening Im Kkeokjeong’s voice.
“If you really must thank someone, thank the man footing the bill. I’m just the figurehead, so leave me out of it.”
At those words, Im Kkeokjeong’s gaze slowly shifted toward the man footing the bill.
“Team Leader Choi.”
His voice burned as though it carried Scorching Yang Qi. Before Im Kkeokjeong could continue, Team Leader Choi cut him off.
“This wasn’t your fault, Mr. Im. It happened because our Guild was looked down on. I failed to prevent it, so if anyone owes an apology, it’s me.”
“Team Leader Choi!”
Im Kkeokjeong was the sort of man who could make a hardened criminal look like a model prisoner simply by standing beside one, and now tears brimmed in his eyes.
When he reached out to embrace him, Team Leader Choi flinched and stepped back.
“B-be careful with your arm.”
“It’s fine. I just want to hug you once.”
“...I’d like to pass that glorious opportunity on to the last person.”
It didn’t seem like much of an honor, but in the end, my turn came.
Silence fell.
There was something I had desperately wanted to say to Im Kkeokjeong once he woke up, but now that I was standing face-to-face with him, my mouth clamped shut like a clam.
Im Kkeokjeong broke the silence first.
“What do you think?”
“About what?”
“My wife and kids. Pretty, right?”
His out-of-nowhere bragging about his family drew a quiet laugh from me.
“Yes. They are.”
“Your sister-in-law is quite the beauty.”
“I’ll give you that. Did you imprison or threaten her?”
“There’s no tree that won’t fall after ten chops. Remember that. I succeeded on the forty-seventh.”
“You just said every tree falls after ten chops.”
Im Kkeokjeong snickered.
“Turns out there are some that won’t. Ten chops didn’t even make a dent.”
“It’s a miracle you weren’t booked as a suspect.”
“You idiot. If I’d given up back then, do you think I could have gotten a beauty like that?”
Im Kkeokjeong’s wife, her face swollen from crying, covered it with one hand and waved the other dismissively.
His two children, both still in elementary school, stared at me with bright, curious eyes as though they had never cried at all.
“Daddy, who is he?”
“Who is he? Who?”
Im Kkeokjeong pulled the clinging children into his arms and answered.
“He’s your uncle. Uncle Taekyung.”
“Uncle Taekyung?”
“Yeah. I’ve told you about him before, right? The handsome, strong uncle.”
So he had told his family about me.
Warmth spread from somewhere deep in my chest. The children’s eyes sparkled even more brightly as they looked at me.
Children were cute and beautiful by nature, but these sisters could have been child actors. So this was the victory of maternal genes.
“Wow! You’re Uncle Taekyung?”
“Nice ta meet you!”
A fond smile spread across my face.
I patted both girls on the head and said to Im Kkeokjeong, “They’re adorable. So innocent.”
“Obviously. Get married and have a daughter yourself. Then you’ll understand why people call men doting dads.”
I’d been nicknamed a doting dad in high school, too. Of course, I hadn’t had a daughter.
In any case, the sight of this close-knit family of four made my heart swell.
Im Kkeokjeong raised his arm stiffly and embraced me. His hand, far weaker than before, patted my back.
Tap. Tap.
“Thank you. I’m always grateful.”
The moment I heard those words, my resolve hardened around a decision I had been carrying all this time.
I can’t make the same mistake again.
I repeated the words to myself and hugged Im Kkeokjeong tightly.
Today, one man had returned to his family and friends.
An hour later, only five members of the Peace Guild remained in the hospital room, including Im Kkeokjeong and me.
Im Kkeokjeong’s wife wanted her husband to rest, but his resolve was firm.
“I almost left my beloved wife and kids behind. I need to hear it now. Everything that happened, without leaving out a single detail.”
The good-natured man who had always been softhearted and full of laughter had gained firm resolve and steel in his spine.
By the time he had heard the entire story, Im Kkeokjeong’s face was rigid.
“It was Ares Guild?”
“Yes.”
“And the Lee Jungryong you mentioned really is that Lee Jungryong?”
“I’m sure.”
A groanlike sigh escaped him.
We had followed the tail called Black Hunter and found Myeongdong Guild. When we stepped on Myeongdong Guild’s torso, the head that emerged was Ares Guild.
The problem was that this was no ordinary head.
“We followed a snake’s tail and found a dragon’s head.”
As I said that, I cast a sidelong glance at Team Leader Choi and Butler Kim. Both of them wore their usual calm expressions.
But I had seen it clearly.
Before Im Kkeokjeong regained consciousness, when they first heard the name Ares Guild, a storm had raged in the eyes of both men.
There’s definitely something going on...
I didn’t know exactly what. Song Song and I had sensed something strange and questioned them relentlessly, but they had clammed up after briefly saying they would tell us once Im Kkeokjeong woke up.
But now it’s time for them to talk.
Perhaps he sensed Song Song’s and my gazes. Team Leader Choi was just about to open his mouth when—
Thud. Thud.
All kinds of sounds mingled together in the hospital hallway. But their footsteps were different. They were unusually heavy, with a deep, resonant echo.
And there was qi.
“They’re coming.”
At my words, everyone rose from their seats one after another.
Sure enough, the footsteps stopped in front of our hospital room.
Knock, knock.
The door opened, revealing a face I had seen only half a day ago.
Go Jun?
Wait. If that bastard was here, then could it be...?
The thought broke off. Go Jun’s face vanished from view as another man strode into the hospital room.
He was nearing seventy, yet his youthful appearance made him look like a man in his forties. He possessed a leader’s charisma and a natural air of intimidation.
Lee Jungryong.
His gaze swept over us before stopping dead on one person. The corner of his mouth lifted slightly.
“You’ve grown a lot.”
Team Leader Choi’s gaze sank deeply as he looked at Lee Jungryong.

As I said that, I cast a sidelong glance at Team Leader Choi and Butler Kim.
Both of them wore their usual calm expressions.
But I had seen it clearly.
Before Im Kkeokjeong regained consciousness, when they first heard the name Ares Guild, a storm had raged in the eyes of both men.
There’s definitely something going on...
I didn’t know exactly what.
Song Song and I had sensed something strange and questioned them relentlessly, but they had clammed up after briefly saying they would tell us once Im Kkeokjeong woke up.
But now it’s time for them to talk.
Perhaps he sensed Song Song’s and my gazes.
Team Leader Choi was just about to open his mouth when—
Thud.
Thud.
All kinds of sounds mingled together in the hospital hallway.
But their footsteps were different.
They were unusually heavy, with a deep, resonant echo.
And there was qi.
“They’re coming.”
At my words, everyone rose from their seats one after another.
Sure enough, the footsteps stopped in front of our hospital room.
Knock, knock.
The door opened, revealing a face I had seen only half a day ago.
Go Jun?
Wait.
If that bastard was here, then could it be...?
The thought broke off.
Go Jun’s face vanished from view as another man strode into the hospital room.
He was nearing seventy, yet his youthful appearance made him look like a man in his forties.
He possessed a leader’s charisma and a natural air of intimidation.
Lee Jungryong.
His gaze swept over us before stopping dead on one person.
The corner of his mouth lifted slightly.
“You’ve grown a lot.”
Team Leader Choi’s gaze sank deeply as he looked at Lee Jungryong.

paragraphs: Me, Im Kkeokjeong, Song Song, and Butler Kim.
Yet the moment Lee Jungryong entered the hospital room, his gaze settled on one person alone.
Team Leader Choi.
“You’ve grown a lot.”
The moment I heard Lee Jungryong’s first words, I felt as though someone had struck me in the back of the head with a sledgehammer.
So this was what Team Leader Choi had been hiding.
Their relationship was clearly more than that of an ordinary superior and subordinate at work.
As far as I know, Team Leader Choi was with Ares Guild for only three or four years.
Even by the most conservative estimate, he must have met Lee Jungryong in his early to mid-twenties. “You’ve grown a lot” wasn’t something you said to a man like that.
It was the sort of thing you heard from your parents’ friends or relatives during the holidays.
“It’s been a long time, Vice Guild Master Lee Jungryong.”
The stiff title and formal tone made Lee Jungryong study Team Leader Choi with interest.
“Vice Guild Master? When you were young, you used to call me Grandpa.”
Grandpa?
That was the second shock. For a moment, I wondered if perhaps... but quickly dismissed the thought.
It was simply what Team Leader Choi had called him as a child. Lee Jungryong couldn’t actually be his grandfather.
Still, they’ve clearly had a close relationship since Team Leader Choi was young.
That alone made Team Leader Choi’s relationship with Lee Jungryong anything but ordinary.
While everyone else stood stunned, only two people remained composed: Butler Kim and Team Leader Choi, who answered calmly.
“That was twenty years ago.”
“Time is frightening. Who would have thought that sweet little boy would turn out like this?”
“The older I got, the more I began to see the things that had once been invisible to me.”
“I received a report that you resigned last year. Come to think of it, I never saw your face even once after you joined the Guild. I must admit, I found that rather disappointing.”
Despite his words, he didn’t look disappointed in the slightest. Neither did Team Leader Choi.
“I felt the same way. If you hadn’t immediately transferred me overseas and barred me from even setting foot in headquarters, we might have seen each other more often.”
“Why? Didn’t you like the overseas branch?”
“I felt it wasn’t where I belonged. That’s all.”
“Not where you belonged...”
“Wasn’t that exactly what you wanted, Vice Guild Master?”
“Me?”
Lee Jungryong let out a quiet laugh.
“So you built yourself a new nest? Even going so far as to borrow someone else’s name?”
“I’m sorry to interrupt.”
Butler Kim, who had remained silent until then, suddenly spoke. His voice was as calm as ever.
“But the Young Master and I are hardly strangers.”
“Oh, who might this be?”
Lee Jungryong widened his eyes in feigned surprise.
The reaction was clearly exaggerated. If he knew Team Leader Choi, there was no way he wouldn’t know Butler Kim, the person closest to him.
“Kim Hwajong? It is Hwajong, isn’t it?”
“It’s been a long time, Senior.”
Butler Kim didn’t refuse Lee Jungryong’s outstretched hand. The two men shook hands, each wearing a faint smile.
Informal speech? And Senior?
Whatever their exact relationship was, they seemed much closer than I’d expected.
“It was a good thing I came in person. The last time we met was... about twenty years ago, wasn’t it?”
“Eighteen years, to be precise. Ship-pal years.”
Was it just my imagination, or had he put extra force into those particular words?
I glanced to the side. Song Song and Im Kkeokjeong looked as though they had seen a ghost.
Ah. So it wasn’t my imagination.
Close, my ass. I must have been blind.
I take it back. Butler Kim didn’t merely dislike Lee Jungryong.
He fucking hated him. Enough to wish he had died.
Butler Kim was a mage, so he wasn’t holding an actual knife, but his tongue was every bit as sharp as a blade.
At his vicious words, Go Jun, who had been standing behind Lee Jungryong like an iron tower, took a step forward.
“Watch your mouth.”
“Watch my mouth?”
“He is not someone you may address so carelessly.”
Butler Kim gave Go Jun an odd look.
“You seem highly skilled at a glance, Hunter. What is your name?”
“I’m Go Jun, head of the Vice Guild Master’s security.”
“I see. Team Leader Seok.”
Butler Kim’s distinctive low voice continued smoothly.
“If you’ve said everything you have to say, shut your mouth and get back behind him. This isn’t a place for the likes of you to interfere.”
Go Jun’s already expressionless face stiffened.
Just as veins began to bulge on his forehead, Lee Jungryong burst into hearty laughter and motioned him back.
“I thought age might have mellowed you, but... your temper hasn’t changed at all. This is the Kim Hwajong I remember.”
“When it comes to a foul temper, you still have me beat by a mile, Senior. Wouldn’t you agree?”
Team Leader Choi cut in coldly.
“Enough of this pointless conversation. Get to the matter at hand.”
How many people in Korea—or the entire world—could speak to Lee Jungryong that way?
Im Kkeokjeong and Song Song gaped at the stormy exchange.
Even I was inwardly astonished by Butler Kim’s behavior, despite having personally witnessed him treat Im Chunsoo, the Guild Master of Sangdong Guild, like a dog several months ago.
What on earth happened between them?
It wasn’t just Team Leader Choi. Even Butler Kim was acting completely unlike his usual self.

“One of you is young and impatient, while the other still hasn’t shed the temper of his youth. Well, I suppose there’s no harm in getting to the point. Though it is a little disappointing, considering I came here as an invited guest.”
“Did you just call this an invitation?”
“You’re mistaken. No one here would invite you, Vice Guild Master.”
“Think carefully. Surely there’s at least one person who did?”
Lee Jungryong had been watching the two of them with amusement. Then he suddenly turned toward me.
“That fellow.”
Silence descended over the room.
With everyone’s eyes on me, I thought for a moment before carefully opening my mouth.
“What kind of bullshit is that?”
The instant I finished speaking, Go Jun let out a low growl. He looked ready to charge like a hunting dog if Lee Jungryong hadn’t shaken his head.
After restraining Go Jun, Lee Jungryong spoke to me.
“Didn’t you say so yourself? That I should come in person and apologize to the victim.”
“Oh.”
I had definitely said that.
To Park Jihoon and Park Tae Seop.
“You look as though you never expected me to come.”
“To be honest, I didn’t. What are you plotting by coming all the way here?”
“You have a tendency to say whatever comes to mind without thinking it through. Since I accepted your invitation, shouldn’t you begin by thanking me?”
Thank him?
I let out a hollow laugh. The rest of his words were so absurd that they weren’t even worth answering.
“Your mouth may be crooked, but at least speak straight. It wasn’t an invitation. It was a demand. A demand for an apology.”
“No. If coming here had not been my own decision, could you—or the Peace Guild, for that matter—have made me move even a single step?”
“That’s...”
“Didn’t you think so yourself? You never truly expected me to come.”
It felt as though someone had dumped a bucket of cold water over me. The words caught in my throat.
Everything he said was true.
Though my heart had cried out for anger and revenge, I had never expected Lee Jungryong to come. Even in the midst of that rage, my mind had coldly compromised with reality.
Lee Jungryong, the man who effectively ruled Ares Guild, was still a giant I couldn’t force to his knees with my current strength.
“A demand is the right of the strong. Words spoken by the weak to the strong can never be demands. They are always requests—or invitations.”
“That’s why I came in response to an invitation. Whatever leverage you think you have over me, that fact will not change. I am Lee Jungryong. I am Ares Guild, and Ares Guild is me.”
His voice was quiet, but it carried weight. Everyone in the Peace Guild, myself included, was left speechless.
At least one thing was clear.
Lee Jungryong hadn’t come here to apologize.
Having driven the overwhelming difference in our power into our minds, he continued with a satisfied smile.
“And this is no way to treat a guest who came to visit a patient. Especially one who brought a gift for him. Isn’t that right, Team Leader Seok?”
“That is correct, Vice Guild Master.”
Go Jun answered like a robot and knocked on the door. A Hunter from the security team who had been waiting outside entered and placed what he was carrying on the table.
A vase filled with hundreds of flowers.
And an envelope.
“Compensation money. If the amount isn’t enough, tell me. I’ll give you as much as you need.”
My gaze remained fixed on the flowers. They were beautiful and white. I had never been particularly fond of flowers, but I had never disliked them, either.
Yet this was the first time in my life that receiving flowers as a gift had made me feel disgusted.
Lilies as a hospital-visit gift.
My dormant anger began crawling back up from the depths.
I rubbed the stiff, tingling back of my neck and muttered,
“What a fucking old bastard...”
This time, even Go Jun couldn’t restrain himself.
With a roar, he charged. His fist slammed into my lower jaw at blinding speed.
Crack!
Blood sprayed with a chilling sound.
I frowned and slowly turned my tilted head. The taste of sticky, salty blood spread through my mouth.
“Damn it. I bit my tongue.”
Go Jun’s eyes widened. He looked back and forth between his fist and me as though he couldn’t believe what he was seeing.
“How?”
“I’m pretty tough. I drank a lot of milk when I was young.”
“I definitely imbued it with mana...”
If it had been fully materialized Fist Energy, I wouldn’t still be standing here like this.
Of course, if that had been the case, I wouldn’t have deliberately let him hit me, either.
I flashed him a grin.
“You should have used everything you had. Enough to finish me in one blow.”
Whoosh!
“Hup!”
Go Jun sucked in a short breath and reached out to knock my arm aside. He was so fast that an ordinary A-rank Hunter couldn’t even compare.
His hand curved like a hook as it snapped toward my wrist.
This really is a grappling technique.
Remembering the surprise I had felt while fighting Park Jihoon, I smoothly twisted my wrist.
Slip.
His hand clawed through empty air. I wound around his wrist, locked it in place, and put my weight into a stomp that crashed down onto the top of his foot.
Crack!
“Urgh!”
The weight of a thousand geun crushed Go Jun’s instep and drove it deep into the solid concrete. Groaning in pain, he raised his arm to shield his face.
But...
“You think that’ll do?”
One thing was certain.
I hadn’t avoided his blow.
Go Jun hadn’t been able to avoid mine.
Crunch!
My fist struck the exact center of his face, breaking his nose in one blow and caving in the flesh beneath it.
His mouth gaped open, spraying blood and white teeth.
Clatter. Thud.
“Fucking bastard. Who said you could throw the first punch?”
It all happened in an instant. Everyone in the hospital room was shocked, but one person’s reaction stood out in particular.
“You bastard...”
The voice that had remained relaxed throughout trembled faintly. Ripples spread through Lee Jungryong’s eyes.
I quickly spoke first, before things could get worse.
“For the record, that was self-defense.”
But the words I heard next were something I could never have anticipated.
“What is your relationship with my older brother?”
“Excuse me? Who?”
“The person who taught you that.”
“If you mean that...”
My eyes widened.
Was this old man talking about martial arts?
But Lee Jungryong was no longer listening to me. His gaze had turned cold and heavy as he stared at Team Leader Choi.
“Did Soyeong have another man?”
I didn’t know who Soyeong was.
But to someone else, that name was apparently a dragon’s reverse scale—a point that must never be touched.
Team Leader Choi clenched his fists, and blue flames blazed in Butler Kim’s eyes.
“Senior. Do you want to die?”
“Answer me.”
“You bastard! Lee Jungryong!”
“Now.”
That was when Team Leader Choi’s tightly sealed lips finally parted.
“You know better than I do what kind of relationship those two had.”
“Then that bastard...”
“You must have already investigated Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
“Are you saying all of it is true?”
“It is exactly as you know it. There isn’t a single lie.”
Lee Jungryong’s eyes trembled.
After looking back and forth between Team Leader Choi and me, he finally turned away. The door opened as though someone had been waiting for the signal, but he came to an abrupt stop before leaving.
He tossed out a single sentence.
“I’ll send someone soon. Once the negotiations are over, hand over the people you’re holding.”
Click.
The door closed behind the last person to leave—the security team Hunter carrying Go Jun on his back.
It felt as though a storm had just swept through the room.
I turned toward Team Leader Choi, who was silently staring at the tightly closed door.
“Who is Soyeong?”
“She was my mother.”
“...What?”
“The mother who gave birth to me and raised me. She passed away a long time ago.”
My mouth fell open despite myself.
What the hell is wrong with that old man?
Lee Jungryong had asked Team Leader Choi whether his late mother had cheated while she was alive—her own son, no less.
“Crazy. Why would he—ah, never mind. You don’t have to answer.”
“Vice Guild Master Lee must have been quite shaken. Even I didn’t expect him to ask so directly.”
To hell with whether he was shaken.
I frantically waved my hand.
“Team Leader, really, it’s fine. You don’t have to tell me.”
“Sometimes I wonder what it would have been like if my mother had been born as someone other than Cheon Taemin’s daughter.”
“All right, that’s enough...”
My body abruptly froze.
What did he just say?
Although I couldn’t move an inch, my mind repeated those three syllables faster than ever.
Cheon Taemin. Cheon Taemin. Cheon Taemin...
“Did you just say Cheon Taemin?”
“If my pronunciation wasn’t incorrect, then you heard me correctly.”
“Could it be... the Cheon Taemin I know?”
“Yes.”
Team Leader Choi nodded and continued.
“He is my maternal grandfather.”
For a moment, my vision spun and my legs wobbled.
Cheon Taemin. He said Cheon Taemin.
I had once harbored doubts about Team Leader Choi’s identity.
A man in his twenties with seemingly limitless ability, whom an A-rank mage known as a hidden hero of the Great Cataclysm called Young Master.
Now I finally understood how all of that had been possible.
It was because his maternal grandfather was Cheon Taemin.
Humanity’s great hero. The world’s greatest Hunter...
Among all the words used to describe Cheon Taemin, the title “Guild Master of Ares Guild” was only one small piece.
The name of the largest piece was an immortal achievement no one else could ever attain.
The man who killed the Demon King. The Slayer.
That Cheon Taemin’s maternal grandson was standing before me.
