It felt as though a storm had just swept through the room.
I turned toward Team Leader Choi, who was silently staring at the tightly closed door.
“Who is Soyeong?”
“She was my mother.”
“...What?”
“The mother who gave birth to me and raised me.
She passed away a long time ago.”
My mouth fell open despite myself.
What the hell is wrong with that old man?
Lee Jungryong had asked Team Leader Choi whether his late mother had cheated while she was alive—her own son, no less.
“Crazy.
Why would he—ah, never mind.
You don’t have to answer.”
“Vice Guild Master Lee must have been quite shaken.
Even I didn’t expect him to ask so directly.”
To hell with whether he was shaken.
I frantically waved my hand.
“Team Leader, really, it’s fine.
You don’t have to tell me.”
“Sometimes I wonder what it would have been like if my mother had been born as someone other than Cheon Taemin’s daughter.”
“All right, that’s enough...”
My body abruptly froze.
What did he just say?
Although I couldn’t move an inch, my mind repeated those three syllables faster than ever.
Cheon Taemin.
Cheon Taemin.
Cheon Taemin...
“Did you just say Cheon Taemin?”
“If my pronunciation wasn’t incorrect, then you heard me correctly.”
“Could it be... the Cheon Taemin I know?”
“Yes.”
Team Leader Choi nodded and continued.
“He is my maternal grandfather.”
For a moment, my vision spun and my legs wobbled.
Cheon Taemin.
He said Cheon Taemin.
I had once harbored doubts about Team Leader Choi’s identity.
A man in his twenties with seemingly limitless ability, whom an A-rank mage known as a hidden hero of the Great Cataclysm called Young Master.
Now I finally understood how all of that had been possible.
It was because his maternal grandfather was Cheon Taemin.
Humanity’s great hero.
The world’s greatest Hunter...
Among all the words used to describe Cheon Taemin, the title “Guild Master of Ares Guild” was only one small piece.
The name of the largest piece was an immortal achievement no one else could ever attain.
The man who killed the Demon King.
The Slayer.
That Cheon Taemin’s maternal grandson was standing before me.

chapters.title: Chapter 288
paragraphs: In the back seat of the spacious limousine, Lee Jungryong held Go Jun’s arm and sent his mana flowing into it.
Go Jun’s limp body twitched, then strength returned to it.
He opened his eyes with difficulty, letting out a faint groan. Lee Jungryong asked, “Are you conscious?”
“...I’m sorry. I should have kept him occupied longer.”
Go Jun lowered his head, his face rigid.
His earlier attack on Jin Taekyung had not been impulsive.

Go Jun was Lee Jungryong’s Disciple and Head of Security. A man with his exceptional composure and self-control would never have done such a thing unless ordered by the master he respected above all others.
Jin Taekyung. I need to see what that bastard is truly capable of.
What would you have me do?
“I’ll buy as much time as I can. Make him show everything he has.”
I never liked the bastard. It seems I’ll finally get to teach him a proper lesson.
He should not have said that last part.
After speaking so boldly, he had failed to withstand even a single blow. He could not bring himself to face Lee Jungryong.
“You exchanged blows with him yourself, so you must have felt it. Tell me exactly how strong he is. Leave nothing out.”
It did not take Go Jun long to answer.
“He’s strong.”
Jin Taekyung had stormed Myeongdong Guild alone. Go Jun had known from the start that he was not someone to take lightly.
But even after taking a mana-infused punch squarely, Taekyung had not fallen—or even retreated a single step. Go Jun had never imagined anyone could possess such absurd toughness.
“I struck him cleanly on the jaw, but he was harder than rebar. I’ve never seen anyone like him.”
Taekyung had not been wearing armor or protected by defensive magic. Go Jun could not understand how he had emerged so completely unscathed.
The bigger problem was that Jin Taekyung did not merely possess exceptional toughness.
“His strength and speed both surpassed mine.”
“What if you had gone all-out from the beginning, Team Leader Seok?”
After a brief hesitation, Go Jun answered stiffly.
“...It would still have been difficult.”
He remembered Taekyung’s lightning-fast hands.

Before he knew what was happening, his arm had been trapped and his foot driven deep into the ground. He had hastily raised his arm to shield his face, but the fist behind it had struck with such monstrous force that it smashed straight through his guard and into his face.
“I don’t know how, but Jin Taekyung has extensive combat experience. He’s on an entirely different level from ordinary Hunters who only fight monsters.”
“And?”
“Pardon?”
“There’s something you haven’t said yet, isn’t there?”
“I believe I told you to leave nothing out.”
The moment Go Jun met Lee Jungryong’s gaze, he understood.
Lee Jungryong had reached the same conclusion.
“You already suspected it.”
“Yes. Today, that suspicion became certainty.”
“You mean...”
Lee Jungryong’s voice sank low.
“There’s no doubt about it. Jin Taekyung has learned a mana cultivation method.”
A mana cultivation method.
A faint ripple disturbed Go Jun’s unwavering gaze. That was how shocking Lee Jungryong’s words were.
“An insignificant F-rank Hunter became this strong in barely half a year. People keep babbling about reawakening and faulty measuring devices, but that’s nothing more than ignorant nonsense.”
Go Jun muttered as if groaning.
“But how...? Aren’t mana cultivation methods among the most closely guarded secrets?”
“Top secret? That phrase is meaningless. As long as someone knows a secret, it can never be absolute.”
“Could Team Leader Choi be responsible?”
Lee Jungryong shook his head.
“That boy Minwoo never learned a mana cultivation method. Neither did Kim Hwajong, who has remained by his side since childhood.”
“Isn’t it something no one knows about? If the Guild Master...”
“Who?”
Go Jun’s words died in his throat. He froze.
The moment he met Lee Jungryong’s dark, sunken gaze, he realized he had said something he should not have.
“I believe I told you never to utter a word about my older brother.”
“I-I’m sorry. It was a slip of the tongue...”
Go Jun’s voice quivered like a wounded bird.

The revelation that Taekyung had learned a mana cultivation method had rattled him enough to break an unspoken taboo. Cheon Taemin, the Guild Master of Ares Guild, was someone who must never be mentioned.
Thud!
Both of Go Jun’s knees struck the floor. He bowed his head deeply.
“Please forgive me, Vice Guild Master.”
“Forgive you? These things happen.”
“Get up.”
Even after carefully lifting his knees from the floor and sitting back down, Go Jun could not look Lee Jungryong straight in the eye.
He had spent years at Lee Jungryong’s side and had seen and learned many things.
To Go Jun, Lee Jungryong inspired both respect and fear.
Faint fear now colored the face that was ordinarily as expressionless as a machine.
“Team Leader Seok.”
Lee Jungryong broke the suffocating silence.
Go Jun lowered his head even further.
“Yes, Vice Guild Master. Please speak.”
“You’re going to be very busy from now on. If you run your mouth as carelessly as you did today, you’ll put me in a very difficult position.”
“I’ll remember that. I’ll never forget it.”
“Strengthen our surveillance of the Peace Guild. Find out whether they have anyone useful, too.”
Go Jun cautiously raised his head.
“Are you planning to expand the security team?”
“Yes. We can’t go on like this. We must prepare for any eventuality.”
“Yes. I’ll put it into action as soon as we return to the Guild.”
“And... keep a close watch on the executives’ movements. Include the status of our overseas branches.”
“I’ll carry it out without a single omission.”
Lee Jungryong’s position within Ares Guild was already secure.
But not everyone followed him as blindly as Go Jun did.
There were always those who harbored discontent, and they watched Lee Jungryong’s every move with suspicion.
The security team, on the other hand, was little more than Lee Jungryong’s private army.
Paid enormous salaries and taught mana cultivation methods, its members offered their absolute loyalty to one man alone: Lee Jungryong.
Yes. Things have been too peaceful for too long.
Lee Jungryong turned toward the window. Beyond the spotless glass, the Han River stretched wide into the distance.
Only thirty-some years ago, its waters had been filled with the corpses of humans and monsters. Now they were clear and clean, as though nothing had ever happened.
Older brother. The world has changed so much.
Lee Jungryong did not speak the thought aloud.
His gaze was already retracing the distant past. Burning cities and dying people. Monster legions charging forward, overturning heaven and earth...
And amid that hellscape, one man had shone alone.
Do not take so much as a single step out from behind me.
Lee Jungryong had been thirty then, filled with cynicism toward the world. The moment he met that man, he was captivated.
Though they did not share a single drop of blood, Lee Jungryong regarded him as an older brother and always looked up to him with both respect and fear.
Even now, past the age of sixty, those memories and emotions remained vivid.
Lee Jungryong was staring silently out the window, lost in thought, when Go Jun’s voice brought him back.
“We’ve arrived.”
At the same moment, the limousine door slid open. Before them stood a skyscraper tall enough to pierce the clouds, surrounded by a forest of buildings like guards protecting a king.
Dozens of waiting Hunters bowed to him. The lapels of their suits bore the emblem of Ares Guild.
“Welcome, Vice Guild Master Lee Jungryong!”
Their shout was perfectly synchronized, as though measured with a ruler.
A faint smile on his lips, the man in power stepped onto the red carpet.
This was a world where even white-haired old men wore wireless earbuds and watched iTube.
Whenever snow fell and icy roads formed, nursing homes shut down, while Old Man Kim and Granny Park chatted through a voice-chat app and played online Go-Stop.
If magic was a mysterious realm of unknowable origins, the internet was the culmination of twenty-first-century civilization.
With a few clicks and keystrokes, anyone could learn what was happening anywhere in the world as easily as reading the palm of their hand.
In a world like this, information about the most famous person among billions was even easier to find.
Tap. Tap-tap.
Cheon Taemin.
His name completed itself after I typed only the initial consonants. It even ranked higher in searches than heaven.
People were more interested in the man who had stopped them from nearly going to heaven than in heaven itself.
I was no different.
Muttering inwardly, I tapped the search result that read “Cheon Taemin—Profile.”
The face I had seen hundreds—no, thousands—of times since elementary school filled my phone screen.
Thick eyebrows and chiseled features. He looked like a handsome Greek god reincarnated.
And...
“He looks like him.”
“Now that I see them side by side, they really do look alike.”
“Whoa. They’re identical.”
They looked alike. So much so that I understood why people said blood would always tell.
Im Kkeokjeong, Song Song, and I stared openmouthed, looking back and forth between the phone and Team Leader Choi.
“Ahem.”
Only when Team Leader Choi finally cleared his throat uncomfortably did we come to our senses.
No, not yet. Come to my senses, my ass.
What the hell is going on?
Things were getting spectacularly insane now, whether in Murim or the modern world.
When Park Jihoon stabbed me in the back and Lee Jungryong appeared out of nowhere, I’d been certain nothing could surprise me anymore...
But this was shock and horror in its purest form.
Not the President’s grandson, but Cheon Taemin’s.
A president’s term lasted five years. Cheon Taemin had no term.
The achievements and Fame attached to his name would remain immortal, passed down through the generations.
He had driven a sword into the Demon King’s heart and saved all humanity. What more needed to be said?
Humanity’s hero. The world’s greatest Hunter, recognized across the globe.
Unprecedented and unmatched. The very definition of both.
Team Leader Choi was Cheon Taemin’s only grandson through his daughter.
Cheon Taemin had only one daughter, and there was no information about any other relatives. Team Leader Choi was probably his sole heir.
Good God. Cheon Taemin’s heir.
The thought alone gave me goose bumps.
I opened my mouth, my voice trembling.
“Team Leader Choi.”
“Yes, go ahead.”
Team Leader Choi answered as though he had been waiting for me to speak. He even looked relieved that the awkward silence had finally been broken.
“If it isn’t too rude, may I ask you something?”
“Anything.”
“Then can I keep calling you Team Leader Choi?”
“What?”
Team Leader Choi stared at me in disbelief.
“What exactly were you planning to call me instead?”
“Mr. Choi Minwoo. Minwoo hyung.”
“I refuse.”
“There’s one more option...”
“Don’t say it. I don’t want to hear it.”
“Please adopt me. I’ll call you Dad. I’ll be a good son.”
Team Leader Choi’s face flushed bright red.
If I had actually been his son, he looked ready to strike me from the family register on the spot.
A moment later, he let out a deep sigh.
“...This isn’t the time for jokes.”
“I’m not joking. I mean it.”
“Mr. Jin Taekyung!”
Team Leader Choi continued in a low, stern voice.
“Didn’t I tell you everything? What kind of situation I’m in?”
“You did. We all heard you.”
Im Kkeokjeong and Song Song nodded.
An hour earlier, after Lee Jungryong had left, Team Leader Choi had told us everything while we were still reeling from the shock.
His true identity. Everything that had happened until now. And why he had been forced to act as he had.

“Lee Jungryong is an extremely ambitious man. He considers me a thorn in his side and has always kept me under surveillance. He made me move from one overseas branch to another to prevent me from setting foot in headquarters.”
Team Leader Choi said he had been surrounded by watchful eyes.

Lee Jungryong had assigned him to dead-end posts to prevent him from producing any notable results, and even then, he had been transferred to a new posting once a year. They called them overseas branches, but it had been little different from exile.
“Cheon Taemin—no. Did the Ares Guild Master simply stand by and watch?”
“As I said, my maternal grandfather...”
Team Leader Choi bit down hard on his lip.
“He’s an extraordinary person. My memories are from when I was a child, but he definitely isn’t someone who thinks like an ordinary person.”

Butler Kim, who had been standing quietly at attention, added, “He was that way in the past, and he remains so now. I served the old master for many years, but not once did I understand his true intentions.”
Was this the dark side of the hero no one knew?
Team Leader Choi sighed and continued.
“Even after I submitted my resignation and left Ares Guild, they must have kept watching me. Later, I founded the Peace Guild... but recruiting even one ordinary mid-rank Hunter proved difficult.”
It was something I had not known until hearing his story, but Im Kkeokjeong and I had not been the Peace Guild’s first members.

Several high-ranking Hunters had joined before us, only to transfer to other Guilds after receiving generous contract offers out of nowhere. Some had even abruptly gone off the grid before they could sign their contracts.
It was probably Lee Jungryong’s doing.
No matter how much money you had, a Guild without Hunters was no Guild at all.
With Ares Guild tightening the screws from every direction, Team Leader Choi had begun searching for people through the Hunter Office.
That was when Im Kkeokjeong and I appeared on his radar.
Fortunately, there had been no significant pressure this time.
Two low-ranked Hunters probably didn’t seem worth bothering with.
And that had been Ares Guild’s miscalculation.
No one could have imagined that an F-rank Hunter who seemed useful only as a porter would create a storm like this.
“This incident is no different. When I heard that you had encountered Lee Jungryong, Mr. Taekyung, I thought it had happened because of me.”
“So?”
“Pardon?”
I vigorously scratched the back of my head.
“So what are you trying to say, Team Leader? You still haven’t said it clearly.”
“The difference in strength is too great for us to make an enemy of Ares Guild.”
“Everyone knows that.”
“Things like this will keep happening.”
“More detail. Be precise.”
Team Leader Choi gritted his teeth.
“I’ll terminate your contracts. If you cut ties with the Peace Guild, Ares Guild won’t bother any of you.”
His voice seethed with emotion. Team Leader Choi closed his eyes and clenched his fists.
I stared at him for a moment, then spoke.
“I don’t want to.”
“What?”
“I said I don’t want to.”
“They’re dinosaurs. We’re ants. We’re weak, so let’s back off before we get hurt worse. That’s what you’re saying, right?”
“Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
“Then it’s simple.”
Team Leader Choi stared at me with wide eyes. I spoke slowly, enunciating every word.
“Let’s get stronger.”
No.
“I’ll make you strong. I will.”

“Even after I submitted my resignation and left Ares Guild, they must have kept watching me.
Later, I founded the Peace Guild... but recruiting even one ordinary mid-rank Hunter proved difficult.”
It was something I had not known until hearing his story, but Im Kkeokjeong and I had not been the Peace Guild’s first members.
Several high-ranking Hunters had joined before us, only to transfer to other Guilds after receiving generous contract offers out of nowhere.
Some had even abruptly gone off the grid before they could sign their contracts.
It was probably Lee Jungryong’s doing.
No matter how much money you had, a Guild without Hunters was no Guild at all.
With Ares Guild tightening the screws from every direction, Team Leader Choi had begun searching for people through the Hunter Office.
That was when Im Kkeokjeong and I appeared on his radar.
Fortunately, there had been no significant pressure this time.
Two low-ranked Hunters probably didn’t seem worth bothering with.
And that had been Ares Guild’s miscalculation.
No one could have imagined that an F-rank Hunter who seemed useful only as a porter would create a storm like this.
“This incident is no different.
When I heard that you had encountered Lee Jungryong, Mr.
Taekyung, I thought it had happened because of me.”
“So?”
“Pardon?”
I vigorously scratched the back of my head.
“So what are you trying to say, Team Leader?
You still haven’t said it clearly.”
“The difference in strength is too great for us to make an enemy of Ares Guild.”
“Everyone knows that.”
“Things like this will keep happening.”
“More detail.
Be precise.”
Team Leader Choi gritted his teeth.
“I’ll terminate your contracts.
If you cut ties with the Peace Guild, Ares Guild won’t bother any of you.”
His voice seethed with emotion.
Team Leader Choi closed his eyes and clenched his fists.
I stared at him for a moment, then spoke.
“I don’t want to.”
“What?”
“I said I don’t want to.”
“They’re dinosaurs.
We’re ants.
We’re weak, so let’s back off before we get hurt worse.
That’s what you’re saying, right?”
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung.”
“Then it’s simple.”
Team Leader Choi stared at me with wide eyes.
I spoke slowly, enunciating every word.
“Let’s get stronger.”
No.
“I’ll make you strong.
I will.”

chapters.title: Chapter 289
paragraphs: “Pardon?”
Team Leader Choi looked more violently shaken than I had ever seen him before.
Even Butler Kim, who at least looked calm, wasn’t much different.
Lingering anger and bewilderment. And questions about what I had said.
I didn’t know they could make faces like that.
Whenever I charged ahead without thinking things through, these two always took two calm steps back and handled the fallout.
For once, they seemed human—just like me.
Feeling strangely moved, I opened my mouth.
“The answer is simple. If our enemies are strong, we get stronger too.”
“Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
Team Leader Choi’s voice was quiet and steady. He had reined in his initial emotions and returned to his usual composed self.
“This isn’t a math problem that can be solved simply because you know the answer. Reaching that answer would require a process more difficult than you can imagine.”
“Then we’ll be fine. If I tutor you, we should be able to solve it eventually, even if it takes some time. Oh, but let’s change the subject. I’m hopeless at math.”
“Have you forgotten? Our opponent is Ares Guild. You may not know this, but I do. I know exactly how powerful they are.”
“Unfortunately, the Young Master is right.”
Team Leader Choi and Butler Kim fell silent after that.
One was the maternal grandson of Cheon Taemin, Guild Master of Ares Guild. The other was a core member who had served Cheon Taemin for many years.
Given their positions, they must have seen and experienced a great deal firsthand. Their blood might have been boiling, but their cool heads had already calculated the answer.
But...
“Team Leader Choi.”
I looked into his eyes, which already said the matter was settled.
“Do you remember what you said to me before we went to Myeongdong Guild?”
“Of course.”
“What did you say back then?”
After a moment’s hesitation, Team Leader Choi parted his lips.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung may seem reckless at first glance, but...”
“I always anticipate the worst-case scenario before acting. And?”
“You always bring back the best possible result.”
“You said you trusted me more than you trusted yourself, Team Leader. Did you only say that because it sounded nice?”
“Absolutely not.”
“I may have been a lousy student, but I’m not stupid enough to risk my life on a game with zero chance of winning. This is doable.”
“Doable...”
“If you can’t believe in yourself, believe in me.”
Light seeped into Team Leader Choi’s eyes as he sensed the sincerity behind my words. It was faint, but I knew what it was.
Hope.
Hope was like a spark. It could flare up or die out in an instant. You had to fan it before it went out.

“Since we’re on the subject, let me ask you something. If I leave the Guild now, will you give up too? I suppose shutting down the Guild, retiring, and farming with Butler Kim wouldn’t be so bad. Lee Jungryong might even supply the fertilizer.”
“Hunter Jin Taekyung!”
Ignoring Butler Kim’s attempt to stop me, I continued.

“You said you wanted to build the greatest Guild in the world. If you send me away, send Uncle Kkeokjeong and Song-i away, and let even the new recruits leave, are the two of you planning to fight Ares Guild by yourselves?”
“Team Leader Choi.”
He remained silent. No answer came.
But the spark in his eyes was still alive.
Before long, a hoarse voice slipped between his lips.
“Ares Guild is an empire. An empire so powerful that even the ten largest Guilds in Korea couldn’t stand against it if they joined forces.”
“Good grief. We’ll have to work hard if we want to catch up with them.”
“I may not know everything about Ares Guild, but I know a great deal. That only makes them seem even more dangerous.”
“It also improves our chances. It means we know our enemy well. Know your enemy and know yourself, and you can fight a hundred battles without disaster. Right?”
“I’ve considered it countless times, but every calculation told me it was impossible.”
“Then run the numbers again.”
“Is it really... possible?”
“Yes.”
“Where exactly did my calculations go wrong? What makes you so confident in your answer?”
He wasn’t asking because he failed to understand.
More than anyone, Team Leader Choi wanted his answer to be wrong. He wanted even the faintest possibility that we could stand against Lee Jungryong.
I was happy to give him the answer he wanted.
“The person talking to you right now.”
“The process of your calculations was accurate. Except for one thing.”
I slowly raised a finger and pointed at my chest.
“Me.”
At that moment, Team Leader Choi’s eyes shook. I could feel the spark in them beginning to fade.
Disappointment, not hope, filled the void it left behind.
“You were included in my calculations, Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
“Of course I was. You wouldn’t be the Team Leader Choi I know otherwise.”
Team Leader Choi was a brilliant man. He possessed natural leadership, exceptional judgment, and the drive to act on it.
He had weighed Peace Guild against Ares Guild with a cool head, and I must have been included on Peace Guild’s side of the scale.
“Everything you’ve shown us until now has been astonishing. No, almost miraculous.”
I already knew what words would follow his fading voice.
“But I’m still not enough?”
Team Leader Choi nodded gravely.
“Even excluding Lee Jungryong, an S-rank Hunter, Ares Guild officially has more than a hundred A-rank Hunters. Their mid- and low-rank Hunters are beyond counting.”
The way he emphasized officially implied that they had even more strength hidden from the public.
And they still have more than a hundred A-rank Hunters.
I had heard the rumors before, but hearing it directly from Team Leader Choi made the true scale of Ares Guild’s power sink in.
No matter how strong I was, in the end, I was still only one pair of hands. Team Leader Choi’s judgment was cold and clear.
But...
“If that’s how you’re calculating it, you’ll have to run the numbers again.”
“Pardon?”
“The formula is right, but the numbers are wrong. I don’t know what value you assigned to me, but you’ll need to multiply it several times over.”
Team Leader Choi’s eyes widened. So did Butler Kim’s, Im Kkeokjeong’s, and Song Song’s.
Considering everything I had done until now, their reaction was understandable.
I had hunted a Named Monster alone, crushed nearly thirty Black Hunters, and confronted a major Guild like Myeongdong Guild head-on.
Leaving everyone frozen like statues, I fixed my gaze on Team Leader Choi.
“I feel like I’ve told you this repeatedly. I’m a man with more secrets than you think.”
Murim was Murim, and the modern world was the modern world.
There had always been a clear boundary in my mind separating the two. But Lee Jungryong and Ares Guild had erased that line.
If none of this had happened, I probably would have kept my secret for the rest of my life.
Was wanting to live quietly too much to ask?
Perhaps this was the fate that came with the power I had been given. If so, it was time to accept it. I couldn’t keep running forever.
To protect the things precious to me from my enemies, I had to become stronger.
“So, what are you going to do now?”
Team Leader Choi still stared at me in disbelief.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung, you never cease to surprise me.”
“Save it. There’ll be plenty more surprises from now on.”
“It will be a dangerous road.”
“I happen to specialize in thorny roads.”
“Far more dangerous than anything you’ve faced until now.”
“Nothing to compare it to, my ass. You just don’t know it. This side is already hell...”
He seemed to have taken my words as a joke.
I watched Team Leader Choi as he finally let out a quiet laugh.
“Team Leader.”
“Yes?”
“Sometimes, it’s okay to be honest.”
The smile vanished from the corners of Team Leader Choi’s mouth. His gaze settled, and his lips pressed into a firm line.
I waited for him to speak. What came next was something I needed to hear directly from him.
Fortunately, I didn’t have to wait long.
“I know this is a presumptuous request, but... would you continue with Peace Guild?”
Yes. That was it.
I grinned and lightly tapped Team Leader Choi on the shoulder. He looked intelligent and cold on the outside, but he was softhearted underneath.
That was why he had tried to send us away despite wanting us to stay. He was afraid we would get hurt.
“Let’s make this work.”
“...Thank you.”
Team Leader Choi offered a fleeting smile before turning toward the others.
Butler Kim, his devoted retainer and someone practically no different from family, spoke first.
“I trust you already know my answer.”
“Thank you, Butler Kim.”
Next was Song Song. When Team Leader Choi asked her the same question he had asked me, she heaved several deep sighs before answering.
“Ares Guild? Ah, the numbers really don’t add up on this one.”
Honestly, that was the most normal reaction. We were openly declaring our intention to make an enemy of Ares Guild. Anyone who welcomed the idea would be strange.
“Double my annual salary. And add hazard pay.”
Song Song wasn’t normal either.
When I stared at her in disbelief, she shrugged.
“What? Why?”
“No reason. I just thought most people would walk away in a situation like this.”
“Do you want me to leave?”
“Now, now. Absolutely not.”
“Do you know why I transferred from Ares Guild to Peace Guild? Why I followed Team Leader Choi even with everyone trying to keep him down?”
“How would I know?”
“Because Team Leader Choi promised me double my salary.”
“My goal is to retire at thirty. If I earn as much as I can over the next two years, I’ll be able to live comfortably for the rest of my life.”
She spoke as though it were nothing, but this was only her roundabout way of saying she wanted to stay with us too. Everyone knew the frugal Song Song had already amassed a small fortune.
“And, well, you seem to have a plan too, so I’ll trust you for now. It’s hard to find a superior as capable and handsome as Team Leader Choi.”
And just like that, Song Song’s decision to stay was settled. Everyone’s gaze, including mine, shifted toward the last person.
“Uncle Kkeokjeong.”
He didn’t answer when I called him. Only after a long silence did he finally speak.
“Taekyung, will I be any help?”
“More than enough.”
“Even though I’m only a D-rank Hunter?”
“People associated with D are the real protagonists, after all. Why not legally change your name while you’re at it? Im D. Kkeokjeong. How does that sound?”
Im Kkeokjeong burst out laughing, then looked Team Leader Choi straight in the eye.
“It wasn’t your fault I got hurt, Team Leader Choi. So don’t blame yourself.”
“No. It was all my fault. Please focus on your recovery and rehabilitation first, then take your time thinking it over. You have a family, Hunter Im.”
“Team Leader Choi.”
“Yes?”
“Do you know what my first thought was when my arms were cut off?”
“Your family?”
He was a woman’s husband and the father of two children.
But Im Kkeokjeong calmly shook his head.
“Ah, I guess I can’t work as a Hunter anymore. That was the first thing that came to mind.”
“I love this work. I spent twenty years going in and out of Gates not merely to earn a living, but because I felt a sense of duty as a Hunter. But...”
Im Kkeokjeong bit down hard on his lip. His gaze remained fixed on his own two arms, wrapped in bandages.
“Can I recover?”
“You can. Absolutely.”
A faint smile spread across Im Kkeokjeong’s lips.
“Then I’m coming too. I can’t abandon a Hunter’s duty over something like this.”
Something churned deep in my chest at the sight.
People dismissed him as a low-rank Hunter in name only, but Im Kkeokjeong was one of the few true Hunters left in this age.
They’re all far too good to stop here.
All right. Strike while the iron was hot.
Having made up my mind, I opened my Skill window for the first time in a long while.
There, among the densely packed entries in the holographic window, I found what I wanted.
System Skill: Martial Arts Manual Creation
Yes. This was the beginning.
With firm resolve, I touched the holographic window.
Beep!
System To create a martial arts manual, you need at least 300 sheets of A4 paper!
What the fuck.

chapters.title: Chapter 290
paragraphs: System Skill Window Martial Arts Manual Creation Grade: None Restriction: Martial arts at Great Completion Description: The caster can create manuals only for martial arts they have achieved Great Completion in. A deeper understanding of the martial art may produce better results. Special Note: Materials are required to create a martial arts manual.
I stared at the Skill information window and thought.
Hold on. When did I get this?
Was it when I achieved Great Completion in the Jin Family’s Manoeuvre Technique? Or the Jin Family’s Spear Technique?
It had been over a year, so my memory was hazy.
I had somehow acquired the Skill, but I had never used it because there had been no opportunity.
No, that wasn’t quite right. It wasn’t that I had no opportunity. I just never intended to use it.
After returning to the modern world, I had occasionally felt the urge whenever I saw the members of Peace Guild. But every time, I reached the same conclusion.
What kind of trouble would I be asking for if I let martial arts leak out?
Imagine everyone else fighting with bronze weapons when some bastard showed up with a steel sword and started cutting down anyone in his path.
Everyone would envy him, then swarm like a pack of dogs to get their hands on that steel sword.
It wasn’t that I didn’t trust the members of Peace Guild, but at the time, I believed holding back was the right decision.
But now there’s no reason to hesitate.
Crossing blows with Lee Jungryong and his subordinates, Park Jihoon and Go Jun, had taught me that the modern world held secrets I knew nothing about.
Their movements and use of mana were distinctly similar to those of Murim martial artists. If the enemy was armed with steel swords, we needed comparable equipment.
I drew a deep breath, sucking a foul stench into my nostrils.
I was currently squatting inside a bathroom stall.
The surroundings were awful, but it was the perfect place to create a martial arts manual without anyone seeing me.
All right. Let’s get started.
I spread out the A4 paper and pen I had bought from the hospital convenience store.
Then I muttered inwardly.
Activate Martial Arts Manual Creation.
Beep.

System All materials are ready. The Martial Arts Manual Creation Skill has been activated. You can create manuals for martial arts that have achieved Great Completion. Currently Available: Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique, Jin Family’s Manoeuvre Technique, Jin Family’s Spear Technique Select the desired martial art.
None of the Fire Gate Clan’s martial arts I had learned had reached Great Completion.
The Jin Family of Taiyuan’s hereditary martial arts, on the other hand, were stable and reasonably powerful.
Of those, I chose the most fundamental.
Select Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique.
Beep.
System Create a martial arts manual for Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique? Y / N
Yes.
Beep! Beep!
System Intelligence insufficient! Brainpower insufficient! Teaching is several times harder than learning! Creating a manual for a Peak Grade martial art requires at least 100 Intelligence!
“...You bastards. Seriously.”
Weeping tears of blood, I opened my Status Window.
The moment I poured my precious points into Intelligence, the hand holding the pen began racing across the A4 paper like lightning.
Scritch-scritch-scritch-scritch!
“Gasp!”
I received two shocks.
The first was the incredible speed. The second was that everything being written was in Chinese.
Fuck this. I can’t work like this.
I began desperately searching for the language settings.
The door slid open.
I entered the hospital room where the Peace Guild members were staying. Everyone had been gathered together talking, but they turned toward me as I came in.
“Where did you go that took so long... Wait, were you in the bathroom?”
Song Song pinched her nose. I answered gloomily.
“How did you know?”
“You reek of shit.”
“Is it that bad?”
“Yeah. I thought a giant turd had walked into the room.”
“Thanks for the kind words. I feel stronger already.”
After spending over an hour inside a stinking bathroom stall, my nose had gone numb.
I answered in a drained voice and handed her the stack of stapled A4 pages.
“Here.”
“What’s this?”
“A love letter for you. I wrote it while I had diarrhea.”
“Blech! Bleegh!”
“What a passionate reaction.”
“Bleeeggh!”
That wasn’t a reaction. She was genuinely retching.
I had thought there was nothing left between us to salvage, but I still couldn’t help the dull ache in a corner of my heart.
“I loved you...”
“Bleeeggh!”
“Hunter Song Song, are you all right?”
As her retching grew more violent, Butler Kim flew to her side and began patting her back.
Meanwhile, the A4 pages Song Song had been waving like the Taegeukgi passed into someone else’s hands.
Team Leader Choi read the words on the first page, then let out a quiet laugh as he looked at me.
“Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique? That’s an unusual title for a love letter.”
“What’s written inside is even more unusual.”
“...Pardon?”
“Keep reading.”
Team Leader Choi was quick on the uptake. He immediately straightened and began turning the pages with a solemn expression.
His eyes raced across handwriting so mechanical that it was hard to believe I had written it myself.
Flip. Flip. Flip...
His pace grew faster and faster, and hot breaths escaped between his lips.
After tearing through ten-odd pages in an instant, he jerked his head up. His eyes had widened like saucers.
“This is...!”
Even I was taken aback by his reaction.
He knows what this is?

It might have been called a martial arts manual, but now that I had made it, anyone unfamiliar with the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique could easily have mistaken the manual for a traditional medicine text.
It detailed the locations and functions of the countless acupoints in the human body, along with the pathways used to circulate internal energy.
Song Song would have read a few pages and closed it, but Team Leader Choi’s reaction went far beyond anything I had expected.
“Do you recognize it?”
“Yes. Of course.”
Then a term I had never heard before slipped from his lips.
“This is a Mana Cultivation Method.”
“A mana what?”
“A Mana Cultivation Method!”
Mana Cultivation Method?
What a bizarre name. Whoever had coined it possessed a strange sense of style.
Butler Kim hurried over when he heard Team Leader Choi raise his voice.
“Did you just say Mana Cultivation Method?”
“Yes. Here.”
Butler Kim took the manual from Team Leader Choi and frantically flipped through the pages.
Before long, he reacted much the same way.
“Gasp.”
“What do you think, Butler Kim?”
“There’s no doubt about it. This is definitely a Mana Cultivation Method. But where on earth did this come from?”
The bathroom.
Team Leader Choi raised a finger and pointed at me.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung...”
“Hunter Jin Taekyung?”
Whip! Crack!
Before Team Leader Choi could finish, Butler Kim’s head snapped toward me with a series of violent cracks.
“How does Hunter Jin Taekyung possess a Mana Cultivation Method?”
I answered calmly.
“For starters, I don’t know what a Mana Cultivation Method is. Naturally, this is the first I’ve heard of this being one. By the way, is your neck all right? I think I just heard a bone break...”
“Is that important right now? This little neck of mine can break for all I care.”
“...It sounds pretty important to me.”
What did he mean, it could break? This old man seemed to be getting tougher by the day.
Of course, that only showed how important this was.
So Lee Jungryong learned a Mana Cultivation Method.
The compound term had sounded strange at first, but after repeating it a few times, it began to roll smoothly off my tongue.
It wasn’t hard to infer from the name that it referred to an internal cultivation technique used by Hunters.
And that Lee Jungryong and his subordinates had learned precisely such a technique.
“Could you please answer my question?”
“Taekyung, this is extremely important.”
Butler Kim and Team Leader Choi looked more grave than ever.
I glanced around as though flustered, then gave them the answer I had prepared in advance.
“Well, my father taught it to me when I was young...”
“Pardon me, but are you referring to your late father?”
Yes.
Team Leader Choi furrowed his brow.
“I understand your late father was an ordinary man.”
“That’s right.”
“Then how did he know a Mana Cultivation Method...?”
“He probably didn’t know either. When he taught it to me, he said it was just a health regimen passed down through our family.”
“A health regimen?”
“A Mana Cultivation Method passed down through the family...”
As the two stared at me in disbelief, I pointed to the cover.
Four neat characters were printed there in lettering as clean as an office document’s font.
Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique
Even the name was perfect.
If Shanxi Province had the Jin Family of Taiyuan, then Gyeonggi Province had the Jin Family of Goyang. Simple as that.
If I claimed it was a family heirloom passed down through the generations, they wouldn’t have much to argue with.
As expected, they were both briefly rendered speechless. I continued.

“It’s a kind of breathing method. My father started teaching it to me when I was young, saying that practicing it would make me healthier. He even made me memorize something called a formula word for word.”
“It is similar to a Mana Cultivation Method, but...”
“Could we see the original? The original manual?”
“After my father passed away, everything was so chaotic... I looked for it after we moved, but it was gone.”
“That’s unfortunate.”
“It is. Fortunately, I memorized every last word.”
It was true that something I owned had disappeared. I had merely slipped the nonexistent original manual for the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique into the story.
Perfect destruction of evidence. When they heard that even the original was gone, both of their shoulders sagged.
I’d love to see their faces if they knew this was the original.
The martial arts manuals people imagined all looked more or less the same.
Half-rotted bamboo slips. Ancient books reeking of rat piss.
They could go play jokgu. I didn’t have any of that crap.
I stood the crisp stack of A4 paper upright and slammed a stapler through it. Murim martial artists would have been appalled, but a twenty-first-century martial arts manual deserved to look the part.
“Still, this is extraordinary. A cultivation technique... I never imagined such a thing truly existed.”
“I’ve seen them mentioned a few times in novels and movies. I believe they called them martial arts.”

“You are correct, Young Master. In a sense, a Mana Cultivation Method is also a form of martial arts. Look here. It says that you circulate and accumulate qi by circulating your energy, does it not? That follows the same principle as a Mana Cultivation Method...”
Yeah, it is martial arts.
While I fought back the words itching to escape my mouth, Team Leader Choi asked me a question.
“Then, Mr. Jin Taekyung, have you been practicing a Mana Cultivation Method—or rather, the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique—since childhood?”
Yes.
“I’m sorry to put it this way, but its effects seem somewhat less impressive than expected...”
Translated directly, he was asking, If you had this, why did you spend seven years as an F-rank Hunter?
A sharp question. Also one I had expected.
I answered without batting an eye.
“As you know, I was quite skilled for an F-rank Hunter. I even received a commendation for graduating at the top of my training center.”
“Ah, yes. I heard about that. I also know you served as a deputy team leader in your former Guild.”
Granted, it had been a tiny, weak Guild, but F-rank Hunters were treated like punching bags wherever they went—like dog shit on the street.

Unless they were related by blood to the Guild’s leadership, it was extremely rare for an F-rank Hunter to serve as a deputy team leader. That was why my appointment had been a subject of conversation within the Guild for quite some time.

“There was a lot of talk about it. Hunters with higher ranks and more experience than me complained about seniority and grumbled that they should have come first... In the end, I proved myself through sheer ability. And the reason I could do that was the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique.”
“Hmm.”
“Looking at it that way, it does seem to have had some effect.”
I knew. This alone wouldn’t be enough to convince them of my past or the effectiveness of the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique.
I smiled faintly and looked around. Song Song had finally stopped retching, and even Im Kkeokjeong was watching me with curiosity, waiting for what I would say next.

chapters.title: Chapter 291
paragraphs: “Suppose you roll a snowball the size of your fist down a hill. What happens? Anyone know?”
Song Song snorted at my question.
“Even a kindergartener could answer that.”
“Then answer it.”
“Obviously, it gets bigger as it rolls downhill.”
“Why?”
“Because it picks up the snow piled on the hill.”
“Yeah, just like my feelings for you.”
“Blegh! Bleeeggh!”
This was addictive.
With Song Song’s renewed retching as my background music, I continued.

“What Song-i just said is correct. But the premise is different here. This isn’t a snow-covered hill. It’s a hill where the snow has already melted. No matter how hard you roll the snowball down it, it won’t get much bigger.”
“The snowball you’re talking about is mana, then.”
“Team Leader Choi, you catch on fast. Yes, a Mana Cultivation Method works the same way. If all you start with is a speck of dust, it’ll still be a speck of dust no matter how much you roll it.”
“The lower the rank, the lower the ceiling. Is that what you mean?”
“Exactly.”
There was a saying that once you were an F-rank, you were an F-rank forever.
That was how difficult it was to break free of the rank you had been assigned.
But on extremely rare occasions, some people managed to pluck that star from the sky.
Second Awakeners. That was what they were called—and it was also the mask I was currently wearing.
“After my second awakening made me a C-rank Hunter, the effects increased dramatically. That was when a little snow finally began to accumulate on what had been a grassy hill.”
“Come to think of it, your results at the time were...”
“My mana reserves were C-rank, but even then, my control was A-rank. You know why, right?”
“The Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique.”
Team Leader Choi groaned.
“So it wasn’t a mistake on the Association’s part.”
As I became famous and my past actions came to light, that part was concluded to have been a measurement error.
As a result, the Bucheon Association, which had conducted the retest, had taken a mountain of abuse. From their perspective, it must have felt deeply unfair.
“The Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique, which you and Butler Kim call a Mana Cultivation Method, has two effects. The first is an increase in mana. And the second is...”
Butler Kim picked up the thread.
“Mana control on an entirely different level.”
“Correct.”
Qi—called mana here and internal energy in Murim—could differ as greatly as heaven and earth depending on how it was used.
The Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique was a Peak martial art. It accumulated qi slowly, but its stability rivaled that of a Supreme Peak martial art.

“Learning it alone should lead to dramatic progress. We’ll keep an eye on the new recruits for now... For the time being, only those of you here should focus on learning the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique. And of course, this must be done in absolute secrecy.”
What was with their reactions?
A heavy silence descended over the hospital room. All four of them stared blankly at me, mouths hanging open.
“Did you just say... you were going to teach us a Mana Cultivation Method?”
“Not a Mana Cultivation Method. The Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique.”
“Yes, yes. The Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique.”
Team Leader Choi’s eyelids trembled.
“You’re going to teach it to us?”
“That’s why I brought it, obviously. Did you think I brought it here just to show off?”
I looked around at everyone and continued.

“As you all know, we won’t last long at our current level. Lee Jungryong won’t come after us right away because of the recent incident, but it’s only a matter of time. But... what if we had the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique?”
Im Kkeokjeong, who had been sitting with his mouth wide open, shouted.
“Jin! Family’s! Cultivation! Technique!”
“Ah, now that’s a good reaction. Anyway, I made this decision after careful consideration, so for the time being, I’d like you to follow my instructions without complaint. Understood?”
The four people here would be the first in line. Next would come the newly hired Hunters.
I would put them through a rigorous screening process, then turn them into both Hunters and martial artists.
Elites capable of handling two or three Hunters of the same rank with ease.
“Well, then...”
I looked over the still-dazed group one by one, then crooked a finger at one of them.
“Let’s start with Team Leader Choi.”
At that moment, a holographic window appeared over his still-stunned face.
Ding.
System A Quest, Back, Back—Let’s See Your Back!, has been generated!
That was a title that made me not want to do it for some reason.

System Quest Back, Back—Let’s See Your Back! Unlike the Murim, your modern life had been peaceful. But reality is a cesspool! Alarmed by this harsh reality, you have decided to pass martial arts on to trustworthy friends. Whether this choice proves poisonous or beneficial... depends on your decisions and abilities. May fortune in the martial arts be with you! Grade: Peak Restriction: Jin Taekyung Mission: Guide the acquisition of Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique (Incomplete) Reward: A considerable amount of EXP Repeat Quest ??? Failure: In the worst-case scenario, suffer qi deviation
Who the hell came up with this quest title?

I really did need to see his back. I had to send internal energy into the Mingmen acupoint in his lower back and teach him how to circulate it. But after reading that title, I suddenly really, really didn’t want to.
“Whew. Team Leader Choi.”
“Yes.”
“Your back.”
“What?”

“Ah, never mind. Take the position I’m about to show you. Butler Kim and everyone else, guard the hospital room and make sure no outsiders enter. Above all, no one is to touch either of us. Understood?”
“Of course.”
Butler Kim nodded firmly and cast a spell. Each time he swept his staff through the air while chanting, an invisible barrier spread around the hospital room.
Meanwhile, Team Leader Choi removed his shirt, awkwardly sat cross-legged, and presented his back to me.
“What are you planning to do to me now?”
“...You really know how to phrase things strangely.”
I ought to give him qi deviation. Damn it.
I placed my hand on Team Leader Choi’s Mingmen acupoint.
From this point on, I had to be extremely careful. Even the most formidable Murim master was practically defenseless while circulating their qi.
“Close your eyes and focus on the mana inside your body. Whatever happens, endure it. Is anything bothering you right now? If so, tell me now.”
“My right shoulder blade is a little...”
“Does it hurt?”
“It’s itchy.”
“...This is driving me crazy. Here?”
Scratch, scratch.
When I reached out and scratched it for him, Team Leader Choi’s voice relaxed considerably.
“Yes, right there. That feels wonderful.”
“They used to call me the Filial Son’s Hand.”
“And the area around my underwear is a little tight, so...”
“Are you crazy? Handle that part yourself. Did I put you in handcuffs?”
“Ah, so that was an option. I’m very tense right now.”
“Whew. It’s all right. Sorry I got worked up for no reason.”
“It isn’t your fault, Taekyung. If I’d known this would happen, I would have worn a thong.”
Does this guy actually know his way around underwear...?
Team Leader Choi was so nervous that he was blurting out whatever came to mind. I warned him in a low, level voice.
“From now on, if you open your mouth, you’re dead. Focus on one thing and one thing only: where the mana is flowing and how.”
“Understood.”
“Even if your shoulder blade itches, endure it. Even if something gets caught in your underwear, endure it. Do you understand?”
“May I ask what exactly we’re about to do?”

“I’m going to move your mana through True Qi Guidance. After that, I’ll perform a Small Circulation according to the formula of the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique, then finish by circulating your qi and regulating your breathing.”
“Did you understand any of that? Be honest.”
“Be honest?”
“Yes.”
After a brief silence, Team Leader Choi answered.
“You lost me at True Qi Guidance.”
“Then close your eyes and shut your mouth. If you start wiggling your ass while saying things like, ‘Something’s caught in my underwear,’ I’ll kill you before I die.”
“I’ll keep that in mind.”
His answer rang with resolve. I felt Team Leader Choi’s body, which had been rigid with tension, gradually relax.
He was a novice taking his first step into the unfamiliar world of martial arts.
It didn’t matter how much social experience Team Leader Choi had accumulated, how many languages he spoke, or what kind of knowledge he possessed.
“Then we’ll begin.”
Everything depended on me now.
After steadying my breathing, I drew internal energy up from my dantian, channeled it through my palm, and sent it into Team Leader Choi’s Mingmen acupoint.
Slowly. Carefully.
Ssshh.
The moment the Scorching Yang Qi, imbued with Extreme Yang energy, entered his body, the System fired a signal flare as if it had been waiting.
Ding.
System True Qi Guidance begins.
I had removed the waste accumulated inside Mom and Hayeon’s bodies once before.
But in terms of difficulty, this was as different as heaven and earth.
True Qi Guidance meant leading the energy inside another person’s body in whatever direction I wanted.
The energy Team Leader Choi possessed was incomparably more abundant than an ordinary person’s.
And cleaner than I expected.
No, let me correct that. It wasn’t merely cleaner than expected. At this level, it was exceptionally clean.
His muscles and bones were sturdy, his sinews and meridians strong, and his acupoints as clear as a highway at dawn. There was hardly any waste inside him.
What the hell? He said he hadn’t learned a Mana Cultivation Method.
Team Leader Choi’s Hunter license was B-rank. The energy I usually sensed from him was exactly at that level.
The only things that set him apart from an ordinary B-rank Hunter were the combat instincts born of his sharp mind and the power of his high-end equipment.
Honestly, for Cheon Taemin’s only blood descendant, he’d always seemed a little disappointing.
Outstanding leadership. A brilliant mind and decisive judgment.
Despite all that, he was inevitably underestimated.
Anyone would pale beside Cheon Taemin, the hero who had saved all of humanity.
But now I had changed my mind a little.
At this level... a little help would be enough for him to reach a higher realm in no time.
An A-rank Hunter? No. I intended to turn Team Leader Choi into a Peak master. His basic hardware was far too good to leave to rot.
If the others were even half as capable as Team Leader Choi, this would be much easier.
With that carefree thought, I sent the Scorching Yang Qi flowing through him. Before long, more than one jiazi’s worth of my internal energy was winding its way through his body.
Whoosh!
I felt the body beneath my palm twitch. By now, he was probably experiencing heat unlike anything he had ever felt before.
Paying it no mind, I gathered the energy scattered throughout his body and drove it through dozens of acupoints.
Team Leader Choi had to remember this. From now on, he would have to travel this path on his own thousands, tens of thousands of times.
Once the body remembers, the rest is easy.
The pace was astonishingly fast.
Before long, the energy I was guiding had reached half a jiazi, and what little waste remained was cleanly burned away by the heat of the Scorching Yang Qi.
Now for the last step.

I had gathered the scattered energy. It was time to store it in the dantian. Once that was done, a complete circulation would be achieved, and he could be said to have taken his first step as a martial artist.
But then...
What the hell is that?
When I reached Team Leader Choi’s dantian, I stopped dead.
A massive mass of qi occupied half of his dantian.
Then came the System notification.
Ding.

sentences.text: “Suppose you roll a snowball the size of your fist down a hill.
What happens?
Anyone know?”
Song Song snorted at my question.
“Even a kindergartener could answer that.”
“Then answer it.”
“Obviously, it gets bigger as it rolls downhill.”
“Why?”
“Because it picks up the snow piled on the hill.”
“Yeah, just like my feelings for you.”
“Blegh!
Bleeeggh!”
This was addictive.
With Song Song’s renewed retching as my background music, I continued.
“What Song-i just said is correct.
But the premise is different here.
This isn’t a snow-covered hill.
It’s a hill where the snow has already melted.
No matter how hard you roll the snowball down it, it won’t get much bigger.”
“The snowball you’re talking about is mana, then.”
“Team Leader Choi, you catch on fast.
Yes, a Mana Cultivation Method works the same way.
If all you start with is a speck of dust, it’ll still be a speck of dust no matter how much you roll it.”
“The lower the rank, the lower the ceiling.
Is that what you mean?”
“Exactly.”
There was a saying that once you were an F-rank, you were an F-rank forever.
That was how difficult it was to break free of the rank you had been assigned.
But on extremely rare occasions, some people managed to pluck that star from the sky.
Second Awakeners.
That was what they were called—and it was also the mask I was currently wearing.
“After my second awakening made me a C-rank Hunter, the effects increased dramatically.
That was when a little snow finally began to accumulate on what had been a grassy hill.”
“Come to think of it, your results at the time were...”
“My mana reserves were C-rank, but even then, my control was A-rank.
You know why, right?”
“The Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique.”
Team Leader Choi groaned.
“So it wasn’t a mistake on the Association’s part.”
As I became famous and my past actions came to light, that part was concluded to have been a measurement error.
As a result, the Bucheon Association, which had conducted the retest, had taken a mountain of abuse.
From their perspective, it must have felt deeply unfair.
“The Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique, which you and Butler Kim call a Mana Cultivation Method, has two effects.
The first is an increase in mana.
And the second is...”
Butler Kim picked up the thread.
“Mana control on an entirely different level.”
“Correct.”
Qi—called mana here and internal energy in Murim—could differ as greatly as heaven and earth depending on how it was used.
The Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique was a Peak martial art.
It accumulated qi slowly, but its stability rivaled that of a Supreme Peak martial art.
“Learning it alone should lead to dramatic progress.
We’ll keep an eye on the new recruits for now...
For the time being, only those of you here should focus on learning the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique.
And of course, this must be done in absolute secrecy.”
What was with their reactions?
A heavy silence descended over the hospital room.
All four of them stared blankly at me, mouths hanging open.
“Did you just say... you were going to teach us a Mana Cultivation Method?”
“Not a Mana Cultivation Method.
The Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique.”
“Yes, yes.
The Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique.”
Team Leader Choi’s eyelids trembled.
“You’re going to teach it to us?”
“That’s why I brought it, obviously.
Did you think I brought it here just to show off?”
I looked around at everyone and continued.
“As you all know, we won’t last long at our current level.
Lee Jungryong won’t come after us right away because of the recent incident, but it’s only a matter of time.
But... what if we had the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique?”
Im Kkeokjeong, who had been sitting with his mouth wide open, shouted.
“Jin!
Family’s!
Cultivation!
Technique!”
“Ah, now that’s a good reaction.
Anyway, I made this decision after careful consideration, so for the time being, I’d like you to follow my instructions without complaint.
Understood?”
The four people here would be the first in line.
Next would come the newly hired Hunters.
I would put them through a rigorous screening process, then turn them into both Hunters and martial artists.
Elites capable of handling two or three Hunters of the same rank with ease.
“Well, then...”
I looked over the still-dazed group one by one, then crooked a finger at one of them.
“Let’s start with Team Leader Choi.”
At that moment, a holographic window appeared over his still-stunned face.
Ding.
System A Quest, Back, Back—Let’s See Your Back!, has been generated!
That was a title that made me not want to do it for some reason.
System Quest Back, Back—Let’s See Your Back!
Unlike the Murim, your modern life had been peaceful.
But reality is a cesspool!
Alarmed by this harsh reality, you have decided to pass martial arts on to trustworthy friends.
Whether this choice proves poisonous or beneficial... depends on your decisions and abilities.
May fortune in the martial arts be with you!
Grade: Peak Restriction: Jin Taekyung Mission: Guide the acquisition of Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique (Incomplete) Reward: A considerable amount of EXP Repeat Quest ???
Failure: In the worst-case scenario, suffer qi deviation
Who the hell came up with this quest title?
I really did need to see his back.
I had to send internal energy into the Mingmen acupoint in his lower back and teach him how to circulate it.
But after reading that title, I suddenly really, really didn’t want to.
“Whew.
Team Leader Choi.”
“Yes.”
“Your back.”
“What?”
“Ah, never mind.
Take the position I’m about to show you.
Butler Kim and everyone else, guard the hospital room and make sure no outsiders enter.
Above all, no one is to touch either of us.
Understood?”
“Of course.”
Butler Kim nodded firmly and cast a spell.
Each time he swept his staff through the air while chanting, an invisible barrier spread around the hospital room.
Meanwhile, Team Leader Choi removed his shirt, awkwardly sat cross-legged, and presented his back to me.
“What are you planning to do to me now?”
“...You really know how to phrase things strangely.”
I ought to give him qi deviation.
Damn it.
I placed my hand on Team Leader Choi’s Mingmen acupoint.
From this point on, I had to be extremely careful.
Even the most formidable Murim master was practically defenseless while circulating their qi.
“Close your eyes and focus on the mana inside your body.
Whatever happens, endure it.
Is anything bothering you right now?
If so, tell me now.”
“My right shoulder blade is a little...”
“Does it hurt?”
“It’s itchy.”
“...This is driving me crazy.
Here?”
Scratch, scratch.
When I reached out and scratched it for him, Team Leader Choi’s voice relaxed considerably.
“Yes, right there.
That feels wonderful.”
“They used to call me the Filial Son’s Hand.”
“And the area around my underwear is a little tight, so...”
“Are you crazy?
Handle that part yourself.
Did I put you in handcuffs?”
“Ah, so that was an option.
I’m very tense right now.”
“Whew.
It’s all right.
Sorry I got worked up for no reason.”

If I’d known this would happen, I would have worn a thong.”
Does this guy actually know his way around underwear...?

chapters.title: Chapter 292
paragraphs: Ding.
System A Sudden Quest, I’ll Take Only Half the Internal Energy I Digest., has been generated. Will you accept it? Y / N
Damn it. Why now?
I was dying to check the Quest window.
But I was in the middle of True Qi Guidance. Circulating my own qi would be one thing, but if I let go of control here, I could easily suffer an Internal Injury.
System If you do not answer within five seconds, the Quest will be canceled automatically. - Five, four, three...
Do I go for it or not?
Judging by the Quest title, it wanted me to do something about that thing in Team Leader Choi’s dantian. Even at a glance, it contained well over one jiazi’s worth of energy.
System Two, one...
Fuck it. I don’t know. It’s not like I’m going to die.
Accept!
Ding.
That had been close. The moment the notification confirmed that the Quest had been accepted, I realized what I had to do.
System The mysterious qi has been dormant for a long time, and its owner lacks the power to control it. Now is the time for you to step forward!
Just as I thought.
I had encountered a situation like this once before in Murim.
I dredged up an old memory.
Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng.
From the moment I first opened my eyes in Murim, the internal energy of the Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng had lain dormant inside my dantian.
It was internal energy that the Third Rate wastrel Jin Taekyung—not me—had been unable to fully digest.
That was when I first learned that even if you consumed an elixir, you couldn’t make its power your own unless you had the ability to digest it.
Just like Team Leader Choi now.
He was an outstanding talent compared to that Third Rate wastrel, but without a Mana Cultivation Method, he had no way to control such an enormous reserve of energy—nearly one jiazi’s worth.
The Quest wanted me to serve as his digestive aid.
But how does Team Leader Choi have that much energy in the first place?
Now that I thought about it, it pissed me off.

I’d been put through the fucking wringer in Murim and had only just managed to accumulate a little more than one jiazi. What the hell had this guy ever done to have such monstrous energy deposited in his dantian?
Ah, right. His maternal grandfather was Cheon Taemin.
Was this what they meant by being born with a hero’s silver spoon?
I gave up on thinking about it. Right now, I needed to focus on breaking down that mysterious energy of unknown origin.
And this time, I was confident.
Let’s do this.
A bolt of Scorching Yang Qi shot forward like a spear and plunged into the solid mass of qi. A combined total of more than two jiazi’s worth of qi collided and tore into each other.
Rumble.
As the clash erupted inside his dantian, Team Leader Choi’s body began to shake violently.
The hospital room had become an impregnable fortress, sealed against all visitors.
Butler Kim, Im Kkeokjeong, and Song Song watched the two young men with fascination.
“Hngh.”
“Hup.”
“Ugh.”
“Kk.”
Every time the veins bulged on Jin Taekyung’s forearm, Team Leader Choi’s body trembled.
Before long, his back arched, and a groan escaped through his clenched teeth.
“Haaagh!”
Song Song muttered as she watched.
“His back arched like a bow...”
Im Kkeokjeong, lying on the bed, asked, “What did you just say, Miss Song?”
“Nothing. I was just saying it was gross and fascinating.”
“Ah, you mean that black sweat?”
Song Song had a lot she wanted to say, but she held it in and nodded.
After all, the black sweat pouring from Team Leader Choi’s entire body was every bit as gross and fascinating.
“My God, what even is that...?”
As a Hunter, you saw all kinds of bizarre things. But this was the first time she had ever seen someone sweat black.
The pitch-black, sticky fluid wasn’t particularly abundant, but it gave off an unbelievable stench.
“Ugh, it reeks.”
“Damn, that smell is awful.”
As the two of them pinched their noses, Butler Kim spoke.
“That is waste accumulated inside his body being expelled through his sweat. It is one of the benefits of a Mana Cultivation Method.”
“Waste?”
“Kim hyung, is that really so impressive?”
“Of course. Even healing magic cannot remove waste from inside the body.”

Song Song thought for a moment, then replied, “It can. A truly top-tier healer could do it. But if what you’re saying is true... that’s incredible. Even healing potions retain trace amounts of Troll toxicity. You’re saying it can flush out that as well.”
“That is one of the remarkable aspects of a Mana Cultivation Method.”
“Who created this Mana Cultivation Method, exactly? And how?”
Song Song was an experienced Hunter, but she had never heard the term Mana Cultivation Method in her life. It was just as unfamiliar to Im Kkeokjeong, despite his twenty-year career.
“Exactly. I’ve been a Hunter all these years, and this is the first I’ve heard of anything like this. Martial arts, sorcery, whatever it is.”
“During the Great Cataclysm, the Elder created the first Mana Cultivation Method. It is treated as a closely guarded secret, so it is only natural that neither of you would know of it.”
“When you say the Elder...”
“You are thinking of the right person.”
Cheon Taemin. The hero who had saved all of humanity and the greatest Hunter in the world.
Butler Kim continued slowly.
“A Mana Cultivation Method is a powerful weapon in its own right. Many incidents occurred because of it, and most have vanished from history. It truly was an age of cataclysmic upheaval.”
What had happened? Why had Cheon Taemin’s Mana Cultivation Method fallen into the hands of an ambitious man like Lee Jungryong instead of his sole blood descendant?
Song Song and Im Kkeokjeong had many more questions, but they fell silent.
It wasn’t merely because Butler Kim’s expression had become unbearably bitter. The moment he finished speaking, an ominous change came over the two men.
“Nggh!”
“Hup!”
Jin Taekyung and Team Leader Choi groaned at the same time.
Thick veins bulged across their exposed skin, and deep furrows formed between their brows.
Team Leader Choi’s reaction grew increasingly violent. His entire body trembled as though caught in an earthquake.
“Team Leader Choi!”
“Is something seriously wrong?”
Song Song and Im Kkeokjeong instinctively stepped forward, but Butler Kim held out an arm to stop them.
“No. There can be no physical contact while practicing a Mana Cultivation Method.”
“Hunter Jin Taekyung is not someone who would put the Young Master in danger.”
Butler Kim looked at the two of them, concern and trust mingling in his eyes.
The trembling intensified, along with the groans of pain.
Before long, his faith was vindicated.
“Haaah...”
At some point, Team Leader Choi’s lips parted, releasing a calm breath.
It signaled the completion of his first complete circulation. It also meant that he had become a martial artist who had learned the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique.
“Young Master?”
At Butler Kim’s call, Team Leader Choi’s eyes slowly opened. Astonishment and joy filled them.
“This is...”
Team Leader Choi—Choi Minwoo—clenched his fists tightly.
The massive energy surging from his dantian raced freely through his body.
Normally, his mana would have remained scattered throughout him. Now he could move it at will.
Not only that, but the amount of mana he possessed had nearly doubled.
So this is a Mana Cultivation Method.
As Choi Minwoo calmly examined his condition, he reconsidered.
No. It isn’t the power of a Mana Cultivation Method. It’s the power of the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique.
And it had only been possible because of one person’s ability.
“Mr. Jin.”
Choi Minwoo slowly turned around. Jin Taekyung still had his eyes closed and was breathing deeply.
The air around him trembled. An active volcano stood there, ready to erupt at any moment.
He’s strong. Unbelievably strong.
Was he always this powerful?
Now that he could properly control his mana, Choi Minwoo could glimpse a fraction of the power Jin Taekyung possessed.
Every breath Jin Taekyung exhaled released waves of fiery qi that heated the hospital room.
It was November. The first snow had fallen only a week ago, yet everyone felt parched, and heat haze shimmered above the floor.
Just then, Choi Minwoo’s eyes slowly widened.
What... is that?
An illusion created by the heat haze? Or something real?
He couldn’t tell. Before he knew it, everyone in the hospital room was staring openmouthed at the sight before them.
Whoosh.
Jin Taekyung’s cross-legged body was rising into the air.
Little by little. Slowly, without stopping.
Above his head, blazing blue flames formed the shape of flower petals.
One flower. Then two.
And just as the third and final flower was about to take shape, Jin Taekyung’s eyes flew open.
Whoosh! Thud!
Like a bird struck by an arrow, Jin Taekyung plummeted and slammed his butt onto the floor. A piercing scream tore from his throat.
“Fuck! My tailbone!”
The air in the hospital room froze solid.
I screamed at the top of my lungs.
“Aaaargh!”
It hurt. My tailbone hurt from slamming into the floor, but my heart hurt ten times more from losing the perfect opportunity.
“It was almost done! I almost had it!”
Damn it. With only one step left to go, the Supreme Peak realm had slipped out of reach.
I didn’t know whether my understanding of martial arts was too shallow or there was some other reason.
Maybe it was both. But what mattered was that I had no idea when another opportunity like this would come.
“Damn iiiit!”
I could have achieved Three Flowers Gather at the Crown in one stroke and become a Supreme Peak master!
As I pounded the floor and wailed, System notifications pierced my ears.
Ding. Ding. Ding.

System Trance has been dispelled! Internal Energy has risen to 100 years! - You have achieved a great feat! You have acquired the Title I’m a Master! - The Sudden Quest, I’ll Take Only Half the Internal Energy I Digest., has been successfully completed! - The Repeat Quest, Back, Back—Let’s See Your Back!, has been successfully completed! - The realm of Fire Gate Divine Technique has risen to Seven Stars! - You have acquired a massive amount of EXP! Level Up! ... ... ...
“Just leave me alone!”

Everything had been perfect. While melting the energy that had been solidified in Team Leader Choi’s dantian, I had absorbed half of it. My mind had gone blank, and I had momentarily slipped into a trance.
But...
“Why! Why can’t I be happy!”
Gaining half a jiazi’s worth of internal energy? Great!
Acquiring a Title, completing Quests, raising the realm of the Fire Gate Divine Technique by one stage, and even leveling up—all of it was great. It was all good, so why!
“Why didn’t I reach the Supreme Peak realm!”
As I howled toward the ceiling, whispers reached my ears.
“Has something happened to Mr. Jin?”
“I’m not certain, but I have heard that some people end up crippled while practicing a Mana Cultivation Method...”
“More importantly, did everyone see those flower petals just now? Was I the only one? Why isn’t anyone saying anything?”
“Song-i, you saw them too? I thought I’d been dropped into the Goyang flower expo.”
The concern and astonishment in their voices snapped me back to my senses.
That was right. It wasn’t over yet. If those three had even half as much energy as Team Leader Choi, I might still have a chance to advance to the Supreme Peak realm.
I still have three test subjects.
With the resolve of Admiral Yi Sun-sin before the Battle of Myeongnyang, I spoke.
“Everyone, pay attention.”
“Take off your tops immediately. That’s an order.”
Ding.
System The Repeat Quest, Back, Back—Let’s See Your Back!, has been generated!
“Back, back—let’s see your back!”
The others edged away, their faces pale with fear.
