Butler Kim, Im Kkeokjeong, and Song Song watched the two young men with fascination.
“Hngh.”
“Hup.”
“Ugh.”
“Kk.”
Every time the veins bulged on Jin Taekyung’s forearm, Team Leader Choi’s body trembled.
Before long, his back arched, and a groan escaped through his clenched teeth.
“Haaagh!”
Song Song muttered as she watched.
“His back arched like a bow...”
Im Kkeokjeong, lying on the bed, asked, “What did you just say, Miss Song?”
“Nothing.
I was just saying it was gross and fascinating.”
“Ah, you mean that black sweat?”
Song Song had a lot she wanted to say, but she held it in and nodded.
After all, the black sweat pouring from Team Leader Choi’s entire body was every bit as gross and fascinating.
“My God, what even is that...?”
As a Hunter, you saw all kinds of bizarre things.
But this was the first time she had ever seen someone sweat black.
The pitch-black, sticky fluid wasn’t particularly abundant, but it gave off an unbelievable stench.
“Ugh, it reeks.”
“Damn, that smell is awful.”
As the two of them pinched their noses, Butler Kim spoke.
“That is waste accumulated inside his body being expelled through his sweat.
It is one of the benefits of a Mana Cultivation Method.”
“Waste?”
“Kim hyung, is that really so impressive?”
“Of course.
Even healing magic cannot remove waste from inside the body.”
Song Song thought for a moment, then replied, “It can.
A truly top-tier healer could do it.
But if what you’re saying is true... that’s incredible.
Even healing potions retain trace amounts of Troll toxicity.
You’re saying it can flush out that as well.”
“That is one of the remarkable aspects of a Mana Cultivation Method.”
“Who created this Mana Cultivation Method, exactly?
And how?”
Song Song was an experienced Hunter, but she had never heard the term Mana Cultivation Method in her life.
It was just as unfamiliar to Im Kkeokjeong, despite his twenty-year career.
“Exactly.
I’ve been a Hunter all these years, and this is the first I’ve heard of anything like this.
Martial arts, sorcery, whatever it is.”
“During the Great Cataclysm, the Elder created the first Mana Cultivation Method.
It is treated as a closely guarded secret, so it is only natural that neither of you would know of it.”
“When you say the Elder...”
“You are thinking of the right person.”
Cheon Taemin.
The hero who had saved all of humanity and the greatest Hunter in the world.
Butler Kim continued slowly.
“A Mana Cultivation Method is a powerful weapon in its own right.
Many incidents occurred because of it, and most have vanished from history.
It truly was an age of cataclysmic upheaval.”
What had happened?
Why had Cheon Taemin’s Mana Cultivation Method fallen into the hands of an ambitious man like Lee Jungryong instead of his sole blood descendant?
Song Song and Im Kkeokjeong had many more questions, but they fell silent.
It wasn’t merely because Butler Kim’s expression had become unbearably bitter.
The moment he finished speaking, an ominous change came over the two men.
“Nggh!”
“Hup!”
Jin Taekyung and Team Leader Choi groaned at the same time.
Thick veins bulged across their exposed skin, and deep furrows formed between their brows.
Team Leader Choi’s reaction grew increasingly violent.
His entire body trembled as though caught in an earthquake.
“Team Leader Choi!”
“Is something seriously wrong?”
Song Song and Im Kkeokjeong instinctively stepped forward, but Butler Kim held out an arm to stop them.
“No.
There can be no physical contact while practicing a Mana Cultivation Method.”
“Hunter Jin Taekyung is not someone who would put the Young Master in danger.”
Butler Kim looked at the two of them, concern and trust mingling in his eyes.
The trembling intensified, along with the groans of pain.
Before long, his faith was vindicated.
“Haaah...”
At some point, Team Leader Choi’s lips parted, releasing a calm breath.
It signaled the completion of his first complete circulation.
It also meant that he had become a martial artist who had learned the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique.
“Young Master?”
At Butler Kim’s call, Team Leader Choi’s eyes slowly opened.
Astonishment and joy filled them.
“This is...”
Team Leader Choi—Choi Minwoo—clenched his fists tightly.
The massive energy surging from his dantian raced freely through his body.
Normally, his mana would have remained scattered throughout him.
Now he could move it at will.
Not only that, but the amount of mana he possessed had nearly doubled.
So this is a Mana Cultivation Method.
As Choi Minwoo calmly examined his condition, he reconsidered.
No.
It isn’t the power of a Mana Cultivation Method.
It’s the power of the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique.
And it had only been possible because of one person’s ability.
“Mr.
Jin.”
Choi Minwoo slowly turned around.
Jin Taekyung still had his eyes closed and was breathing deeply.
The air around him trembled.
An active volcano stood there, ready to erupt at any moment.
He’s strong.
Unbelievably strong.
Was he always this powerful?
Now that he could properly control his mana, Choi Minwoo could glimpse a fraction of the power Jin Taekyung possessed.
Every breath Jin Taekyung exhaled released waves of fiery qi that heated the hospital room.
It was November.
The first snow had fallen only a week ago, yet everyone felt parched, and heat haze shimmered above the floor.
Just then, Choi Minwoo’s eyes slowly widened.
What... is that?
An illusion created by the heat haze?
Or something real?
He couldn’t tell.
Before he knew it, everyone in the hospital room was staring openmouthed at the sight before them.
Whoosh.
Jin Taekyung’s cross-legged body was rising into the air.
Little by little.
Slowly, without stopping.
Above his head, blazing blue flames formed the shape of flower petals.
One flower.
Then two.
And just as the third and final flower was about to take shape, Jin Taekyung’s eyes flew open.
Whoosh!
Thud!
Like a bird struck by an arrow, Jin Taekyung plummeted and slammed his butt onto the floor.
A piercing scream tore from his throat.
“Fuck!
My tailbone!”
The air in the hospital room froze solid.
I screamed at the top of my lungs.
“Aaaargh!”
It hurt.
My tailbone hurt from slamming into the floor, but my heart hurt ten times more from losing the perfect opportunity.
“It was almost done!
I almost had it!”
Damn it.
With only one step left to go, the Supreme Peak realm had slipped out of reach.
I didn’t know whether my understanding of martial arts was too shallow or there was some other reason.
Maybe it was both.
But what mattered was that I had no idea when another opportunity like this would come.
“Damn iiiit!”
I could have achieved Three Flowers Gather at the Crown in one stroke and become a Supreme Peak master!
As I pounded the floor and wailed, System notifications pierced my ears.
Ding.
Ding.
Ding.
System Trance has been dispelled!
Internal Energy has risen to 100 years! - You have achieved a great feat!

You have acquired the Title I’m a Master! - The Sudden Quest, I’ll Take Only Half the Internal Energy I Digest., has been successfully completed! - The Repeat Quest, Back, Back—Let’s See Your Back!, has been successfully completed! - The realm of Fire Gate Divine Technique has risen to Seven Stars! - You have acquired a massive amount of EXP!
Level Up! ... ... ...
“Just leave me alone!”
Everything had been perfect.
While melting the energy that had been solidified in Team Leader Choi’s dantian, I had absorbed half of it.
My mind had gone blank, and I had momentarily slipped into a trance.
But...
“Why!
Why can’t I be happy!”
Gaining half a jiazi’s worth of internal energy?
Great!
Acquiring a Title, completing Quests, raising the realm of the Fire Gate Divine Technique by one stage, and even leveling up—all of it was great.
It was all good, so why!
“Why didn’t I reach the Supreme Peak realm!”
As I howled toward the ceiling, whispers reached my ears.
“Has something happened to Mr.
Jin?”
“I’m not certain, but I have heard that some people end up crippled while practicing a Mana Cultivation Method...”
“More importantly, did everyone see those flower petals just now?
Was I the only one?
Why isn’t anyone saying anything?”
“Song-i, you saw them too?
I thought I’d been dropped into the Goyang flower expo.”
The concern and astonishment in their voices snapped me back to my senses.
That was right.
It wasn’t over yet.
If those three had even half as much energy as Team Leader Choi, I might still have a chance to advance to the Supreme Peak realm.
I still have three test subjects.
With the resolve of Admiral Yi Sun-sin before the Battle of Myeongnyang, I spoke.
“Everyone, pay attention.”
“Take off your tops immediately.
That’s an order.”
Ding.
System The Repeat Quest, Back, Back—Let’s See Your Back!, has been generated!
“Back, back—let’s see your back!”
The others edged away, their faces pale with fear.

paragraphs: Sss. Hooo.
Only the soft sound of breathing drifted through the hospital room. Standing guard at the door, I watched the others focus on circulating their qi and regulating their breathing.
Their cross-legged postures had been awkward at first, but they were gradually getting the hang of it.
Not bad.
Team Leader Choi, Butler Kim, Song Song, and finally Im Kkeokjeong.
Before sunset, all four had succeeded in completing a complete circulation. Before long, they were able to perform the Small Circulation on their own.
Not bad for a first step. No, this is better than I expected.
None of the others possessed energy as vast as Team Leader Choi’s, but Butler Kim and Song Song were mages. They were already adept at handling mana and adapted quickly.
The biggest surprise, however, was someone else.
Im Kkeokjeong.
I thought he’d struggle for a while...
I’d forgotten. Im Kkeokjeong was the only Second Awakener among everyone I knew. Had it come from grueling effort? Or a stroke of heavenly luck?
Whatever the reason, Im Kkeokjeong had already once broken past the limits given to him.
Maybe there was a reason he underwent a Second Awakening.
Judging by what he had shown me, Im Kkeokjeong might have the greatest potential for growth.
He was still a D-rank Hunter. He had plenty of steps left to climb.
I won’t have to worry about the aftereffects of his injuries, either.
Repeatedly circulating his qi would naturally improve his Muscles and Bones and Sinews and Meridians.
If Im Kkeokjeong could overcome the psychological issues, such as his trauma, he would be able to return to the Guild before long.
And then...
The Guild will have changed quite a bit by then, too.
The changes had already begun. Lee Jungryong had drawn the knife hidden up his sleeve and turned it against us. Now he owed us compensation for it.
With that compensation as its foundation, the Peace Guild would achieve astonishing growth. These people needed to stand at the forefront.
Someone had to run the Guild. Someone else had to identify talented, trustworthy people and turn them into loyal members of the Peace Guild.
And those people would be given martial arts.
We need blades of our own.
The moment that thought crossed my mind, Team Leader Choi finished his Small Circulation and opened his eyes with an exhale. A sharp gleam flashed through them.
Starting with him, the others opened their eyes one after another.
Ding.
System Thanks to your excellent instruction, several people have reached One Star in the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique. - The Title Trainee has changed to Training Instructor!
A martial arts drill instructor, huh.
Was this heaven telling me to work them to death for a while?
I grinned at the people still savoring the afterglow of circulating their qi.
A week passed in the blink of an eye.

During that time, Lee Jungryong and the Peace Guild secretly concluded their negotiations, two more mutated Gate incidents occurred, and a post on a Hunter community site drew a great deal of attention.
How I Got Hired by the Peace Guild
I’m a C-rank Hunter who used to work on the Security Team of a certain Guild.

I was originally with a major Guild, but my senior coworker was such a pain in the ass (he’s a traitor to the country) that the stress got too bad. I quit a few days ago and was browsing job sites when I saw that the Peace Guild had opened its general recruitment. So I applied on a whim, you know?
Then I didn’t hear anything back, so I figured I’d been rejected.
I already knew their selection process was brutal, so I wasn’t expecting anything in the first place.
But they contacted me after two weeks and told me to report to work tomorrow!
Anyone else starting with me tomorrow, raise your hand!

Under normal circumstances, the post would have been dismissed as the ramblings of an attention seeker.
However, the post proudly took first place in the weekly rankings, accompanied by countless recommendations and comments from people making a pilgrimage to the site.
All because of another post uploaded the following evening.
Guys, that web-novel villain from yesterday was for real;
I’m one of the people who got accepted by the Peace Guild this time. Today, I was touring the Guild house with the other new hires when I saw Lord Fuck, you know?

I was just watching him from a distance, terrified by the majesty of him dragging around slippers with the soles torn off, when he suddenly made a U-turn, grabbed one of us, and asked if he was from the \ Guild Security Team.
The dopey-looking guy said yes, and Lord Fuck started laughing like a maniac, yelled, “Irasshaimase!” and all that shit, then left.
I knew Lord Fuck had a weird personality, but he seems to be an even bigger lunatic than I imagined.
(Photo attached.)
I’m posting all the proof before I go so nobody says I’m lying.

I asked a Senior who joined earlier than me, and he told me to sleep as much as I could on the way there. └ Why? └ Maybe the company dinner is going to last a long time. Who likes drinking with people they aren’t even close to? └ (OP): Maybe? Oh, I think we’re here. └ Don’t drink too much. And don’t forget to come back with the rest of the story. └ Have fun! └ (OP): It looks like a good restaurant. I’m looking forward to seeing what we’re having for dinner, haha. I’ll be back soon.
That was the OP’s final comment.
“We’ll be having dinner inside a Gate.”
Murmurs rose from all around at my declaration.
“Excuse me?”
“Huh?”
“Sorry, but did I hear you correctly?”
“I think you said we’re having dinner at a Gate. I must have misheard.”
“Ah, right.”
I didn’t even need to look at their faces. The ones having that innocent conversation were the new hires on their first day.
The people who had joined only two or three weeks earlier, however, reacted differently.
“I knew this would happen.”
“Ah, fuck...”
“Good thing I brought potions.”
“Hyung, do you have any arrows to spare?”
“Yeah. I brought an extra two hundred for emergencies, just in case.”
“Then could I get a hundred?”
They hadn’t joined even a month apart, but their reactions were worlds apart.
The veterans swore under their breath like they were sighing, then swiftly pulled armor and equipment from their backpacks.
Clack! Clack! Clack!
Was this how a teacher felt?
A satisfied smile spread across my face at the results of repeated training.
I turned toward the greenhorns who still had no idea what was happening and asked,
“You all brought everything with you, right?”
The new hires nodded.
“Uh, yes. You told us to bring it all, so...”
“Put your bags down, take out your equipment, and put it on.”
“Excuse me? Is this some kind of mock battle?”
“Mock battle, my ass. You don’t improve much doing that. Real combat is best.”
Suspicion crept into their innocent eyes.
“Then, perhaps...”
“Are we really going into a Gate?”
“Yes. A raid to celebrate joining the Peace Guild! What do you think? Sounds great, right?”
“The new people don’t seem too excited. What does everyone else think?”
The people I’d worked to the bone for the past few weeks gritted their teeth and shouted.
“That’s a wonderful idea!”
“As expected of King Taekyung.”
“Wow. This. Is. Great!”
Hmm. Just as I thought.
This was also the effect of learning. They clearly remembered what had happened to the few brave souls who had openly contradicted my opinions.
The logic of we can’t be the only ones who suffer had probably played a part as well.
Exactly. Everyone should suffer together.
If the new hires were Pomeranians, the others were already Tosa mastiffs.
With the atmosphere blazing with the determination to die together, the new hires hesitated before shouting,
“B-But nobody told us about this! The notice said we’d only be doing a simple workshop for the first week after joining the Guild...”
“Yes. This is the workshop.”
“What Guild holds a workshop inside a Gate? For an entire week!”
“The Peace Guild.”
“That’s ridiculous!”
“Does everyone else think so, too?”
I turned my head slightly. The Senior Tosa mastiffs who had tasted hell for several weeks bared their teeth and shouted.
“Why wouldn’t it make sense? It does! Absolutely!”
“Obviously this is a workshop!”
“Who rents a vacation house for a workshop these days? You’re supposed to bond by killing monsters together inside a Gate!”
“We can’t be the only ones getting fucked!”
That last shout was so blatant it bordered on desperate. Hearing it forced me to reflect deeply.
I guess I need to work them even harder.
They couldn’t be allowed to think of this as suffering. I planned to condition—or rather, train—them until they accepted all of it as perfectly natural.
“All right, everyone quiet!”
Ding.
System The effect of the Title Training Instructor activates! - The trainees who heard your shout become tense!
“Form ranks!”
“Form raaanks!”
“Too quiet! Form ranks!”
“Form raaanks!”
Even after repeating the command back in unison, they all looked dazed.
I smiled at their bitter expressions.
“Now, follow me inside in order. Left foot. Left foot.”
Clack! Clack! Clack!
The human train set off toward the Gate.

That was the OP’s final comment.
“We’ll be having dinner inside a Gate.”
Murmurs rose from all around at my declaration.
“Excuse me?”
“Huh?”
“Sorry, but did I hear you correctly?”
“I think you said we’re having dinner at a Gate.
I must have misheard.”
“Ah, right.”
I didn’t even need to look at their faces.
The ones having that innocent conversation were the new hires on their first day.
The people who had joined only two or three weeks earlier, however, reacted differently.
“I knew this would happen.”
“Ah, fuck...”
“Good thing I brought potions.”
“Hyung, do you have any arrows to spare?”
“Yeah.
I brought an extra two hundred for emergencies, just in case.”
“Then could I get a hundred?”
They hadn’t joined even a month apart, but their reactions were worlds apart.
The veterans swore under their breath like they were sighing, then swiftly pulled armor and equipment from their backpacks.
Clack!
Clack!
Clack!
Was this how a teacher felt?
A satisfied smile spread across my face at the results of repeated training.
I turned toward the greenhorns who still had no idea what was happening and asked,
“You all brought everything with you, right?”
The new hires nodded.
“Uh, yes.
You told us to bring it all, so...”
“Put your bags down, take out your equipment, and put it on.”
“Excuse me?
Is this some kind of mock battle?”
“Mock battle, my ass.
You don’t improve much doing that.
Real combat is best.”
Suspicion crept into their innocent eyes.
“Then, perhaps...”
“Are we really going into a Gate?”
“Yes.
A raid to celebrate joining the Peace Guild!
What do you think?
Sounds great, right?”
“The new people don’t seem too excited.
What does everyone else think?”
The people I’d worked to the bone for the past few weeks gritted their teeth and shouted.
“That’s a wonderful idea!”
“As expected of King Taekyung.”
“Wow.
This.
Is.
Great!”
Hmm.
Just as I thought.
This was also the effect of learning.
They clearly remembered what had happened to the few brave souls who had openly contradicted my opinions.
The logic of we can’t be the only ones who suffer had probably played a part as well.
Exactly.
Everyone should suffer together.
If the new hires were Pomeranians, the others were already Tosa mastiffs.
With the atmosphere blazing with the determination to die together, the new hires hesitated before shouting,
“B-But nobody told us about this!
The notice said we’d only be doing a simple workshop for the first week after joining the Guild...”
“Yes.
This is the workshop.”
“What Guild holds a workshop inside a Gate?
For an entire week!”
“The Peace Guild.”
“That’s ridiculous!”
“Does everyone else think so, too?”
I turned my head slightly.
The Senior Tosa mastiffs who had tasted hell for several weeks bared their teeth and shouted.
“Why wouldn’t it make sense?
It does!
Absolutely!”
“Obviously this is a workshop!”
“Who rents a vacation house for a workshop these days?
You’re supposed to bond by killing monsters together inside a Gate!”
“We can’t be the only ones getting fucked!”
That last shout was so blatant it bordered on desperate.
Hearing it forced me to reflect deeply.
I guess I need to work them even harder.
They couldn’t be allowed to think of this as suffering.
I planned to condition—or rather, train—them until they accepted all of it as perfectly natural.
“All right, everyone quiet!”
Ding.
System The effect of the Title Training Instructor activates! - The trainees who heard your shout become tense!
“Form ranks!”
“Form raaanks!”
“Too quiet!
Form ranks!”
“Form raaanks!”
Even after repeating the command back in unison, they all looked dazed.
I smiled at their bitter expressions.
“Now, follow me inside in order.
Left foot.
Left foot.”
Clack!
Clack!
Clack!
The human train set off toward the Gate.

chapters.title: Chapter 294
paragraphs: A week ago, after several days of relentless negotiations with Lee Jungryong’s side, Team Leader Choi got everything he wanted.
Exclusive rights to more than twenty Gates, real estate, and an enormous amount of cash. I didn’t know the exact figure, but the total value was clearly astronomical.
They were valuable spoils we could never have obtained if the ten Black Hunters and the close aides dispatched by Myeongdong Guild Master Park Tae Seop hadn’t fallen into our hands.
The same went for this place.
Calling out the cadence, I led the way through the mana field.
Ssshhhk.
That sticky, unpleasant, yet familiar sensation unique to mana washed over me, and everything around me changed.
Ding.
System You have entered the A-rank Gate, Black Wizard’s Black Forest! Quest Gate Raid has been automatically generated!
“Left foot, left foot! One, two, three, four! Halt!”
“One, two! Fall in!”
By the time the human train came to a stop amid crisp call-and-response, more than fifty people had entered the Gate.
Darkness blanketed the forest, and faint moonlight filtered through the gaunt branches.
The new hires, who had realized what was happening too late, looked around in panic.
“Gasp!”
“W-We’re screwed.”
“Wait. What rank is this Gate? Why is it so huge?”
The third-week Tosa mastiffs, on the other hand, were completely unfazed.
“Black Wizard’s Black Forest again?”
“Ugh, I’m going to puke.”
“Good thing I brought my war hammer.”
They had joined less than a month apart, but the difference between them was enormous.
The day-one pups listening to the Tosa mastiffs turned deathly pale.
“B-Black Wizard’s Black Forest?”
“It’s an A-rank Gate!”
An A-rank Gate: Black Wizard’s Black Forest.
Even people who knew nothing about the place could get a rough idea from the name alone. The eerie atmosphere, the forest so unsettling that the mere sight of it sent chills down your spine.
This was a realm ruled by a black wizard—a necromancer.
“Lord Fuck! Senior Jin Taekyung!”
One of the pups rushed over and pleaded with me.
“Please, can’t you let me out?”
“Why?”
“I’m really scared of ghosts. Regular monsters are fine, but ghouls and skeletons... I don’t think I can handle them.”
“Trauma?”
“Nothing that serious. I’m just scared.”
“Perfect. This is a great chance to experience them in 4D. They’re monsters, anyway.”
“No, that’s not...”
“And I’m pretty sure you wrote on your Guild application that you didn’t have any problems like that.”
“I only wrote that so I’d get accepted in the first place... Please. I can’t even watch horror movies with my girlfriend.”
“Oh, you have a girlfriend. I see. Over here!”
I crooked a finger.
From among the grinning Tosa mastiffs, one man shot forward like a bullet.
“You called?”
“Yeah.”
It was Kim Jinsoo, who had quietly taken on the role of leader among the Tosa mastiffs.
He had good leadership skills and excellent combat ability, so whenever we went on a raid together, he served as my right hand.
Of course, I’d long since stopped speaking formally to him.
“I have a special assignment for you. It concerns this gentleman here.”
“Yes.”
“Put him in front.”
The pup had just begun to sigh in relief when he sucked in a sharp breath.
“D-Did you say in front?”
“Why? Is there a problem? Judging by that tower shield, you’re clearly a tank.”
“If you want to sit this out, go ahead. Just be prepared to get fired.”
“F-Fired?”
“If you refuse to join a raid because you’re afraid of ghosts, why would I keep employing you? Besides, are there any ghosts inside a Gate? They’re all monsters. Jinsoo, am I wrong?”
Kim Jinsoo answered without hesitation.
“You are absolutely right—a hundred, a thousand times over.”
“If everything here were a ghost, why would I bring Hunters? I’d bring exorcists instead. Right?”
“Absolutely right—a thousand, ten thousand times over.”
“That’s our Jinsoo. You certainly have a way with words.”
“Thank you.”
“So, would you like to remain a Hunter with the Peace Guild, or would you rather get fired and change careers to become an exorcist?”
The pup replied, his face rigid.
“I-I’ll be a Hunter.”
“Then if you run away during combat, I’ll send you to heaven with my own hands. Okay?”
“O-Okay.”
“Okay. Front! Okay! Heaven!”
I waved my hand, and Kim Jinsoo grabbed the man by the arm and dragged him away.
We’d put them through a fairly rigorous selection process, but there was always one guy like that wherever you went.
What? He’s so scared of ghosts that he can’t even watch a horror movie with his girlfriend?
Damn it. What a load of bullshit.
I wasn’t angry about the girlfriend part. Really.
Whooosh.
The eerie wind circling through the forest made the empty space at my side feel cold. I shuddered once, then stepped toward the trees.
The conversation behind me gradually faded into the distance.
“E-Excuse me, mister.”
The frightened voice of one of the pups mixed with the Tosa mastiff’s blunt reply.
“What?”
“Where is Hunter Jin Taekyung going?”
“He’s going to round up the prey.”
“What?”
“That guy’s nickname is the Pied Piper.”
The Tosa mastiff added cheerfully,
“I can’t be the only one going through hell. Let’s do our best together.”
I roamed the forest, making enough noise to ensure everything nearby could hear me, and it didn’t take long to get a response.
Crack! Rumble!
—Guaaaar!
—Ngh... nghhh...
Click, clack, clatter-clatter-clatter!
Grotesque cries rang out as the corpses sleeping beneath the earth and inside their graves awakened.
Ghouls with rotting flesh dripping from their bodies. Skeletons with not a scrap of flesh left on their gaunt white bones.
In an instant, the cursed dead known as Undead Monsters covered the forest and hills.
“Hey, hey! I’m going slowly, so make sure you keep up! Got it?”
—Guaaaaaar!
Rat-tat-tat-tat!
The old image of zombies shambling around with limp bodies was hopelessly outdated.
More than once, seeing these bastards sprint had made me wonder if they had trained at Taereung Athletes’ Village.
Of course, they still weren’t fast enough to catch me.
We’ve got new hires today, so I should bring back a smaller group.
I raced through the forest, glancing over my shoulder every so often to check their numbers.
There were roughly a hundred and fifty of them.
That was three times the number of people on our side, but even this was fewer than usual.
For one thing, ghouls and skeletons weren’t particularly powerful monsters. For another, our side had prepared thoroughly and developed plenty of nerve.
There’s a reason I call them Tosa mastiffs.

Three times their number was standard, and sometimes I’d brought back more than ten times as many monsters. After I’d shown them the threshold of hell a few times, a fierce glint had begun to burn in their eyes.

Of course, whenever things seemed genuinely dangerous, I stepped in from time to time even if I had been watching from the sidelines. Thanks to that, we had suffered injuries, but there had been no deaths.
After we repeated the process several times a day, I became both their common enemy and someone they trusted.
I don’t want to go this far, but... I don’t have a choice.
This was an intensive crash course. I needed to plant weeds capable of surviving harsh conditions in the Peace Guild’s yard as quickly as possible.
In less than a month, several people had already given up and transferred to other teams. I hadn’t tried to stop them, nor did I resent them for leaving.
The decision is theirs to make.
Everyone had a life of their own. I had only stepped into theirs for a little while.
I could present them with choices, but I had no right to force them to choose.
Ssshhhoooom!
As befitted an A-rank Gate, Black Wizard’s Black Forest was vast.
But the area I had explored was only a tiny fraction of it. Keeping my pace under control, I soon saw the Gate entrance ahead.
“Here they come!”
“Jin Taekyung, you son of a bitch...”
“Still, maybe because it’s their first time, he didn’t bring that many.”
“Gasp! Skeletons!”
Some loudly announced the monsters’ arrival, while others cursed me or calmly assessed the enemy’s numbers.
The greenhorns had no real combat experience yet, and I could see them shrinking back in fear.
Of course, the human Tosa mastiffs who had already experienced my brutal training weren’t about to stand idle.
“What the fuck are you doing over there? The line’s giving way!”
“Don’t back up. Hold your shield tight. What? You need to piss? Then piss yourself!”
“New people, get a grip. That Jin Taekyung bastard isn’t going to help you. He even started a charity foundation in advance because someone might die here!”
They were making me out to be complete trash.
It was absurd, but I held my tongue. Fine. That was what it took to snap the rookies out of their panic.
People badmouth even the king behind his back. What can you do?
Of course, I memorized every face.
As I approached the Hunters who had already formed their battle line, I sprang into the tallest tree and shouted,
“Shields together!”
Rumble!
Everyone moved in perfect unison.
Like dogs left staring up after the chicken they had been chasing, the undead monsters gazed toward the distant treetop before turning their grotesque faces away.
Then they spotted the more than fifty Hunters arrayed on the hill where the Gate entrance stood.
One of the skeletons raised its Bone Sword high and unleashed a hideous shriek.
—GRAAAAR!
It wasn’t an ordinary skeleton.
The bones that should have been exposed were wrapped in battered armor, and the Bone Sword raised as though to pierce the moon blazed with an ominous aura blacker than the night sky.
“A Skeleton Knight?”
Just because they were all skeletons didn’t mean they were all the same rank.
Skeleton Soldiers, Mages, Warriors...
Their abilities and strength varied wildly from one individual to the next, and Skeleton Knights were powerful monsters universally recognized as A-rank.
I’ve encountered them often in the Black Forest, but there’s something different about that one.
Encountering an A-rank monster like a Skeleton Knight inside an A-rank Gate was perfectly normal. They were stationed throughout the Black Forest, each commanding lower-level Warriors and Mages.
I narrowed my eyes and studied it.
Then—
—GRAAAH!
—GROOOAR!
Tss-tss-tss-tss!
Two more monstrous cries rang out, followed by two surging streams of aura.
I muttered in surprise,
“Three Skeleton Knights in one group?”
That was a first.
A skeleton horde was an army, and its knight was the general who led it. Every independent army had only one general.
Did three hordes form an alliance?
But my prediction was spectacularly wrong.
Rattling their bones, the two newly appeared knights approached the Skeleton Knight that had emerged first. They dropped to one knee and drove their Bone Swords into the ground.
It was an unmistakable act of submission.
Purple light flashed within the empty hollows where the first knight’s eyes should have been.
Fwoooosh!
The light bursting from that abyssal darkness was intense.
The moment our gazes met, it erupted into blazing flame.
—GRAAAAR!
Krrrck!
The creature roared, and its body began to change.
Every bone grew thicker and longer, its surface gleaming with a strange black sheen.
The transformation didn’t end there.
Shrrrraaaak!
Its armor, rusted and cracked in places, restored itself as though time were flowing backward. Broken chains reconnected, and the faded skull emblem on its chest regained its vivid color.
Finally, a dark green cloak fluttered in the wind.
Once the transformation was complete, the creature stared silently at its palm.
Instead of bare white bone, it saw a hand encased in a sturdy gauntlet.
And then—
“Not. Bad.”
The air surrounding the forest trembled.
Everyone, myself included, stared at it in speechless silence.
A Skeleton Knight. A great knight reduced to a corrupted undead.
But it was no longer a Skeleton Knight.
System Level 105 Skeleton Warlord
“Come. Down. Hu. Man.”
Its blazing purple eyes fixed directly on me.

chapters.title: Chapter 295
paragraphs: Gleaming armor. A dark green cloak fluttering like wings. Purple ghost fire burning in empty eye sockets.
And then... there was a voice.
“Come. Down. Hu. Man.”
The moment I heard that metallic, scraping voice, I nearly fell out of the tree.
It spoke?
This wasn’t the first time something like this had happened. The Wyvern I’d killed in the past, “One-Eyed Carus,” had been capable of speech too.
But a monster speaking wasn’t something to take lightly.
“A Named Monster...”
The words escaped me like a groan.
That was right. As far as anyone knew, only Named Monsters were capable of speech.
And that very Named Monster had just been born before my eyes.
No—not born.
It had evolved.
System Level 105 Skeleton Warlord
Evolution?
I had never heard of or seen a Named Monster appearing this way before.
What is this, Digimon?
Wait, are monsters that kind of monster? They can evolve too?
I was already about five hundred light-years removed from an ordinary life, and even I was bewildered. The other Guild members’ reactions went without saying.
“What is that?”
“Wait, didn’t it just say something?”
“I’ve never seen anything like that, not even in a monster encyclopedia...”
Of course they hadn’t.
Named Monsters were mutants. Every individual possessed different traits and varied in strength. No one could know what one would be like until it appeared.
But why now, of all times?
I licked my dry lips.
I didn’t know how powerful that Skeleton Warlord was, but it clearly possessed strength worthy of a Named Monster.
And on top of that, there are two A-rank Skeleton Knights.
The remaining hundred and fifty or so were all B-rank Skeleton Mages or Warriors. They were practically an army, which made them extremely troublesome.
Still, if I took on the Warlord and the two Knights—their commander and core fighting force—it was a battle we could win.
We’ve been raiding nonstop.
Only fifty Guild members had entered the Gate.
But more than half of them were Tosa mastiffs who had endured my whip and survived hellish special training.
They had fought so many Skeletons over the past week that they were sick of the sight of them. As long as they kept their heads, they could handle enemies two or three times their number.
And the new recruits are plenty capable too.
We paid salaries at least as high as the major Guilds, so we had selected only the best.
This time, I had personally taken part in multiple evaluations, including the interviews, and even scored their potential for growth.
To weather the typhoon that was Ares Guild, I had selected the finest saplings and transplanted them into the Peace Guild’s front yard.
We’ll have to accept some risk, but this is a fight worth taking on.
Team Leader Choi and the other three had suspended most of their Guild duties to focus entirely on training the Jin Family’s cultivation technique.
The battle would have been much easier with them here, but even if they had been present, I wouldn’t have sent them in.
A dagger hidden up one’s sleeve was deadly precisely because it remained hidden. I couldn’t reveal it with so many eyes watching.
Having reached a decision, I called out to one person.
“Jinsoo!”
“Yes, sir!”
Kim Jinsoo, who was effectively serving as deputy team leader, answered promptly. I pointed my dagger at the Skeleton Warlord.
The green ghost fire in its hollow eye sockets remained fixed on me.
“That’s a Named Monster.”
A sharp gasp rose from among the Guild members.

Most of them had been Hunters for less than two years. A person could spend twenty years in this field without ever encountering a Named Monster, and now they had to fight one. The tension was plain on their faces.
But Kim Jinsoo was different. His surprise lasted only a moment before he calmly nodded.
“I see.”
“Oh? You’re doing a pretty good job pretending to be calm.”
“I’m a little shaken myself, but we can’t just stand around in a daze and let it kill us.”
Well, look at him.
I’d known from the beginning that he had guts, but this was unusual courage for someone in his first year.
Perhaps sensing my gaze, Kim Jinsoo smiled faintly and added, “If the situation were hopeless, you would’ve given the signal to retreat long ago. Am I right?”
“Hmm.”
“...Uh, did I get that wrong?”
“No.”
I chuckled and shook my head.
“You’re right. This is a fight we can take on.”
“Oh.”
“I’ll handle those three over there. You take the rest. How long can you hold out?”
Kim Jinsoo thought for a moment before answering.
“The new recruits don’t have much experience... but we should still be able to hold out for an hour.”
“An hour?”
“Yes. At least an hour.”
The instant Kim Jinsoo answered confidently, the Skeleton Warlord slowly opened its jaws and released a strange, indescribable resonance.
“GRAAAAAH!”
Beep!
System Level 105 Skeleton Warlord has used a Special Skill! Special Skill Summon the Dead has activated! The sleeping dead answer their commander’s call!
It was a howl that sent a chill down my spine—and a cry that awakened the cursed dead.
Crack. Crack-crack-crack!
Soil burst upward, and the ground trembled. Piles of pale bones rose all around us, assembled themselves into skeletons, and joined the ranks.
Bone Swords caked with dirt. Wooden shields tangled with fine roots. Among the Skeleton Warriors, I could even see Mages wearing necklaces engraved with skulls.
There were even two more A-rank Skeleton Knights.
Adding the newcomers to the existing Skeleton army brought their numbers to well over three hundred.
I watched in silence for a moment before speaking.
“Jinsoo.”
“Yes.”
“Can you still do an hour?”
“Uh, well...”
“Be honest.”
“...I think we can manage about thirty minutes.”
“Really?”
“Yes. The situation has gotten a little worse, but we can probably do it.”
Kim Jinsoo continued, staring uneasily at the Skeleton Warlord.
“As long as that bastard doesn’t pull any more crap.”
“I think it will.”
“No way.”
“GRAAAAAH!”
“See? I was right.”
Kim Jinsoo groaned.
“Oh, come on.”
Beep!

System Level 105 Skeleton Warlord has used a Special Skill! Special Skill Commander’s Rally has activated! The Strength, Agility, and Magic of the monsters under the Skeleton Warlord’s command have been enhanced! The enemies’ momentum rises sharply!
The Skeleton Warlord howled!
The effect was incredible!
I activated Qi Sense and saw that every single one of them had gained five Levels.
The aura radiating from the Skeleton army of more than three hundred was on an entirely different level from before.
I glanced aside and found Kim Jinsoo staring blankly.
“Thirty minutes. Still possible?”
The bastard was cursing me with his eyes now.
To be fair, even I thought that was asking too much. Clicking my tongue, I gave my next order without hesitation.
“Fall back slowly. Don’t provoke them.”
“How far should we retreat?”
“To the path right in front of the Gate. Make sure we can get out at any time.”
“The path is narrow, so it should be easier to fight them there.”
“Exactly.”
As Kim Jinsoo had said, the path in front of the Gate was so narrow that five grown men could barely pass shoulder to shoulder.
Even Skeletons, whose frames were naturally thinner, could only fit seven or eight abreast.
However...
“Go straight out.”
There was no head-on battle in my revised plan.
“Huh?”
“Take the kids and get outside the Gate.”
Dismay spread across Kim Jinsoo’s face.
“Then what about you, Senior?”
“Do you think they’ll play tag while you leave? Someone has to buy time.”
“Senior! That’s dangerous!”
“Jinsoo. No—my dear Peace Guild members.”
I looked down solemnly. Fifty Guild members craned their necks like baby birds as they stared up at me.
“I—and the Peace Guild—always put the safety of our Guild members first.”
Several of the Tosa mastiffs muttered just loudly enough for me to hear.
“That’s the biggest load of bullshit I’ve heard all year.”
“I think I nearly died seven times this week.”
“More like ten for me.”
Meanwhile, the eyes of the day-one pups trembled.
“Senior!”
“Ahh, Lord Fuck!”
“You’d go this far for us...!”
I continued in a voice thick with emotion.
“I’ll risk any danger for your safety. Even if my arm gets blown off! Even if my leg gets blown off! I will send every one of you back into the arms of those who love you!”
Several of them cried out in a surge of emotion.
“We can fight!”
“Please let us fight alongside you!”
I bit my lip hard and shook my head.
“I can’t! Someone has to make the sacrifice, and in a situation like this, I’m the best one to step forward!”
“But still...!”
Whoooosh! Shrrrk!
Before anyone could continue, an ominous black aura came hurtling toward us.
The Skeleton Warlord sliced horizontally through a massive tree dozens of meters tall and several meters around, then shouted in a voice like metal scraping against metal.
“I. Will. Kill. Every. Last. One. Of. You!”
Swish. Tap!
I leaped lightly from the tree and shouted, “Everyone, return to the Gate! I’ll cover the rear!”
This time, no one tried to stop me.
The army of more than three hundred Skeletons had begun to advance.
Clatter. Thud. Clatter. Thud.
The monsters marched in perfect ranks and files, their momentum utterly menacing.
The Warlord’s Special Skill had filled their steps with power, and faint lights flickered within their hollow skulls.
“GRAAAAH!”
When one of the Skeleton Knights, serving as a deputy commander, let out a fierce cry, rusted arrows and attack magic rose from the rear and shot toward the Peace Guild members.
Fwish-fwish-fwish! Whoooosh!
“Block them!”
“Tanks! Keep your shields up! Continue falling back slowly!”
“Covering fire!”
The two forces were about three hundred paces apart. To retreat safely, we needed to widen the distance further.
I swung White Flame and blocked the army’s advance.
“You bastards! How dare you threaten our precious Peace Guild members!”
Sssshhhk! Crack!
The power behind my spear shattered bone, while Spear Energy erupted from its transparent spearhead and slashed in every direction.
The moment I took down ten of them in a single blow, three Skeleton Knights charged me at once.
“GRAAAAH!”
“GRAAAAH!”
Sssshhhk!
Three streams of black aura narrowly grazed different parts of my body.
Blood trickled from my nape where the pressure had sliced it open, and anguished cries erupted from the Guild members who had already reached the narrow path.
“Aah! Senior!”
“Look out!”
Clang-clang-clang!
I deflected the relentless barrage of aura and shouted as if struggling to speak.
“Go! I’ll catch up soon!”
“Jinsoo! Get going!”
After a moment’s hesitation, Kim Jinsoo began leading the Guild members toward the Gate.
“You have to come back!”
I gave him a faint smile and nodded.
“Yeah.”
“I’m sorry, Senior!”
“It’s fine. Go!”
“Urgh!”
Kim Jinsoo hesitated until the very end, then disappeared beyond the Gate.
Now only the hundreds of Skeletons packed tightly into the narrow path and I remained.
“F. O. O. L. I. S. H.”
Clatter-clatter-clatter!
The bones parted like the Red Sea, and the Skeleton Warlord emerged through the opening.
“H. A. V. E. Y. O. U. R. E. S. I. G. N. E. D. Y. O. U. R. S. E. L. F. T. O. D. I. E, H. U. M. A. N?”
But I wasn’t listening.
Only after sweeping my gaze over every inch of our surroundings did I finally sigh in relief.
“Phew. They’re finally all gone.”
“Those kids are way too sentimental for their own good. When the Team Leader tells you to leave, you’re supposed to run. What do they mean, help? Right?”
I wiped the blood from my nape. I’d tried to keep the cut shallow, but it was deeper than expected.
About 0.2 centimeters?
“Damn. What a waste of blood.”
The purple ghost fire in the Warlord’s eye sockets flickered uneasily.
“W. H. A. T. I. N. T. H. E. W. O. R. L. D. A. R. E. Y. O. U. P. L. O. T. T. I. N. G?”
“Nothing much.”
I smiled with satisfaction at the EXP—no, the Skeleton army—filling the narrow path without a single gap.
“You’re all going to die here. That’s all you need to know.”
“W. H. A. T?”
Instead of answering, I drew a deep breath.
The muscles throughout my body writhed, and the fire dragon coiled inside my dantian began to move according to the formula of the Fire Gate Divine Technique.
Then, in the next instant, I became one with the spear in my hand and shot forward.
“One Annihilation.”
KRAAAAAAASH!

chapters.title: Chapter 296
paragraphs: How much time had passed?
He could no longer remember his name, his family, his friends or lover... He could not even remember where he had been born or what kind of life he had lived.
After passing through a long, deep darkness, he suddenly came to his senses and found himself in a forest.
Where is this?
The question lasted only a moment.
Soon, the instincts of a monster seized him, and he began fighting without purpose. He fought the humans who had once been his own kind, and he fought monsters as well.

An outstanding knight in life, he grew ever stronger as he cultivated his mana. Eventually, he even surpassed the black wizard who ruled the vast Black Forest and controlled every dead thing sleeping within it.
“Y-you bastard! How dare a mere Skeleton Knight...!”
“GRAAAAAH!”
Crack!
Thus, the fallen knight became the new master of the Black Forest.
And at last, he rose to become a chosen being.
Commander of the Skeleton army.
Skeleton Warlord was his new name.
So this is what it feels like?

It was astonishing. Everything around him had changed. He did not know why, but the mana flowing through the Black Forest had grown denser, and immense power surged through his body despite it being nothing more than bones.
To him, newly reborn as something else, a mere handful of humans was utterly insignificant.
There aren’t many of them, and they’re all terrified.
To humans, death was simply another name for fear.
Now that he was already one of the dead, the humans’ terror was nothing but amusing.
Run. Then bring me more—more lives!
He was now the master of the Black Forest and commander of the dead.
The larger groups of humans they brought would soon become his soldiers. Once he commanded thousands, tens of thousands of the dead...
The Black Forest would no longer be enough for him.
Only then could he be reborn not as a mere commander of the dead, but as a true lord.
I will leave this place and conquer a wider territory.
That was when, as he watched the fifty or so humans flee in panic with satisfaction, one of them caught his eye.
That one...
A human surrounded by three Skeleton Knights, frantically exchanging blows with them.
Strangely enough, unlike the other humans who spoke in a bizarre language, he could understand every word that came from this one’s mouth.
“I’m fine! Hurry up and go!”
How was this possible? Such fluent command of the Demon Realm language.
Was he perhaps a monster in human form?
He knew nothing of the System applied to Jin Taekyung, much less the function of the Integrated Language Pack.
He simply wanted to turn that one—who seemed useful enough for a human—into one of the dead and take him as a subordinate.
“F. O. O. L. I. S. H. H. U. M. A. N.”
But he should have known.
The foolish one was himself.
“Phew. They’re finally all gone.”
He should never have led his entire army into this narrow path.
“You’re all going to fucking die here. That’s all you need to know.”
“W. H. A. T?”
He soon learned the answer to his question.
“One Annihilation.”
Whoooosh!
The moment a vortex wreathed in blue flame erupted into the air, fear crept over the Skeleton Warlord.
It was an emotion he had forgotten long ago—the fear of death, which had become more a friend than something to dread.
“E. V. E. R. Y. O. N. E. D. O. D. G. E—!”
The Warlord could not finish speaking.
Blue flames swept through the narrow path, engulfing him and hundreds of Skeletons.
KRAAAAAAASH!

System All internal energy and Stamina have been depleted! Status abnormality: Exhaustion has been applied! Defeated Level 92 Skeleton Knight! Gained a considerable amount of EXP! Defeated Level 75 Skeleton Warrior! Gained a small amount of EXP! Defeated Level 78 Skeleton Mage! Gained a small amount of EXP...!
Beep. Beep. Beep.
The System notifications drilled endlessly into my ears.
My vision spun, and my legs buckled.
I had never imagined the spear shaft in my hand could feel this heavy.
As the spearhead slowly sank toward the ground, I barely managed to drive it into the earth and use it to support myself.
Fuck, I’m dying.
One Annihilation was the only—and strongest—skill I possessed. It used internal energy and Stamina as fuel to unleash more explosive power than anything else.
Unlike the first time, my rising martial arts realm now allowed me to control how much force I put into it. But the aftermath was still devastating.
One Annihilation is as dangerous as it is destructive. I won’t survive long if I keep thinking in terms of all or nothing.
The best choice was to achieve the greatest result with the least amount of power.
As someone who always pursued efficient combat, I could not afford to use One Annihilation recklessly. A final move meant that if it failed, there would be no next move.
But this time was different.
If I don’t use it now, when will I get another chance?
A narrow path. Hundreds of monsters packed together without a single gap.
It was practically a stage built for One Annihilation.
I had exhausted my full strength and fallen into the Exhaustion status, but there was a contingency for every action.
Beep.
System Massacre! Gained a massive amount of EXP! Level Up! Gained Points! All status abnormalities have been recovered!
The notification I had been waiting for sounded, and a refreshing sensation swept through my entire body.
Whoooosh.
The dantian that had been emptied by the aftermath of One Annihilation filled once more, and strength returned to my trembling limbs.
Only then did my whitened vision clear, allowing me to see the results of One Annihilation.
I had expected something like this, but the reality was beyond anything I had imagined.
I marveled at the sight spread out before me.
Crackle. Crackle-crackle.
The force of One Annihilation had widened the narrow path to twice its original width.
The enormous trees and rocks that had surrounded it had been uprooted, and piles of bones engulfed in flames slowly burned across the blackened ground.
How many did I send straight to the grave in one shot?
There were still some that were breathing—
No. They were undead monsters, so they were already dead. I should say still moving.
In any case, fewer than fifty remained. Even those were practically incapable of fighting.
Did I kill... about three hundred?
Now I understood why the System had called it a massacre.
Of course, compared to that grand choice of words, the EXP it gave me was absolutely pathetic.
“What’s the point of leveling up only once? So stingy.”
Clicking my tongue, I began finishing off the remaining Skeletons.
Every little bit added up. With the EXP required for each level rising like a mountain, every single trash mob mattered.
“Kreeeek. Krik.”
Crack!
I crushed the skull of a Skeleton crawling along with both legs missing.
Beep.
System Defeated Level 73 Skeleton Warrior! Gained a small amount of EXP!
Damn. The EXP really was stingy.
I grumbled as I turned my head to search for the next monster.
“Oh. Ohhh. Could that be...!”
Then my eyes flew open, and a warm feeling spread through one corner of my chest.
Heart pounding with excitement, I approached the creature buried in a mound of dirt.
A Skeleton, trembling with only its head remaining.
The green ghost fire that had once blazed like a torch had shriveled to a tiny flame, like a candle flickering in the wind. But it was still enough for me to identify him.
Level 105 Skeleton Warlord
I smiled broadly and waved at the skull.
“Nice to meet you, friend!”
“You were here! Why didn’t you say so sooner? Why were you just sitting there?”
“Krik. Kreeeek?”
Look at this sly bastard, pretending to be a Skeleton Warrior.
Feigning disappointment, I raised the spearhead.
“Ah, what? You were just a trash mob. I guess I’ll kill you.”
“W. A. I. T!”
“Whoa. It can talk. Could it be...?”
“Y. E. S. That. Is. Right. It. Is. I.”
The Skeleton Warlord opened its eyes wide and continued.
“Master. Of. The. Black. Forest. Commander. Who. Leads. The. Dead. This. Body. Is. The. Warlord.”
“Wow! Warlord!”
“Only. Now. Do. You. Recognize. Me?”
“Wow! EXP!”
Sensing something was wrong, the Warlord hurriedly continued.
“Surely you do not intend to kill me?”
This bastard... Look how smoothly he talks now that he’s desperate.
“Who said anything about killing? You’re already dead.”
“Could this body not die and die again, a hundred times over?”
“...Are you Jeong Mong-ju?”
Has this guy actually read the Song of My Single Heart?
When I stared at him in disbelief, the Warlord clacked his jaw.
“Human. Instead. Of. This. Why. Do. You. Not. Make. A. Deal. With. Me?”
“A deal?”
“That. Is. Right. I. Can. Give. You. Many. Things.”
“You make the first offer.”
“Make. The. First. Offer? What. Does. That. Mean?”
“List what you can give me. I’ll listen and decide.”
The Warlord fell silent for a moment as though deep in thought, then answered.
“I. Am. The. Ruler. Of. The. Forest. I. Shall. Bestow. This. Vast. Black. Forest. Upon. You!”
“The Black Forest is ours.”
“We have exclusive rights to the Gate, so it doesn’t matter.”
“Exclusive. Rights. To. The. Gate? I. Do. Not. Know. What. That. Is. But. Becoming. The. Ruler. Of. The. Forest. Would. Be. Far. Better!”
“No, it wouldn’t. I’d much rather come here whenever the monsters respawn, round them all up, and farm them.”
“R-round. Us. Up? How. Dare. A. Mere. Human. Hunt. Us!”
“Yeah. I’m thinking of sending one more on its way right now.”
Crack.
When I tightened my grip around his skull, the Warlord’s jaw trembled violently, and he shouted in panic.
“Wait! Wait! I. Just. Heard. A. Strange. Sound!”
“Come to think of it, you don’t even have a cochlea. How can you hear anything? What a fascinating creature.”
“There. Is. A. Crack. In. The. Crown. Of. My. Skull! If. This. Continues. I. Will. Be. Erased!”
“Wow! Fucking sweet EXP!”
“You. Insolent. Wretch! I. Am. The. Ruler. Of. The. Black. Forest. And. The. Commander. Of. The. Dead—”
Crack!
“O. Ruler. Of. The. Black. Forest! O. Lord. Of. The. Dead! Please. Show. Mercy!”
That turnaround was Hyuk Mujin-tier at the very least.
Having such a long conversation with a monster was certainly novel, but it was time to stop playing around.
“Inventory open. Summon dagger.”
Shing.
When I held the dark-blue blade in front of his eyes, the Warlord asked anxiously,
“W-what are you going to do, sir?”
“Huh? Nothing much. Close your eyes and stay still. It’ll be over soon.”
“O-over? What do you mean?”
“Shh. Keep your jaw still. If even a bone gets cut, the resale value will drop.”
The corpse of the Wyvern I had killed before, One-Eyed Carus, had been worth its weight in gold. But I had no idea which parts of this Skeleton would be valuable.
Still, a Named Monster’s skull ought to sell for a pretty penny as a decoration, right?
A prize was still a prize. The surface of his bones gleamed with a black sheen and was actually rather beautiful.
I planned to erase him for good first, then gather up the bones nearby.
“Wait! Please, wait!”
Clack! Clack-clack-clack-clack!
God, this guy was noisy.
Just as I was about to grab the Warlord’s jaw, which kept jerking up and down without pause, he shouted.
“E-EXP! I will give you EXP!”
“Huh? I’m already here to collect it, so will you stay still? Besides, you don’t even know what EXP is.”
“No! I will give it to you! I will have my subordinates find it and bring it to you somehow!”
“What the hell are you talking about? EXP isn’t an item...”
I stopped speaking.
A thought had flashed through my mind.
Could this actually work?
“You said you were the master of the Black Forest, right?”
“Y-yes. Yes, yes!”
“How many subordinates do you have?”
“All! All of them! Not right away, but if I search the Black Forest, I can summon more than a thousand!”
“A thousand?”
“More than a thousand at the bare minimum! Have you forgotten who I am?”
“A Skeleton Warlord.”
“Y-yes. No soldier can defy its commander. The lesser creatures would never dare oppose me!”
“Hmm.”
“I will find whatever you want, even if I have to scour the entire Black Forest—or turn it upside down!”
I organized my thoughts as I gazed into the green ghost fire flickering desperately in his eyes.
The deliberation did not last long.
“Hey.”
“Yes.”
“Let’s work together on a job.”
“What kind of job...?”
“Something like that. You just have to do what I tell you.”
At my sinister smile, the Warlord’s skull began to tremble.

He could no longer remember his name, his family, his friends or lover...
He could not even remember where he had been born or what kind of life he had lived.
After passing through a long, deep darkness, he suddenly came to his senses and found himself in a forest.
Where is this?
The question lasted only a moment.
Soon, the instincts of a monster seized him, and he began fighting without purpose.
He fought the humans who had once been his own kind, and he fought monsters as well.
An outstanding knight in life, he grew ever stronger as he cultivated his mana.
Eventually, he even surpassed the black wizard who ruled the vast Black Forest and controlled every dead thing sleeping within it.
“Y-you bastard!
How dare a mere Skeleton Knight...!”
“GRAAAAAH!”
Crack!
Thus, the fallen knight became the new master of the Black Forest.
And at last, he rose to become a chosen being.
Commander of the Skeleton army.
Skeleton Warlord was his new name.
So this is what it feels like?
It was astonishing.
Everything around him had changed.
He did not know why, but the mana flowing through the Black Forest had grown denser, and immense power surged through his body despite it being nothing more than bones.
To him, newly reborn as something else, a mere handful of humans was utterly insignificant.
There aren’t many of them, and they’re all terrified.
To humans, death was simply another name for fear.
Now that he was already one of the dead, the humans’ terror was nothing but amusing.
Run.
Then bring me more—more lives!
He was now the master of the Black Forest and commander of the dead.
The larger groups of humans they brought would soon become his soldiers.
Once he commanded thousands, tens of thousands of the dead...
The Black Forest would no longer be enough for him.
Only then could he be reborn not as a mere commander of the dead, but as a true lord.
I will leave this place and conquer a wider territory.
That was when, as he watched the fifty or so humans flee in panic with satisfaction, one of them caught his eye.
That one...
A human surrounded by three Skeleton Knights, frantically exchanging blows with them.
Strangely enough, unlike the other humans who spoke in a bizarre language, he could understand every word that came from this one’s mouth.
“I’m fine!
Hurry up and go!”
How was this possible?
Such fluent command of the Demon Realm language.
Was he perhaps a monster in human form?
He knew nothing of the System applied to Jin Taekyung, much less the function of the Integrated Language Pack.
He simply wanted to turn that one—who seemed useful enough for a human—into one of the dead and take him as a subordinate.

A.

The foolish one was himself.
“Phew.
They’re finally all gone.”
He should never have led his entire army into this narrow path.
“You’re all going to fucking die here.
That’s all you need to know.”

A.

“One Annihilation.”
Whoooosh!

Defeated Level 78 Skeleton Mage!

One Annihilation is as dangerous as it is destructive.

chapters.title: Chapter 297
paragraphs: Inhale. Exhale.
Choi Minwoo took a long, deep breath.
As he accepted the qi permeating the air, he awakened the mass of qi sleeping in his lower abdomen.
Mana.
The source of an Awakened’s power. Their greatest weapon against monsters.
But Jin Taekyung, the man who had taught him the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique, called mana by another name.
Internal energy.
The more Choi Minwoo saw of Jin Taekyung, the more mysterious the man seemed. He turned ideas no one else would have dared imagine into reality—and made them work.
There was no way anything taught by such a man could be ordinary.
Dantian, internal energy, circulating one’s qi, the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique...
Each new side of Jin Taekyung came as a surprise, but this time, Minwoo was downright bewildered.
He taught me the Mana Cultivation Method as if it were nothing.
Choi Minwoo knew how extraordinary the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique was.
No. Any Hunter—or even an ordinary person with the slightest knowledge of the field—would recognize its value at once.
If a Hunter was a sword, the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique was a whetstone.
Even the dullest blade could be honed sharp.
Considering both the technique’s effectiveness and its rarity...
Its value would quite literally be astronomical.

The sheer nerve it takes to casually hand over such an incredible secret art. The skill to defeat a Named Monster alone. The courage to stand his ground against Lee Jungryong and the Ares Guild... Is there anyone else like him?
With each passing day, Choi Minwoo realized more clearly just how remarkable Jin Taekyung was.
And how incredibly lucky he himself was.
I can’t disappoint him.
That was why Choi Minwoo devoted himself to practicing the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique, even cutting into his sleep.
And the results were already beginning to show.
Swoooosh.
After spending so long circulating his qi that he lost all track of time, the immense energy passed through hundreds of acupoints and swelled ever so slightly.
Only a week ago, he had not even known it existed.
For a moment, the conversation he had shared with Jin Taekyung that day flashed through Choi Minwoo's mind.
“Wow, Team Leader.”
“Yes?”
“Did you happen to eat anything special when you were young? Ginseng, maybe, or one of those round pills?”
“Not at all. My meals were always organic, but I never took anything separately.”
“And I bet you’ve never caught so much as a common cold, from childhood until now. Am I right?”
“That is correct. How did you know?”
“Your muscles and bones... No, I mean, your body is exceptionally well-built.”
“Is that so? But wouldn’t that be true of any Hunter?”
“It’s not because you’re a Hunter. You were born with an outstanding physique. My guess is that your grandfather did something for you.”
“My grandfather...?”
“Yes. Does anything come to mind?”
“I’m not sure. I was too young to remember much. Butler Kim told me that my grandfather came to see me occasionally, but... that’s all.”
“Hmm. Personally, that seems like the only possible explanation.”
Choi Minwoo suddenly thought of his grandfather. Had the last time he saw him been before he started elementary school?
The face in his memory was blurry, while the photographs online were crystal clear. By any measure, they had been far from a close grandfather and grandson.
But if such a huge mass of energy had been hidden inside me... Could my grandfather really have done something?
The unexpected trace of his grandfather made Choi Minwoo's heart pound.
As if responding to him, the energy coursing through his body shuddered.
The enormous power Jin Taekyung called one jiazi made one final sweeping circuit, then settled gently into the dantian beneath his navel.
At that moment, Choi Minwoo opened his eyes as an electric thrill ran through him.
“Phew.”
The lingering afterglow of circulating his qi escaped with his long exhalation.
Choi Minwoo did not know it, but he had just reached Four Stars in the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique. It was an astonishingly rapid achievement, almost impossible to believe after only a week.
Yet it had been possible because Choi Minwoo possessed one jiazi of immense internal energy and such exceptional Muscles and Bones that even Jin Taekyung had nodded in approval.
The others aren’t finished yet.
Choi Minwoo looked around and saw three people still absorbed in circulating their qi.
Seated at regular intervals around the room were Butler Kim, Song Song, and Im Kkeokjeong.
The fact that all four of them were learning the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique was the strictest of secrets.
They were currently inside Choi Minwoo’s private training room, protected by ironclad security.
I shouldn’t disturb them.
Jin Taekyung had warned him about the dangers of qi deviation until he was sick of hearing it.
Choi Minwoo slipped out of the training room as carefully as possible, then picked up the phone he had switched off earlier.
Less than a minute later, his jaw dropped.
Breaking-news alerts were updating across the screen at a blinding pace.
- The return of a Named Monster! Korea in crisis!
- An anomaly at the A-rank Gate, Black Wizard’s Black Forest.
- Jin Taekyung volunteers as bait. Witness testimonies: “He possesses a noble spirit of sacrifice.” “A Benefactor I will never forget.”
- Hunter Association formulating a response and preparing to dispatch a rescue team.
- Peace Guild representative: “We are currently unable to reach the leadership...”
- Netizens unleash criticism over the Association’s sluggish response. Jin Taekyung has been isolated for twenty minutes.
- Will a miracle occur?
“W-what is this?”
What did they mean, sacrifice? And what was this about being isolated?
Jin Taekyung was supposed to be clearing the Gate with his Guild members. How had that turned into a sacrifice?
And where had this Named Monster suddenly come from?
Choi Minwoo stood frozen, eyes wide, before hurriedly pulling himself together.
This isn’t the time to stand around.
He knew Jin Taekyung’s abilities well.
But if Taekyung had volunteered as bait and sent the Guild members out ahead of him, then he had to be facing an overwhelming threat.
This is... really dangerous.
Just as Choi Minwoo gripped his phone hard enough to crush it, the tightly shut door of the training room opened and three people emerged.
“Ah, that feels refreshing.”
“Uncle, doesn’t my skin look better?”
“Ah, Young Master. You were already out—”
“Butler Kim!”
One urgent shout was enough.
The three of them immediately sensed that something serious had happened, and their faces hardened.
Butler Kim calmly asked, “What happened?”
“We have to get to Jin Taekyung. Right now!”
The entrance to the A-rank Gate, Black Wizard’s Black Forest, was already swarming with people.
Hunters from the Association and other Guilds had been dispatched to secure the area. Reporters had even risked their lives for a scoop.
The voices of hundreds upon hundreds of people filled the area with a constant murmur.
“Do you think Jin Taekyung is dead?”
“His chances aren’t good. We haven’t heard a thing for an hour.”
“But he’s already taken down a Named Monster once...”
“Ah, that Wyvern? Impressive, sure. Very impressive, but...”
The senior reporter speaking with his junior tapped the ash from his cigarette.

“If you’re going to call yourself a Hunter beat reporter, then use your head. Didn’t you hear the interview with the Peace Guild members who were with Jin Taekyung? There wasn’t just a Named Monster. They said there were hundreds of other monsters too. That changes everything.”
“Is it really that bad?”

“Hey, the only reason things have gotten this far is because it's Jin Taekyung. If it were anyone else, we wouldn't even be saying things like ‘probably’ or ‘it's difficult.’ What Hunter do you think could hold out alone for an hour? Rescue preparations, my ass. They'd already be preparing to recover his body.”
The junior reporter let out a low groan.
“So it's really that bad.”
“It’s completely fucked. And we’re insane too, hanging around here trying to scribble out an article in the middle of all this.”
“Still, they wouldn’t have allowed us to cover it if they couldn’t guarantee some degree of safety, right?”
“Can’t you see them over there? More than thirty A-rank Hunters showed up.”
The senior reporter gestured with his chin toward several dozen Hunters who looked formidable even at a glance.
The ones who stood out most wore emblems of a crossed sword and shield on their chests.
“The Ares Guild sent people too.”
“They only just arrived. Those bastards will blow off even the government if they don’t like the odds... No idea what brought them here.”
“Do you think they came to rescue Jin Taekyung?”
“Who knows? Maybe. Or maybe they’re planning to claim the Named Monster for themselves.”
Named Monsters were worth an unbelievable amount.
Even One-Eyed Carus, the Wyvern Jin Taekyung had most recently killed, had been valued in the trillions of won despite having only just awakened as a Named Monster.
“But... shouldn’t the rescue operation be starting by now? We have enough firepower.”
“We do. But I doubt those guys see it that way.”
“What?”
“Never mind. Forget it.”
The senior reporter fell silent.
He had spent nearly twenty years in the field and was a veteran among veterans. He had eyes and ears everywhere, and he had seen and heard plenty over the years.
Jin Taekyung must have gotten on their nerves.
He had recently heard some strange news from a reliable source.
There were signs of unusual tension between the Myeongdong and Peace Guilds.
Only a handful of people knew about it, and the story had quickly died down as idle gossip. But the instincts he had honed over many years whispered that something was going on.
And now the Ares Guild shows up.
There was nothing strange about Korea’s largest Guild stepping forward when a Named Monster appeared.
Still, something felt wrong. It was an uneasiness he could not put into words.
The reporter was looking toward the assembled leadership when he suddenly frowned.
You’re going to rub your palms raw, you idiot.
The Seoul Branch President, who could be considered the person in overall charge of this operation, was busily rubbing his palms in front of a man who looked to be in his thirties.
What was that guy's name again? Plaster statue? Go Jun?
He was supposedly the Ares Guild’s security team leader—the right-hand man of Lee Jungryong, the Guild’s de facto Guild Master.
Watching the Seoul Branch President fawn over him as though he would gladly cut out his own liver for the man, the reporter began to understand why the rescue operation was being delayed.
“These bastards sure are having fun.”
That was what the Senior reporter muttered in a voice barely loud enough to hear before grinding out his half-smoked cigarette.
“The Peace Guild!”
“What? Where?”
“Hey, hey! Get the cameras ready!”
The crowd erupted into commotion. Broadcasting crews shouted, and every eye turned in the same direction.
Four people.
Three men and one woman carved a path through the crowd as though parting the Red Sea. They made it all the way to the Gate before Hunters from the Seoul Branch moved to stop them.
“Get out of our way.”
Choi Minwoo stood at the front, his voice low and steady. The Seoul Branch President hurried over to answer him.
“Safety has not yet been confirmed. We need more time before we can begin the rescue operation...”
“More time? Here?”
“Just a little longer. A little longer will be enough.”
“Nearly an hour has already passed.”
His voice remained calm, but flames flickered in his eyes. The three people behind him looked no different.
“We have to save him now.”
“Not yet. Follow procedure.”
“Whose procedure? The Association’s? Or...”
For one brief moment, Choi Minwoo’s gaze swept over Go Jun, who stood behind the Association president.
He clenched his lips, then continued.
“Pull back the Association’s Hunters. The Peace Guild will enter on its own.”
“You must know that would violate regulations.”
The president answered in an authoritative tone and snapped his fingers.
The Seoul Association’s Hunters surrounded the Peace Guild members, open reluctance on their faces.
“It won’t take much longer. Be patient and wait.”
Those words snapped the last thread of Choi Minwoo’s patience.
He shouted as if spitting out a ball of fire.
“My friend is in there!”
Click! Flash!
Cameras captured the scene as dazzling flashes burst all around him.
Choi Minwoo paid them no attention. He continued shouting, his voice thick with fury.
“He could die! We have to save him!”
When he thought of Jin Taekyung fighting for his life against a Named Monster leading an army of hundreds of Skeletons, his anger erupted like an active volcano.
“Get the fuck out of the way, you bastards!”
The Skeleton Warlord spoke in a majestic voice.
“In the commander’s name, I order you. Rise, my loyal subordinates. Mighty soldiers of my legion!”
At that moment, someone smacked the Warlord’s skull with lightning-fast hands.
Whack!
“For fuck’s sake. Why does your incantation have to be so goddamn long? I told you to make it quick.”
“No answer?”
“...Yessir.”
The Warlord muttered in a resigned voice.
“Come on, grow. Skeletons, skeletons...”
Whoooosh!
Demonic qi burst from the Warlord and spread through the Black Forest.
A bright smile appeared on the young man's lips as he watched Skeletons spring up one after another from the clearing.
“Wow. Another bumper harvest.”

Even the dullest blade could be honed sharp.

The sheer nerve it takes to casually hand over such an incredible secret art.

“Hmm.

Had the last time he saw him been before he started elementary school?
The face in his memory was blurry, while the photographs online were crystal clear.

Could my grandfather really have done something?
The unexpected trace of his grandfather made Choi Minwoo's heart pound.

The enormous power Jin Taekyung called one jiazi made one final sweeping circuit, then settled gently into the dantian beneath his navel.
At that moment, Choi Minwoo opened his eyes as an electric thrill ran through him.
“Phew.”
The lingering afterglow of circulating his qi escaped with his long exhalation.
Choi Minwoo did not know it, but he had just reached Four Stars in the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique.
It was an astonishingly rapid achievement, almost impossible to believe after only a week.

Seated at regular intervals around the room were Butler Kim, Song Song, and Im Kkeokjeong.
The fact that all four of them were learning the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique was the strictest of secrets.
They were currently inside Choi Minwoo’s private training room, protected by ironclad security.
I shouldn’t disturb them.
Jin Taekyung had warned him about the dangers of qi deviation until he was sick of hearing it.

Breaking-news alerts were updating across the screen at a blinding pace.
- The return of a Named Monster!
Korea in crisis!
- An anomaly at the A-rank Gate, Black Wizard’s Black Forest.
- Jin Taekyung volunteers as bait.
Witness testimonies: “He possesses a noble spirit of sacrifice.” “A Benefactor I will never forget.”
- Hunter Association formulating a response and preparing to dispatch a rescue team.
- Peace Guild representative: “We are currently unable to reach the leadership...”
- Netizens unleash criticism over the Association’s sluggish response.
Jin Taekyung has been isolated for twenty minutes.
- Will a miracle occur?

What did they mean, sacrifice?

Jin Taekyung was supposed to be clearing the Gate with his Guild members.
How had that turned into a sacrifice?

Choi Minwoo stood frozen, eyes wide, before hurriedly pulling himself together.
This isn’t the time to stand around.
He knew Jin Taekyung’s abilities well.
