chapters.title: Chapter 298
paragraphs: “Come on, grow. Skeletons, skeletons...”
Beep!
System Lv. 105 Skeleton Warlord has used a special Skill! - Special Skill, Summon the Dead, has been activated! - The sleeping dead answer the Commander’s call!
I had never felt so at ease.
Every time I watched a Skeleton shoot up like a bean sprout, happiness welled up inside me.
Is this how farmers feel?
What a bumper crop. What a harvest.
I beamed and swung my sickle—no, my spear—and began reaping.
Every time I smashed the skull of a Skeleton that had only just awakened, a beautiful sound rang out.
Ding. Ding. Ding.
System You have defeated Lv. 71 Skeleton Warrior! - You have gained a small amount of EXP! - You have defeated Lv. 70 Skeleton Archer! - You have gained a small amount of EXP!
The Skeleton Warlord, now forced to offer up his subordinates as EXP, muttered sorrowfully.
“Ah, my soldiers. Forgive your disloyal commander. To fall prey to the schemes of a wicked human and be erased before you could demonstrate your true strength...”
I was about to swing my spear at the next one when I suddenly stopped.
“What did you just say?”
“I called you a wicked human!”
Well, look at this guy.

He was supposed to be groveling, yet here he was glaring at me and talking back. Apparently, his fury at being demoted from commander of the great undead army to EXP factory manager had overcome his fear of Erasure.
“I would rather be erased than offer my soldiers to you!”
“Whether you get erased is for me to decide. More importantly, repeat what you said before that.”
“Wicked human!”
“Not that.”
“Not that? Then what?”
“You said they didn’t get to show their true strength, right?”
“...What of it?”
“Come to think of it, you have some weird Skill. Commander’s Rally, or whatever it was.”
“H-how do you know about that?!”
“Oh, right. No wonder something felt off. I forgot all about it.”
I beamed and stroked the Warlord’s skull.
“Use it.”
The Warlord asked again, sounding genuinely baffled.
“Commander’s Rally? Why?”
“The buff raises their Levels. I need to squeeze every last bit of EXP out of them.”
“So hurry up and use it. If you do a good job, I might even let you go.”
“R-really?”
“There’s a saying in the human world: a man’s word is worth a thousand pieces of gold. It means a man always keeps his word.”
“A man who lost his mama is worth a thousand pieces of gold? What a strange saying.”
“Why would he lose his mama? Making mom jokes now, you fucking bastard? Maybe I should just erase you.”
Crack.
When I tightened my grip around his head, the Skeleton Warlord cried out in alarm.
“Wait! My bone—it’s cracking! My bone!”
“Lord, I’m sending one up.”
“Wait!”
“So are you going to do it or not?”
The Warlord’s green pupils darted anxiously from side to side.
For a Skeleton, he displayed a surprisingly wide range of emotions. After a moment, he finally forced out an answer.
“I-I’ll do it.”
“Good choice.”
“But do not misunderstand. This is not submission. It is a contract!”
“A contract?”
“That is right! Not obedience, but a contract mutually agreed upon by both parties!”
“...This bastard is more human than I am, and he’s a Skeleton. So what are the terms?”
“In exchange for cooperating with you, wicked human, you will guarantee my current position.”
“The master of the Black Forest and commander of the undead army?”
“Correct! In addition, cease this indiscriminate and barbaric slaughter!”
What had I just heard?
A monster, of all things, had just told me to stop my indiscriminate and barbaric slaughter. My head spun for a moment.
“Are you out of your mind? Is that something a monster should be saying?”
“How insulting. I am a Skeleton Warlord possessed of cool judgment and intelligence. Though I may have become one of the fallen undead, the spirit of chivalry remains engraved deep within my soul.”
“...If you had upheld chivalry, you wouldn’t have fallen like this in the first place.”
“...The truth is, my memories of life were erased when I became undead.”
“Then don’t go on about chivalry. You’re a real piece of work.”
Still, perhaps because he was a Named Monster, he was clearly different from ordinary monsters that were ruled by instinct and did nothing but howl.
Anyway, a contract.
I considered it carefully, then finally spoke.
“Fine. I’ve decided.”
“Human. Will you accept my contract?”
“No. I don’t want to.”
I continued as the green light in his eyes quivered with confusion.
“I’m okay with the first proposal. You can be the master of the Black Forest and the commander of the army, or whatever. But...”
“But?”
“From now on, you’re the Peace Guild’s EXP factory manager. In exchange for guaranteeing your position, you’ll supply me with as many Skeletons as I want.”
“That is absurd!”
“Don’t like it?”
“I would rather be erased than become a human puppet!”
“Your wish has been received, valued customer.”
Crack.
The Skeleton Warlord, a crack running across the crown of his skull, answered in a solemn voice.
“On second thought, it is not such a bad contract.”
“A commander cannot abandon his soldiers. Human, as master of the Black Forest and commander of the undead army, I accept your proposal.”
“You just said you’d rather be erased than become a human puppet.”
“An army falls apart without its commander. Do not misunderstand. I am merely enduring a moment of humiliation for the sake of the soldiers waiting for me.”
“But those are the very soldiers you have to offer up.”
“I will remember their noble sacrifice until the day I am erased. So, how much is this month’s tribute? No—how many troops must I offer?”
Look at him, giving them away without holding back since he wasn’t the one being destroyed.
At this point, he wasn’t a puppet. He was a snail bride.
When I stared at him with an utterly dumbfounded expression, the world’s first pro-human Named Monster, the Skeleton Warlord, hurriedly began chanting.
“Grow stronger, Skeletons, Skeletons!”
Beep!

System Lv. 105 Skeleton Warlord has used a special Skill! - Special Skill, Commander’s Rally, has been activated! - The Strength, Agility, and Magic of the monsters under the Skeleton Warlord’s command have been enhanced! - The enemies’ Levels have increased by 5!
...He can do it all by himself now.
The harvesting was easy.
The first time was the hard part. After two or three repetitions, I got the hang of it.
The Skeleton Warlord made full use of his abilities as a commander to gather the tribute troops as quickly as possible.
“Legion! Assemble!”
Clatter, clatter!
Around a hundred freshly sprouted Skeletons gathered in one place. All I had to do was unleash Spear Energy at the monsters assembled under his command, and EXP came raining down.
Swoooosh! Boom!
Ding. Ding. Ding.
The sound of EXP rolling in brought a smile to my face. As he watched, the Warlord muttered in satisfaction.
“Hmm. This is much faster and easier.”
“Human. Have you witnessed my command ability? This is the majesty of a commander.”
What a pro-human bastard.
Watching him take pride in devising a more efficient way to offer up his soldiers, I felt like I finally understood why his soul had become corrupted.
If the winds of liberation ever swept through the Black Forest, the Skeleton independence fighters would put him at the very top of their purge list.
Why do I feel like I’m the invader here?
Feeling strangely conflicted, I began collecting the loot.
Skeletons were one of the most dirt-poor monster species around. Their so-called by-products were either rusty weapons that could cause tetanus or half-rotted bones.
You could at least get beef and bone broth from a Minotaur carcass. Apparently, no matter how long you simmered Skeleton bones, all you got was the taste of a grave.
“Oh, a Magic Gem and some armor.”
At least Skeleton Knights, which appeared about as often as beans in a drought, sometimes left behind one or two Magic Gems and decent pieces of Equipment like these.
Of course, even that only happened once in a blue moon.
“A Magic Gem this size should easily fetch tens of millions of won.”
Sending the Guild members away had been the right call. I got to monopolize both the EXP and the Magic Gems—the best of both worlds.
As I happily pocketed a Magic Gem the size of an adult’s fist, the Warlord asked me a question.
“Wicked human. What are you doing?”
“Can’t you tell? Collecting the fruits of my labor.”
“Do you intend to absorb it later?”
“Absorb it? Don’t be ridiculous. Of course I’m going to sell it.”
“Foolish. Magic Gems are the source of power. Is it not only natural to eat them and grow stronger?”
“That’s something monsters like you do. Humans are different.”
It was common knowledge that humans weren’t monsters’ only enemies.
Monsters often fought among themselves, and some grew stronger by devouring the monsters they defeated.
“Is that so? Humans are truly an incomprehensible race. You could grow stronger by absorbing Magic Gems... Is this thing called money really so wonderful?”
“We need money to live whether we like it or not. Besides, humans can’t absorb Magic Gems.”
The energy contained within Magic Gems was commonly known as demonic qi. It was the foundation of a monster’s strength, but to humans, it was no different from poison.
It was a type of qi, but the easiest way to understand it was to think of it as a contaminant.
After I gave him a rough explanation, the Warlord tilted his skull.
“You cannot absorb it? How strange. A group of humans I encountered long ago used Troll blood to heal their bodies.”
“Ah, potions? That goes through a purification process...”
“Then why not purify Magic Gems as well? Just as you do with the Troll blood you call potions.”
“If it were that simple, we’d have purified them long ago. You really are simpleminded, just like a monster.”
If Troll blood was a fruit-flavored drink with one percent fruit flavoring, a Magic Gem was one hundred percent fresh fruit juice.
People couldn’t even remove all the toxicity from potions, yet he was suggesting we absorb Magic Gems.
I let out a short laugh and continued.
“Anyway, humans can’t absorb Magic Gems.”
“Why?”
“Stop asking questions, you question-mark murderer. That’s the established academic consensus. I’ve never heard or seen anything like that.”
“I have never heard of a human like you, either.”
I was about to smack the Warlord’s skull when I stopped.
Wait. He has a point.
There’s no need to be bound by common sense all the time.
Wasn’t I living proof that common sense didn’t apply to everything?
Even the so-called accepted academic consensus was only a conclusion based on what people currently knew.
The Mana Cultivation Method is the same.
Only a tiny handful of people knew it existed.
I hadn’t even considered that before getting tangled up with the Ares Guild.
Their private league had remained unchanged both before and after the appearance of monsters, and its secrets had always been shared only within the boundaries they had drawn.
Absorbing a Magic Gem...
Should I give it a try?
Just as I was about to open my Inventory and take out the Magic Gem again, the Warlord spoke.
“Heh heh. You look as though you have just been struck. Wicked and foolish human.”
“Oh. Want me to hit your skull with an Erasure Punch?”
“...That was a rash remark. I apologize.”
“You apologized within three seconds, so I’ll allow it.”
Having escaped Erasure by observing the universal three-second rule, the Skeleton Warlord muttered,
“There is no greater humiliation. Consider yourself fortunate that I have not grown stronger, human.”
“You started as a Skeleton Knight and became master of the Black Forest through a coup. I’d say you’ve risen pretty far.”
“I am a Warlord now! Master of the Black Forest and—”
“Commander of the undead army. Yeah, yeah. I’m getting calluses on my ears from hearing it.”
I only learned later that he had taken over the Black Forest.
He had defeated the black wizard, who had practically been its true master. He must have absorbed an incredible number of Magic Gems.

“So this is a complete human—or rather, Skeleton—victory. Going from an ordinary Skeleton Knight to the master of the Black Forest, and even evolving into a Warlord... You must have absorbed an enormous number of Magic Gems from the black wizard, right?”
“What are you talking about? He did not possess any Magic Gems.”
“Huh?”
“Besides, the black wizard was the one who summoned me directly. Until recently, his commands were absolute. A summoned creature cannot defy its summoner.”
“Then how...”
“You mean, how was I able to defeat him?”
The green light in the Skeleton Warlord’s eyes narrowed.

“I do not know the reason myself. Not long ago, I suddenly felt that I had escaped his control. Perhaps you could say that I climbed one step higher when my magical power surpassed that of my summoner.”
“Suddenly?”
“Yes. My magical power increased tremendously, all at once.”
What was he talking about?
But just as the Warlord said, even he couldn’t properly explain what had happened to him.
After thinking for a long time, he managed to add only one thing.
“Borrowing a human expression, it felt as if I had been possessed by a ghost.”
“...Is that something a Skeleton can say?”
Maybe that bastard isn’t actually a Skeleton.
It was at that moment, as I stared at the Warlord with an incredulous expression, that—
“Hmm?”
The Warlord’s skull rolled around atop his neck, then stopped facing one direction.
The green light in his eyes shone as he gazed south and clacked his jaw.
“An intruder.”
“An intruder?”
“I am master of the Black Forest. I know everything that happens within it. More wicked humans have just set foot in my territory.”
“They’re my friends, you idiot.”
Whack!
I gave the back of his head a hearty smack, picked up the Warlord’s skull, and headed toward the Gate entrance.

I had never felt so at ease.
Every time I watched a Skeleton shoot up like a bean sprout, happiness welled up inside me.
Is this how farmers feel?
What a bumper crop.
What a harvest.
I beamed and swung my sickle—no, my spear—and began reaping.
Every time I smashed the skull of a Skeleton that had only just awakened, a beautiful sound rang out.
Ding.
Ding.
Ding.
System You have defeated Lv.
71 Skeleton Warrior! - You have gained a small amount of EXP! - You have defeated Lv.
70 Skeleton Archer! - You have gained a small amount of EXP!
The Skeleton Warlord, now forced to offer up his subordinates as EXP, muttered sorrowfully.
“Ah, my soldiers.
Forgive your disloyal commander.
To fall prey to the schemes of a wicked human and be erased before you could demonstrate your true strength...”
I was about to swing my spear at the next one when I suddenly stopped.
“What did you just say?”
“I called you a wicked human!”
Well, look at this guy.
He was supposed to be groveling, yet here he was glaring at me and talking back.
Apparently, his fury at being demoted from commander of the great undead army to EXP factory manager had overcome his fear of Erasure.
“I would rather be erased than offer my soldiers to you!”
“Whether you get erased is for me to decide.
More importantly, repeat what you said before that.”
“Wicked human!”
“Not that.”
“Not that?
Then what?”
“You said they didn’t get to show their true strength, right?”
“...What of it?”
“Come to think of it, you have some weird Skill.
Commander’s Rally, or whatever it was.”
“H-how do you know about that?!”
“Oh, right.
No wonder something felt off.
I forgot all about it.”
I beamed and stroked the Warlord’s skull.
“Use it.”
The Warlord asked again, sounding genuinely baffled.
“Commander’s Rally?
Why?”
“The buff raises their Levels.
I need to squeeze every last bit of EXP out of them.”
“So hurry up and use it.
If you do a good job, I might even let you go.”
“R-really?”
“There’s a saying in the human world: a man’s word is worth a thousand pieces of gold.
It means a man always keeps his word.”
“A man who lost his mama is worth a thousand pieces of gold?
What a strange saying.”
“Why would he lose his mama?
Making mom jokes now, you fucking bastard?
Maybe I should just erase you.”
Crack.
When I tightened my grip around his head, the Skeleton Warlord cried out in alarm.
“Wait!
My bone—it’s cracking!
My bone!”
“Lord, I’m sending one up.”
“Wait!”
“So are you going to do it or not?”
The Warlord’s green pupils darted anxiously from side to side.
For a Skeleton, he displayed a surprisingly wide range of emotions.
After a moment, he finally forced out an answer.
“I-I’ll do it.”
“Good choice.”
“But do not misunderstand.
This is not submission.
It is a contract!”
“A contract?”
“That is right!
Not obedience, but a contract mutually agreed upon by both parties!”
“...This bastard is more human than I am, and he’s a Skeleton.
So what are the terms?”
“In exchange for cooperating with you, wicked human, you will guarantee my current position.”
“The master of the Black Forest and commander of the undead army?”
“Correct!
In addition, cease this indiscriminate and barbaric slaughter!”
What had I just heard?
A monster, of all things, had just told me to stop my indiscriminate and barbaric slaughter.
My head spun for a moment.
“Are you out of your mind?
Is that something a monster should be saying?”
“How insulting.
I am a Skeleton Warlord possessed of cool judgment and intelligence.
Though I may have become one of the fallen undead, the spirit of chivalry remains engraved deep within my soul.”
“...If you had upheld chivalry, you wouldn’t have fallen like this in the first place.”
“...The truth is, my memories of life were erased when I became undead.”
“Then don’t go on about chivalry.
You’re a real piece of work.”
Still, perhaps because he was a Named Monster, he was clearly different from ordinary monsters that were ruled by instinct and did nothing but howl.
Anyway, a contract.
I considered it carefully, then finally spoke.
“Fine.
I’ve decided.”
“Human.
Will you accept my contract?”
“No.
I don’t want to.”
I continued as the green light in his eyes quivered with confusion.
“I’m okay with the first proposal.
You can be the master of the Black Forest and the commander of the army, or whatever.
But...”
“But?”
“From now on, you’re the Peace Guild’s EXP factory manager.
In exchange for guaranteeing your position, you’ll supply me with as many Skeletons as I want.”
“That is absurd!”
“Don’t like it?”
“I would rather be erased than become a human puppet!”
“Your wish has been received, valued customer.”
Crack.
The Skeleton Warlord, a crack running across the crown of his skull, answered in a solemn voice.
“On second thought, it is not such a bad contract.”
“A commander cannot abandon his soldiers.
Human, as master of the Black Forest and commander of the undead army, I accept your proposal.”
“You just said you’d rather be erased than become a human puppet.”
“An army falls apart without its commander.
Do not misunderstand.
I am merely enduring a moment of humiliation for the sake of the soldiers waiting for me.”
“But those are the very soldiers you have to offer up.”
“I will remember their noble sacrifice until the day I am erased.
So, how much is this month’s tribute?
No—how many troops must I offer?”
Look at him, giving them away without holding back since he wasn’t the one being destroyed.
At this point, he wasn’t a puppet.
He was a snail bride.
When I stared at him with an utterly dumbfounded expression, the world’s first pro-human Named Monster, the Skeleton Warlord, hurriedly began chanting.
“Grow stronger, Skeletons, Skeletons!”
Beep!
System Lv.

105 Skeleton Warlord has used a special Skill! - Special Skill, Commander’s Rally, has been activated! - The Strength, Agility, and Magic of the monsters under the Skeleton Warlord’s command have been enhanced! - The enemies’ Levels have increased by 5!
...He can do it all by himself now.
The harvesting was easy.
The first time was the hard part.
After two or three repetitions, I got the hang of it.
The Skeleton Warlord made full use of his abilities as a commander to gather the tribute troops as quickly as possible.
“Legion!
Assemble!”
Clatter, clatter!
Around a hundred freshly sprouted Skeletons gathered in one place.
All I had to do was unleash Spear Energy at the monsters assembled under his command, and EXP came raining down.
Swoooosh!
Boom!
Ding.
Ding.
Ding.
The sound of EXP rolling in brought a smile to my face.
As he watched, the Warlord muttered in satisfaction.
“Hmm.
This is much faster and easier.”
“Human.
Have you witnessed my command ability?
This is the majesty of a commander.”
What a pro-human bastard.
Watching him take pride in devising a more efficient way to offer up his soldiers, I felt like I finally understood why his soul had become corrupted.
If the winds of liberation ever swept through the Black Forest, the Skeleton independence fighters would put him at the very top of their purge list.
Why do I feel like I’m the invader here?
Feeling strangely conflicted, I began collecting the loot.
Skeletons were one of the most dirt-poor monster species around.
Their so-called by-products were either rusty weapons that could cause tetanus or half-rotted bones.
You could at least get beef and bone broth from a Minotaur carcass.
Apparently, no matter how long you simmered Skeleton bones, all you got was the taste of a grave.
“Oh, a Magic Gem and some armor.”
At least Skeleton Knights, which appeared about as often as beans in a drought, sometimes left behind one or two Magic Gems and decent pieces of Equipment like these.
Of course, even that only happened once in a blue moon.
“A Magic Gem this size should easily fetch tens of millions of won.”
Sending the Guild members away had been the right call.
I got to monopolize both the EXP and the Magic Gems—the best of both worlds.
As I happily pocketed a Magic Gem the size of an adult’s fist, the Warlord asked me a question.
“Wicked human.
What are you doing?”
“Can’t you tell?
Collecting the fruits of my labor.”
“Do you intend to absorb it later?”
“Absorb it?
Don’t be ridiculous.
Of course I’m going to sell it.”
“Foolish.
Magic Gems are the source of power.
Is it not only natural to eat them and grow stronger?”
“That’s something monsters like you do.
Humans are different.”
It was common knowledge that humans weren’t monsters’ only enemies.
Monsters often fought among themselves, and some grew stronger by devouring the monsters they defeated.
“Is that so?
Humans are truly an incomprehensible race.
You could grow stronger by absorbing Magic Gems...

“We need money to live whether we like it or not.
Besides, humans can’t absorb Magic Gems.”
The energy contained within Magic Gems was commonly known as demonic qi.
It was the foundation of a monster’s strength, but to humans, it was no different from poison.
It was a type of qi, but the easiest way to understand it was to think of it as a contaminant.
After I gave him a rough explanation, the Warlord tilted his skull.
“You cannot absorb it?
How strange.
A group of humans I encountered long ago used Troll blood to heal their bodies.”
“Ah, potions?
That goes through a purification process...”
“Then why not purify Magic Gems as well?
Just as you do with the Troll blood you call potions.”
“If it were that simple, we’d have purified them long ago.
You really are simpleminded, just like a monster.”
If Troll blood was a fruit-flavored drink with one percent fruit flavoring, a Magic Gem was one hundred percent fresh fruit juice.
People couldn’t even remove all the toxicity from potions, yet he was suggesting we absorb Magic Gems.

“Why?”
“Stop asking questions, you question-mark murderer.
That’s the established academic consensus.
I’ve never heard or seen anything like that.”
“I have never heard of a human like you, either.”

paragraphs: “It looks like we can begin now.”
The Seoul Branch President finally gave the go-ahead more than ten minutes after the Peace Guild, led by Choi Minwoo, began protesting.

A Gate was a fierce battlefield where life and death could be decided in an instant. No one expected Jin Taekyung to survive after being left alone against a Named Monster commanding hundreds of Skeletons.
“Do you think he’s still alive?”
“It’s been exactly one hour and eight minutes. We’ll be lucky if we can recover his body.”
“Damn it. This isn’t a rescue operation. It’s a body-recovery operation.”
“Can they really do this? Every second matters, and they’re just dragging their feet.”

“What else can they do? This isn’t an ordinary A-rank Gate. A Named Monster appeared. If you look at it from the Association’s perspective, you can understand their position. If they rush in and cause a major disaster, it’s all over.”
Hunters preparing to enter and reporters filming the scene stood around talking in groups.
Some were furious about the delayed rescue operation. Others defended the Association’s decision.
But no one mentioned the possibility that Jin Taekyung had survived. There was no need to state the obvious.
“Still, the Peace Guild really got screwed.”

“Yeah. Jin Taekyung is already... Well, it’s unfortunate, but that’s how things turned out. And they openly raised hell with the Seoul Branch President in front of the cameras. The backlash is going to be brutal.”
“Exactly. That guy’s a political appointee, and he’s already ridiculously sensitive about the media.”
Choi Minwoo’s face hardened as he listened to the whispers around him.
Whatever repercussions the Peace Guild might suffer later?
He didn’t give a damn.
Who the hell says he’s dead?
He wanted to charge forward right then and there. He wanted to grab the idiots spouting that nonsense by the collar, then knock down the Association Hunters blocking his way.
The only reason he had waited this long was something Butler Kim had said while holding him back more than ten minutes earlier.
“Didn’t you say so yourself, Young Master? That you trusted Mr. Jin Taekyung more than you trusted yourself?”
Those words had forced him to rein in his anger.
It was true. Taekyung had always shown them miracles. He had always made the impossible possible. Today was simply another extension of that.
Choi Minwoo believed it.
He wanted to believe it.
Isn’t that right, Mr. Jin Taekyung?
He drew a deep breath and stepped forward. Around fifty Peace Guild members followed him, their faces filled with resolve.
“The Peace Guild will take the lead.”
The Seoul Branch President gave him a hostile look.
“That falls under my authority as the commander of this operation. Yet from the way you’re speaking, that sounded more like a notification than a request.”
“That’s correct.”
“What?”
“Would you like me to repeat myself? I said it was a notification.”
Before the Association President could respond, Choi Minwoo continued in an icy voice.
“I have no intention of delaying any longer, and no reason to keep talking to you. The Peace Guild will take the lead.”
“How dare you—!”
The Association President’s face flushed red enough to burst.
That was when a flat voice came from behind him.
“Let them.”
The Association President turned his head.
Go Jun, Lee Jungryong’s right-hand man and Head of Security, stood with his arms folded and his face expressionless.
“Team Leader Seok?”
“Please consider the feelings of the Peace Guild members who have lost a comrade they shared so many hardships with. The media will look favorably on it as well.”
“B-but there’s a Named Monster inside the Gate. If we put untested Hunters at the front, something unfortunate could happen...”
The Association President fell silent beneath Go Jun’s cold gaze.
For a moment, he had forgotten. The man before him was no mere team leader in the Ares Guild. He was Lee Jungryong’s Head of Security and right-hand man.
He had also forgotten that the “unfortunate incident” he feared was precisely what Go Jun wanted.
The Association President deliberated only briefly.
“Let the Peace Guild take the lead. Then, three minutes later, the Association and the Ares Guild will...”
But Choi Minwoo had already turned and begun walking toward the Gate.
The gazes of the Association President, Go Jun, and countless others clung to him, but he paid them no attention.
“Let’s go. We’re going to save Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
At Choi Minwoo’s quiet words, a roar thundered across the grounds, loud enough to make their ears ring.
Butler Kim, Im Kkeokjeong, Song Song, and around fifty Peace Guild members followed Choi Minwoo, cutting through the hundreds of Hunters like a current as they advanced toward the Gate.
That was when Butler Kim’s resonant shout rang out.
“All Peace Guild members, form an attack formation!”
Clack-clack-clack!
Armor and blades flashed in the sunlight as they moved. In an instant, the Peace Guild members formed a wedge and shot forward like a single arrow.
At their head, Choi Minwoo charged toward the magic field with a thunderous cry.
“Enter!”
Swoooosh!
Never before had the Gate’s magic felt so unpleasant.
Choi Minwoo opened his eyes, a sense of foreboding stirring deep in his chest.
His heart sank.
This is...
Scorched earth.
Was there any better way to describe the sight before him?
From the hill where the Gate entrance stood, they had a clear view of the trail below.
It was completely engulfed in flames.
Mr. Jin Taekyung.
The foreboding he had felt while passing through the Gate seemed to be slowly taking shape.
Im Kkeokjeong spoke from behind him, his voice trembling.
“Team Leader Choi. What if Taekyung...”
“Stop. We’re in the middle of an operation. Don’t jump to conclusions.”
But this time, even Team Leader Choi’s words failed to reassure them.
The situation before them looked that hopeless. Im Kkeokjeong wasn’t the only one shaken. Every member of the Peace Guild was in turmoil.
No. It can’t be.
Choi Minwoo bit down hard on his lip, steadying himself, then moved forward with heavy steps.
“We’ll continue our approach. Stay alert and keep advancing.”
They moved cautiously forward, prepared for monsters to appear at any moment.
But the closer they came to the trail, the deeper their despair grew.
“This can’t be...”
A mountain of shattered bones and weapons. Ash blanketing the blackened ground.
There was no trace of life anywhere in that place, where death and destruction reigned. Nor was there any sign of the one person they had so desperately hoped to find.
Dead? Him?
The same question flashed through everyone’s mind.
Those who had known Jin Taekyung the longest could only blink at the unbelievable sight.
Butler Kim’s words broke the suffocating silence like a doctor delivering his final verdict.
“According to the results of the detection magic... we found no movement or living creatures within a three-hundred-meter radius.”
Choi Minwoo’s eyelids trembled.
“You mean...”
“I’m sorry.”
His face devastated, Butler Kim extended a hand. Something rose into the air from the direction he indicated and slowly flew toward them.
“That’s...”
“Judging by the considerable magic I can sense from it, it appears to be a trace left by the Named Monster.”
A palm-sized metal fragment rested in Butler Kim’s hand.
Its black sheen remained undiminished despite the ash covering it. Several people sucked in sharp breaths when they saw the chilling skull emblem.
“The skull emblem! Th-that’s part of the armor the Named Monster was wearing!”
“That’s right! We saw it clearly.”
Then someone searching the area cried out.
“There’s a dagger here too! It isn’t the kind of equipment Skeletons use!”
“It belongs to Senior Jin Taekyung. It’s the one he used all the time.”
As shock settled over the group, Butler Kim spoke in a subdued voice.
“It appears he was oxidized along with every enemy, including the Named Monster...”
The air around the trail seemed to crackle.
Now everything was certain. Jin Taekyung was dead. He had thrown away his own life, taking his enemies with him as companions on the road to the afterlife and leaving his comrades behind.
Im Kkeokjeong’s wail finally shattered the seemingly endless silence.
“Ghk. Nghh...”
A faint tremor began in his hands, climbed through his arms, shoulders, and back, then spread through his entire body. Tears poured from Im Kkeokjeong’s large eyes.
“Taekyung... Taekyung... Nghh!”
No one mocked him as his massive frame shook with sobs.
Their grief might differ in depth, but everyone there felt the same.
Grief over Jin Taekyung’s death. Guilt that they had been unable to fight alongside him. And the helplessness they felt toward themselves.
The Peace Guild members’ eyes grew red and bloodshot. Tears streamed down Butler Kim’s and Song Song’s cheeks.
Only one person did not cry.
Choi Minwoo.
He’s dead. Jin Taekyung is dead.
His dark eyes swept over the trail, where acrid smoke still curled into the air.
It felt as though Taekyung might be hiding somewhere even now, ready to spring out like a jack-in-the-box.
I thought you could survive anything.
His chest suddenly tightened.
He had not felt this way since losing his parents.
His grief swelled like a balloon, stretching taut, ready to burst at any moment.
Then a voice drifted over.
“My, what a gruesome sight.”
“Jin Taekyung is nowhere to be seen. It appears he really is dead.”
Choi Minwoo slowly turned around.
Hundreds of people had just entered the trail. At the head of the Association and the other Hunters participating in the rescue operation stood two men.
“It seems the rescue has failed. Wouldn’t you agree, Association President?”
“Indeed. Everything’s been reduced to ash. I wonder if we’ll even be able to find the body. More importantly, where is the Named Monster?”
“We’ll have to search thoroughly, but according to the detection magic, it appears all the problems you were concerned about have been resolved.”
At Go Jun’s words, the Association President’s heavily furrowed face broke into a broad smile.
“Oh, that’s welcome news. I thought we might have another casualty on our hands.”
“Your judgment allowed us to minimize our losses, Association President.”

“Nonsense. This was all thanks to the Ares Guild stepping forward. Once everything is settled, I’ll make absolutely certain that you receive a commendation plaque. Ha ha. It’ll be the first achievement of my term, so I’m thinking of holding a grand ceremony... Guild Master Lee Jungryong will attend, won’t he?”
“He’s not the Guild Master. He’s the Vice Guild Master.”
“Ah, of course. Goodness, I’ve become so forgetful with age.”
A dry smile touched the corner of Go Jun’s mouth.
“That happens. And if a commendation plaque is presented, the Vice Guild Master will be delighted to attend.”
“I’ll finally get to see him again. Please put in a good word for me, Team Leader Seok.”
“I’m sure he’ll be quite pleased if I simply report exactly what I’ve seen and heard.”
“Ha ha.”
The conversation between Go Jun and the Association President was a sharp needle—a needle capable of popping Choi Minwoo’s ballooning emotions.
“Shut your mouth.”
Every sound died at once.
The Association President belatedly realized what he had heard, and his face twisted with rage. But Go Jun responded before he could.
“You’d do well to watch your mouth.”
“I told you to shut it.”
“Young man, you don’t know the meaning of manners. Don’t you agree, Team Leader Choi Minwoo of the Peace Guild?”
The words were barbed.

To Go Jun, Choi Minwoo was a kite with its string cut. The Ares Guild founded by his grandfather was already as good as Lee Jungryong’s. And now that Jin Taekyung, the troublesome figure they had been watching, was dead, there was no reason to hide his fangs any longer.
“I understand that you’re distraught over the death of a Guild member, but you need to calm down.”
Choi Minwoo ground out his reply.
“He could have survived if you bastards hadn’t stalled.”
“We did our best. The Association President’s judgment was correct as well. And...”
Go Jun continued in a cold, dry voice.
“You people bear some responsibility too. Don’t you agree?”
“What were you doing while Jin Taekyung was dying? Leisurely reading the newspaper in your office? Or drinking at a bar in the middle of the day?”
Choi Minwoo bit his lip.
Everything Go Jun said was true.
Because he had trusted Jin Taekyung, he had set everything else aside and devoted himself to training.
But...
At least Choi Minwoo himself should not have done that.
Another needle flew at him as he struggled to speak.
“You killed Jin Taekyung. All of you did—you pathetic weaklings who forgot your duty.”
Go Jun let out a short laugh.
“It’s too late for regrets. The dead don’t come back.”
Choi Minwoo clenched his fists until they felt ready to burst.
Then—
“What the fuck are you talking about, you motherfucking bastard?”
The voice was low but powerful, piercing every ear.
Those who did not recognize it stared around in confusion at the sudden profanity.
Those who did froze like statues.
No way...
Choi Minwoo slowly turned his head.
Far down the trail, someone was trudging toward them.
“You finished the whole forty-ninth-day memorial rite while I was off taking a piss, you fucking bastard.”
Jin Taekyung hawked a wad of phlegm onto the ground.
“Square up, asshole.”

sentences.text: “It looks like we can begin now.”
The Seoul Branch President finally gave the go-ahead more than ten minutes after the Peace Guild, led by Choi Minwoo, began protesting.
A Gate was a fierce battlefield where life and death could be decided in an instant.
No one expected Jin Taekyung to survive after being left alone against a Named Monster commanding hundreds of Skeletons.
“Do you think he’s still alive?”
“It’s been exactly one hour and eight minutes.
We’ll be lucky if we can recover his body.”
“Damn it.
This isn’t a rescue operation.
It’s a body-recovery operation.”
“Can they really do this?
Every second matters, and they’re just dragging their feet.”
“What else can they do?
This isn’t an ordinary A-rank Gate.
A Named Monster appeared.
If you look at it from the Association’s perspective, you can understand their position.
If they rush in and cause a major disaster, it’s all over.”
Hunters preparing to enter and reporters filming the scene stood around talking in groups.
Some were furious about the delayed rescue operation.
Others defended the Association’s decision.
But no one mentioned the possibility that Jin Taekyung had survived.
There was no need to state the obvious.
“Still, the Peace Guild really got screwed.”
“Yeah.
Jin Taekyung is already...
Well, it’s unfortunate, but that’s how things turned out.
And they openly raised hell with the Seoul Branch President in front of the cameras.
The backlash is going to be brutal.”
“Exactly.
That guy’s a political appointee, and he’s already ridiculously sensitive about the media.”
Choi Minwoo’s face hardened as he listened to the whispers around him.
Whatever repercussions the Peace Guild might suffer later?
He didn’t give a damn.
Who the hell says he’s dead?
He wanted to charge forward right then and there.
He wanted to grab the idiots spouting that nonsense by the collar, then knock down the Association Hunters blocking his way.
The only reason he had waited this long was something Butler Kim had said while holding him back more than ten minutes earlier.
“Didn’t you say so yourself, Young Master?
That you trusted Mr.
Jin Taekyung more than you trusted yourself?”
Those words had forced him to rein in his anger.
It was true.
Taekyung had always shown them miracles.
He had always made the impossible possible.
Today was simply another extension of that.
Choi Minwoo believed it.
He wanted to believe it.
Isn’t that right, Mr.
Jin Taekyung?
He drew a deep breath and stepped forward.
Around fifty Peace Guild members followed him, their faces filled with resolve.
“The Peace Guild will take the lead.”
The Seoul Branch President gave him a hostile look.
“That falls under my authority as the commander of this operation.
Yet from the way you’re speaking, that sounded more like a notification than a request.”
“That’s correct.”
“What?”
“Would you like me to repeat myself?
I said it was a notification.”
Before the Association President could respond, Choi Minwoo continued in an icy voice.
“I have no intention of delaying any longer, and no reason to keep talking to you.
The Peace Guild will take the lead.”
“How dare you—!”
The Association President’s face flushed red enough to burst.
That was when a flat voice came from behind him.
“Let them.”
The Association President turned his head.
Go Jun, Lee Jungryong’s right-hand man and Head of Security, stood with his arms folded and his face expressionless.
“Team Leader Seok?”
“Please consider the feelings of the Peace Guild members who have lost a comrade they shared so many hardships with.
The media will look favorably on it as well.”
“B-but there’s a Named Monster inside the Gate.
If we put untested Hunters at the front, something unfortunate could happen...”
The Association President fell silent beneath Go Jun’s cold gaze.
For a moment, he had forgotten.
The man before him was no mere team leader in the Ares Guild.
He was Lee Jungryong’s Head of Security and right-hand man.
He had also forgotten that the “unfortunate incident” he feared was precisely what Go Jun wanted.
The Association President deliberated only briefly.
“Let the Peace Guild take the lead.
Then, three minutes later, the Association and the Ares Guild will...”
But Choi Minwoo had already turned and begun walking toward the Gate.
The gazes of the Association President, Go Jun, and countless others clung to him, but he paid them no attention.
“Let’s go.
We’re going to save Mr.
Jin Taekyung.”
At Choi Minwoo’s quiet words, a roar thundered across the grounds, loud enough to make their ears ring.
Butler Kim, Im Kkeokjeong, Song Song, and around fifty Peace Guild members followed Choi Minwoo, cutting through the hundreds of Hunters like a current as they advanced toward the Gate.
That was when Butler Kim’s resonant shout rang out.
“All Peace Guild members, form an attack formation!”
Clack-clack-clack!
Armor and blades flashed in the sunlight as they moved.
In an instant, the Peace Guild members formed a wedge and shot forward like a single arrow.
At their head, Choi Minwoo charged toward the magic field with a thunderous cry.
“Enter!”
Swoooosh!
Never before had the Gate’s magic felt so unpleasant.
Choi Minwoo opened his eyes, a sense of foreboding stirring deep in his chest.
His heart sank.
This is...
Scorched earth.
Was there any better way to describe the sight before him?
From the hill where the Gate entrance stood, they had a clear view of the trail below.
It was completely engulfed in flames.
Mr.
Jin Taekyung.
The foreboding he had felt while passing through the Gate seemed to be slowly taking shape.
Im Kkeokjeong spoke from behind him, his voice trembling.
“Team Leader Choi.
What if Taekyung...”
“Stop.
We’re in the middle of an operation.
Don’t jump to conclusions.”
But this time, even Team Leader Choi’s words failed to reassure them.
The situation before them looked that hopeless.
Im Kkeokjeong wasn’t the only one shaken.
Every member of the Peace Guild was in turmoil.
No.
It can’t be.
Choi Minwoo bit down hard on his lip, steadying himself, then moved forward with heavy steps.
“We’ll continue our approach.
Stay alert and keep advancing.”
They moved cautiously forward, prepared for monsters to appear at any moment.
But the closer they came to the trail, the deeper their despair grew.
“This can’t be...”
A mountain of shattered bones and weapons.
Ash blanketing the blackened ground.
There was no trace of life anywhere in that place, where death and destruction reigned.
Nor was there any sign of the one person they had so desperately hoped to find.
Dead?
Him?
The same question flashed through everyone’s mind.
Those who had known Jin Taekyung the longest could only blink at the unbelievable sight.
Butler Kim’s words broke the suffocating silence like a doctor delivering his final verdict.
“According to the results of the detection magic... we found no movement or living creatures within a three-hundred-meter radius.”
Choi Minwoo’s eyelids trembled.
“You mean...”
“I’m sorry.”
His face devastated, Butler Kim extended a hand.
Something rose into the air from the direction he indicated and slowly flew toward them.
“That’s...”
“Judging by the considerable magic I can sense from it, it appears to be a trace left by the Named Monster.”
A palm-sized metal fragment rested in Butler Kim’s hand.
Its black sheen remained undiminished despite the ash covering it.
Several people sucked in sharp breaths when they saw the chilling skull emblem.
“The skull emblem!
Th-that’s part of the armor the Named Monster was wearing!”
“That’s right!
We saw it clearly.”
Then someone searching the area cried out.
“There’s a dagger here too!
It isn’t the kind of equipment Skeletons use!”
“It belongs to Senior Jin Taekyung.
It’s the one he used all the time.”
As shock settled over the group, Butler Kim spoke in a subdued voice.
“It appears he was oxidized along with every enemy, including the Named Monster...”
The air around the trail seemed to crackle.
Now everything was certain.
Jin Taekyung was dead.
He had thrown away his own life, taking his enemies with him as companions on the road to the afterlife and leaving his comrades behind.
Im Kkeokjeong’s wail finally shattered the seemingly endless silence.
“Ghk.
Nghh...”
A faint tremor began in his hands, climbed through his arms, shoulders, and back, then spread through his entire body.
Tears poured from Im Kkeokjeong’s large eyes.
“Taekyung...
Taekyung...
Nghh!”
No one mocked him as his massive frame shook with sobs.
Their grief might differ in depth, but everyone there felt the same.
Grief over Jin Taekyung’s death.
Guilt that they had been unable to fight alongside him.
And the helplessness they felt toward themselves.
The Peace Guild members’ eyes grew red and bloodshot.
Tears streamed down Butler Kim’s and Song Song’s cheeks.
Only one person did not cry.
Choi Minwoo.
He’s dead.
Jin Taekyung is dead.
His dark eyes swept over the trail, where acrid smoke still curled into the air.
It felt as though Taekyung might be hiding somewhere even now, ready to spring out like a jack-in-the-box.
I thought you could survive anything.
His chest suddenly tightened.
He had not felt this way since losing his parents.
His grief swelled like a balloon, stretching taut, ready to burst at any moment.
Then a voice drifted over.
“My, what a gruesome sight.”
“Jin Taekyung is nowhere to be seen.
It appears he really is dead.”
Choi Minwoo slowly turned around.
Hundreds of people had just entered the trail.
At the head of the Association and the other Hunters participating in the rescue operation stood two men.
“It seems the rescue has failed.
Wouldn’t you agree, Association President?”
“Indeed.
Everything’s been reduced to ash.
I wonder if we’ll even be able to find the body.
More importantly, where is the Named Monster?”
“We’ll have to search thoroughly, but according to the detection magic, it appears all the problems you were concerned about have been resolved.”
At Go Jun’s words, the Association President’s heavily furrowed face broke into a broad smile.
“Oh, that’s welcome news.
I thought we might have another casualty on our hands.”
“Your judgment allowed us to minimize our losses, Association President.”
“Nonsense.
This was all thanks to the Ares Guild stepping forward.
Once everything is settled, I’ll make absolutely certain that you receive a commendation plaque.
Ha ha.
It’ll be the first achievement of my term, so I’m thinking of holding a grand ceremony...
Guild Master Lee Jungryong will attend, won’t he?”
“He’s not the Guild Master.
He’s the Vice Guild Master.”
“Ah, of course.
Goodness, I’ve become so forgetful with age.”
A dry smile touched the corner of Go Jun’s mouth.
“That happens.
And if a commendation plaque is presented, the Vice Guild Master will be delighted to attend.”
“I’ll finally get to see him again.
Please put in a good word for me, Team Leader Seok.”
“I’m sure he’ll be quite pleased if I simply report exactly what I’ve seen and heard.”
“Ha ha.”
The conversation between Go Jun and the Association President was a sharp needle—a needle capable of popping Choi Minwoo’s ballooning emotions.
“Shut your mouth.”
Every sound died at once.
The Association President belatedly realized what he had heard, and his face twisted with rage.
But Go Jun responded before he could.
“You’d do well to watch your mouth.”
“I told you to shut it.”
“Young man, you don’t know the meaning of manners.
Don’t you agree, Team Leader Choi Minwoo of the Peace Guild?”
The words were barbed.
To Go Jun, Choi Minwoo was a kite with its string cut.
The Ares Guild founded by his grandfather was already as good as Lee Jungryong’s.
And now that Jin Taekyung, the troublesome figure they had been watching, was dead, there was no reason to hide his fangs any longer.
“I understand that you’re distraught over the death of a Guild member, but you need to calm down.”
Choi Minwoo ground out his reply.
“He could have survived if you bastards hadn’t stalled.”
“We did our best.
The Association President’s judgment was correct as well.
And...”
Go Jun continued in a cold, dry voice.
“You people bear some responsibility too.
Don’t you agree?”
“What were you doing while Jin Taekyung was dying?
Leisurely reading the newspaper in your office?
Or drinking at a bar in the middle of the day?”
Choi Minwoo bit his lip.
Everything Go Jun said was true.
Because he had trusted Jin Taekyung, he had set everything else aside and devoted himself to training.
But...
At least Choi Minwoo himself should not have done that.
Another needle flew at him as he struggled to speak.
“You killed Jin Taekyung.
All of you did—you pathetic weaklings who forgot your duty.”
Go Jun let out a short laugh.
“It’s too late for regrets.
The dead don’t come back.”
Choi Minwoo clenched his fists until they felt ready to burst.
Then—
“What the fuck are you talking about, you motherfucking bastard?”
The voice was low but powerful, piercing every ear.
Those who did not recognize it stared around in confusion at the sudden profanity.
Those who did froze like statues.
No way...
Choi Minwoo slowly turned his head.
Far down the trail, someone was trudging toward them.
“You finished the whole forty-ninth-day memorial rite while I was off taking a piss, you fucking bastard.”
Jin Taekyung hawked a wad of phlegm onto the ground.
“Square up, asshole.”

chapters.title: Chapter 300
paragraphs: The Black Wizard’s Black Forest. No, now it would be more accurate to call it the Skeleton Warlord’s Black Forest.
Either way, the gloomy forest was disgustingly vast and tangled. Without the Warlord surveying everything inside the Gate as clearly as the palm of his hand, I would have gotten lost along the way.
- I knew you were wicked, but you are stupid as well. What would you have done without me?
“Right. Which way now?”
- Turn right in one hundred paces.
“...How does this bastard even know the words ‘turn right’?”
One captured Warlord was worth ten GPS units.
Swoooosh!
Following the Warlord’s directions, I shot through the forest at dazzling speed.

Perhaps it was thanks to the half-jiazi of internal energy I had gained while performing True Qi Guidance on Team Leader Choi, but even as I used my movement technique with all my strength, my internal energy continued surging up like an inexhaustible spring.
More is always better.
After I had run for a while, the sounds of people moving and talking gradually drew closer.
My unbelievably enhanced eyesight picked out familiar faces beyond the brush, hundreds of meters away.
Team Leader Choi and Butler Kim. Uncle Kkeokjeong and Song Song too?
I could also see the new Guild members I had sent out about an hour earlier.
Forget those guys. Why were the people who should’ve been busting their asses circulating their qi all the way out here?
Then the facts I had forgotten flashed through my mind.
Oh. Right.
I had known there would be an uproar outside.

That was why I had planned to deal with the Warlord and the Skeleton army, then leave immediately. But the unexpected discovery of an EXP factory had gotten me so excited that I’d wandered away from the scene instead.
Things must have gone completely insane outside by now.
Then again, considering the supposed emergency, they had taken their sweet time getting here. At least an hour had passed since I sent the new Guild members out of the Gate.
I’ll explain what happened. It’ll be fine.
I was about to step out of the brush when someone shouted.
“The skull emblem! Y-yes, this is the armor the Named Monster was wearing!”
“We found a dagger too! This isn’t equipment used by Skeletons!”
“It’s the dagger Senior Jin Taekyung used!”
At the succession of shouts, Im Kkeokjeong burst into tears.
“Hk, nghh!”
“Taekyung. Taekyung... Nghh!”
No way. Was this what I thought it was?
As I stood there with my mouth hanging open, the Warlord rolled its green, glowing eyes toward me.
- It appears those humans believe you are dead.
“Uh, yeah. There seems to be a huge misunderstanding.”
- Then should you not stop hiding like a rat and go out there?
But the situation was already spiraling out of control.
Song Song and Butler Kim suddenly began shedding tears, and even the Guild members lowered their heads with red-rimmed eyes.
The path grew heavy with grief and mourning.
No. I couldn’t possibly walk out into this atmosphere.
What would happen if I showed up now and said, “Surprise! You thought I was dead, but I’m alive!”
What do you think? They’d curse me to hell and back.
The thought of dealing with the aftermath made me break into a cold sweat. Even so, I had to clear up the misunderstanding before the mood got any worse.
But first, there was someone I needed to deal with.
“You stay inside for a while.”
- Hmm? What do you mean?
“I don’t know if this’ll work... but people might be startled, so get inside for now.”
- Inside where?
Ignoring the Warlord’s puzzled question, I immediately muttered the command in my mind.
Open Inventory. Store.
Pop.
At the same time as the command, the Warlord’s skull vanished from my hand.
The Inventory was a space that living creatures could not enter. However, since the Skeleton Warlord was an undead monster that had lost its vitality long ago, it seemed to work.
“Oh, it worked.”
- Gah! Where am I?
“What the hell? You can talk from inside?”
Was it because the Inventory and I were connected?
I had never tried putting anything alive inside before, so this was a first.
As I marveled at the situation, the Warlord’s shrill voice rang through my head.
- What have you done to me? Release me this instant!
“Yeah. That’s not happening.”
- Do you think you will escape unscathed after doing this to me?
“I think I’ll live a long and healthy life, remain safe and sound, and never grow old or die.”
- It’s so suffocating! I’m going insane in here!
“Why would you suffocate? You don’t breathe in the first place.”
- You insolent wretch!
“Ah, you’re loud. Should I just make you disappear?”
The Warlord’s voice brightened at once.
- This is a far more comfortable space than I expected.
“Good. Rest comfortably. And even if you do come out, don’t say a word in front of the people.”
- Understood. But...
“But what?”
- For a wicked human, you appear to have quite a few friends. Another considerable number of intruders have entered.
A moment later, I narrowed my eyes as hundreds of Hunters surged toward us like a cloud.
The Warlord was only half right. There were certainly a lot of them, but they weren’t my friends.
Especially the bastard leading the charge like a triumphant general.
Go Jun?
Why the hell was that bastard here?
The middle-aged man stuck to his side like his soulmate was someone I had seen several times on television and in the newspapers.
Even the Seoul Branch President came?
The Ares Guild and the Seoul Branch had both shown up.
This had become much bigger than I’d expected, which made it even harder to reveal myself.
I anxiously waited for the right moment. Then I overheard the two men talking and let out a hollow laugh.
“Would you look at these bastards.”
I had only caught fragments of their conversation, but it was enough to understand what was happening.
Lee Jungryong had sent Go Jun to eliminate the threat I posed, while the Association President wanted a connection to someone as powerful as Lee Jungryong.
Well, this was...
“Beautiful. Absolutely beautiful.”
One bastard wanted to delay the rescue operation to make sure I died, and the other had eagerly accepted his proposal. They were both pieces of shit from the same cesspool.
Even if it meant getting my hands dirty, I had to clean up this shit myself. It was hard to walk around without a care when turds like these were scattered across the road.
“It’s too late for regrets. The dead don’t come back.”
I saw Go Jun laugh quietly as he mocked Team Leader Choi. Without hesitation, I pushed through the brush and walked out.
“What the fuck are you talking about, you motherfucking bastard?”
At least one of them needed to be taught a lesson.
Shock, disbelief, bewilderment.
With every step, gazes filled with different emotions flew toward me and struck me in the face.
As I passed, I patted the shoulders of Team Leader Choi and the Guild members, who had frozen at my appearance.
Greetings could wait. I needed to clean up that lump of shit before it stank any worse.
Step. Step. Tap.
My final step brought me to a stop in front of two men.
“You were... alive?”
“J-Jin Taekyung, Hunter?”
I gazed at the two pairs of trembling eyes belonging to Go Jun and the Seoul Branch President, then looked at Go Jun.
“Why? Disappointed I’m alive?”
“...Of course not.”
“That’s strange. Your answer came half a beat late.”
“You’re imagining things.”
Go Jun continued in a steadier voice.
“We were all searching for you. Where were you?”
“Oh, I went nearby to take a piss. But by the time I got back, you’d practically finished the funeral procession and even held the forty-ninth-day memorial rite.”
“Urinate?”
“I drank a lot of water before entering the Gate.”
“You certainly took your time.”
“It’s a symbol of virility. If you’re interested, I can show you how to make a rainbow with my piss. It’s really pretty.”
“...Judging by the nonsense you’re spouting, you seem perfectly fine.”
“I’m always perfectly fine. But...”
I smiled faintly.
“Are you sick? The way nothing but dogshit keeps pouring out of your mouth makes me think you might have rabies.”
“I have to admit, listening to you was pretty entertaining. A commendation plaque this, a commendation plaque that—you were making a whole fucking production out of it.”
Go Jun wasn’t the only one whose face stiffened.
The Seoul Branch President, who had been silently swallowing as he listened to us, cut in with a flushed face.
“Young man, you have quite a filthy mouth.”
“Yes, my mouth’s a little filthy. But who are you?”
The Association President frowned at my curt response.
“You don’t know me?”
“Are you the President?”
“No.”
“Then you need to introduce yourself. How else would I know?”
“Good heavens. In all my years...”
Clicking his tongue, the Association President thrust out his chest, his arrogant face radiating authority.
His fat chest bulged beneath the suit jacket he had gone to the trouble of wearing into the Gate.
“I am Lee Woojoong.”
“Oh, Lee Woojoong.”
I scratched my chin with an innocent expression.
“Do you happen to know Kim Jeonghee?”
“Kim Jeonghee? Do you mean the Association elder?”
“No. She’s my mother.”
“Lady Kim Jeonghee. My mother.”
The Association President was briefly lost for words. Then he asked incredulously,
“So what? What am I supposed to do about that?”

“That’s what I wanted to ask you. Normally, people say what organization they’re from, then give their position and name. If you leave all that out and just say ‘Lee Woojoong,’ what am I supposed to do with that? You might as well have said ‘gynecomastia.’”
“What did you say?”
“So who exactly are you, Mr. Lee Woojoong?”
“I’m Lee Woojoong! The Seoul Branch President of the Hunter Association!”
“Ah. Nice to meet you.”
“Two twos are four. Two threes are six. Two nines are fuckin’ eighteen.”
“How dare you!”
I let out a short laugh as the Association President’s face turned bright red, as though he might explode at any moment.

I knew perfectly well that the Seoul Branch President was one of the most important posts of all. Even so, I made no effort to hide my contempt because he was a human being who deserved to be despised.
A man who’s supposed to be responsible for Hunters’ safety and rights pulled something like this.
If anyone other than me had been left inside this Gate, they would have died.
The Association President had known that, yet he had delayed the rescue for an entire hour. All so he could curry favor with the Ares Guild—or rather, with Lee Jungryong.
“Jin Taekyung, what the hell kind of man are you?”
I stared coldly at the Association President as he shouted and pointed a finger at me.
“What kind of man am I? The kind who killed two Named Monsters alone while waiting an entire hour for a rescue team.”
“Th-that...”
The Association President flinched at my aura and took a step backward.
But the distance between us didn’t widen. I matched him step for step.
Step.
One step.
“President Lee Woojoong.”
“B-back away.”
Step.
Another step.
“If you’re the Association President, work for the Hunter Association. Don’t work for a Guild.”
“I-I have no idea what you’re talking about.”
“Would you like me to make it clear? In front of everyone?”
Step. Tap.
As I took the third and final step, a strong hand closed around my shoulder.
“That’s far enough.”
I grinned at Go Jun as he stepped between us.
“Get your hand off me. You smell like shit.”
“Do you enjoy escalating things?”
“Why? Are you scared?”
“Scared?”
Go Jun gave a dry laugh and whispered in my ear.
“You’re the ones who should be afraid. Everyone behind me is either an Ares Guild Hunter or an Association Hunter. If you want to get out of here alive, you’d better watch your mouth.”
“Oh, so if things go bad, you’ll bury everyone here and walk away? That’s a bit too big for you. Can you handle it?”
“That’s why I’m holding back. Consider yourself lucky.”
“Scary. By the way, are you all right after I beat the shit out of you last time? Drink a good potion?”
Go Jun’s eyes went flat.
“What a childish taunt.”
“Look in a mirror. Judging by your expression, it worked pretty damn well.”
“I’m telling you one last time. Back off.”
“And I’m telling you for the last last time. Take your hand off me.”
Huff.
Hot, foul breath spilled from his mouth.
Go Jun glared at me with sunken eyes, then took several steps back and muttered,
“If it hadn’t been for my Master’s special order... you would have died here.”
“Your Master? Oh, Jungryong?”
“How’s Jungryong doing? Isn’t it about time you found him a place in a retirement community?”
That was the decisive blow.
Go Jun trembled from head to toe as though he had been electrocuted. His eyes flew wide, blazing with a light unlike anything I had seen when we fought at the hospital.
“If you think this will end the same way it did last time... I’ll make you regret it.”
“Regret?”
I beamed and spread my arms wide.
“You talk too much. Quit posturing and come at me.”
Whoooosh!

They’d curse me to hell and back.
The thought of dealing with the aftermath made me break into a cold sweat.
Even so, I had to clear up the misunderstanding before the mood got any worse.
But first, there was someone I needed to deal with.
“You stay inside for a while.”
- Hmm?
What do you mean?
“I don’t know if this’ll work... but people might be startled, so get inside for now.”
- Inside where?
Ignoring the Warlord’s puzzled question, I immediately muttered the command in my mind.
Open Inventory.
Store.
Pop.
At the same time as the command, the Warlord’s skull vanished from my hand.
The Inventory was a space that living creatures could not enter.
However, since the Skeleton Warlord was an undead monster that had lost its vitality long ago, it seemed to work.
“Oh, it worked.”
- Gah!
Where am I?
“What the hell?
You can talk from inside?”
Was it because the Inventory and I were connected?
I had never tried putting anything alive inside before, so this was a first.
As I marveled at the situation, the Warlord’s shrill voice rang through my head.
- What have you done to me?
Release me this instant!
“Yeah.
That’s not happening.”
- Do you think you will escape unscathed after doing this to me?
“I think I’ll live a long and healthy life, remain safe and sound, and never grow old or die.”
- It’s so suffocating!
I’m going insane in here!
“Why would you suffocate?
You don’t breathe in the first place.”
- You insolent wretch!
“Ah, you’re loud.
Should I just make you disappear?”
The Warlord’s voice brightened at once.
- This is a far more comfortable space than I expected.
“Good.
Rest comfortably.
And even if you do come out, don’t say a word in front of the people.”
- Understood.
But...
“But what?”
- For a wicked human, you appear to have quite a few friends.
Another considerable number of intruders have entered.
A moment later, I narrowed my eyes as hundreds of Hunters surged toward us like a cloud.
The Warlord was only half right.
There were certainly a lot of them, but they weren’t my friends.
Especially the bastard leading the charge like a triumphant general.
Go Jun?
Why the hell was that bastard here?
The middle-aged man stuck to his side like his soulmate was someone I had seen several times on television and in the newspapers.
Even the Seoul Branch President came?
The Ares Guild and the Seoul Branch had both shown up.
This had become much bigger than I’d expected, which made it even harder to reveal myself.
I anxiously waited for the right moment.
Then I overheard the two men talking and let out a hollow laugh.
“Would you look at these bastards.”
I had only caught fragments of their conversation, but it was enough to understand what was happening.
Lee Jungryong had sent Go Jun to eliminate the threat I posed, while the Association President wanted a connection to someone as powerful as Lee Jungryong.
Well, this was...
“Beautiful.
Absolutely beautiful.”
One bastard wanted to delay the rescue operation to make sure I died, and the other had eagerly accepted his proposal.
They were both pieces of shit from the same cesspool.
Even if it meant getting my hands dirty, I had to clean up this shit myself.
It was hard to walk around without a care when turds like these were scattered across the road.
“It’s too late for regrets.
The dead don’t come back.”
I saw Go Jun laugh quietly as he mocked Team Leader Choi.
Without hesitation, I pushed through the brush and walked out.
“What the fuck are you talking about, you motherfucking bastard?”
At least one of them needed to be taught a lesson.
Shock, disbelief, bewilderment.
With every step, gazes filled with different emotions flew toward me and struck me in the face.
As I passed, I patted the shoulders of Team Leader Choi and the Guild members, who had frozen at my appearance.
Greetings could wait.
I needed to clean up that lump of shit before it stank any worse.
Step.
Step.
Tap.
My final step brought me to a stop in front of two men.
“You were... alive?”
“J-Jin Taekyung, Hunter?”
I gazed at the two pairs of trembling eyes belonging to Go Jun and the Seoul Branch President, then looked at Go Jun.
“Why?
Disappointed I’m alive?”
“...Of course not.”
“That’s strange.
Your answer came half a beat late.”
“You’re imagining things.”
Go Jun continued in a steadier voice.
“We were all searching for you.
Where were you?”
“Oh, I went nearby to take a piss.
But by the time I got back, you’d practically finished the funeral procession and even held the forty-ninth-day memorial rite.”
“Urinate?”
“I drank a lot of water before entering the Gate.”
“You certainly took your time.”
“It’s a symbol of virility.
If you’re interested, I can show you how to make a rainbow with my piss.
It’s really pretty.”
“...Judging by the nonsense you’re spouting, you seem perfectly fine.”
“I’m always perfectly fine.
But...”
I smiled faintly.
“Are you sick?
The way nothing but dogshit keeps pouring out of your mouth makes me think you might have rabies.”
“I have to admit, listening to you was pretty entertaining.
A commendation plaque this, a commendation plaque that—you were making a whole fucking production out of it.”
Go Jun wasn’t the only one whose face stiffened.
The Seoul Branch President, who had been silently swallowing as he listened to us, cut in with a flushed face.
“Young man, you have quite a filthy mouth.”
“Yes, my mouth’s a little filthy.
But who are you?”
The Association President frowned at my curt response.
“You don’t know me?”
“Are you the President?”
“No.”
“Then you need to introduce yourself.
How else would I know?”
“Good heavens.
In all my years...”
Clicking his tongue, the Association President thrust out his chest, his arrogant face radiating authority.
His fat chest bulged beneath the suit jacket he had gone to the trouble of wearing into the Gate.
“I am Lee Woojoong.”
“Oh, Lee Woojoong.”
I scratched my chin with an innocent expression.
“Do you happen to know Kim Jeonghee?”
“Kim Jeonghee?
Do you mean the Association elder?”
“No.
She’s my mother.”
“Lady Kim Jeonghee.
My mother.”
The Association President was briefly lost for words.
Then he asked incredulously,
“So what?
What am I supposed to do about that?”
“That’s what I wanted to ask you.
Normally, people say what organization they’re from, then give their position and name.
If you leave all that out and just say ‘Lee Woojoong,’ what am I supposed to do with that?
You might as well have said ‘gynecomastia.’”
“What did you say?”
“So who exactly are you, Mr.
Lee Woojoong?”
“I’m Lee Woojoong!
The Seoul Branch President of the Hunter Association!”
“Ah.
Nice to meet you.”
“Two twos are four.
Two threes are six.
Two nines are fuckin’ eighteen.”
“How dare you!”
I let out a short laugh as the Association President’s face turned bright red, as though he might explode at any moment.
I knew perfectly well that the Seoul Branch President was one of the most important posts of all.
Even so, I made no effort to hide my contempt because he was a human being who deserved to be despised.
A man who’s supposed to be responsible for Hunters’ safety and rights pulled something like this.
If anyone other than me had been left inside this Gate, they would have died.
The Association President had known that, yet he had delayed the rescue for an entire hour.
All so he could curry favor with the Ares Guild—or rather, with Lee Jungryong.
“Jin Taekyung, what the hell kind of man are you?”
I stared coldly at the Association President as he shouted and pointed a finger at me.
“What kind of man am I?
The kind who killed two Named Monsters alone while waiting an entire hour for a rescue team.”
“Th-that...”
The Association President flinched at my aura and took a step backward.
But the distance between us didn’t widen.
I matched him step for step.
Step.
One step.
“President Lee Woojoong.”
“B-back away.”
Step.
Another step.
“If you’re the Association President, work for the Hunter Association.
Don’t work for a Guild.”
“I-I have no idea what you’re talking about.”
“Would you like me to make it clear?
In front of everyone?”
Step.
Tap.
As I took the third and final step, a strong hand closed around my shoulder.
“That’s far enough.”
I grinned at Go Jun as he stepped between us.
“Get your hand off me.
You smell like shit.”
“Do you enjoy escalating things?”
“Why?
Are you scared?”
“Scared?”
Go Jun gave a dry laugh and whispered in my ear.
“You’re the ones who should be afraid.
Everyone behind me is either an Ares Guild Hunter or an Association Hunter.
If you want to get out of here alive, you’d better watch your mouth.”
“Oh, so if things go bad, you’ll bury everyone here and walk away?
That’s a bit too big for you.
Can you handle it?”
“That’s why I’m holding back.
Consider yourself lucky.”
“Scary.
By the way, are you all right after I beat the shit out of you last time?
Drink a good potion?”
Go Jun’s eyes went flat.
“What a childish taunt.”
“Look in a mirror.
Judging by your expression, it worked pretty damn well.”
“I’m telling you one last time.
Back off.”
“And I’m telling you for the last last time.
Take your hand off me.”
Huff.
Hot, foul breath spilled from his mouth.
Go Jun glared at me with sunken eyes, then took several steps back and muttered,
“If it hadn’t been for my Master’s special order... you would have died here.”
“Your Master?
Oh, Jungryong?”
“How’s Jungryong doing?
Isn’t it about time you found him a place in a retirement community?”
That was the decisive blow.
Go Jun trembled from head to toe as though he had been electrocuted.
His eyes flew wide, blazing with a light unlike anything I had seen when we fought at the hospital.
“If you think this will end the same way it did last time...
I’ll make you regret it.”
“Regret?”
I beamed and spread my arms wide.
“You talk too much.
Quit posturing and come at me.”
Whoooosh!
